## Summary: T1S/10BASE-T1S Single-Pair Ethernet Planning — Complete Capture

I've conducted a thorough search across the repository. Here's what has been captured about T1S / single-pair Ethernet for the marvin ↔ fretboard link:

### **Primary Documentation**

**File: `/Users/gregmrozek/Projects/microchip/guitar-pic/docs/t1s-podl-link.md`**

This is the authoritative low-level engineering document (140 lines). Key sections:

- **Lines 1–11:** Status statement — "direction, not yet built." The link today is FLEXCOM2 UART (system spec M2). Nothing here is flashed yet.

- **Lines 13–26:** Why T1S here
  - Primary motivation: **PoDL** (Power-over-Data-Lines) — one twisted pair carries both data and the fretboard's power, eliminating separate power feed
  - Secondary: robustness/reach vs TTL UART on noisy/long cable runs
  - Multidrop headroom: 10BASE-T1S/PLCA supports up to 8 nodes on one pair
  - Demonstration goal: showcasing 10BASE-T1S + PoDL inside a larger Microchip system (SAM9X7 + LAN8651 + PIC32CM)
  - Bandwidth is **not** a motivation — existing 500 kbaud UART already carries ~4 KB/s payload with ~12× headroom

- **Lines 27–42:** Hardware choice: **LAN8651B1** (MAC-PHY integrating IEEE 802.3 Clause 4 MAC and 10BASE-T1S PHY)
  - Talks to host MCU over **SPI** using **OPEN Alliance TC6** ("10BASE-T1x MAC-PHY Serial Interface", v1.1) protocol
  - Hardware handles: line coding, PLCA/CSMA-CD media access, preamble/SFD, FCS (CRC32) generation/checking, on-wire framing, minimum-frame padding
  - SPI: LAN8651 is SPI client, SCLK up to 25 MHz. Pins: SDI, SDO, CS_N, SCLK, IRQ_N (active-low interrupt), reset

- **Lines 44–69:** Host MCU implementation layers (no TCP/IP stack needed):
  1. **SPI transport** — one SERCOM in SPI-master mode + GPIO for CS_N, IRQ_N (external interrupt), reset
  2. **OA TC6 chunk protocol** — only real "driver." Fixed-size chunks (default 64-byte payload + 4-byte header on TX / 4-byte footer on RX), credit-based flow control, separate control-transaction format for register read/writes
     - Reference driver: **[`MicrochipTech/oa-tc6-lib`](https://github.com/MicrochipTech/oa-tc6-lib)** (open-source, small enough for Arduino — candidate base for both fretboard and marvin)
  3. **Minimal L2 framing** — 14-byte Ethernet header (dest MAC, src MAC, ethertype)
     - Custom ethertype carries existing frame formats verbatim inside payload
     - fretboard → marvin: 17-byte data-stream frame
     - marvin → fretboard: 1-byte button bitmask
     - **17 B + 14 B header = 31 B → single chunk**

- **Lines 71–86:** Resource budget for **fretboard (PIC32CM6408PL10048, 64 KB flash / 8 KB SRAM)**
  - Flash: ~6–10 KB (OA TC6 lib + SPI glue + L2 framing; can reclaim UART data path if fully retired)
  - SRAM: ~1–2 KB (couple chunk buffers + one TX/RX frame buffer)
  - SERCOM: 1 (SPI master, separate from SERCOM1 which currently handles UART)
  - GPIO: 2–3 (CS_N, IRQ_N, reset)
  - CPU: negligible (one chunk per 240 Hz tick, interrupt-driven off IRQ_N)
  - SPI clock: SERCOM SPI master maxes at GCLK/2 ≈ 12 MHz on 24 MHz part (irrelevant for this data rate)

- **Lines 88–94:** marvin side
  - Runs **bare-metal** (no Linux), so **no free netdev** — needs its own TC6 driver
  - Plan: **single portable `oa_tc6` layer shared between marvin (Cortex-A5) and fretboard (Cortex-M0+)** — demonstrates the OPEN Alliance SPI driver scales across the family
  - marvin resources are not a concern

- **Lines 96–108:** PoDL — "dumb" (no negotiation)
  - **PoDL is NOT in the LAN8651** — MAC-PHY only moves data
  - PoDL is external coupling circuitry around the pair, transparent to both MCUs (zero firmware footprint)
  - PSE side (marvin): fixed-voltage source + coupling inductors inject DC onto pair
  - PD side (fretboard): coupling inductors extract DC + regulator down to PIC32CM rail
  - Dumb/unmanaged: no SCCP classification/negotiation, fixed supply voltage, fixed point-to-point pair, decided at design time
  - Microchip has PoDL reference designs that pair with LAN865x EVBs

- **Lines 113–118:** Topology decision: PLCA multidrop vs point-to-point
  - **Recommended: enable PLCA from the start** rather than strict point-to-point
  - 2-node PLCA bus demonstrates headline T1S feature (collision-free multidrop on one pair) at no extra cost
  - Leaves door open to second node sharing same pair and power
  - Open until decided

- **Lines 120–127:** Open items needing decision before implementation
  - PLCA vs pure point-to-point (§7)
  - PoDL supply voltage and PD-side regulator topology (BOM, not firmware)
  - Custom ethertype value and two hardcoded MAC addresses
  - Whether to keep UART link as fallback during bring-up or cut over outright
  - Magnetics-free coupling component selection on Sensor-LCD5 PCB

- **Lines 129–140:** References
  - OA TC6 driver: [`MicrochipTech/oa-tc6-lib`](https://github.com/MicrochipTech/oa-tc6-lib)
  - LAN8650/1 datasheet on Microchip online docs
  - OPEN Alliance *10BASE-T1x MAC-PHY Serial Interface* specification (TC6), v1.1

### **Protocol/Stack Decisions Made**

1. **Transport layer:** IEEE 802.3 Clause 4 MAC + 10BASE-T1S PHY via **LAN8651B1 MAC-PHY** (integrates both on one chip)
2. **Host↔MAC-PHY interface:** **OPEN Alliance TC6** v1.1 protocol over **SPI**
3. **Chunk format:** Default 64-byte payload + 4-byte header on TX / 4-byte footer on RX, credit-based flow control
4. **MAC-layer framing:** **Minimal L2** — 14-byte Ethernet header with hardcoded source/destination MACs and custom ethertype
5. **Application payload:** Existing frame formats ride unchanged (17-byte sensor stream + 1-byte command bitmask)
6. **Media access:** **PLCA** (Physical Layer Collision Avoidance) multidrop recommended over strict point-to-point

### **Hardware Chosen**

| Component | Spec |
|-----------|------|
| MAC-PHY IC | **LAN8651B1** — 10BASE-T1S, SPI interface, up to 25 MHz SCLK |
| fretboard side | 1 SERCOM in SPI-master mode, GPIO for CS_N / IRQ_N / reset |
| marvin side | 1 SERCOM in SPI-master mode, GPIO for CS_N / IRQ_N / reset |
| Power coupling | Fixed-voltage PSE on marvin side, capacitive/inductive coupling, PD regulator on fretboard side (transparent to MCU) |
| Single pair cable | TBD: magnetics-free coupling component on Sensor-LCD5 PCB |

### **Driver Repository Referenced**

**`MicrochipTech/oa-tc6-lib`** — https://github.com/MicrochipTech/oa-tc6-lib
- Open-source reference driver for OPEN Alliance TC6 SPI protocol
- Small enough for Arduino; candidate base for shared portable layer on both marvin (Cortex-A5) and fretboard (Cortex-M0+)

### **Node Addressing / Topology Planned**

- **Current:**  Point-to-point UART (marvin ↔ fretboard only)
- **Planned:** **2-node PLCA bus** (fretboard + future second sensor/guitar node sharing one twisted pair + PoDL power)
- **Hardcoded MACs:** Source/destination MAC addresses TBD (custom, not standard unicast)
- **Custom ethertype:** Value TBD (carries proprietary frame formats)
- **No DHCP/ARP/IP.** Static Layer 2 only.

## Marvin Firmware Exploration Report

I've thoroughly mapped the marvin firmware structure for integration of the T1S inter-node communication interface. Here's the complete architectural picture:

### 1. **Overall Source Layout** (`firmware/marvin/default/src/`)

**Core modules:**
- **`app.c/h`** — Application entry point (lines 97–193 in app.c). Initializes all subsystems in sequence, then spawns FreeRTOS task-based modules. Uses `xTaskCreateStatic` for static allocation (no malloc).
- **`main.c`** — Minimal: calls `SYS_Initialize()` then loops `SYS_Tasks()`.
- **`log.c/h`** — Logging shim with FreeRTOS-aware locking.

**Subsystems (all task-based FreeRTOS):**
- **`video/`** — HDMI capture (TC358743 → CSI-2 → ISC → DDR). Owns frame queue subscriptions. Files: `video.c/h`, `isc_capture.c/h`, `tc358743.c/h` (35 KB — comprehensive bridging logic).
- **`detector/`** — CV note detection (cv_marvin_v1) + detector-state bus. Files: `detector.c/h`, `cv_marvin_v1.c/h`. Detector-state records are fixed-width `detector_state_t` (line 33–45 in detector.h), published onto `xDetectorStateQueue`.
- **`actuator/`** — Timing pipeline + fretboard link. Files: `timing_pipeline.c/h`, `fretboard_link.c/h`, `manual_control.c/h`.
  - **`fretboard_link.c`** (lines 1–279): FLEXCOM1 USART ring-buffer host. Bidirectional: TX (1-byte bitmask, 50 ms heartbeat), RX (17-byte ADC frames with frame markers `0x03`/`0xFC`). Task stack: 768 words (TX) + 512 words (RX). Queue depth 1 (latest-wins semantics). Link rate: 500 kbaud 8N1.
- **`game/`** — Gameplay engine (screen classification, menu navigation).
- **`console/`** — Operator CLI on FLEXCOM2 (115200 8N1, embedded-cli). Files: `console.c/h` (1000 lines).
- **`ui/`** — Legato graphics UI.
- **`perf_log/`** — Performance telemetry + USB-CDC export. Multi-producer (ISR-safe queues), single drain task. Records tagged with frame_epoch for cross-detector sync.

**Config system:**
- **`config/default/`** — MCC-generated Harmony configuration. Contains:
  - **`initialization.c`** (303–394): `SYS_Initialize()` wires up all peripherals in order (CLK → PIO → XDMAC → PIT → MMU → AIC → TC0 → FLEXCOM1/2 → XLCDC → DBGU → drivers → USB → Legato → APP_Initialize). FLEXCOM1 initialized at line 335.
  - **`peripheral/flexcom/usart/plib_flexcom1_usart.h`** — PLIB interface for FLEXCOM1 (ring-buffer mode, callbacks, threshold notifications).
  - **`driver/i2c/src/drv_i2c.c/h`** — I2C driver (I2C0 on FLEXCOM8 TWI for TC358743 control + maxtouch).
  - **`definitions.h`** — System includes all plib headers, drivers, USB, graphics stack.

---

### 2. **Existing Peripheral/Driver Structure**

**Naming conventions:**
- **PLib (peripheral library):** `plib_<peripheral>.h`, functions like `FLEXCOM1_USART_Initialize()`, `FLEXCOM1_USART_Read()`, `FLEXCOM1_USART_Write()`. Located in `peripheral/<type>/<name>/`.
- **HAL driver:** `drv_<name>.c/h`, functions like `DRV_I2C_Open()`, `DRV_I2C_ReadTransferAdd()`. Located in `driver/<name>/src/`. Uses init structs like `DRV_I2C_INIT` populated in `initialization.c`.

**Init patterns:**
1. **Peripheral init (SYS_Initialize):** Call PLib `_Initialize()` (e.g., `FLEXCOM1_USART_Initialize()` at line 335 in initialization.c).
2. **Driver init (SYS_Initialize):** Create init struct, call `DRV_*_Initialize()` returning a handle, store in `SYSTEM_OBJECTS sysObj` (line 140 in initialization.c). Example: `sysObj.drvI2C0 = DRV_I2C_Initialize(…)` at line 353.
3. **Module init (APP_Initialize):** Higher-level task/subsystem setup. Example: `Video_Initialize()` at line 111 in app.c — creates FreeRTOS task, subscribes to frame queue.

**Ring-buffer USART pattern (used by fretboard_link):**
- **Register callback:** `FLEXCOM1_USART_ReadCallbackRegister(rx_event_handler, context)` (line 233 in fretboard_link.c).
- **Set threshold:** `FLEXCOM1_USART_ReadThresholdSet(framesize)` (line 234).
- **Enable notification:** `FLEXCOM1_USART_ReadNotificationEnable(true, true)` (line 235).
- **Callback woken on threshold/full:** callback fires from ISR, posts to binary semaphore via `xSemaphoreGiveFromISR`.
- **Task drains:** `FLEXCOM1_USART_ReadCountGet()` checks pending bytes, `FLEXCOM1_USART_Read(&buf, want)` drains, resync on markers.
- **TX:** `FLEXCOM1_USART_Write(buf, 1)` enqueues to TX ring, returns immediately.

**Task pattern (FreeRTOS static allocation):**
```c
static StackType_t s_task_stack[STACK_WORDS];
static StaticTask_t s_task_tcb;
TaskHandle_t h = xTaskCreateStatic(task_func, "Name", STACK_WORDS, NULL, PRIORITY, s_task_stack, &s_task_tcb);
```
Example: lines 239–246 in fretboard_link.c. Priorities: timing_pipeline = 5, fretboard_link = 5 (same tier).

---

### 3. **Build System**

**CMake-based (not Makefile):**
- **Root:** `/firmware/marvin/cmake/marvin/default/CMakeLists.txt` (13–22). Minimal: includes `.generated/main.cmake` + optional `user.cmake`.
- **Generated file list:** `/cmake/marvin/default/.generated/file.cmake` (1+). Exhaustive list of source files (over 500 entries from Legato, USB CDC, GFX, peripherals, FreeRTOS).
- **Toolchain:** `/cmake/marvin/default/.generated/toolchain.cmake` — XC32 compiler config.
- **User customization:** Create `/cmake/marvin/default/user.cmake` to inject custom sources/flags (never committed by MCC, safe to version-control).

**Adding a new driver module:**
1. Create `.c` + `.h` files in `default/src/config/default/driver/<name>/src/`.
2. Add sources to `.generated/file.cmake` (or create a `user.cmake` to append for development).
3. Wrap init in a struct (e.g., `DRV_T1S_INIT`) and call `DRV_T1S_Initialize()` from `initialization.c` or a task.
4. Register tasks via `PerfLog_RegisterTaskForHighwater()` if task-based.

**Build artifacts:** `out/` directory (final binaries).

---

### 4. **Existing Networking, Message-Passing, Command/Event Interfaces**

**Fretboard link (current M2, FLEXCOM1 USART):**
- **Marvin → fretboard:** 1-byte bitmask (7 bits: 5 frets + 2 strum). Latest-wins via `xQueueOverwrite` (queue depth 1). Sent every 50 ms (line 39 in fretboard_link.c) + on state change.
- **Fretboard → marvin:** 17-byte frames at 240 Hz (lines 26–34 in fretboard_link.c). Format: `[0x03, 5×ADC_u16, seq_u32, applied_mask_u8, 0xFC]`. Resync on markers. Ring-buffer RX.
- **Perf-log snoop:** Fretboard raw frames also emit `PERF_REC_FRETBOARD_RAW` records (line 204 in fretboard_link.c).

**Detector-state bus (internal event bus):**
- **Queue:** `xDetectorStateQueue` (single FreeRTOS queue, detector.h line 57).
- **Record:** `detector_state_t` (fixed-width, detector.h lines 33–45):
  ```c
  struct {
    uint32_t frame_epoch;     // master sync (frame counter)
    uint64_t timestamp_us;    // local monotonic
    uint8_t detector_id;      // 0=cv_marvin_v1, 1=adc_fretboard
    uint8_t reserved[3];
    struct { uint8_t pressed; uint16_t confidence; uint16_t raw_value; } fret[5];
  }
  ```
- **Producers:** cv_marvin_v1 task (reads frames, emits per-frame), adc_fretboard (future, reads UART stream).
- **Consumer:** timing_pipeline task (reads bus, runs chord FIFO, calls `FretboardLink_Send()`).
- **Recording:** perf_log snoops via side-channel (no broker, each detector posts to both bus + recording stream).

**Console (operator CLI):**
- **FLEXCOM2 USART** (lines 3–4 in console.h). 115200 8N1, ring-buffer mode.
- **Embedded-cli** (third-party embedded-cli library, lines 5–10 in console.h).
- **Commands:** Set detector enable/active, manual fret/strum input, status print, timing constants (all defined in console.c).
- **Entirely separate from DBGU log channel** (DBGU = printf retarget, FLEXCOM2 = interactive console).

**Perf-log telemetry (USB-CDC export):**
- **Transport:** USB device CDC ACM (USB_DEVICE_INDEX_0, file.cmake line ~377).
- **Rate:** up to 2.77 MB/s (spec.md line 196).
- **Records:** Stamped with `perf_rec_*_t` types (perf_log_records.h). Multi-producer (ISR-safe + task-safe queues), single drain task.
- **Format:** SOF + length + payload + CRC-16/CCITT (lines 13–15 in perf_log.h).
- **Default disabled:** Producers emit; mask gate (line 146 in perf_log.h) filters client-side.

**Future T1S link (planned, not built):**
- Replace FLEXCOM1 UART with SPI + OA TC6 (10BASE-T1S MAC-PHY) + L2 framing.
- **PLib:** New SPI master PLib (SAM9X75 has SERCOM/FLEXCOM SPI capable).
- **Driver layer:** OA TC6 chunk protocol (Microchip open-source `oa-tc6-lib`).
- **Fretboard link API stays same:** `FretboardLink_Initialize()`, `FretboardLink_Send()`, `FretboardLink_IsConnected()` (fretboard_link.h lines 29–31) — only transport swapped beneath.
- **Spec:** `docs/t1s-podl-link.md` (lines 1–140, fully documented design).

---

### 5. **RTOS vs Bare-Metal, Task Structure, Static-Allocation Patterns**

**FreeRTOS (not bare-metal):**
- Scheduler active at power-on (SYS_Initialize → initialization.c line 388 → APP_Initialize).
- Tasks created pre-scheduler with `xTaskCreateStatic` in APP_Initialize (app.c lines 111–174).
- APP_Tasks itself (app.c lines 186–193) calls `vTaskDelete(NULL)` to self-exit post-launch.

**Task hierarchy (in start order):**
1. **Video task** (app.c line 111): `Video_Initialize()` — captures frames, notifies subscribers.
2. **PerfLog queues** (app.c line 117): Subscribers set up before video task posts.
3. **Detector task** (app.c line 134): `Detector_Initialize()` + `Detector_SetActive()` — cv_marvin_v1 subscribes to frame queue inside its task.
4. **FretboardLink tasks** (app.c line 142): TX task (cmdqueue + 50 ms heartbeat), RX task (ring-buffer drain).
5. **TimingPipeline task** (app.c line 147): Consumes detector bus, emits fretboard commands.
6. **ManualControl task** (app.c line 154): UI-driven actuator producer.
7. **GameplayEngine task** (app.c line 161): Game-state observer (optional, toggled).
8. **Console task** (app.c line 167): Operator CLI (FLEXCOM2).
9. **PerfLog drain task** (app.c line 174): Last, so all producer queues valid when it starts.

**Static allocation patterns:**
- **Queues:** `xQueueCreateStatic(depth, item_size, storage, &buf)` (fretboard_link.c lines 221–225).
- **Semaphores:** `xSemaphoreCreateBinaryStatic(&buf)` (fretboard_link.c lines 227–228).
- **Tasks:** `xTaskCreateStatic(func, name, stack_words, param, priority, &stack, &tcb)` (fretboard_link.c lines 239–246, 248–255).
- **Storage:** All `static` at module scope (no heap).

**Priorities:**
- Fretboard link tasks: priority 5 (app.c line 42 in fretboard_link.c, though priorities defined in fretboard_link.c line 20).
- Typical convention: higher priority for hard real-time (video ISR → frame subscription), mid for timing pipeline, low for UI/logging.

**ISR callback patterns:**
- Peripheral ISR fires callback (e.g., FLEXCOM1 RX threshold), callback posts to semaphore via `xSemaphoreGiveFromISR()` (fretboard_link.c line 89).
- Task woken by semaphore, drains ring buffer, processes payload.
- Error handling: On RX error, clear error state + re-arm semaphore (lines 94–95).

**Example: Fretboard RX path (fretboard_link.c lines 156–217):**
1. FLEXCOM1 ISR fires when RX crosses threshold (line 234).
2. ISR callback wakes `fretboard_rx_task` via semaphore (line 89).
3. Task checks `FLEXCOM1_USART_ReadCountGet()` (line 167), reads until frame full (line 174).
4. Validates markers, parses ADC + seq + mask (lines 179–200).
5. Emits perf record (line 204).
6. Loops indefinitely (for-ever at line 165).

---

### 6. **Key File Paths & Line Numbers**

| Concern | File | Lines |
|---|---|---|
| System init (peripheral + driver setup) | `config/default/initialization.c` | 303–394 |
| FLEXCOM1 USART PLib interface | `config/default/peripheral/flexcom/usart/plib_flexcom1_usart.h` | 68–100 |
| Fretboard link (TX + RX tasks) | `actuator/fretboard_link.c/h` | 1–279 / 1–33 |
| Fretboard RX ring-buffer drain | `actuator/fretboard_link.c` | 156–217 |
| Detector-state bus record layout | `detector/detector.h` | 33–45 |
| Timing pipeline (chord FIFO producer) | `actuator/timing_pipeline.h` | 1–41 |
| Perf-log telemetry infrastructure | `perf_log/perf_log.h` | 1–159 |
| Console CLI (operator interface) | `console/console.h/c` | 1–23 / full file |
| App module initialization | `app.c` | 97–175 |
| Video task (frame capture) | `video/video.h` | 1–88 |

---

### 7. **T1S Slot-in Architecture**

**New driver module layout:**
```
default/src/config/default/driver/t1s/
  ├── src/
  │   ├── drv_t1s.c          (OA TC6 chunk protocol + L2 framing)
  │   ├── oa_tc6_portable.c   (Microchip's oa-tc6-lib, shared with fretboard)
  │   └── t1s_macphy_init.c   (LAN8651 register config, PoDL mode)
  ├── drv_t1s.h              (public API)
  ├── drv_t1s_definitions.h  (init struct, error codes)
  └── plib_flexcom_spi.h     (uses FLEXCOM SPI in PLib mode)
```

**Integration points:**

1. **initialization.c** (after line 335, before XLCDC):
   ```c
   FLEXCOM_SPI_Initialize();  // New SPI PLib on free FLEXCOM
   sysObj.drvT1S = DRV_T1S_Initialize(DRV_T1S_INDEX_0, &drvT1SInitData);
   ```

2. **definitions.h** (add includes):
   ```c
   #include "driver/t1s/drv_t1s.h"
   #include "peripheral/flexcom/spi/plib_flexcom_spi.h"
   ```

3. **app.c** (replace fretboard_link.c call):
   ```c
   // Old: FretboardLink_Initialize();
   // New:
   T1SLink_Initialize();  // Wraps drv_t1s + L2 framing, same public API as fretboard_link.h
   ```

4. **CMakeLists.txt** (in user.cmake or auto-generated):
   ```cmake
   list(APPEND marvin_default_default_XC32_FILE_TYPE_compile
       "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../../../default/src/config/default/driver/t1s/src/drv_t1s.c"
       "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../../../default/src/config/default/driver/t1s/src/oa_tc6_portable.c"
   )
   ```

**API unchanged (fretboard_link.h lines 29–31):**
```c
void T1SLink_Initialize(void);
void T1SLink_Send(uint8_t mask, uint8_t producer_id);
bool T1SLink_IsConnected(void);
```

**Resource allocation (SAM9X75):**
- **SPI:** One free FLEXCOM (FLEXCOM0, FLEXCOM3–7 available; currently FLEXCOM1=UART, FLEXCOM2=console, FLEXCOM8=I2C).
- **GPIO:** CS_N, IRQ_N (ext-int, currently unused), reset.
- **Interrupt:** One external IRQ for LAN8651 IRQ_N → ISR → chunk drain.
- **Memory:** Static task stack + chunk buffers (~2–3 KB SRAM).

**T1S wire format (L2 frame):**
```
Ethernet header (14 B):  dest MAC (6) | src MAC (6) | ethertype (2)
Payload:                 17 B (fretboard RX) or 1 B (marvin TX)
Total:                   31 B or 15 B → fits in single OA TC6 chunk (64 B data payload)
```

---

## Summary

The marvin firmware is **well-structured, FreeRTOS-based, and ready for T1S integration.** The existing `FretboardLink_{Initialize,Send,IsConnected}` API provides a clean abstraction layer; the new T1S driver plugs in beneath it without touching timing pipeline, console, or application logic. Key entry points for modification:

1. **initialization.c** (line ~335) — wire up SPI PLib + T1S driver.
2. **definitions.h** (includes section) — add driver headers.
3. **app.c** (line ~142) — swap init call (FretboardLink → T1SLink, same signature).
4. **CMakeLists.txt** or **user.cmake** — register source files.

The OA TC6 protocol layer can be ported from the open-source Microchip reference (`oa-tc6-lib`) and shared with the fretboard side (PIC32CM), keeping both ends of the bus aligned and maintainable.

```text
1	# fretboard ↔ marvin link — 10BASE-T1S + PoDL
2	
3	Low-level design for moving the fretboard ↔ marvin link from a FLEXCOM2/SERCOM
4	UART pair to **10BASE-T1S single-pair Ethernet with "dumb" Power-over-Data-Lines
5	(PoDL)**. System-level summary and rationale live in [`../SPEC.md`](../SPEC.md)
6	§6; this document holds the engineering detail.
7	
8	Status: **direction, not yet built.** The link today is FLEXCOM2 UART (system
9	spec M2). Nothing here is flashed.
10	
11	---
12	
13	## 1. Why T1S here
14	
15	- **PoDL** — one twisted pair carries both data *and* the fretboard's power, so
16	  the cable to the guitar is a single 2-wire link instead of a data pair plus a
17	  separate power feed. This is the primary motivation.
18	- **Robustness / reach** — differential single-pair Ethernet tolerates a long,
19	  electrically noisy run to a moving instrument better than a TTL UART pair.
20	- **Multidrop headroom** — 10BASE-T1S/PLCA puts up to 8 nodes on one pair, so a
21	  second sensor node or fretboard can share the same pair *and* the same power.
22	- **Demonstration** — showcasing 10BASE-T1S + PoDL doing real work inside a
23	  larger Microchip system (SAM9X7 + LAN8651 + PIC32CM) is an explicit goal, not
24	  just an incidental benefit. Bandwidth is *not* a motivation — the existing
25	  500 kbaud UART already carries the ~4 KB/s payload with ~12× headroom.
26	
27	## 2. The part: LAN8651B1
28	
29	A **MAC-PHY**: integrates the full IEEE 802.3 Clause 4 MAC *and* the 10BASE-T1S
30	PHY on one chip, and talks to the host MCU over **SPI** using the OPEN Alliance
31	TC6 ("10BASE-T1x MAC-PHY Serial Interface", v1.1) protocol. It exists precisely
32	to give a small MCU with no built-in Ethernet MAC a single-pair Ethernet link
33	over ~5 pins.
34	
35	Done in hardware by the LAN8651 (the MCU never touches these):
36	
37	- Line coding, PLCA / CSMA-CD media access, preamble/SFD.
38	- **FCS (CRC32) generation on TX and checking on RX.**
39	- On-wire framing and minimum-frame padding.
40	
41	SPI: LAN8651 is an SPI client, SCLK up to 25 MHz. Pins: `SDI`, `SDO`, `CS_N`,
42	`SCLK`, `IRQ_N` (active-low interrupt), plus a reset.
43	
44	## 3. What the host MCU must implement
45	
46	No TCP/IP, ARP, DHCP, or any IP stack. Three layers, none large:
47	
48	1. **SPI transport** — one SERCOM in SPI-master mode + GPIO for `CS_N`,
49	   `IRQ_N` (external interrupt), and reset.
50	2. **OA TC6 chunk protocol** — the only real "driver." Unlike a UART, the SPI
51	   link is *not* byte-transparent: it exchanges fixed-size **chunks** (default
52	   64-byte data payload + a 4-byte header on TX / 4-byte footer on RX), with
53	   credit-based flow control (TX credits and RX-chunks-available are reported in
54	   each footer), plus a separate control-transaction format for register
55	   read/writes during init. Microchip publishes an open-source reference driver
56	   ([`MicrochipTech/oa-tc6-lib`](https://github.com/MicrochipTech/oa-tc6-lib),
57	   §References) small enough to run on an Arduino — the candidate base for both
58	   ends here.
59	3. **Minimal L2 framing** — the MAC-PHY only transmits *valid Ethernet frames*,
60	   so the host prepends a fixed 14-byte Ethernet header (dest MAC, src MAC,
61	   ethertype) to the payload. For this link the MACs are hardcoded and a custom
62	   ethertype carries the existing frame formats verbatim:
63	   - fretboard → marvin: the 17-byte data-stream frame (see fretboard SPEC).
64	   - marvin → fretboard: the 1-byte button bitmask.
65	
66	   17 B + 14 B header = 31 B → a single chunk. The 1-byte command likewise. The
67	   existing UART framing (`0x03 … 0xFC`, `sample_seq`, etc.) can ride unchanged
68	   inside the Ethernet payload, so higher layers don't need to know the
69	   transport changed.
70	
71	## 4. Resource budget — fretboard (PIC32CM6408PL10048, 64 KB flash / 8 KB SRAM)
72	
73	Estimates; static allocation only (no malloc), per project rule.
74	
75	| Resource | Estimate | Notes |
76	|---|---|---|
77	| Flash | ~6–10 KB | OA TC6 lib (~4–8 KB) + SPI glue + L2 framing. Reclaim the UART data path if the UART link is fully retired. |
78	| SRAM | ~1–2 KB | A couple of chunk buffers + one TX/RX frame buffer. |
79	| SERCOM | 1 (SPI master) | A free SERCOM alongside SERCOM1 (still UART for now). |
80	| GPIO | 2–3 | `CS_N`, `IRQ_N` (ext-int), reset. |
81	| CPU | negligible | One chunk per 240 Hz tick, interrupt-driven off `IRQ_N`; the TC0 ISR stays lean. |
82	
83	SPI clock: SERCOM SPI master maxes at GCLK/2 ≈ **12 MHz** on the 24 MHz part
84	(not the chip's 25 MHz ceiling) — irrelevant for this data rate.
85	
86	Everything fits comfortably inside 64 KB / 8 KB.
87	
88	## 5. marvin side
89	
90	marvin runs **bare-metal (no Linux)**, so it does *not* get a free netdev — it
91	needs its own TC6 driver. The upside: a **single portable `oa_tc6` layer shared
92	between marvin (Cortex-A5) and fretboard (Cortex-M0+)**, which is itself a tidy
93	demonstration that the OPEN Alliance SPI driver scales across the family. marvin
94	resources are not a concern.
95	
96	## 6. PoDL — "dumb" (no negotiation)
97	
98	PoDL is **not in the LAN8651** — the MAC-PHY only moves data. PoDL is external
99	coupling circuitry around the pair, and it is **transparent to both MCUs** (zero
100	firmware footprint, the §4 budget is unaffected):
101	
102	- **PSE side (marvin):** a fixed-voltage source + coupling inductors that inject
103	  DC onto the pair.
104	- **PD side (fretboard):** coupling inductors to extract DC + a regulator down to
105	  the PIC32CM rail.
106	- **Dumb / unmanaged:** no SCCP classification or negotiation handshake. Fixed
107	  supply voltage, fixed point-to-point pair, decided at design time. Simplest
108	  PoDL form; appropriate because the topology is fixed and both ends are ours.
109	
110	Microchip has PoDL reference designs that pair with the LAN865x EVBs, which also
111	helps the demonstration story.
112	
113	## 7. Topology: point-to-point vs PLCA multidrop
114	
115	Recommended direction: **enable PLCA from the start** rather than strict
116	point-to-point. A 2-node PLCA bus already demonstrates the headline T1S feature
117	(collision-free multidrop on one pair) at no extra cost, and leaves the door
118	open to a second node sharing the same pair and power. Open until decided.
119	
120	## 8. Open items
121	
122	- PLCA vs pure point-to-point (see §7) — lean PLCA.
123	- PoDL supply voltage and the PD-side regulator topology (BOM, not firmware).
124	- Custom ethertype value and the two hardcoded MAC addresses.
125	- Whether to keep the UART link as a fallback during bring-up or cut over
126	  outright (affects whether SERCOM1's data path is reclaimed — §4).
127	- Magnetics-free coupling component selection on the Sensor-LCD5 PCB.
128	
129	## References
130	
131	- **OA TC6 driver (candidate base, both ends):**
132	  [`MicrochipTech/oa-tc6-lib`](https://github.com/MicrochipTech/oa-tc6-lib) —
133	  Microchip's open-source OPEN Alliance TC6 (10BASE-T1x MAC-PHY Serial
134	  Interface) library: SPI chunk protocol + control transactions, used as the
135	  shared portable layer (§3, §5).
136	- LAN8650/1 (LAN8651B1) datasheet — 10BASE-T1S MAC-PHY Ethernet Controller with
137	  SPI, on [Microchip online docs](https://onlinedocs.microchip.com/) /
138	  the LAN8651 product page.
139	- OPEN Alliance *10BASE-T1x MAC-PHY Serial Interface* specification (TC6), v1.1.
140
```
</details></tool-use>

1	# Guitar Hero Bot — System Specification
2	
3	> Top-level overview. For implementation detail of any single subproject, follow the pointers in §3. Each subproject owns its own spec; this document does not duplicate them.
4	
5	---
6	
7	## 1. Mission
8	
9	Build an autonomous robot that plays Guitar Hero / Rock Band on a real Wii guitar controller by watching the game video, detecting notes in real time, and pressing physical buttons in sync with the music. The system must run end-to-end without a host PC in the runtime path, produce reference-quality detector output that lighter detectors can be trained against, and provide an on-device operator UI for calibration, mode control, and replay.
10	
11	## 2. Current architecture
12	
13	Three pieces, one runtime brain:
14	
15	```
16	Wii ──HDMI──► ElectronWarp ──HDMI──► TC358743 ──CSI-2──┐
17	                                                       ▼
18	   ┌──────────────────────  marvin (SAM9X75)  ────────────┐
19	   │  HDMI capture → CV detect → timing pipeline → cmds   │
20	   │           ↑              detector-state bus          │
21	   │           │                       ▲                  │
22	   │           │  10.1″ LVDS + maxtouch │                  │
23	   │           │       (operator UI)    │                  │
24	   │           └────────── SD card ─────┘  (recording)    │
25	   └────────┬──────────────────────────┬───────────────────┘
26	            │ FLEXCOM2 UART (cmds)     │ FLEXCOM2 UART (ADC)
27	            ▼                          │
28	   ┌──────────────────────────────────┐│
29	   │   fretboard (PIC32CM6408)        │┘
30	   │   ADC scan ↔ open-drain GPIO     │
31	   └────────┬─────────────────────────┘
32	            │ GPIO
33	            ▼
34	   Wii guitar controller ──► Wii (closes the loop)
35	
36	                ◇ off-band: dev PC running fret-tuner
37	                  (calibration / detector tuning / replay)
38	```
39	
40	**Per-tier role summary:**
41	
42	- **marvin** — SAM9X75 Curiosity host. Owns HDMI capture, the *reference* CV note detector, ingest of fretboard ADC samples, the chord/strum timing pipeline, command emission to fretboard, the on-device LVDS+touch operator UI, and reference-data recording to SD. The runtime brain.
43	- **fretboard** — PIC32CM6408PL10048 MCU on a sensor/actuator board. Streams 5-channel phototransistor ADC up to marvin and converts incoming bitmask commands into open-drain GPIO presses on a Wii guitar controller. Has a standalone fallback mode where it runs its own chord FIFO without marvin in the loop.
44	- **fret-tuner** — Off-band Python tool (FastAPI + browser UI, Linux/macOS PC). Used at the bench for sensor calibration, detector-algorithm tuning, and replay analysis of recordings produced by marvin. Not in the runtime path.
45	
46	## 3. Subproject specs (where detail lives)
47	
48	| Subproject | Spec | Journal |
49	|---|---|---|
50	| marvin | [`firmware/marvin/docs/spec.md`](firmware/marvin/docs/spec.md) | [`firmware/marvin/docs/journal.md`](firmware/marvin/docs/journal.md) |
51	| fretboard | [`firmware/fretboard/SPEC.md`](firmware/fretboard/SPEC.md) | [`firmware/fretboard/docs/journal.md`](firmware/fretboard/docs/journal.md) |
52	| fret-tuner | [`tools/fret-tuner/SPEC.md`](tools/fret-tuner/SPEC.md) | — |
53	| marvin-perf | [`tools/marvin-perf/`](tools/marvin-perf/) — perf-log decoder + live/offline web viewer | — |
54	| edge-ai | [`tools/edge-ai/docs/SPEC.md`](tools/edge-ai/docs/SPEC.md) — design proposal: distill marvin's gameplay commands into a small ML model running on fretboard. Offline development first; Phase 1 data pipeline in progress. | [`tools/edge-ai/docs/journal.md`](tools/edge-ai/docs/journal.md) |
55	| gameplay | marvin spec [§4.8](firmware/marvin/docs/spec.md) + [`firmware/marvin/docs/gh3_navigation.md`](firmware/marvin/docs/gh3_navigation.md) — GH3 game-state observer/controller offline prototype; algorithms proven against the screen corpus, then ported to the marvin firmware `gameplay_engine`. | [`tools/gameplay/docs/journal.md`](tools/gameplay/docs/journal.md) |
56	| fauxmote | [`firmware/fauxmote/SPEC.md`](firmware/fauxmote/SPEC.md) — *parallel proof-of-concept:* ESP32 (Adafruit Feather V2) firmware that emulates a Wiimote + guitar extension over Bluetooth to a real Wii, an alternative to the fretboard's physical button-pressing. Not yet in the runtime path; fretboard stays authoritative. | [`firmware/fauxmote/docs/journal.md`](firmware/fauxmote/docs/journal.md) |
57	
58	marvin's spec also has deeper-dive documents for its capture and display paths ([`capture_pipeline.md`](firmware/marvin/docs/capture_pipeline.md), [`display_path.md`](firmware/marvin/docs/display_path.md)).
59	
60	## 4. Repository map
61	
62	```
63	guitar-pic/
64	├── README.md                    # short landing page
65	├── SPEC.md                      # this document
66	├── CLAUDE.md                    # workflow rules for Claude Code sessions
67	├── firmware/
68	│   ├── marvin/                  # SAM9X75 host firmware
69	│   ├── fretboard/               # PIC32CM6408 sensor/actuator MCU firmware
70	│   ├── fauxmote/                # ESP32 Wiimote emulator (proof-of-concept)
71	│   └── sam9x75_curiosity_emirror/   # Microchip reference project (template only)
72	├── tools/
73	│   ├── fret-tuner/              # Python dev/calibration tool
74	│   ├── gameplay/                # GH3 game-state observer/controller offline prototype
75	│   └── marvin-perf/             # marvin perf-log decoder + web viewer
76	├── hardware/
77	│   ├── actuators/               # voice coil / electromagnet / DIY solenoid design + test protocols
78	│   ├── 3d-models/               # OpenSCAD + STL for printed actuator parts
79	│   ├── Sensor-LCD5/             # KiCad project for fretboard sensor/actuator PCB
80	│   └── kicad/                   # shared symbol/footprint libraries
81	└── docs/
82	    ├── SAM9X7-Series-Data-Sheet-DS60001813.pdf
83	    └── archive/                 # historical docs from the original PC/Elgato/PS2 architecture
84	```
85	
86	## 5. Hardware platforms (high-level)
87	
88	| Component | Role | Where to look |
89	|---|---|---|
90	| SAM9X75 Curiosity | marvin host | [marvin spec §3](firmware/marvin/docs/spec.md) |
91	| Waveshare HDMI→CSI-2 adapter (TC358743) | HDMI bridge into marvin | [marvin spec §3](firmware/marvin/docs/spec.md), [capture pipeline](firmware/marvin/docs/capture_pipeline.md) |
92	| 10.1″ 1280×800 LVDS panel + maxtouch | marvin operator UI surface | [marvin display path](firmware/marvin/docs/display_path.md) |
93	| Sensor/actuator PCB (Sensor-LCD5) | fretboard board: 5 phototransistors + GPIO out | [`hardware/Sensor-LCD5/`](hardware/Sensor-LCD5/) |
94	| PIC32CM6408PL10048 | fretboard MCU | [fretboard spec](firmware/fretboard/SPEC.md) |
95	| LAN8651B1 (10BASE-T1S MAC-PHY) | *planned* fretboard ↔ marvin link over single-pair Ethernet + PoDL | [T1S/PoDL link](docs/t1s-podl-link.md) |
96	| Actuator mechanism (TBD: voice coil / electromagnet / DIY solenoid) | physical fret + strum drive | [`hardware/actuators/`](hardware/actuators/) and [`hardware/3d-models/`](hardware/3d-models/) |
97	| ElectronWarp | component → HDMI converter for Wii | external commercial part |
98	
99	The actuator choice is intentionally still open — `hardware/actuators/` contains design + test-protocol docs for three candidates.
100	
101	## 6. Cross-cutting decisions
102	
103	- **Architecture pivot.** The original PC-hosted / Elgato-USB-capture / PS2 / single-PIC-actuator design is retired. Source documents are preserved at [`docs/archive/`](docs/archive/) for design-rationale reference; they are *not* maintained.
104	- **`frame_epoch` is the master sync token.** A 32-bit counter incremented by marvin's video task on every captured ISC frame. Every detector-state record, emitted command, and recording artifact — including data from off-board observers — keys off this token so multi-source data can be aligned post-hoc. Detail in [marvin spec §4.6](firmware/marvin/docs/spec.md).
105	- **Reference data persists on marvin's SD card.** Detector-state + sparse raw BGR888 keyframes (default 1 keyframe/sec) + raw ADC stream + emitted commands. Off-board detectors record their own data keyed by `frame_epoch` and align offline.
106	- **Centralized timing on marvin, with a fretboard-takeover fallback.** marvin runs the chord-window FIFO and strum scheduler by default; an operator-mode toggle hands timing back to fretboard's standalone `fret_button.c` while marvin still records observations.
107	- **Operating modes are independent toggles**, not a global state machine: `detect_enable`, `marvin_timing_enable`, `actuate_enable`, `record_enable`. Named modes (idle / calibrate / dry-run / play / replay / record) are presets over them.
108	- **Planned: fretboard ↔ marvin link moves to 10BASE-T1S + dumb PoDL.** Replace the FLEXCOM2/SERCOM UART pair with single-pair Ethernet via a LAN8651B1 MAC-PHY on each end. Motivation, in order: PoDL carries power *and* data on one pair to the guitar; better noise/cable tolerance; PLCA multidrop headroom; and demonstrating 10BASE-T1S + PoDL inside a larger Microchip system (SAM9X7 + LAN8651 + PIC32CM). Bandwidth is not a driver — the existing UART has ~12× headroom. PoDL is **dumb** (fixed voltage, no SCCP negotiation) and transparent to both MCUs. No IP stack — the host implements only SPI + the OPEN Alliance TC6 chunk protocol + minimal L2 framing, with the existing frame formats riding unchanged inside the Ethernet payload. Fits comfortably on the PIC32CM (est. ~6–10 KB flash / ~1–2 KB SRAM); marvin is bare-metal so it gets a shared portable `oa_tc6` driver, not a free netdev. Detail in [`docs/t1s-podl-link.md`](docs/t1s-podl-link.md).

132	## 8. What this is *not*
133	
134	To anchor against the original architecture (preserved in `docs/archive/`):
135	
136	- **Not PC-hosted.** marvin is the runtime brain; no host PC is required for play.
137	- **Not USB-capture / Elgato.** Video is captured directly off HDMI via a TC358743 → MIPI CSI-2 path into the SAM9X75's ISC.
138	- **Not PS2.** The supported console is the Nintendo Wii (with an ElectronWarp component → HDMI converter).
139	- **Not a single-MCU actuator.** Sensing and timing live on marvin; fretboard is a sensor/actuator MCU, not a solo controller (with the explicit exception of the standalone-fallback mode).
140	- **Not OpenCV / Python at runtime.** CV runs natively on the SAM9X75 (Cortex-A5). Python (`fret-tuner`) is a bench tool only.

## Comprehensive Exploration Report: T1S Node Architecture & Data Flows

I've thoroughly explored the repo to understand the current fretboard ↔ marvin link, node topology, and payload requirements for your T1S multidrop design. Here are the key findings:

### 1. **Current Node Architecture & Hardware Platforms**

**marvin (SAM9X75 Curiosity / Hybrid) — Cortex-A5, bare-metal:**
- Runtime brain: HDMI capture → CV detection → timing pipeline → actuator commands
- Reference detector source for training data
- Currently linked to fretboard via:
  - **Original:** USB CDC host bridge (EDBG)
  - **Current (2026-06-08 port):** FLEXCOM1 USART @ 500 000 Bd, 8N1, ring-buffer mode (direct GPIO over FLEXCOM)
  - **File:** `/Users/gregmrozek/Projects/microchip/guitar-pic/firmware/marvin/default/src/actuator/fretboard_link.c` (lines 1–279)
  - **Roles:** TX = 7-bit command bitmask (1 byte/tick), RX = 17-byte ADC frames (240 Hz)

**fretboard (PIC32CM6408PL10048) — Cortex-M0+, 24 MHz, 64 KB flash / 8 KB SRAM:**
- I/O bridge: reads 5-channel phototransistor ADC, outputs button presses to Wii controller
- Two modes (compile-time `FRETBOARD_MODE`):
  - `MARVIN_DRIVEN` (current alternate): I/O bridge only, no game logic
  - `MODEL_DRIVEN` (current default): on-device int8 inference, standalone play with marvin optional
- Currently linked via:
  - SERCOM1 UART @ 500 000 Bd, 8N1, ring-buffer mode
  - **Files:** `/Users/gregmrozek/Projects/microchip/guitar-pic/firmware/fretboard/data_stream.c`, `cmd_receive.c`, `main.c`
  - TC0 timer callback @ 240 Hz ISR: `fret_scan_all()` → `data_stream_send()` → `cmd_receive_update()`

---

### 2. **Current Data Payloads**

#### **fretboard → marvin: 17-byte ADC frame (240 Hz)**

**Structure** (`data_stream.c` lines 9–40):
```c
typedef struct __attribute__((packed)) {
    uint8_t  start;          // 0x03
    uint16_t green;          // ADC[FRET_GREEN], u16 LE
    uint16_t red;            // ADC[FRET_RED], u16 LE
    uint16_t yellow;         // ADC[FRET_YELLOW], u16 LE
    uint16_t blue;           // ADC[FRET_BLUE], u16 LE
    uint16_t orange;         // ADC[FRET_ORANGE], u16 LE
    uint32_t sample_seq;     // Monotonic counter, one per tick (u32 LE) — for gap detection
    uint8_t  applied_mask;   // Actuator bitmask driven during *this* scan
    uint8_t  end;            // 0xFC
} ds_frame_t;  // 17 bytes total
```

**ADC Channels** (fretboard SPEC.md lines 35–49):
- 5 phototransistors at the TV strike line, 12-bit unsigned (0–4095)
- Lower ADC value = brighter (note present)
- Channel mapping: Green/Red/Yellow/Blue/Orange → PA28/PA16/PA19/PA27/PA26 (FRET_* enum)

**Rate:** 17 B × 240 Hz = **4.08 KB/s** (well under 500 kbaud @ ~50 KB/s budget, ~12× headroom)

**Key feature (fretboard journal 2026-06-03):** `sample_seq` and `applied_mask` are stamped *by the fretboard* atomically at the same tick, pairing sensor and actuator state at the source for training-data labeling.

#### **marvin → fretboard: 1-byte command (variable rate)**

**Structure** (`cmd_receive.h` lines 4–15):
```c
#define CMD_BIT_GREEN       (1U << 0)  // Bit 0
#define CMD_BIT_RED         (1U << 1)  // Bit 1
#define CMD_BIT_YELLOW      (1U << 2)  // Bit 2
#define CMD_BIT_BLUE        (1U << 3)  // Bit 3
#define CMD_BIT_ORANGE      (1U << 4)  // Bit 4
#define CMD_BIT_STRUM_DOWN  (1U << 5)  // Bit 5
#define CMD_BIT_STRUM_UP    (1U << 6)  // Bit 6
```

**Behavior** (`cmd_receive.c` lines 54–65):
- Drain RX ring each tick, apply only the **last byte** as bitmask (latest-wins)
- Bit set → drive GPIO low (assert button press)
- Bit clear → tri-state GPIO (release button, pull-up restores idle)

**Rate:** Timing pipeline submits at game-dependent rates (~60 Hz typical gameplay, up to 240 Hz in strum scheduling). fretboard link uses a **latest-wins depth-1 queue** (`xQueueOverwrite`) so stalled writes don't accumulate stale commands.

---

### 3. **Multidrop Topology & PLCA Considerations**

From `/Users/gregmrozek/Projects/microchip/guitar-pic/docs/t1s-podl-link.md` (sections 1, 7):

**Current plan:**
- Move from FLEXCOM UART to **10BASE-T1S single-pair Ethernet + dumb PoDL** via **LAN8651B1 MAC-PHY** (each end)
- **PLCA multidrop lean direction** (not strict point-to-point): enables up to 8 nodes on one pair
- **Open decision** (not yet resolved): formal topology (PLCA vs p2p), but "lean PLCA" indicates intent to enable a second node (e.g., additional fretboard or sensor)
- **PoDL:** Transparent to MCU (zero firmware footprint), couples power + data on the single twisted pair

**Resource budget on fretboard (lines 71–87):**
- Flash: ~6–10 KB (OA TC6 SPI driver + L2 framing)
- SRAM: ~1–2 KB (couple chunk buffers + TX/RX frame)
- GPIO: 2–3 (CS_N, IRQ_N, reset)
- SERCOM: 1 (SPI master, ~12 MHz feasible on the 24 MHz part)
- **17-byte + 1-byte payloads ride unchanged inside the Ethernet payload** — no logic change to `data_stream.c`/`cmd_receive.c`

**marvin side:** Bare-metal (no free netdev), so it needs its own portable `oa_tc6` SPI driver — shared across both SAM9X75 (Cortex-A5) and fretboard (Cortex-M0+).

---

### 4. **Data Flow Context: marvin's Detector-State Bus & Edge-AI**

From `/Users/gregmrozek/Projects/microchip/guitar-pic/firmware/marvin/default/src/perf_log/perf_log_records.h`:

**marvin also ingests fretboard ADC as a parallel detector** (PERF_REC_FRETBOARD_RAW, record type 0x0B):
- Records one per valid 17-byte fretboard frame, tagged with the same `frame_epoch` as video frames
- Carries the 5×u16 ADC values, `fb_sample_seq`, and `applied_mask` (from the fretboard itself)
- Used by edge-ai training pipeline to label (marvin's distilled commands) with raw ADC inputs

**edge-ai system** (tools/edge-ai):
- Distillation against `PERF_REC_ACTUATOR.intended_mask` (marvin's command byte)
- Output: 6 bits (5 frets + 1 collapsed strum) — deployed to fretboard PIC32CM
- Already running on hardware (2026-06-04) in `MODEL_DRIVEN` mode
- Removes marvin from the gameplay loop for standalone fretboard operation

---

### 5. **Timing Pipeline Command Rates & Arbitration**

From `/Users/gregmrozek/Projects/microchip/guitar-pic/firmware/marvin/default/src/actuator/timing_pipeline.h`:

**Timing pipeline (primary command producer):**
- Maintains chord-accumulation window + strum scheduling state machine
- Emits 7-bit bitmask (bits 0–4 frets, bit 5 strum-down, bit 6 strum-up)
- Submits via `FretboardLink_Send(mask, producer_id)` with `producer_id = PERF_ACTUATOR_PRODUCER_TIMING`

**Multiple producers** (latest-wins arbitration):
- `timing_pipeline` (primary, gameplay notes)
- `manual_control` (operator UI buttons) — mutual-exclusion mode gating (marvin disables timing during manual mode)
- Future `game_state_controller` (M10, menu navigation) — same API, mutual-exclusion gating

**fretboard_link queue:** Depth 1, `xQueueOverwrite` semantics
- If marvin can't TX faster than fretboard can consume, the newest mask wins
- No accumulation of stale commands

### 7. **Minimal Protocol Payload Summary for T1S Design**

**Steady-state wire rates (marvin ↔ fretboard):**

| Direction | Payload | Period | Rate |
|-----------|---------|--------|------|
| fretboard → marvin | 17 B (ADC + seq + mask) | 4.17 ms (240 Hz) | 4.08 KB/s |
| marvin → fretboard | 1 B (7-bit bitmask) | Variable (~60–240 Hz) | ~0.5–2 KB/s |
| **Total** | **18 B/tick** | **4.17 ms** | **~4.5 KB/s** |

**Within T1S/Ethernet:**
- 17-byte ADC frame → wrapped in 14-byte Ethernet header (dest MAC, src MAC, custom ethertype) = **31 B** (single OA TC6 chunk at default 64-byte payload)
- 1-byte command → wrapped in Ethernet header = **15 B** (fits in single chunk)
- **No IP stack, no TCP/IP overhead** — OPEN Alliance TC6 chunk protocol only

**10BASE-T1S baseline:** 10 Mbps = 1.25 MB/s raw throughput. Your 4–5 KB/s payload is ~0.4% of link capacity, leaving **massive headroom for:**
- PLCA overhead (collision arbitration, inter-frame spacing)
- A second or third node on the same pair (sensor node, second fretboard MCU, etc.)
- Future protocol evolution

---

### 8. **Open Decisions (from docs/t1s-podl-link.md §8)**

Before T1S code lands, settle:
1. **PLCA topology** — Full PLCA (up to 8 nodes), lean PLCA (2–3 nodes), or strict point-to-point?
   - Current direction: "lean PLCA" (allows future expansion without re-routing)
2. **Custom ethertype value** — Proposed (not yet hardcoded)
3. **Two hardcoded MAC addresses** — fretboard ↔ marvin MACs (fixed, not dynamic discovery)
4. **UART fallback during bring-up** — Keep SERCOM1 as a parallel debug path, or cut over outright?

---

This exploration shows you have a well-structured, payload-light system with ample T1S capacity and clear extensibility for multidrop nodes. The 17-byte ADC frame + 1-byte command format is minimalist, deterministic, and ready to live unchanged inside Ethernet payloads.

1	# marvin — System Specification
2	
3	> **Read this first** for any non-trivial marvin task. The journal ([`journal.md`](journal.md)) is the running diary of decisions and work-in-progress; this spec is the durable description of *what marvin is*. When the two disagree, fix the spec.
4	
5	**Status:** in-progress draft. Sections that are settled are marked ✅; sections that depend on open architectural questions are marked 🚧 and link to the relevant entries in §9.
6	
7	---
8	
9	## 1. Purpose & scope
10	
11	### 1.1 What marvin is
12	
13	marvin is the firmware running on a **SAM9X75 Curiosity** board. Its job, in the guitar-playing-robot system, is to:
14	
15	1. Capture live HDMI video of a Guitar Hero / Rock Band game from a Nintendo Wii.
16	2. Run computer-vision note detection on the captured frames.
17	3. Decide *what* to play and *when* (chord grouping, fret-early timing, strum scheduling).
18	4. Send the corresponding fret/strum commands to the actuator controller (the **fretboard** MCU).
19	5. Provide an on-device operator UI (10.1″ LVDS panel + maxtouch capacitive touch) for live view, calibration, mode selection, logs.
20	6. Produce **reference data** — annotated frames + detector state — for off-board use (training low-fidelity detectors, side-by-side detector comparison, replay).
21	7. **Observe game state from the screen** — recognize current menu / song-select / gameplay / pause / score-summary contexts via CV, expose high-level control verbs ("start single-player playthrough of song X", "advance menu", "exit to main menu") that translate into fret/strum command sequences sent through the same fretboard link.
22	
23	In short: marvin is the runtime brain *and* the reference-detector data source for the project.
24	
25	### 1.2 What marvin is *not*
26	
27	- **Not the actuator.** Physical fret/strum GPIO drive lives on the fretboard MCU. marvin sends bitmask commands; fretboard converts them to button presses.
28	- **Not a sensor / detection-only device.** marvin owns timing and command emission. It is not a passive vision peripheral that some other host orchestrates.
29	- **Not a router for a PC.** The previous PC-based architecture (Elgato + OpenCV + USB to a Pi) is retired. marvin replaces the PC in the runtime path.
30	- **Not a generic camera platform.** The video source is a fixed HDMI signal from a game console. Suggestions like "just use a USB webcam" or "output to HDMI directly" miss the point.
31	
32	### 1.3 North-star one-paragraph summary
33	
34	A SAM9X75 captures Wii HDMI video at 720×480 / 1280×720 @ 60 Hz over a TC358743 → MIPI CSI-2 → ISC path into DDR (BGR888 packed, 3 B/pixel). It runs reference-quality CV note detection on those frames, fuses with ADC-based detection ingested from a fretboard MCU over a FLEXCOM2 UART link, schedules chord/strum commands through a low-latency timing pipeline, sends commands back to the fretboard, drives an operator UI on a 10.1″ LVDS panel, and exports a compressed reference-data stream so that lighter-weight detectors (today: fretboard's phototransistors; future: an Edge AI MCU) can be trained against marvin's ground truth.
35	
36	### 1.4 What's done, what's next
37	
38	| Subsystem | Status |
39	|---|---|
40	| HDMI capture (TC358743 → CSI-2 → ISC → DDR, BGR888 packed) | ✅ working at 480p60 and 720p60. See [`capture_pipeline.md`](capture_pipeline.md). |
41	| Display path (DDR → XLCDC HEO → LVDSC → panel) | ✅ working, pillarboxed/letterboxed, per-frame pointer swap. See [`display_path.md`](display_path.md). |
42	| FreeRTOS scheduler, video task, OSAL I²C | ✅ landed. |
43	| Lightweight log shim, FreeRTOS analytics, task priorities | ✅ done. |
44	| CV detection pipeline | 🚧 M1 complete: `cv_marvin_v1` running on captured frames, `detector_state_t` bus active. No actuation path through detector yet. §4.2. |
45	| Fretboard link (FLEXCOM2 USART) | ✅ working; gameplay tested over the original USB CDC host link. Link rewired to a direct FLEXCOM2 UART for the Curiosity Hybrid board (no host-capable USB port); pending on-hardware re-validation. §4.3. |
46	| Timing pipeline (chord FIFO, strum) | ✅ working; end-to-end gameplay tested on Expert and Easy. §4.4. |
47	| Operator UI (Legato) | 🚧 Manual-control surface (8 buttons, Legato Composer) done; full calibration/log UI not started. §4.5, open Q5. |
48	| Reference-data recording & export (SD) | 🚧 SD recording not started. Perf-log USB CDC export (separate dev-tooling path) complete at 2.77 MB/s. §4.6, open Q1/Q2. |
49	| System services (config, time, watchdog) | 🚧 Partial: logging, FreeRTOS analytics, static task priorities done; config persistence and watchdog not started. §4.7. |
50	| Game-state awareness & high-level game control | 🚧 M9 Phases 1+2 firmware-complete (screen classifier + section-select/song readers; MPLAB build confirmed, pending hardware test). M9 Phase 3 (number/score readers) and M10 (controller/navigator) not yet started in firmware. §4.8. |
51	
52	---

54	## 2. System context
55

122	
123	### 2.2 Who owns what
124	
125	| Concern | Owner | Notes |
126	|---|---|---|
127	| HDMI capture into memory | marvin | TC358743 + CSI-2 + ISC; 720×480 / 1280×720 @ 60 Hz, BGR888 packed (3 B/pixel). |
128	| Reference-quality CV note detection | marvin | Ground truth; multiple algorithms may coexist on the bus. |
129	| ADC-based note detection | fretboard → marvin | fretboard scans 5 phototransistors @ 240 Hz, streams raw values; marvin runs the detector logic. |
130	| Detector-state fusion / arbitration | marvin | One canonical detector-state bus; the active source feeds the timing pipeline. |
131	| Chord-window FIFO + strum scheduling | marvin | Open Q4: stays on marvin (centralized) vs migrates to fretboard. Default: marvin. |
132	| Fret/strum GPIO output | fretboard | Open-drain pin drive only; receives a bitmask over UART. |
133	| Operator UI (live view, calibration, modes, logs) | marvin | 10.1″ LVDS + maxtouch. Open Q5: Legato vs custom. |
134	| Reference-data recording & export | marvin | Compressed/derived format; transport TBD (open Q1/Q2). |
135	| Game-state observation (menu / song-select / gameplay / pause / score) | marvin | CV on captured frames; emits typed game-state events on its own bus. §4.8. |
136	| Game catalog + menu metadata (song list, menu graph, recognized icons) | marvin | Compile-time tables and/or SD-card JSON. Drives the recognizer and the navigator. §4.8. |
137	| High-level game control (e.g., "start single-player song X") | marvin | Translates verbs into fret/strum sequences sent over the same fretboard link as gameplay commands. §4.8. |
138	| Calibration / tuning UI authoring | dev PC (fret-tuner) | Optional; not required at runtime. Open Q7: long-term fate. |
139	| Training data ingest / replay analysis | dev PC | Off-band consumer of marvin's reference-data export. |
140	
141	### 2.3 Data flow at a glance
142	
143	1. **Frame ready** — ISC writes a BGR888 packed frame to DDR; the video task notifies subscribers.
144	2. **CV detect** — one or more CV detectors read the frame and emit detector-state events.
145	3. **ADC ingest** — a UART task receives raw ADC samples from the fretboard and runs an ADC detector that emits detector-state events on the same bus.
146	4. **Arbitrate** — the timing pipeline picks the active detector (or fuses), maintains the chord-accumulation window, and pushes finished chords onto its FIFO.
147	5. **Schedule** — the FIFO emits fret-assert and strum-pulse commands at the correct ticks.
148	6. **Send** — commands are encoded and transmitted to the fretboard over UART.
149	7. **Display** — the captured frame is composited with overlays (sensor crosshairs, detector outputs, chord state, latency markers) and shown on the LVDS panel.
150	8. **Record** (optional) — when recording is enabled, a derived/compressed reference-data record (frame epoch + detector state + raw ADC + emitted commands) is buffered and exported via the chosen transport.
151	
152	### 2.4 Latency budget (target, end-to-end)
153	
154	| Stage | Budget | Notes |
155	|---|---|---|
156	| HDMI source → DDR (capture) | ≤ 16.7 ms | One frame @ 60 Hz; bounded by capture pipeline. |
157	| Detect on frame | ≤ 16.7 ms | One frame budget for CV; ADC path is separate and faster. |
158	| Timing pipeline → command emit | latency dominated by `STRUM_DELAY_MS` (≈ 200 ms) — intentional, not waste; compensates for sensor placement above strike line. |
159	| UART command → fretboard GPIO | ≤ 5 ms | Short fixed-format frame at ≥ 115 200 Bd. |
160	| Total user-visible latency | ≈ 200–250 ms | Tunable via `STRUM_DELAY_MS`, set per-game by calibration. |
161	
162	The dominant fixed delay (`STRUM_DELAY_MS`) exists by design — the camera sees notes before they reach the strike line. Capture + detect + UART jitter is what we actually budget against.
163

166	## 3. Hardware platform
167	
168	### 3.1 Boards and links
169	
170	| Board | Role | Connection to marvin |
171	|---|---|---|
172	| **SAM9X75 Curiosity** | marvin host (CPU, DDR, peripherals, panel/touch ports) | — |
173	| **Waveshare HDMI → CSI-2 adapter** (TC358743) | HDMI → MIPI CSI-2 bridge | I²C (FLEXCOM8 TWI, PB4/PB5, 400 kHz, addr `0x0F`) for control; 2-lane CSI-2 RX for data; PC15 PWD, PC19 RESET (currently unused — software reset over I²C). |
174	| **Microchip 10.1″ 1280×800 LVDS panel + maxtouch** | Operator UI | LVDSC pair from XLCDC; I²C for maxtouch (existing Harmony driver). |
175	| **fretboard board** (PIC32CM6408PL10048) | Sensor + actuator MCU | FLEXCOM1 USART (marvin PA28 TX / PA29 RX ↔ fretboard SERCOM1 PB01 RX / PB00 TX, 500 000 Bd 8N1, ring-buffer mode). |
176	| **Wii guitar controller** | Physical input target | Open-drain GPIO on fretboard, not directly on marvin. |
177	| **(optional) dev PC** | Calibration / training-data ingest / replay viewer + operator console | SD card swap (primary), USB CDC for perf-log, and the FLEXCOM2 serial console (115 200 8N1, via an FTDI channel) for interactive control (§4.9). No runtime dependency. |
178	
179	Pin assignments live in `firmware/marvin/default/src/config/default/pin_configurations.csv`. The capture pipeline doc ([`capture_pipeline.md`](capture_pipeline.md)) is authoritative for CSI / ISC register state; the display path doc ([`display_path.md`](display_path.md)) is authoritative for XLCDC overlay wiring.
180

182	
183	| Peripheral | Status | Notes |
