200	
201	---
202	
203	## 4. Subsystems
204	
205	### 4.1 Video capture & display ✅
206	
207	Working end-to-end. See [`capture_pipeline.md`](capture_pipeline.md) and [`display_path.md`](display_path.md) for register-level detail. The video task (`video.c`, FreeRTOS) owns the capture pipeline and a frame queue that other tasks subscribe to. Display intent and capture intent are decoupled (commit `e28c497`); a software scaler can be inserted between capture and display when source ≠ panel native.
208	
209	**What this subsystem owns:**
210	- TC358743 init, source detection, EDID, format negotiation.
211	- ISC DMA configuration and frame buffer rotation in DDR.
212	- XLCDC overlay window placement (pillarbox/letterbox) for the active source.
213	- Frame-ready notification to subscribers (CV detect, recording, UI overlay).
214	
215	**What it doesn't own:**
216	- CV processing (§4.2).
217	- Recording / export (§4.6).
218	- UI widgets / chrome (§4.5) — only the pixel composition for the live-view layer.
219	
220	### 4.2 CV detection pipeline + detector-state bus 🚧
221	
222	#### 4.2.1 Role
223	
224	This is what makes marvin the *reference detector*. It runs computer-vision note detection on captured frames and publishes a structured detector-state record per frame onto a shared bus. Other detectors (fretboard ADC; future Edge-AI unit) publish onto the same bus. The timing pipeline (§4.4) consumes the bus.
225	
226	#### 4.2.2 Detector model
227	
228	A **detector** is anything that turns observation data into a `detector_state_t` event. marvin will host at least:
229	
230	- `cv_marvin_v1` — the reference vision detector. Reads RGB888-packed (3 B/pixel) frames from the video frame queue; emits one `detector_state_t` per frame.
231	- `adc_fretboard` — runs on top of raw ADC samples streamed from the fretboard MCU (§4.3); emits `detector_state_t` events at the fretboard's 240 Hz rate.
232	
233	Future detectors may include alternate CV algorithms running in parallel for comparison, or off-board detectors (Edge-AI MCU) feeding state in over UART/Ethernet.
234	
235	#### 4.2.3 detector_state record (canonical shape)
236	
237	```
238	typedef struct {
239	    uint32_t frame_epoch;     // master sync token (§4.6.4)
240	    uint64_t timestamp_us;    // monotonic, marvin-local
241	    uint8_t  detector_id;     // 0=cv_marvin_v1, 1=adc_fretboard, ...
242	    uint8_t  reserved[3];
243	    struct {
244	        uint8_t  pressed;     // 0/1 hard call
245	        uint16_t confidence;  // 0..65535, detector-defined
246	        uint16_t raw_value;   // detector-defined: ADC sample, pixel mean, etc.
247	    } fret[5];                // FRET_GREEN..FRET_ORANGE
248	} detector_state_t;
249	```
250	
251	Fields are fixed-width, naturally aligned, little-endian — this is also the on-disk record layout for the state log (§4.6.5). `frame_epoch` is the master clock for cross-detector and cross-recording sync.
252	
253	#### 4.2.4 Bus mechanics
254	
255	- A single FreeRTOS queue (`xDetectorStateQueue`) carries `detector_state_t` records, one entry per detector emit.
256	- The timing pipeline task (§4.4) is the sole consumer.
257	- The recording task (§4.6) snoops the queue via a side-channel: each producer publishes simultaneously to the timing-pipeline queue and to a recording stream buffer. (Single producer→multiple consumers is implemented by tee'ing inside each detector, not by a broker; keeps queue semantics blocking and simple.)
258	- Detectors run on their own FreeRTOS tasks (one per detector instance) so a slow detector cannot stall the frame pipeline.
259	
260	#### 4.2.5 Reference-detector responsibilities
261	
262	`cv_marvin_v1` is a *first-class* subsystem, not a debug aid. Its detector state is the ground-truth label for any reference-data recording (§4.6). Implications:
263	
264	- Algorithm changes are versioned (`cv_marvin_v1`, `cv_marvin_v2`, …). The version is stamped into recordings so training data stays attributable.
265	- Calibration (sensor/strike-line ROIs in pixel space) is stored in the system config (§4.7) and reproducibly applied at startup.
266	- The detector must run within one frame-time (≤ 16.7 ms) on Cortex-A5 — concrete algorithm choice is a future decision, but the budget is set.
267	
268	#### 4.2.6 Open questions surfaced here
269	
270	- Initial CV algorithm — pixel-mean threshold per ROI, edge-trough, optical-flow-based, or learned. (Defer; bring up the simplest first to validate end-to-end.)
271	- ADC-detector logic location — port `fretboard/fret_button.c`'s detection (hysteresis edges) into marvin (`adc_fretboard` runs on raw samples), or have fretboard pre-process and stream edges. (Default: marvin runs the detector on raw samples; fretboard stays dumb.)
272	
273	### 4.3 Fretboard link ✅
274	
275	Direct **FLEXCOM1 USART** link between marvin and the fretboard MCU — a plain UART wire, no USB. marvin's `PA28` (FLEXCOM1_IO0, `GUITAR_TX`) and `PA29` (FLEXCOM1_IO1, `GUITAR_RX`) connect to the fretboard's SERCOM1 (`PB01` RX / `PB00` TX). Both ends run **500 000 baud, 8N1**. The FLEXCOM1 USART runs in Harmony ring-buffer mode so RX never drops bytes between reads. (Was FLEXCOM2 until the console moved onto FLEXCOM2 — see §4.9.)
276	
277	- **Marvin → fretboard:** command bitmask (which frets to assert + strum direction). 1-byte bitmask, no framing. `fretboard_link_task` writes the latest mask via `FLEXCOM1_USART_Write`.
278	- **Fretboard → marvin:** raw ADC stream (5 channels × 16-bit) at 240 Hz, in a 17-byte start/end-bracketed frame (`0x03 … 0xFC`, with `sample_seq` + `applied_mask`). The FLEXCOM1 RX ring fills continuously from its ISR; a persistent read-threshold notification wakes `fretboard_rx_task`, which drains the ring, resyncs on the frame markers, and republishes each valid frame as a `PERF_REC_FRETBOARD_RAW` perf-log record (default-disabled, host enables via `PERF_CMD_SET_TYPE_MASK`). This is the on-board capture path until the SD-card recorder lands; it's also the substrate for the future `adc_fretboard` detector (§4.2).
279	- **Standalone fallback:** when marvin's timing pipeline is disabled (see §4.4 and §6), the fretboard runs its own existing chord FIFO (`fret_button.c`) and continues to stream ADC + emitted-command telemetry to marvin for capture/display.
280	
281	### 4.4 Timing pipeline 🚧
282	
283	Centralized on marvin by default. Owns:
284	
285	- Chord-accumulation window (`CHORD_WINDOW_MS` ≈ 20–40 ms).
286	- Pending-chord FIFO with per-chord `press_at` / `strum_at` ticks.
287	- Per-fret release scheduling.
288	- Strum direction alternation and pulse generation.
289	- `STRUM_DELAY_MS` / `FRET_EARLY_MS` / `STRUM_PULSE_MS` constants — initial values port from `tools/fret-tuner/SPEC.md` and `firmware/fretboard/SPEC.md`.
290	
291	**Disable / handoff mode:** an operator-mode toggle (§6) deactivates marvin's pipeline. fretboard then runs its own existing pipeline; marvin still ingests ADC + emitted-command telemetry for recording/display, but does not emit commands.
292	
293	### 4.5 UI / operator surface 🚧
294	
295	10.1″ 1280×800 LVDS panel + maxtouch capacitive touch. Functional surfaces required:
296	
297	- Live game view (capture composited with detector overlays — sensor crosshairs, detection events, latency markers).
298	- Calibration / tuning (per-fret ROI placement, threshold values, timing constants).
299	- Mode + run controls (idle, calibrate, dry-run, play, replay, record).
300	- Logs / history / stats (recent commands, miss/hit counts, dropped frames).
301	
302	**UI framework — open Q5.** Legato is already pulled in for capture init and could absorb the operator UI directly (heavy but in-tree). Alternative: a lightweight custom widget layer over GFX2D / direct framebuffer composition. Decision deferred until we attempt the first non-trivial screen (calibration overlay).
303	
304	### 4.6 Reference-data recording & export 🚧
305	
306	#### 4.6.1 Goals (in priority order)
307	
308	1. **Edge-AI training data** — produce labelled frames + ground-truth detector state suitable for training low-fidelity detectors (fretboard's photo-detector logic; future Edge-AI MCU).
309	2. **Replay / sanity check** — let the user (offline) scrub through a recorded session to investigate misses.
310	3. **Multi-detector sync** — independent detectors (fretboard ADC, future Edge-AI) record their own data alongside marvin's; everyone sync's on a shared frame epoch.
311	
312	Live off-device streaming for side-by-side comparison is *not* on the MVP critical path.
313	
314	#### 4.6.2 Transport — SD card
315	
316	Recordings are persisted to an SD card via SDMMC + a simple filesystem (FAT32 via Harmony's FILE_SYSTEM service). The card is removed and read on a workstation; no live network path is required for MVP.
317	
318	Bandwidth ceiling: SDMMC sustained write ≥ 5 MB/s on Class-10 cards is reliably achievable. The recording format below is sized to land well below that.
319	
320	#### 4.6.3 Format — detector-state + sparse keyframes
321	
322	A recording is a **directory** on the SD card, containing:
323	
324	```
325	recordings/
326	└── 2026-05-20T14-32-08/
327	    ├── manifest.json          // session metadata, calibration snapshot, detector versions
328	    ├── state.bin              // dense detector_state_t records, all detectors, all frames
329	    ├── commands.bin           // emitted fret/strum commands with frame_epoch
330	    ├── adc_raw.bin            // raw fretboard ADC stream with frame_epoch interleave
331	    └── keyframes/
332	        ├── 000000.bgr         // raw BGR888 keyframe (no encoder), filename = frame_epoch
333	        ├── 000060.bgr
334	        └── ...
335	```
336	
337	- **`state.bin`** — append-only, fixed-size `detector_state_t` records (§4.2.3). At 60 Hz × 2 detectors × ~28 B = ~3.4 KB/s. Trivial.
338	- **`commands.bin`** — fret/strum bitmask + direction + emit timestamp + frame_epoch, ~16 B per emit. Sparse.
339	- **`adc_raw.bin`** — fretboard 17-byte frames at 240 Hz with `frame_epoch` annotation = ~4.1 KB/s. Modest. Until the SD recorder lands, the same data is available live as `PERF_REC_FRETBOARD_RAW` records (28 B framed) in any marvin-perf capture (default-disabled; enable with `set-mask`).
340	- **Keyframes** — raw BGR888 packed dump every N captured frames. At 720×480 × 3 B = 1.04 MB/keyframe. Default cadence: **1 keyframe per second** (60-frame stride) → 1.04 MB/s sustained. Configurable (every 30 / 60 / 120 / 600 frames). At 1 fps a 5-minute session is ~312 MB — comfortable on any modern SD card.
341	- No software JPEG / video encode. SAM9X75 has no hardware JPEG; CPU encode at 60 fps is infeasible. Keyframes stay raw; offline tools can transcode if desired.
342	
343	Filename convention: directory name is ISO-8601 timestamp at session start (UTC); keyframe filenames are zero-padded `frame_epoch` so chronological order matches lexical order.
344	
345	#### 4.6.4 Sync token — `frame_epoch`
346	
347	A 32-bit counter incremented by the video task on every captured ISC frame (rolls over after ~830 days @ 60 Hz). Every record in a session — `state.bin`, `commands.bin`, `adc_raw.bin`, keyframe filenames, off-board detector data — is keyed by `frame_epoch`. This is the master clock for the entire system, including any later-added detectors that record independently and need to align their data with marvin's.
348	
349	For records that don't fall on a frame boundary (ADC samples emitted between video frames), the most-recent `frame_epoch` is used and the sub-frame offset is captured by `timestamp_us`.
350	
351	#### 4.6.5 manifest.json
352	
353	Minimum fields:
354	
355	```json
356	{
357	  "schema_version": 1,
358	  "session_started_utc": "2026-05-20T14:32:08Z",
359	  "marvin_firmware_git": "<hash>",
360	  "capture": { "width": 720, "height": 480, "fps": 60, "format": "BGR888" },
361	  "keyframe_stride_frames": 60,
362	  "detectors": [
363	    { "id": "cv_marvin_v1", "version": "1.0.0", "calibration": { ... } },
364	    { "id": "adc_fretboard", "version": "1.0.0", "thresholds": { ... } }
365	  ],
366	  "timing": { "chord_window_ms": 20, "strum_delay_ms": 220, "fret_early_ms": 50, "strum_pulse_ms": 50 },
367	  "ended_utc": null
368	}
369	```
370	
371	Written at session start; `ended_utc` is patched on a clean stop.
372	
373	#### 4.6.6 On-device buffering
374	
375	A FreeRTOS task (`record_task`) owns SD writes. State / command / ADC streams are small and write through directly. Keyframes are larger — a single keyframe at 1.04 MB cannot block the video pipeline, so the record task receives a **frame buffer pointer** (the same DDR buffer the ISC writes into; refcounted by the video task) and writes from DDR while the next frame is being captured into another buffer. We need ≥ 3 capture frame buffers (one capturing, one displaying, one being recorded) when recording is active; today the video task already has multiple frames pre-allocated — exact count is verified during implementation.
376	
377	If the SD write FIFO falls behind (rare; only a sustained-throughput problem), the recorder drops keyframes (logs a `RECORD_DROP` event into `state.bin`'s metadata channel) but **never** drops detector-state records.
378	
379	#### 4.6.7 Off-board detectors recording independently
380	
381	When a future Edge-AI detection unit is brought online, it can:
382	
383	- Subscribe to marvin's `frame_epoch` over a chosen link (UART/Ethernet/etc.).
384	- Record its own observations (e.g. its own sensor data + its own detector output) in its own format, *keyed by marvin's `frame_epoch`*.
385	- Be aligned post-hoc against marvin's reference recording during training.
386	
387	The spec does not constrain how off-board detectors store their data — only the sync contract (`frame_epoch` timeline) is canonical.
388	
389	#### 4.6.8 On-demand full-frame snapshot (USB CDC) ✅
390	
391	Independent of the SD recording path above (M4, not started), marvin can export a single full-resolution frame on demand over the existing perf-log USB CDC link. The host sends `PERF_CMD_SNAPSHOT`; the perf-drain task copies the current frame once into a staging buffer and streams it back as a top-to-bottom run of full-width `PERF_STRIP_SNAPSHOT` band records (each ≤ `PERF_STRIP_MAX_BYTES`), all sharing one `frame_epoch`, the last flagged `PERF_STRIP_FLAG_LAST`. Bands are written straight to the sink (bypassing the small strip pool) and paced by the wire; emit is not gated by the STRIP type mask. `marvin-perf snapshot` reassembles and saves the frame (`.bgr` + sidecar `.json`, plus `.png` via Pillow). This is the offline-study on-ramp for the game-state work (§4.8) — no in-runtime role.
392	
393	### 4.7 System services 🚧
394	
395	Cross-cutting services not owned by any one subsystem:
396	
397	- **Logging** ✅ severity-filtered printf shim (commit `a79042f`).
398	- **Time** ✅ TC0 / SYS_TIME for OSAL.
399	- **Config persistence** 🚧 calibration values, mode toggles, last-used recording stride. Storage TBD (a config file on SD vs internal flash).
400	- **Watchdog** 🚧 not yet enabled.
401	- **OTA** ⚪ out of scope for now.
402	
403	### 4.8 Game-state awareness & control 🚧
404	
405	Note on numbering: this subsystem is logically a peer of §4.2–§4.6 (a video-frame consumer that emits typed events plus a controller that issues actuator commands). It lives at §4.8 only to avoid renumbering existing sections referenced from the journal and milestones.
406	
407	#### 4.8.1 Role
408	
409	Two related capabilities, both grounded in CV on the captured video stream:
410	
411	1. **Game-state observer.** Watch the screen; recognize what context the game is currently in — main menu, song-select, difficulty-select, in-game (gameplay), pause, score summary, etc. Surface that as typed events that the operator UI can render and the orchestrator below can act on.
412	2. **Game controller.** Expose high-level verbs ("start a single-player playthrough of song X on Hard", "go to the main menu", "select Practice mode"). Translate each verb into a sequence of fret/strum commands using the recognized current state and a known menu graph, monitor the screen for the expected state transitions, retry or back out on mismatch.
413	
414	This is *not* the gameplay note-detection path (§4.2). cv_marvin_v1 plays notes during gameplay; the game-state module decides *what to play* at the session level (which song, which difficulty, which mode) and gets us there from any starting screen.
415	
416	Recognition is bootstrapped offline: the on-demand snapshot path (§4.6.8) collects a corpus of real GH3 screens, detection algorithms are prototyped host-side in Python (`tools/gameplay/`) against that corpus, and only the proven GH3-specific logic is ported into the firmware `gameplay_engine` module. Per Q10, the approach favors fixed-region/color/glyph matching over general CV — GH3's screens, fonts, and layouts are static.
417	
418	**M9 progress:** Phase 1 (screen-context classifier: main_menu / song_select / gameplay / pause / score) and Phase 2 (section-select and song-name readers) are prototyped and ported to firmware (`gameplay_engine.c`); the MPLAB build is confirmed. Phase 3 (number/score readers) is not yet started. The firmware module is pending hardware validation.
419	
420	#### 4.8.2 Module shape
421	
422	- Owns its own FreeRTOS task (`game_task`).
423	- Subscribes to the video frame queue via the same multi-subscriber API used by detectors (§4.2.4); it is a video-frame consumer, **not** a detector. Its events do not flow on `xDetectorStateQueue`.
424	- Emits typed events on a separate, narrow bus (`xGameStateQueue`) — current_state changes, ambiguity warnings, error states.
425	- Orchestrator state for high-level verbs (current goal, expected next state, retry counter) lives inside `game_task`.
426	- Issues control commands by writing fret/strum bitmasks into the same fretboard-link path used by gameplay. Whether this routes through the timing pipeline (§4.4) or bypasses it is open Q11.
427	
428	#### 4.8.3 Game catalog & menu metadata
429	
430	The recognizer and the navigator both depend on per-game data:
431	
432	- **Recognizer templates.** Per-state visual signatures used by the CV recognizer — could be small reference images (template matching), color histograms, or text regions for OCR. Format chosen with the recognizer algorithm (open Q10).
433	- **Menu graph.** Nodes = recognized game states; edges = button sequences that move between them (e.g., "main_menu → song_select" = `[STRUM_DOWN, STRUM_DOWN, GREEN]`). Used by the navigator to plan a verb.
434	- **Song catalog.** Per-supported-game list of songs with the menu coordinates needed to select each one (which difficulty submenu, ordinal position in the list, etc.). Possibly augmented with metadata (BPM, length, expected difficulty score) for UI display and for reference-data labeling.
435	
436	Storage: compile-time tables for the per-game graph + a JSON or similar on the SD card for songlists and any user-editable bits. Exact split deferred until first concrete game is added.
437	
438	Scope today: target is **one game** — Guitar Hero (Wii) — to validate the design. Adding a second game is a metadata addition (new template set + new menu graph + new song catalog), not a structural change.
439	
440	#### 4.8.4 Interaction with other subsystems
441	
442	- **Detection (§4.2):** independent. cv_marvin_v1 runs only when the game-state observer reports `gameplay`. Outside gameplay, cv_marvin_v1 may be disabled to free CPU.
443	- **Timing pipeline (§4.4):** during gameplay the timing pipeline drives the actuators from detector-state. Outside gameplay it's idle, and the game-state controller drives actuators directly. Coordination and arbitration between the two is open Q11.
444	- **Operator UI (§4.5):** consumes game-state events to display the current screen the game is on; offers verbs as buttons / song-list pickers.
445	- **Recording (§4.6):** game-state transitions are useful session metadata. Either annotated into `state.bin` as a side channel or a sibling file (`game_state.bin`). To be decided when the recorder lands.
446	- **Fretboard link (§4.3):** shared command path. The fretboard MCU does not know whether a press is "gameplay note" or "menu navigation" — they're the same wire bits.
447	
448	#### 4.8.5 Open questions surfaced here
449	
450	See §9 for tracking entries. In summary:
451	
452	- **Q10** — Recognizer algorithm: template matching vs simple OCR vs region/color heuristics vs a small CNN. Trade-off is robustness vs CPU cost vs metadata authoring effort.
453	- **Q11** — Command-path arbitration between game-state controller and timing pipeline. Default is "they don't run at the same time" (gameplay vs menu), but the boundary needs to be explicit.
454	
455	### 4.9 Operator command console ✅
456	
457	An **interactive text console** over **FLEXCOM2 USART (115 200 8N1, ring-buffer mode)** — marvin's `PA13` (FLEXCOM2_IO0, `CLI_TX`) / `PA14` (FLEXCOM2_IO1, `CLI_RX`) — deliberately on a separate channel from the DBGU log/printf chatter — log output stays on DBGU, console I/O stays on FLEXCOM2, so neither pollutes the other.
458	
459	- **Why not Harmony `SYS_CONSOLE`/`SYS_COMMAND`:** those are MCC-config-coupled and live in regenerated files (this board already carries ~10 re-apply patches against clobbered generated code). The console is instead a small in-tree module (`console/console.{h,c}`) in the same shape as `fretboard_link`/`perf_log`: it owns the USART plib directly, is fully statically allocated, and is kept out of MCC via `user.cmake`.
460	- **Library:** [embedded-cli](https://github.com/funbiscuit/embedded-cli) (vendored under `default/src/third_party/embedded-cli/`, MIT), used in static-allocation mode (a fixed `CLI_UINT` buffer → no `malloc`). Provides line editing, history, and tab-completion.
461	- **Mechanics:** one FreeRTOS task drains the FLEXCOM2 RX ring (woken by a 1-byte read-threshold notification, like `fretboard_rx_task`), feeds bytes to embedded-cli, and runs the dispatcher. Output is written byte-by-byte into the TX ring.
462	- **Commands (v0):** `status`, `detect <cv|adc> <on|off>`, `active <cv|adc>`, `timing <on|off>`, `manual <on|off>`, `fret <g|r|y|b|o> <0|1>`, `strum <down|up>` — dispatching into the existing `Detector_*`, `TimingPipeline_SetEnabled`, and `ManualControl_*` setters. The binding table is a plain static array; adding a command is one row. Maps onto the §6 operating-mode toggles. (`record`/`game_*` toggles and runtime timing-constant setters are deferred until those subsystems / setters exist.)
463	
464	---
465	
466	## 5. External interfaces 🚧
467	
468	To be expanded once §4.3 (fretboard wire protocol) is settled. Will document:
469	
470	- Marvin ↔ fretboard UART framing, byte-for-byte.
471	- Recording on-disk binary layouts (the `_t` structs from §4.2.3 and §4.6 in canonical form, including endianness).
472	- USB-CDC dev console framing (if any), Ethernet ref-data stream framing (if/when added).

474	## 6. Operating modes 🚧
475	
476	Default model: independent toggles (matches `tools/fret-tuner/SPEC.md`'s detect/actuate split). Confirmed direction; concrete toggle list:
477	
478	| Toggle | Effect |
479	|---|---|
480	| `detect_enable` | CV + ADC detectors run; detector-state bus is active. |
481	| `marvin_timing_enable` | marvin's chord FIFO / strum scheduler runs. When off, fretboard runs its own pipeline (§4.4 fallback). |
482	| `actuate_enable` | Commands are actually sent to fretboard. When off, marvin computes commands but suppresses them (dry-run). |
483	| `record_enable` | Recording task writes to SD. |
484	| `game_observe_enable` | Game-state observer task runs; `xGameStateQueue` is active. |
485	| `game_control_enable` | Game-state controller may issue actuator commands for menu navigation / session setup. Suppressed during `gameplay` state when timing pipeline is driving. |
486	
487	A handful of named composite modes (idle, calibrate, dry-run, play, replay, record) are presets over these toggles. Replay specifically requires loading a prior recording from SD and playing detector-state events back through the timing pipeline against the original keyframes — UI affordance for that comes later.

1	# Fretboard Firmware Specification
2	
3	## Overview
4	
5	Firmware for PIC32CM6408PL10048 (Cortex-M0+, 24 MHz) that acts as an
6	**I/O bridge** between a Guitar Hero controller and an off-board host.
7	Five phototransistors above the TV strike line are sampled and streamed
8	out continuously; the host runs detection / chord / strum logic and
9	sends back a single-byte bitmask that drives the controller's button
10	GPIOs directly.
11	
12	In its `MARVIN_DRIVEN` mode the firmware contains **no game logic** — it only
13	scans ADCs, emits frames, and applies received bitmasks. A second build-time
14	mode, **`MODEL_DRIVEN`** (`FRETBOARD_MODE` in `main.c`, the current default),
15	makes the board standalone: an on-device int8 neural net (`model_infer.c`,
16	weights in the generated `model_weights.h`) maps the ADC window to the button
17	bitmask itself, no host required. SW0 toggles it; LED0 shows the state.
18	Inference runs in the main loop; the 240 Hz TC0 ISR only samples and applies.
19	See [`docs/journal.md`](docs/journal.md) and edge-ai
20	[`runtime.md`](../../tools/edge-ai/docs/runtime.md).
21	
22	## Hardware
23	
24	### Target
25	
26	| Spec | Value |
27	|------|-------|
28	| Device | PIC32CM6408PL10048 |
29	| Core | ARM Cortex-M0+ |
30	| Clock | 24 MHz |
31	| Toolchain | XC32 5.10 |
32	| Programmer | PKOB nano |
33	
34	### Pin Map
35	
36	#### Sensor Inputs (ADC)
37	
38	Five phototransistors positioned above the TV strike line. Each
39	produces an analog voltage that drops when a note passes the sensor.
40	ADC reads 12-bit unsigned (0–4095); lower values indicate note
41	presence.
42	
43	| Channel | ADC Input | Pin |
44	|---------|-----------|-----|
45	| Green | AIN28 | PA28 |
46	| Red | AIN16 | PA16 |
47	| Yellow | AIN19 | PA19 |
48	| Blue | AIN27 | PA27 |
49	| Orange | AIN26 | PA26 |
50	
51	#### Button Outputs (Open-Drain GPIO)
52	
53	Each button output is normally tri-stated (input mode). To "press" a
54	button the pin is driven low (clear + output-enable). To "release" it
55	the pin returns to input mode, which floats the line and lets the
56	guitar controller's own pull-up restore the idle state.
57	
58	| Function | Pin | Cmd bit |
59	|----------|-----|---------|
60	| Green fret | PA06 | 0 |
61	| Red fret | PA05 | 1 |
62	| Yellow fret | PA07 | 2 |
63	| Blue fret | PA04 | 3 |
64	| Orange fret | PA01 | 4 |
65	| Strum down | PA03 | 5 |
66	| Strum up | PA00 | 6 |
67	
68	#### UART (SERCOM1)
69	
70	| Function | Pin |
71	|----------|-----|
72	| TX (data stream out) | PB00 |
73	| RX (command in) | PB01 |
74	
75	Baud: **500 000**, 8N1.
76	
77	## Software Architecture
78	
79	### Processing Loop
80	
81	`TC0` is configured to fire a periodic callback at **240 Hz**
82	(≈4.17 ms period). Each tick runs three stages in sequence from the
83	timer ISR:
84	
85	```
86	TC0 callback (240 Hz)
87	    |
88	    v
89	fret_scan_all()          Blocking ADC read of all 5 channels
90	    |
91	    v
92	data_stream_send()       17-byte frame over SERCOM1 TX
93	    |
94	    v
95	cmd_receive_update()     Drains SERCOM1 RX, applies latest bitmask
96	```
97	
98	`main()` is just init + idle loop; all work happens in the TC0 ISR.
99	
100	### Module Descriptions
101	
102	#### fret_scan ([fret_scan.c](fret_scan.c) / [fret_scan.h](fret_scan.h))
103	
104	Reads all five ADC channels sequentially using blocking polling.
105	Results are stored in a static array and accessed via
106	`fret_scan_result(channel)`.
107	
108	The channel enum defines the canonical fret ordering used throughout
109	the firmware:
110	
111	```
112	FRET_GREEN = 0, FRET_RED = 1, FRET_YELLOW = 2, FRET_BLUE = 3, FRET_ORANGE = 4
113	```
114	
115	#### data_stream ([data_stream.c](data_stream.c) / [data_stream.h](data_stream.h))
116	
117	Emits one 17-byte little-endian frame per tick over SERCOM1 TX:
118	
119	| Offset | Size | Field |
120	|-------:|-----:|-------|
121	| 0 | 1 | start = `0x03` |
122	| 1 | 2 | green (uint16) |
123	| 3 | 2 | red |
124	| 5 | 2 | yellow |
125	| 7 | 2 | blue |
126	| 9 | 2 | orange |
127	| 11 | 4 | sample_seq (uint32) — monotonic, one per tick |
128	| 15 | 1 | applied_mask — actuator bitmask driven this scan |
129	| 16 | 1 | end = `0xFC` (`~start`) |
130	
131	`sample_seq` lets the host reconstruct true sample order and detect frames
132	dropped in transit (it advances per tick even when a send is skipped).
133	`applied_mask` is the bitmask `cmd_receive` currently drives, captured in the
134	same tick as the scan so sensor and actuator state are paired at the source
135	(used by edge-ai training-data export). The frame is dropped silently if the
136	TX free-buffer count is below the frame size. At 240 Hz this is 4 080 B/s —
137	well within the 50 000 B/s budget at 500 000 baud.
138	
139	#### cmd_receive ([cmd_receive.c](cmd_receive.c) / [cmd_receive.h](cmd_receive.h))
140	
141	Drains the SERCOM1 RX buffer each tick. The **last byte received** in
142	the tick is interpreted as a button bitmask and applied directly:
143	
144	| Bit | Output |
145	|----:|--------|
146	| 0 | Green fret |
147	| 1 | Red fret |
148	| 2 | Yellow fret |
149	| 3 | Blue fret |
150	| 4 | Orange fret |
151	| 5 | Strum down |
152	| 6 | Strum up |
153	
154	Bit set → drive low (assert). Bit clear → tri-state (release).
155	
156	Note: only the most recent byte each tick is honoured. The host is
157	expected to send commands at a rate ≤ the loop rate; older bytes in
158	the same tick are coalesced away.
159	
160	## Tools
161	
162	### Host-side data-stream monitor
163	
164	[`tools/ds_monitor.py`](tools/ds_monitor.py) opens the serial port,
165	resyncs on `0x03 … 0xFC` framing, and reports actual frame rate, byte
166	rate, framing-error count, and current ADC values once per second.
167	
168	The script declares its dependencies inline (PEP 723) and is run via
169	[`uv`](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) — no manual venv or `pip install`
170	needed:
171	
172	```
173	./tools/ds_monitor.py /dev/tty.usbmodem<...>
174	# or, equivalently:
175	uv run tools/ds_monitor.py /dev/tty.usbmodem<...>
176	```
177	
178	Defaults: `--baud 500000 --expect-hz 240`.
179	
180	## Build System
181	
182	MPLAB Extensions for VS Code. Project config is in
183	`.vscode/fretboard.mplab.json`. Source files are listed in the
184	`fileSets[0].files` array. MCC/Harmony-generated code lives under
185	`fretboard-mcc/` and should not be edited.
186	
187	## File Map
188	
189	| File | Purpose |
190	|------|---------|
191	| [main.c](main.c) | Init + TC0 callback wiring |
192	| [fret_scan.c](fret_scan.c) / [.h](fret_scan.h) | ADC channel scanning |
193	| [data_stream.c](data_stream.c) / [.h](data_stream.h) | UART output frame |
194	| [cmd_receive.c](cmd_receive.c) / [.h](cmd_receive.h) | UART input bitmask |
195	| [tools/ds_monitor.py](tools/ds_monitor.py) | Host-side frame-rate / content check |
196	| `fret_detect.c` / `.h` | **Orphaned** (see [docs/journal.md](docs/journal.md)) |
197	| `fret_button.c` / `.h` | **Orphaned** (see [docs/journal.md](docs/journal.md)) |
198	| `fretboard-mcc/` | MCC Harmony peripheral libraries (generated) |
199
```

Patch the hook to emit a `LOG_ERR` line naming the offending task before the spin (carefully — the stack is already corrupt, so the hook should avoid using locals or large stack frames). Already nearly bit us once: 2026-05-21 freeze in `open_cdc()` was first misdiagnosed as a stack overflow because we had no visibility into actual stack usage of the FBL task. MCC's FreeRTOS Harmony component does not expose a knob for an app-specific counter source. Append at the end of `FreeRTOSConfig.h` (just before `#endif`):
130	     ```c
131	     extern uint64_t SYS_TIME_Counter64Get(void);
132	     #define configRUN_TIME_COUNTER_TYPE             uint64_t
133	     #define portCONFIGURE_TIMER_FOR_RUN_TIME_STATS()
134	     #define portGET_RUN_TIME_COUNTER_VALUE()        SYS_TIME_Counter64Get()
135	     ```
136	     `SYS_TIME` is already initialised by Harmony before the scheduler starts, so the configure macro is a no-op. `SYS_TIME_Counter64Get` returns the full 64-bit TC0 CH0 counter; the matching `configRUN_TIME_COUNTER_TYPE = uint64_t` overrides FreeRTOS's `uint32_t` default so cumulative `ulRunTimeCounter` values don't wrap (uint32_t at 266 MHz wraps after ~16 s of accumulated CPU time across all tasks, which made percentages garbage almost immediately). Bare `extern` (rather than including a Harmony header) keeps `FreeRTOSConfig.h` consumable by low-level kernel sources that don't pull in `definitions.h`.

138	  7. **`drv_usb_udphs_device.c` — multi-IRP DMA arming in completion ISRs.** Stock UDPHS device driver only programs the DMA channel in `IRPSubmit`'s queue-empty branch (line 1604+); IRPs appended to a non-empty queue link in (line 2273-2284 of patched file via `iterator->next = irp_t`) but never get armed for transmission. `Tasks_ISR_DMA` advances `irpQueue = irp->next` after firing the callback but does not re-program DMA hardware. 139	
140	      Fix is additive (no refactor of working code): add a static helper `F_DRV_USB_UDPHS_DEVICE_ArmDmaForIrp` just before `DRV_USB_UDPHS_DEVICE_IRPSubmit`, mirroring the existing inline DMA-program block (~80 lines covering both DEVICE_TO_HOST and HOST_TO_DEVICE directions). Then add a call after the queue advance in **two** places:
141	
142	      - `Tasks_ISR_DMA` immediately after `endpointObj->irpQueue = irp->next; irp->callback(...)` — the normal DMA-completion path.
143	      - The ZLP-completion path inside `Tasks_ISR` (under "endpoint interrupt on a DMA capable endpoint, so it should be a ZLP"), same place: after queue advance.
144	
145	      Both call sites guarded by `if (endpointObj->irpQueue != NULL)`. Patch markers `/* PATCH: */` make the change findable after MCC regen. Helper carries the same cache-clean and DMA-program shape as the inline original, including the `__DSB(); __ISB();` barriers and the `SYS_CACHE_CleanDCache_by_Addr` for the IRP data buffer.
146	
147	      Without this patch, the lever-1 multi-IRP work (`queueSizeWrite=3`, `USB_DEVICE_CDC_QUEUE_DEPTH_COMBINED=5`) accepts writes but only ever transmits the first of any batch. With it, multi-IRP pipelining works as designed at the driver level. Patch is specific to Harmony USB v3.16.0 device driver; check whether future versions wire the post-completion arm and obviate the patch.
148	
149	  8. **`driver/input/drv_maxtouch.c` — bounded maXTouch init so an absent touch panel can't hang the whole system.** Stock `mxt_initialize()` does `while (1) { mxt_read_info_block(); if (!error) break; }`. With the display/maXTouch panel disconnected the info-block read never succeeds, so it spins forever — and because each `mxt_read_info_block()` allocates from the FreeRTOS heap (heap_1, no free), the retries leak until the heap is exhausted and the system hangs in `vApplicationMallocFailedHook`. This is exactly what blocked the JTAG load-to-RAM bring-up (fault landed in `DRV_MAXTOUCH_Tasks`, `xNextFreeByte`=40,944/40,960). Three-part fix: (a) `__mxt_read_reg` now propagates the real `DRV_I2C_WriteReadTransfer` result (`? 0 : -EIO`) instead of hardcoding `ret = 0`, so a NAK from an absent controller is detected at the *first* read and bails before the second, garbage-sized `OSAL_Malloc`; (b) `mxt_initialize` retries at most `MXT_INIT_MAX_ATTEMPTS` (10, 20 ms apart) then returns the error; (c) `DRV_MAXTOUCH_Tasks` `DEVICE_STATE_MXT_INITIALIZE` parks the driver in `DEVICE_STATE_ERROR` (not READY) on failure, so the rest of the system runs headless without touch. Syntax-checked clean with XC32 v4.60, then **validated on hardware (2026-06-08)**: with the display/maXTouch panel disconnected, marvin loaded via the JTAG load-to-RAM flow now boots *past* maXTouch init (driver → `DEVICE_STATE_ERROR`) and runs headless — PC samples land in `DRV_USB_UDPHS_DEVICE_IRPSubmit` / `USB_DEVICE_CDC_Read` (perf-log USB-CDC path) and advance across the codebase, instead of hanging at `vApplicationMallocFailedHook`. 1	# Project rules
2	
3	These rules apply to every session on this repo. Follow them without being reminded.
4	
5	## Git commits require explicit approval
6	
7	Never run `git commit` on your own initiative. Always ask first and wait for explicit confirmation before committing — even when wrapping up a session or completing a doc sweep.
8	
9	## Specs orient you; journals track progress
10	
11	The repo has three subprojects (marvin, fretboard, fret-tuner) plus a top-level system spec.
12	
13	- **[`SPEC.md`](SPEC.md) is the cross-subproject overview** — read it first if a task spans subprojects or if you're new to the repo. It points at each subproject's spec and journal.
14	- For non-trivial work inside a single subproject, read that subproject's spec **and** journal first (see below).
15	
16	## Journals are the source of truth for planning and progress
17	
18	This repo uses working journals to track planning, decisions, open questions, and work-in-progress *outside* the chat context so they survive across sessions, compactions, and restarts.
19	
20	Current journals:
21	
22	- `firmware/marvin/docs/journal.md` — marvin firmware (SAM9X75 vision-based guitar-playing robot)
23	  - System-level spec for marvin lives at `firmware/marvin/docs/spec.md` — **read it first** alongside the journal on any non-trivial marvin task. The spec is the durable description of what marvin is (purpose, subsystems, interfaces, milestones); the journal is the running diary.
24	- `firmware/fretboard/docs/journal.md` — fretboard firmware (PIC32CM I/O bridge: ADC stream out + button-bitmask in)
25	  - Spec for fretboard lives at `firmware/fretboard/SPEC.md` — read it alongside the journal on any non-trivial fretboard task.
26	- `tools/edge-ai/docs/journal.md` — edge-ai (distill marvin's gameplay commands into a small ML model for the fretboard MCU)
27	  - Specs for edge-ai live under `tools/edge-ai/docs/` (`SPEC.md` + the doc map there) — read them alongside the journal on any non-trivial edge-ai task.
28	- `firmware/fauxmote/docs/journal.md` — fauxmote (ESP32 firmware emulating a Wiimote + guitar extension to a real Wii; parallel proof-of-concept)
29	  - Spec for fauxmote lives at `firmware/fauxmote/SPEC.md` — read it alongside the journal on any non-trivial fauxmote task.
30	- `tools/gameplay/docs/journal.md` — gameplay (offline host-side prototype for marvin's GH3 game-state observer/controller; algorithms proven against the screen corpus, then ported to a firmware `gameplay_engine`)
31	  - Orienting docs: marvin `spec.md` §4.8 and `firmware/marvin/docs/gh3_navigation.md` — read them alongside the journal on any non-trivial gameplay task.
32	
33	When working on a subproject that has a journal:
34	
35	1. **Read the journal first.** Before responding to any non-trivial request, read the journal for that subproject. It contains the current focus, phased plan, open questions, decision log, and session log — the state you need to be useful.
36	2. **Update the journal as you go.** When we make a decision, resolve an open question, finish a plan phase, or finish a session, reflect that in the journal. Newest entries at the top within each section.
37	   - Decisions → append to the decision log with date and rationale.
38	   - Resolved open questions → remove from "Open questions" and add to the decision log with the answer and rationale.
39	   - Plan progress → check off phase items; add sub-bullets for anything learned during implementation.
40	   - Session close → add a dated session-log entry summarizing what happened.
41	3. **Prefer updating the journal over restating plans in chat.** If I'd otherwise write a multi-paragraph plan in chat, it belongs in the journal — the chat is ephemeral, the journal isn't.
42	4. **If a new subproject needs a journal, create one** using the same structure as `firmware/marvin/docs/journal.md`, and add it to the list above in this file.
43	
44	## Code comments describe current code only
45	
46	Comments in source files explain **what the code currently does and why**, when that's non-obvious. They are not a development diary.
47	
48	Do not put any of the following in source comments — they belong in the journal, commit messages, or PR descriptions:
49	
50	- Narrative of how the code evolved ("previously we did X, now we do Y", "this replaces the old …")
51	- Debug notes, troubleshooting history, or why something *doesn't* work
52	- TODO lists for future features (use the journal or an issue tracker)
53	- References to tasks, tickets, or past conversations ("fix for Greg's bug", "see chat from 2026-05-01")
54	- Extensive block comments explaining design rationale — a one-line "why" is fine; multi-paragraph prose goes in the journal
55	
56	**Default to no comment.** Only add one when removing it would confuse a future reader. If you catch yourself wanting to write a paragraph, write it in the journal instead and link from the code if needed (e.g. `// see firmware/marvin/docs/journal.md`).

1	# Guitar Hero Bot — System Specification
2	
3	> Top-level overview. For implementation detail of any single subproject, follow the pointers in §3. Each subproject owns its own spec; this document does not duplicate them.
4	
5	---
6	
7	## 1. Mission
8	
9	Build an autonomous robot that plays Guitar Hero / Rock Band on a real Wii guitar controller by watching the game video, detecting notes in real time, and pressing physical buttons in sync with the music. The system must run end-to-end without a host PC in the runtime path, produce reference-quality detector output that lighter detectors can be trained against, and provide an on-device operator UI for calibration, mode control, and replay.
10	
11	## 2. Current architecture
12	
13	Three pieces, one runtime brain:
14	
15	```
16	Wii ──HDMI──► ElectronWarp ──HDMI──► TC358743 ──CSI-2──┐
17	                                                       ▼
18	   ┌──────────────────────  marvin (SAM9X75)  ────────────┐
19	   │  HDMI capture → CV detect → timing pipeline → cmds   │
20	   │           ↑              detector-state bus          │
21	   │           │                       ▲                  │
22	   │           │  10.1″ LVDS + maxtouch │                  │
23	   │           │       (operator UI)    │                  │
24	   │           └────────── SD card ─────┘  (recording)    │
25	   └────────┬──────────────────────────┬───────────────────┘
26	            │ FLEXCOM2 UART (cmds)     │ FLEXCOM2 UART (ADC)
27	            ▼                          │
28	   ┌──────────────────────────────────┐│
29	   │   fretboard (PIC32CM6408)        │┘
30	   │   ADC scan ↔ open-drain GPIO     │
31	   └────────┬─────────────────────────┘
32	            │ GPIO
33	            ▼
34	   Wii guitar controller ──► Wii (closes the loop)
35	
36	                ◇ off-band: dev PC running fret-tuner
37	                  (calibration / detector tuning / replay)
38	```
39	
40	**Per-tier role summary:**
41	
42	- **marvin** — SAM9X75 Curiosity host. Owns HDMI capture, the *reference* CV note detector, ingest of fretboard ADC samples, the chord/strum timing pipeline, command emission to fretboard, the on-device LVDS+touch operator UI, and reference-data recording to SD. The runtime brain.
43	- **fretboard** — PIC32CM6408PL10048 MCU on a sensor/actuator board. Streams 5-channel phototransistor ADC up to marvin and converts incoming bitmask commands into open-drain GPIO presses on a Wii guitar controller. Has a standalone fallback mode where it runs its own chord FIFO without marvin in the loop.
44	- **fret-tuner** — Off-band Python tool (FastAPI + browser UI, Linux/macOS PC). Used at the bench for sensor calibration, detector-algorithm tuning, and replay analysis of recordings produced by marvin. Not in the runtime path.
45	
46	## 3. Subproject specs (where detail lives)
47	
48	| Subproject | Spec | Journal |
49	|---|---|---|
50	| marvin | [`firmware/marvin/docs/spec.md`](firmware/marvin/docs/spec.md) | [`firmware/marvin/docs/journal.md`](firmware/marvin/docs/journal.md) |
51	| fretboard | [`firmware/fretboard/SPEC.md`](firmware/fretboard/SPEC.md) | [`firmware/fretboard/docs/journal.md`](firmware/fretboard/docs/journal.md) |
52	| fret-tuner | [`tools/fret-tuner/SPEC.md`](tools/fret-tuner/SPEC.md) | — |
53	| marvin-perf | [`tools/marvin-perf/`](tools/marvin-perf/) — perf-log decoder + live/offline web viewer | — |
54	| edge-ai | [`tools/edge-ai/docs/SPEC.md`](tools/edge-ai/docs/SPEC.md) — design proposal: distill marvin's gameplay commands into a small ML model running on fretboard. Offline development first; Phase 1 data pipeline in progress. | [`tools/edge-ai/docs/journal.md`](tools/edge-ai/docs/journal.md) |
55	| gameplay | marvin spec [§4.8](firmware/marvin/docs/spec.md) + [`firmware/marvin/docs/gh3_navigation.md`](firmware/marvin/docs/gh3_navigation.md) — GH3 game-state observer/controller offline prototype; algorithms proven against the screen corpus, then ported to the marvin firmware `gameplay_engine`. | [`tools/gameplay/docs/journal.md`](tools/gameplay/docs/journal.md) |
56	| fauxmote | [`firmware/fauxmote/SPEC.md`](firmware/fauxmote/SPEC.md) — *parallel proof-of-concept:* ESP32 (Adafruit Feather V2) firmware that emulates a Wiimote + guitar extension over Bluetooth to a real Wii, an alternative to the fretboard's physical button-pressing. Not yet in the runtime path; fretboard stays authoritative. | [`firmware/fauxmote/docs/journal.md`](firmware/fauxmote/docs/journal.md) |
57	
58	marvin's spec also has deeper-dive documents for its capture and display paths ([`capture_pipeline.md`](firmware/marvin/docs/capture_pipeline.md), [`display_path.md`](firmware/marvin/docs/display_path.md)).
59	
60	## 4. Repository map
61	
62	```
63	guitar-pic/
64	├── README.md                    # short landing page
65	├── SPEC.md                      # this document
66	├── CLAUDE.md                    # workflow rules for Claude Code sessions
67	├── firmware/
68	│   ├── marvin/                  # SAM9X75 host firmware
69	│   ├── fretboard/               # PIC32CM6408 sensor/actuator MCU firmware
70	│   ├── fauxmote/                # ESP32 Wiimote emulator (proof-of-concept)
71	│   └── sam9x75_curiosity_emirror/   # Microchip reference project (template only)
72	├── tools/
73	│   ├── fret-tuner/              # Python dev/calibration tool
74	│   ├── gameplay/                # GH3 game-state observer/controller offline prototype
75	│   └── marvin-perf/             # marvin perf-log decoder + web viewer
76	├── hardware/
77	│   ├── actuators/               # voice coil / electromagnet / DIY solenoid design + test protocols
78	│   ├── 3d-models/               # OpenSCAD + STL for printed actuator parts
79	│   ├── Sensor-LCD5/             # KiCad project for fretboard sensor/actuator PCB
80	│   └── kicad/                   # shared symbol/footprint libraries
81	└── docs/
82	    ├── SAM9X7-Series-Data-Sheet-DS60001813.pdf
83	    └── archive/                 # historical docs from the original PC/Elgato/PS2 architecture
84	```
85	
86	## 5. Hardware platforms (high-level)
87	
88	| Component | Role | Where to look |
89	|---|---|---|
90	| SAM9X75 Curiosity | marvin host | [marvin spec §3](firmware/marvin/docs/spec.md) |
91	| Waveshare HDMI→CSI-2 adapter (TC358743) | HDMI bridge into marvin | [marvin spec §3](firmware/marvin/docs/spec.md), [capture pipeline](firmware/marvin/docs/capture_pipeline.md) |
92	| 10.1″ 1280×800 LVDS panel + maxtouch | marvin operator UI surface | [marvin display path](firmware/marvin/docs/display_path.md) |
93	| Sensor/actuator PCB (Sensor-LCD5) | fretboard board: 5 phototransistors + GPIO out | [`hardware/Sensor-LCD5/`](hardware/Sensor-LCD5/) |
94	| PIC32CM6408PL10048 | fretboard MCU | [fretboard spec](firmware/fretboard/SPEC.md) |
95	| LAN8651B1 (10BASE-T1S MAC-PHY) | *planned* fretboard ↔ marvin link over single-pair Ethernet + PoDL | [T1S/PoDL link](docs/t1s-podl-link.md) |
96	| Actuator mechanism (TBD: voice coil / electromagnet / DIY solenoid) | physical fret + strum drive | [`hardware/actuators/`](hardware/actuators/) and [`hardware/3d-models/`](hardware/3d-models/) |
97	| ElectronWarp | component → HDMI converter for Wii | external commercial part |
98	
99	The actuator choice is intentionally still open — `hardware/actuators/` contains design + test-protocol docs for three candidates.
100	
101	## 6. Cross-cutting decisions
102	
103	- **Architecture pivot.** The original PC-hosted / Elgato-USB-capture / PS2 / single-PIC-actuator design is retired. Source documents are preserved at [`docs/archive/`](docs/archive/) for design-rationale reference; they are *not* maintained.
104	- **`frame_epoch` is the master sync token.** A 32-bit counter incremented by marvin's video task on every captured ISC frame. Every detector-state record, emitted command, and recording artifact — including data from off-board observers — keys off this token so multi-source data can be aligned post-hoc. Detail in [marvin spec §4.6](firmware/marvin/docs/spec.md).
105	- **Reference data persists on marvin's SD card.** Detector-state + sparse raw BGR888 keyframes (default 1 keyframe/sec) + raw ADC stream + emitted commands. Off-board detectors record their own data keyed by `frame_epoch` and align offline.
106	- **Centralized timing on marvin, with a fretboard-takeover fallback.** marvin runs the chord-window FIFO and strum scheduler by default; an operator-mode toggle hands timing back to fretboard's standalone `fret_button.c` while marvin still records observations.
107	- **Operating modes are independent toggles**, not a global state machine: `detect_enable`, `marvin_timing_enable`, `actuate_enable`, `record_enable`. Named modes (idle / calibrate / dry-run / play / replay / record) are presets over them.
108	- **Planned: fretboard ↔ marvin link moves to 10BASE-T1S + dumb PoDL.** Replace the FLEXCOM2/SERCOM UART pair with single-pair Ethernet via a LAN8651B1 MAC-PHY on each end. Motivation, in order: PoDL carries power *and* data on one pair to the guitar; better noise/cable tolerance; PLCA multidrop headroom; and demonstrating 10BASE-T1S + PoDL inside a larger Microchip system (SAM9X7 + LAN8651 + PIC32CM). Bandwidth is not a driver — the existing UART has ~12× headroom. PoDL is **dumb** (fixed voltage, no SCCP negotiation) and transparent to both MCUs. No IP stack — the host implements only SPI + the OPEN Alliance TC6 chunk protocol + minimal L2 framing, with the existing frame formats riding unchanged inside the Ethernet payload. Fits comfortably on the PIC32CM (est. ~6–10 KB flash / ~1–2 KB SRAM); marvin is bare-metal so it gets a shared portable `oa_tc6` driver, not a free netdev. Detail in [`docs/t1s-podl-link.md`](docs/t1s-podl-link.md).
109	
110	## 7. Project-wide phasing
111	
112	| Status | Item |
113	|---|---|
114	| ✅ | marvin HDMI capture → DDR (BGR888 packed) at 480p60 and 720p60 |
115	| ✅ | marvin DDR → 10.1″ LVDS panel display (HEO, per-frame swap, pillarboxed/letterboxed) |
116	| ✅ | marvin FreeRTOS scheduler, video task, static task priorities, analytics |
117	| ✅ | fretboard standalone play (phototransistors + open-drain GPIO) |
118	| ✅ | fret-tuner used at the bench for detector tuning |
119	| ✅ | marvin perf-log USB CDC export — live RTOS analytics + pixel strip viewer (`tools/marvin-perf`) |
120	| ✅ | **M1** — marvin reference detector v0 (`cv_marvin_v1` running, `detector_state_t` bus active) |
121	| ✅ | **M2** — fretboard ↔ marvin link (commands flowing; link rewired USB CDC host → FLEXCOM2 UART for the Curiosity Hybrid board, pending on-hardware re-validation) |
122	| ✅ | **M3** — end-to-end play (timing pipeline + fretboard actuation; Expert and Easy tested) |
123	| 🚧 | **M4** — recording-to-SD (detector-state + keyframes + ADC + commands) |
124	| 🚧 | **M5** — operator UI v0; manual-control surface (8 buttons) done; full live-view + mode-toggle UI not started |
125	| 🚧 | **M6**+ — calibration UI, replay, fretboard-takeover validation |
126	| 🚧 | **M9** — game-state observer: Phases 1+2 (screen classifier + section-select/song readers) ported to firmware `gameplay_engine`, MPLAB build confirmed, pending hardware test; Phase 3 (number/score readers) not started |
127	| 🚧 | **M10** — game-state controller: navigator/closed-loop algorithm complete in `tools/gameplay` prototype; firmware port not started |
128	| 🔭 | **T1S link** — re-architect fretboard ↔ marvin onto 10BASE-T1S + dumb PoDL (LAN8651B1 each end). Direction only; not started. [Detail](docs/t1s-podl-link.md) |
129	
130	Detail (definitions of done, demos) in [marvin spec §8](firmware/marvin/docs/spec.md).
131	
132	## 8. What this is *not*
133	
134	To anchor against the original architecture (preserved in `docs/archive/`):
135	
136	- **Not PC-hosted.** marvin is the runtime brain; no host PC is required for play.
137	- **Not USB-capture / Elgato.** Video is captured directly off HDMI via a TC358743 → MIPI CSI-2 path into the SAM9X75's ISC.
138	- **Not PS2.** The supported console is the Nintendo Wii (with an ElectronWarp component → HDMI converter).
139	- **Not a single-MCU actuator.** Sensing and timing live on marvin; fretboard is a sensor/actuator MCU, not a solo controller (with the explicit exception of the standalone-fallback mode).
140	- **Not OpenCV / Python at runtime.** CV runs natively on the SAM9X75 (Cortex-A5). Python (`fret-tuner`) is a bench tool only.

```text
1	# Fretboard Firmware Specification
2	
3	## Overview
4	
5	Firmware for PIC32CM6408PL10048 (Cortex-M0+, 24 MHz) that acts as an
6	**I/O bridge** between a Guitar Hero controller and an off-board host.
7	Five phototransistors above the TV strike line are sampled and streamed
8	out continuously; the host runs detection / chord / strum logic and
9	sends back a single-byte bitmask that drives the controller's button
10	GPIOs directly.
11	
12	In its `MARVIN_DRIVEN` mode the firmware contains **no game logic** — it only
13	scans ADCs, emits frames, and applies received bitmasks. A second build-time
14	mode, **`MODEL_DRIVEN`** (`FRETBOARD_MODE` in `main.c`, the current default),
15	makes the board standalone: an on-device int8 neural net (`model_infer.c`,
16	weights in the generated `model_weights.h`) maps the ADC window to the button
17	bitmask itself, no host required. SW0 toggles it; LED0 shows the state.
18	Inference runs in the main loop; the 240 Hz TC0 ISR only samples and applies.
19	See [`docs/journal.md`](docs/journal.md) and edge-ai
20	[`runtime.md`](../../tools/edge-ai/docs/runtime.md).
21	
22	## Hardware
23	
24	### Target
25	
26	| Spec | Value |
27	|------|-------|
28	| Device | PIC32CM6408PL10048 |
29	| Core | ARM Cortex-M0+ |
30	| Clock | 24 MHz |
31	| Toolchain | XC32 5.10 |
32	| Programmer | PKOB nano |
33	
34	### Pin Map
35	
36	#### Sensor Inputs (ADC)
37	
38	Five phototransistors positioned above the TV strike line. Each
39	produces an analog voltage that drops when a note passes the sensor.
40	ADC reads 12-bit unsigned (0–4095); lower values indicate note
41	presence.
42	
43	| Channel | ADC Input | Pin |
44	|---------|-----------|-----|
45	| Green | AIN28 | PA28 |
46	| Red | AIN16 | PA16 |
47	| Yellow | AIN19 | PA19 |
48	| Blue | AIN27 | PA27 |
49	| Orange | AIN26 | PA26 |
50	
51	#### Button Outputs (Open-Drain GPIO)
52	
53	Each button output is normally tri-stated (input mode). To "press" a
54	button the pin is driven low (clear + output-enable). To "release" it
55	the pin returns to input mode, which floats the line and lets the
56	guitar controller's own pull-up restore the idle state.
57	
58	| Function | Pin | Cmd bit |
59	|----------|-----|---------|
60	| Green fret | PA06 | 0 |
61	| Red fret | PA05 | 1 |
62	| Yellow fret | PA07 | 2 |
63	| Blue fret | PA04 | 3 |
64	| Orange fret | PA01 | 4 |
65	| Strum down | PA03 | 5 |
66	| Strum up | PA00 | 6 |
67	
68	#### UART (SERCOM1)
69	
70	| Function | Pin |
71	|----------|-----|
72	| TX (data stream out) | PB00 |
73	| RX (command in) | PB01 |
74	
75	Baud: **500 000**, 8N1.
76	
77	## Software Architecture
78	
79	### Processing Loop
80	
81	`TC0` is configured to fire a periodic callback at **240 Hz**
82	(≈4.17 ms period). Each tick runs three stages in sequence from the
83	timer ISR:
84	
85	```
86	TC0 callback (240 Hz)
87	    |
88	    v
89	fret_scan_all()          Blocking ADC read of all 5 channels
90	    |
91	    v
92	data_stream_send()       17-byte frame over SERCOM1 TX
93	    |
94	    v
95	cmd_receive_update()     Drains SERCOM1 RX, applies latest bitmask
96	```
97	
98	`main()` is just init + idle loop; all work happens in the TC0 ISR.
99	
100	### Module Descriptions
101	
102	#### fret_scan ([fret_scan.c](fret_scan.c) / [fret_scan.h](fret_scan.h))
103	
104	Reads all five ADC channels sequentially using blocking polling.
105	Results are stored in a static array and accessed via
106	`fret_scan_result(channel)`.
107	
108	The channel enum defines the canonical fret ordering used throughout
109	the firmware:
110	
111	```
112	FRET_GREEN = 0, FRET_RED = 1, FRET_YELLOW = 2, FRET_BLUE = 3, FRET_ORANGE = 4
113	```
114	
115	#### data_stream ([data_stream.c](data_stream.c) / [data_stream.h](data_stream.h))
116	
117	Emits one 17-byte little-endian frame per tick over SERCOM1 TX:
118	
119	| Offset | Size | Field |
120	|-------:|-----:|-------|
121	| 0 | 1 | start = `0x03` |
122	| 1 | 2 | green (uint16) |
123	| 3 | 2 | red |
124	| 5 | 2 | yellow |
125	| 7 | 2 | blue |
126	| 9 | 2 | orange |
127	| 11 | 4 | sample_seq (uint32) — monotonic, one per tick |
128	| 15 | 1 | applied_mask — actuator bitmask driven this scan |
129	| 16 | 1 | end = `0xFC` (`~start`) |
130	
131	`sample_seq` lets the host reconstruct true sample order and detect frames
132	dropped in transit (it advances per tick even when a send is skipped).
133	`applied_mask` is the bitmask `cmd_receive` currently drives, captured in the
134	same tick as the scan so sensor and actuator state are paired at the source
135	(used by edge-ai training-data export). The frame is dropped silently if the
136	TX free-buffer count is below the frame size. At 240 Hz this is 4 080 B/s —
137	well within the 50 000 B/s budget at 500 000 baud.
138	
139	#### cmd_receive ([cmd_receive.c](cmd_receive.c) / [cmd_receive.h](cmd_receive.h))
140	
141	Drains the SERCOM1 RX buffer each tick. The **last byte received** in
142	the tick is interpreted as a button bitmask and applied directly:
143	
144	| Bit | Output |
145	|----:|--------|
146	| 0 | Green fret |
147	| 1 | Red fret |
148	| 2 | Yellow fret |
149	| 3 | Blue fret |
150	| 4 | Orange fret |
151	| 5 | Strum down |
152	| 6 | Strum up |
153	
154	Bit set → drive low (assert). Bit clear → tri-state (release).
155	
156	Note: only the most recent byte each tick is honoured. The host is
157	expected to send commands at a rate ≤ the loop rate; older bytes in
158	the same tick are coalesced away.
159	
160	## Tools
161	
162	### Host-side data-stream monitor
163	
164	[`tools/ds_monitor.py`](tools/ds_monitor.py) opens the serial port,
165	resyncs on `0x03 … 0xFC` framing, and reports actual frame rate, byte
166	rate, framing-error count, and current ADC values once per second.
167	
168	The script declares its dependencies inline (PEP 723) and is run via
169	[`uv`](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) — no manual venv or `pip install`
170	needed:
171	
172	```
173	./tools/ds_monitor.py /dev/tty.usbmodem<...>
174	# or, equivalently:
175	uv run tools/ds_monitor.py /dev/tty.usbmodem<...>
176	```
177	
178	Defaults: `--baud 500000 --expect-hz 240`.
179	
180	## Build System
181	
182	MPLAB Extensions for VS Code. Project config is in
183	`.vscode/fretboard.mplab.json`. Source files are listed in the
184	`fileSets[0].files` array. MCC/Harmony-generated code lives under
185	`fretboard-mcc/` and should not be edited.
186	
187	## File Map
188	
189	| File | Purpose |
190	|------|---------|
191	| [main.c](main.c) | Init + TC0 callback wiring |
192	| [fret_scan.c](fret_scan.c) / [.h](fret_scan.h) | ADC channel scanning |
193	| [data_stream.c](data_stream.c) / [.h](data_stream.h) | UART output frame |
194	| [cmd_receive.c](cmd_receive.c) / [.h](cmd_receive.h) | UART input bitmask |
195	| [tools/ds_monitor.py](tools/ds_monitor.py) | Host-side frame-rate / content check |
196	| `fret_detect.c` / `.h` | **Orphaned** (see [docs/journal.md](docs/journal.md)) |
197	| `fret_button.c` / `.h` | **Orphaned** (see [docs/journal.md](docs/journal.md)) |
198	| `fretboard-mcc/` | MCC Harmony peripheral libraries (generated) |
199

32	## Open questions
33	
34	1. **No corruption signalling on the wire.** A bit-flip inside the 5 uint16 payload bytes is silently accepted — only out-of-range start/end bytes are caught. At 500 000 baud over EDBG-CDC this is probably fine, but if we ever see suspect detector behaviour, adding a Fletcher-16 byte (matching marvin's wire format) is a one-byte frame growth.
35	
36	2. **No host→firmware framing.** Command stream is raw bitmask bytes with no start byte. A spurious byte (e.g. line glitch on RX) becomes a button command. Acceptable for now because the line is short and runs over the same EDBG-CDC pair as TX, but worth revisiting if we see ghost presses.
37	
38	3. **T1S link transport — direction, not yet built.** Plan to move the marvin link from the SERCOM1 UART to **10BASE-T1S single-pair Ethernet + dumb PoDL** via a LAN8651B1 MAC-PHY (system spec §6 + [`../../../docs/t1s-podl-link.md`](../../../docs/t1s-podl-link.md)). Fretboard-side cost is an OA TC6 SPI driver + minimal L2 framing (~6–10 KB flash / ~1–2 KB SRAM, one free SERCOM in SPI mode + CS_N/IRQ_N/reset GPIO); the 17-byte data frame + 1-byte command formats ride unchanged inside the Ethernet payload, so `data_stream.c`/`cmd_receive.c` need no logic change — only the transport under them swaps. Open sub-items: PLCA-multidrop vs point-to-point (lean PLCA), custom ethertype + the two hardcoded MACs, and whether to keep the UART as a bring-up fallback (decides if SERCOM1's data path is reclaimed). PoDL is transparent to the MCU (zero firmware footprint). Decide before any code lands.

11	- **`MARVIN_DRIVEN`** (I/O bridge) — 240 Hz TC0 callback: scan five ADCs, emit a 17-byte frame on SERCOM1 TX, drain RX and apply the latest button bitmask. Frame carries `sample_seq` + the applied actuator bitmask (edge-ai training-data sync). Chord/strum logic off-board.
12	- **`MODEL_DRIVEN`** (new, current default — standalone edge-ai inference) — the on-device int8 model ([`model_infer.c`](../model_infer.c), weights in [`model_weights.h`](../model_weights.h)) reads the ADC window and drives the buttons itself; marvin disconnected. **SW0 (PB03)** toggles model control, **LED0 (PB02)** shows enabled (boots disabled). The 240 Hz TC0 ISR only samples + applies the latest command + streams; `model_infer_run()` runs in the **main loop** (it overruns the tick if put in the ISR — see decision log + edge-ai `runtime.md` §3). Build at `-O2`/`-O3`.
13	
14	Baud is 500 000. Host checks: [`tools/ds_monitor.py`](../tools/ds_monitor.py) (framing) and [`../../../tools/marvin-perf/fretboard_rate.py`](../../../tools/marvin-perf/fretboard_rate.py) (true tick rate from `sample_seq` + strums/s).
15	
16	---
17	
18	## Decision log
19	
20	| Date | Decision | Rationale |
21	|------|----------|-----------|
22	| 2026-06-04 | **Added `MODEL_DRIVEN` mode: on-device int8 inference (`model_infer.c/.h` + generated `model_weights.h`), SW0/LED0 enable toggle, and inference run in the main loop — NOT the TC0 ISR.** Active model is a swappable `model_def_t` pointer (`model_infer_set_model`). Build at `-O2`/`-O3`. | Standalone bring-up of the edge-ai model (edge-ai journal 2026-06-04). **Inference must not run in the 240 Hz ISR**: measured on hardware, doing so dropped the callback rate to ~150–190 Hz (so the model's 250 ms window/lag went wrong) *and* starved the interrupt-driven SERCOM TX (recv ~22 fps, heavy drops). Moving `model_infer_run()` to the main loop and having the ISR only sample + apply a `volatile uint8_t` latest-command restored clean 240/240 Hz. The pointer-swap model_def lets per-difficulty weights be selected at runtime and keeps the door open for serial-loaded weights (RAM headroom confirmed; 8 KB SRAM). SW0 (PB03 active-low momentary, debounced) toggles control; LED0 (PB02) shows state; boots disabled (outputs released). `MARVIN_DRIVEN` stays the alternate build for the I/O-bridge path. |
23	| 2026-06-03 | Data-stream frame grows 12→17 bytes: `0x03 \| g r y b o (5×u16 LE) \| sample_seq (u32 LE) \| applied_mask (u8) \| 0xFC`. `sample_seq` is a monotonic counter incremented once per tick in `data_stream_send` (before the TX-buffer check, so a dropped send shows as a gap); `applied_mask` comes from a new `cmd_receive_current_mask()` getter. Resolves open-questions #3 and #4. | Closes the edge-ai data-sync hole (edge-ai journal 2026-06-03). Pairing the actuator state with the ADC scan *in the same frame* makes label↔feature alignment atomic at the source, instead of marvin reconstructing it across its bursty USB RX and separate TX clocks — which Phase-2 training showed floored strum timing at ~20 ms. The seq counter lets the host reconstruct true 240 Hz ordering and detect dropped frames. Callback order is scan→send→receive, so `current_mask` at send time is exactly the state driven *during* this scan. Wire-format break: requires marvin's RX parser + `perf_rec_fretboard_raw_t` (schema v4) to update in lockstep. 17 B × 240 Hz = 4.08 KB/s, still ~12× under the 500 000-baud budget. |
24	| 2026-06-02 | Leave the orphaned `fret_detect.*` and `fret_button.*` modules in place (still in MPLAB fileSet, still building, no callers). Don't delete, don't move to a `fallback/` directory. | Marvin's 2026-05-20 decision keeps a "fretboard-takeover" fallback mode in scope — `fret_button.c` is the existing implementation of that mode and is cheap to keep around. Cost is small (a few KB of flash + the stale `#include "fret_detect.h"` in `data_stream.c`). Revisit if the takeover mode is formally dropped or if these files start drifting against a refactor. |
25	| 2026-06-02 | Loop period moved to 240 Hz, driven by TC0 callback (was 500 Hz from SYSTICK). | Game logic now runs on marvin; the host is the rate-setter and 240 Hz comfortably covers Guitar Hero note-onset timing while leaving SAM9X75 RX-side budget. TC0 callback removes any drift from a polled-SYSTICK loop. |
26	| 2026-06-02 | SERCOM1 baud raised to 500 000 (was lower). | At 240 Hz × 12-byte TX frames + sporadic RX command bytes, 500 000 baud (≈ 50 000 B/s usable) gives ~17× headroom over the 2 880 B/s steady-state — plenty for jitter and back-pressure without flow control. |
27	| 2026-06-02 | Data-stream frame is 12 bytes: `0x03 | g | r | y | b | o | 0xFC` (5×u16 LE). | Pressed-state booleans removed; with detection on the host, raw ADC values are the only payload that matters. Smaller frame ⇒ more TX headroom, simpler host parser. |
28	| 2026-06-02 | Command receive: drain RX each tick, apply only the **last byte** as a 7-bit button bitmask. | The host is expected to send commands at ≤ tick rate; coalescing avoids working through stale bitmasks if anything backs up. Single-byte format means no framing/CRC overhead in either direction — corruption window is one tick at worst. |
29	
30	---
31	
32	## Open questions
33	
34	1. **No corruption signalling on the wire.** A bit-flip inside the 5 uint16 payload bytes is silently accepted — only out-of-range start/end bytes are caught. At 500 000 baud over EDBG-CDC this is probably fine, but if we ever see suspect detector behaviour, adding a Fletcher-16 byte (matching marvin's wire format) is a one-byte frame growth.
35	
36	2. **No host→firmware framing.** Command stream is raw bitmask bytes with no start byte. A spurious byte (e.g. line glitch on RX) becomes a button command. Acceptable for now because the line is short and runs over the same EDBG-CDC pair as TX, but worth revisiting if we see ghost presses.
37	
38	3. **T1S link transport — direction, not yet built.** Plan to move the marvin link from the SERCOM1 UART to **10BASE-T1S single-pair Ethernet + dumb PoDL** via a LAN8651B1 MAC-PHY (system spec §6 + [`../../../docs/t1s-podl-link.md`](../../../docs/t1s-podl-link.md)). Fretboard-side cost is an OA TC6 SPI driver + minimal L2 framing (~6–10 KB flash / ~1–2 KB SRAM, one free SERCOM in SPI mode + CS_N/IRQ_N/reset GPIO); the 17-byte data frame + 1-byte command formats ride unchanged inside the Ethernet payload, so `data_stream.c`/`cmd_receive.c` need no logic change — only the transport under them swaps. Open sub-items: PLCA-multidrop vs point-to-point (lean PLCA), custom ethertype + the two hardcoded MACs, and whether to keep the UART as a bring-up fallback (decides if SERCOM1's data path is reclaimed). PoDL is transparent to the MCU (zero firmware footprint). Decide before any code lands.
39	
40	> Resolved 2026-06-03 (see decision log): #3 "no sample timestamp" and #4 "no applied actuator state" — both fixed by growing the frame to 17 bytes with `sample_seq` + `applied_mask`.

1	# fretboard ↔ marvin link — 10BASE-T1S + PoDL
2	
3	Low-level design for moving the fretboard ↔ marvin link from a FLEXCOM2/SERCOM
4	UART pair to **10BASE-T1S single-pair Ethernet with "dumb" Power-over-Data-Lines
5	(PoDL)**. System-level summary and rationale live in [`../SPEC.md`](../SPEC.md)
6	§6; this document holds the engineering detail.
7	
8	Status: **direction, not yet built.** The link today is FLEXCOM2 UART (system
9	spec M2). Nothing here is flashed.
10	
11	---
12	
13	## 1. Why T1S here
14	
15	- **PoDL** — one twisted pair carries both data *and* the fretboard's power, so
16	  the cable to the guitar is a single 2-wire link instead of a data pair plus a
17	  separate power feed. This is the primary motivation.
18	- **Robustness / reach** — differential single-pair Ethernet tolerates a long,
19	  electrically noisy run to a moving instrument better than a TTL UART pair.
20	- **Multidrop headroom** — 10BASE-T1S/PLCA puts up to 8 nodes on one pair, so a
21	  second sensor node or fretboard can share the same pair *and* the same power.
22	- **Demonstration** — showcasing 10BASE-T1S + PoDL doing real work inside a
23	  larger Microchip system (SAM9X7 + LAN8651 + PIC32CM) is an explicit goal, not
24	  just an incidental benefit. Bandwidth is *not* a motivation — the existing
25	  500 kbaud UART already carries the ~4 KB/s payload with ~12× headroom.
26	
27	## 2. The part: LAN8651B1
28	
29	A **MAC-PHY**: integrates the full IEEE 802.3 Clause 4 MAC *and* the 10BASE-T1S
30	PHY on one chip, and talks to the host MCU over **SPI** using the OPEN Alliance
31	TC6 ("10BASE-T1x MAC-PHY Serial Interface", v1.1) protocol. It exists precisely
32	to give a small MCU with no built-in Ethernet MAC a single-pair Ethernet link
33	over ~5 pins.
34	
35	Done in hardware by the LAN8651 (the MCU never touches these):
36	
37	- Line coding, PLCA / CSMA-CD media access, preamble/SFD.
38	- **FCS (CRC32) generation on TX and checking on RX.**
39	- On-wire framing and minimum-frame padding.
40	
41	SPI: LAN8651 is an SPI client, SCLK up to 25 MHz. Pins: `SDI`, `SDO`, `CS_N`,
42	`SCLK`, `IRQ_N` (active-low interrupt), plus a reset.
43	
44	## 3. What the host MCU must implement
45	
46	No TCP/IP, ARP, DHCP, or any IP stack. Three layers, none large:
47	
48	1. **SPI transport** — one SERCOM in SPI-master mode + GPIO for `CS_N`,
49	   `IRQ_N` (external interrupt), and reset.
50	2. **OA TC6 chunk protocol** — the only real "driver." Unlike a UART, the SPI
51	   link is *not* byte-transparent: it exchanges fixed-size **chunks** (default
52	   64-byte data payload + a 4-byte header on TX / 4-byte footer on RX), with
53	   credit-based flow control (TX credits and RX-chunks-available are reported in
54	   each footer), plus a separate control-transaction format for register
55	   read/writes during init. Microchip publishes an open-source reference driver
56	   ([`MicrochipTech/oa-tc6-lib`](https://github.com/MicrochipTech/oa-tc6-lib),
57	   §References) small enough to run on an Arduino — the candidate base for both
58	   ends here.
59	3. **Minimal L2 framing** — the MAC-PHY only transmits *valid Ethernet frames*,
60	   so the host prepends a fixed 14-byte Ethernet header (dest MAC, src MAC,
61	   ethertype) to the payload. For this link the MACs are hardcoded and a custom
62	   ethertype carries the existing frame formats verbatim:
63	   - fretboard → marvin: the 17-byte data-stream frame (see fretboard SPEC).
64	   - marvin → fretboard: the 1-byte button bitmask.
65	
66	   17 B + 14 B header = 31 B → a single chunk. The 1-byte command likewise. The
67	   existing UART framing (`0x03 … 0xFC`, `sample_seq`, etc.) can ride unchanged
68	   inside the Ethernet payload, so higher layers don't need to know the
69	   transport changed.
70	
71	## 4. Resource budget — fretboard (PIC32CM6408PL10048, 64 KB flash / 8 KB SRAM)
72	
73	Estimates; static allocation only (no malloc), per project rule.
74	
75	| Resource | Estimate | Notes |
76	|---|---|---|
77	| Flash | ~6–10 KB | OA TC6 lib (~4–8 KB) + SPI glue + L2 framing. Reclaim the UART data path if the UART link is fully retired. |
78	| SRAM | ~1–2 KB | A couple of chunk buffers + one TX/RX frame buffer. |
79	| SERCOM | 1 (SPI master) | A free SERCOM alongside SERCOM1 (still UART for now). |
80	| GPIO | 2–3 | `CS_N`, `IRQ_N` (ext-int), reset. |
81	| CPU | negligible | One chunk per 240 Hz tick, interrupt-driven off `IRQ_N`; the TC0 ISR stays lean. |
82	
83	SPI clock: SERCOM SPI master maxes at GCLK/2 ≈ **12 MHz** on the 24 MHz part
84	(not the chip's 25 MHz ceiling) — irrelevant for this data rate.
85	
86	Everything fits comfortably inside 64 KB / 8 KB.
87	
88	## 5. marvin side
89	
90	marvin runs **bare-metal (no Linux)**, so it does *not* get a free netdev — it
91	needs its own TC6 driver. The upside: a **single portable `oa_tc6` layer shared
92	between marvin (Cortex-A5) and fretboard (Cortex-M0+)**, which is itself a tidy
93	demonstration that the OPEN Alliance SPI driver scales across the family. marvin
94	resources are not a concern.
95	
96	## 6. PoDL — "dumb" (no negotiation)
97	
98	PoDL is **not in the LAN8651** — the MAC-PHY only moves data. PoDL is external
99	coupling circuitry around the pair, and it is **transparent to both MCUs** (zero
100	firmware footprint, the §4 budget is unaffected):
101	
102	- **PSE side (marvin):** a fixed-voltage source + coupling inductors that inject
103	  DC onto the pair.
104	- **PD side (fretboard):** coupling inductors to extract DC + a regulator down to
105	  the PIC32CM rail.
106	- **Dumb / unmanaged:** no SCCP classification or negotiation handshake. Fixed
107	  supply voltage, fixed point-to-point pair, decided at design time. Simplest
108	  PoDL form; appropriate because the topology is fixed and both ends are ours.
109	
110	Microchip has PoDL reference designs that pair with the LAN865x EVBs, which also
111	helps the demonstration story.
112	
113	## 7. Topology: point-to-point vs PLCA multidrop
114	
115	Recommended direction: **enable PLCA from the start** rather than strict
116	point-to-point. A 2-node PLCA bus already demonstrates the headline T1S feature
117	(collision-free multidrop on one pair) at no extra cost, and leaves the door
118	open to a second node sharing the same pair and power. Open until decided.
119	
120	## 8. Open items
121	
122	- PLCA vs pure point-to-point (see §7) — lean PLCA.
123	- PoDL supply voltage and the PD-side regulator topology (BOM, not firmware).
124	- Custom ethertype value and the two hardcoded MAC addresses.
125	- Whether to keep the UART link as a fallback during bring-up or cut over
126	  outright (affects whether SERCOM1's data path is reclaimed — §4).
127	- Magnetics-free coupling component selection on the Sensor-LCD5 PCB.
128	
129	## References
130	
131	- **OA TC6 driver (candidate base, both ends):**
132	  [`MicrochipTech/oa-tc6-lib`](https://github.com/MicrochipTech/oa-tc6-lib) —
133	  Microchip's open-source OPEN Alliance TC6 (10BASE-T1x MAC-PHY Serial
134	  Interface) library: SPI chunk protocol + control transactions, used as the
135	  shared portable layer (§3, §5).
136	- LAN8650/1 (LAN8651B1) datasheet — 10BASE-T1S MAC-PHY Ethernet Controller with
137	  SPI, on [Microchip online docs](https://onlinedocs.microchip.com/) /
138	  the LAN8651 product page.
139	- OPEN Alliance *10BASE-T1x MAC-PHY Serial Interface* specification (TC6), v1.1.
140
```
</details></tool-use>

1	# marvin — System Specification
2	
3	> **Read this first** for any non-trivial marvin task. The journal ([`journal.md`](journal.md)) is the running diary of decisions and work-in-progress; this spec is the durable description of *what marvin is*. When the two disagree, fix the spec.
4	
5	**Status:** in-progress draft. Sections that are settled are marked ✅; sections that depend on open architectural questions are marked 🚧 and link to the relevant entries in §9.
6	
7	---
8	
9	## 1. Purpose & scope
10	
11	### 1.1 What marvin is
12	
13	marvin is the firmware running on a **SAM9X75 Curiosity** board. Its job, in the guitar-playing-robot system, is to:
14	
15	1. Capture live HDMI video of a Guitar Hero / Rock Band game from a Nintendo Wii.
16	2. Run computer-vision note detection on the captured frames.
17	3. Decide *what* to play and *when* (chord grouping, fret-early timing, strum scheduling).
18	4. Send the corresponding fret/strum commands to the actuator controller (the **fretboard** MCU).
19	5. Provide an on-device operator UI (10.1″ LVDS panel + maxtouch capacitive touch) for live view, calibration, mode selection, logs.
20	6. Produce **reference data** — annotated frames + detector state — for off-board use (training low-fidelity detectors, side-by-side detector comparison, replay).
21	7. **Observe game state from the screen** — recognize current menu / song-select / gameplay / pause / score-summary contexts via CV, expose high-level control verbs ("start single-player playthrough of song X", "advance menu", "exit to main menu") that translate into fret/strum command sequences sent through the same fretboard link.
22	
23	In short: marvin is the runtime brain *and* the reference-detector data source for the project.
24	
25	### 1.2 What marvin is *not*
26	
27	- **Not the actuator.** Physical fret/strum GPIO drive lives on the fretboard MCU. marvin sends bitmask commands; fretboard converts them to button presses.
28	- **Not a sensor / detection-only device.** marvin owns timing and command emission. It is not a passive vision peripheral that some other host orchestrates.
29	- **Not a router for a PC.** The previous PC-based architecture (Elgato + OpenCV + USB to a Pi) is retired. marvin replaces the PC in the runtime path.
30	- **Not a generic camera platform.** The video source is a fixed HDMI signal from a game console. Suggestions like "just use a USB webcam" or "output to HDMI directly" miss the point.
31	
32	### 1.3 North-star one-paragraph summary
33	
34	A SAM9X75 captures Wii HDMI video at 720×480 / 1280×720 @ 60 Hz over a TC358743 → MIPI CSI-2 → ISC path into DDR (BGR888 packed, 3 B/pixel). It runs reference-quality CV note detection on those frames, fuses with ADC-based detection ingested from a fretboard MCU over a FLEXCOM2 UART link, schedules chord/strum commands through a low-latency timing pipeline, sends commands back to the fretboard, drives an operator UI on a 10.1″ LVDS panel, and exports a compressed reference-data stream so that lighter-weight detectors (today: fretboard's phototransistors; future: an Edge AI MCU) can be trained against marvin's ground truth.
35	
36	### 1.4 What's done, what's next
37	
38	| Subsystem | Status |
39	|---|---|
40	| HDMI capture (TC358743 → CSI-2 → ISC → DDR, BGR888 packed) | ✅ working at 480p60 and 720p60. See [`capture_pipeline.md`](capture_pipeline.md). |
