122	
123	### 2.2 Who owns what
124	
125	| Concern | Owner | Notes |
126	|---|---|---|
127	| HDMI capture into memory | marvin | TC358743 + CSI-2 + ISC; 720×480 / 1280×720 @ 60 Hz, BGR888 packed (3 B/pixel). |
128	| Reference-quality CV note detection | marvin | Ground truth; multiple algorithms may coexist on the bus. |
129	| ADC-based note detection | fretboard → marvin | fretboard scans 5 phototransistors @ 240 Hz, streams raw values; marvin runs the detector logic. |
130	| Detector-state fusion / arbitration | marvin | One canonical detector-state bus; the active source feeds the timing pipeline. |
131	| Chord-window FIFO + strum scheduling | marvin | Open Q4: stays on marvin (centralized) vs migrates to fretboard. Default: marvin. |
132	| Fret/strum GPIO output | fretboard | Open-drain pin drive only; receives a bitmask over UART. |
133	| Operator UI (live view, calibration, modes, logs) | marvin | 10.1″ LVDS + maxtouch. Open Q5: Legato vs custom. |
134	| Reference-data recording & export | marvin | Compressed/derived format; transport TBD (open Q1/Q2). |
135	| Game-state observation (menu / song-select / gameplay / pause / score) | marvin | CV on captured frames; emits typed game-state events on its own bus. §4.8. |
136	| Game catalog + menu metadata (song list, menu graph, recognized icons) | marvin | Compile-time tables and/or SD-card JSON. Drives the recognizer and the navigator. §4.8. |
137	| High-level game control (e.g., "start single-player song X") | marvin | Translates verbs into fret/strum sequences sent over the same fretboard link as gameplay commands. §4.8. |
138	| Calibration / tuning UI authoring | dev PC (fret-tuner) | Optional; not required at runtime. Open Q7: long-term fate. |
139	| Training data ingest / replay analysis | dev PC | Off-band consumer of marvin's reference-data export. |
140	
141	### 2.3 Data flow at a glance
142	
143	1. **Frame ready** — ISC writes a BGR888 packed frame to DDR; the video task notifies subscribers.
144	2. **CV detect** — one or more CV detectors read the frame and emit detector-state events.
145	3. **ADC ingest** — a UART task receives raw ADC samples from the fretboard and runs an ADC detector that emits detector-state events on the same bus.
146	4. **Arbitrate** — the timing pipeline picks the active detector (or fuses), maintains the chord-accumulation window, and pushes finished chords onto its FIFO.
147	5. **Schedule** — the FIFO emits fret-assert and strum-pulse commands at the correct ticks.
148	6. **Send** — commands are encoded and transmitted to the fretboard over UART.
149	7. **Display** — the captured frame is composited with overlays (sensor crosshairs, detector outputs, chord state, latency markers) and shown on the LVDS panel.
150	8. **Record** (optional) — when recording is enabled, a derived/compressed reference-data record (frame epoch + detector state + raw ADC + emitted commands) is buffered and exported via the chosen transport.
151	
152	### 2.4 Latency budget (target, end-to-end)
153	
154	| Stage | Budget | Notes |
155	|---|---|---|
156	| HDMI source → DDR (capture) | ≤ 16.7 ms | One frame @ 60 Hz; bounded by capture pipeline. |
157	| Detect on frame | ≤ 16.7 ms | One frame budget for CV; ADC path is separate and faster. |
158	| Timing pipeline → command emit | latency dominated by `STRUM_DELAY_MS` (≈ 200 ms) — intentional, not waste; compensates for sensor placement above strike line. |
159	| UART command → fretboard GPIO | ≤ 5 ms | Short fixed-format frame at ≥ 115 200 Bd. |
160	| Total user-visible latency | ≈ 200–250 ms | Tunable via `STRUM_DELAY_MS`, set per-game by calibration. |
161	
162	The dominant fixed delay (`STRUM_DELAY_MS`) exists by design — the camera sees notes before they reach the strike line. Capture + detect + UART jitter is what we actually budget against.
163

169	
170	| Board | Role | Connection to marvin |
171	|---|---|---|
172	| **SAM9X75 Curiosity** | marvin host (CPU, DDR, peripherals, panel/touch ports) | — |
173	| **Waveshare HDMI → CSI-2 adapter** (TC358743) | HDMI → MIPI CSI-2 bridge | I²C (FLEXCOM8 TWI, PB4/PB5, 400 kHz, addr `0x0F`) for control; 2-lane CSI-2 RX for data; PC15 PWD, PC19 RESET (currently unused — software reset over I²C). |
174	| **Microchip 10.1″ 1280×800 LVDS panel + maxtouch** | Operator UI | LVDSC pair from XLCDC; I²C for maxtouch (existing Harmony driver). |
175	| **fretboard board** (PIC32CM6408PL10048) | Sensor + actuator MCU | FLEXCOM1 USART (marvin PA28 TX / PA29 RX ↔ fretboard SERCOM1 PB01 RX / PB00 TX, 500 000 Bd 8N1, ring-buffer mode). |
176	| **Wii guitar controller** | Physical input target | Open-drain GPIO on fretboard, not directly on marvin. |
177	| **(optional) dev PC** | Calibration / training-data ingest / replay viewer + operator console | SD card swap (primary), USB CDC for perf-log, and the FLEXCOM2 serial console (115 200 8N1, via an FTDI channel) for interactive control (§4.9). No runtime dependency. |

```text
41	/* Bound the RX wait so a missed notification can't wedge the parser; the

62	static StaticSemaphore_t s_rx_notify_buf;
63	
64	/* A UART has no enumeration step — the link is up once Initialize has armed
65	 * the peripheral. Kept so producers and the heartbeat path can gate sends. */
66	static volatile bool s_link_up;
67	
68	/* Asserted-mask snapshot: most recent byte accepted into the FLEXCOM1 TX ring.
69	 * Producer-side intent goes out on the same wire byte but may be overwritten
70	 * before it transmits if Send is called faster than the link services. The
71	 * PERF_REC_ACTUATOR record carries both. */
72	static volatile uint8_t  s_last_sent_byte;

74	/* Last send result + timestamp, snapshotted into the ACTUATOR record so the
75	 * host can read Send-to-ack latency. A ring-buffer Write copies the byte and
76	 * returns immediately, so "ack" is the enqueue instant. */
77	static volatile int32_t  s_last_ack_result;
78	static volatile uint64_t s_last_ack_ts_counter;

80	static void rx_event_handler(FLEXCOM_USART_EVENT event, uintptr_t context)
81	{
82	    (void)context;
83	    BaseType_t hpw = pdFALSE;
84	
85	    switch (event)
86	    {
87	        case FLEXCOM_USART_EVENT_READ_THRESHOLD_REACHED:
88	        case FLEXCOM_USART_EVENT_READ_BUFFER_FULL:
89	            (void)xSemaphoreGiveFromISR(s_rx_notify, &hpw);
90	            break;
91	        case FLEXCOM_USART_EVENT_READ_ERROR:
92	            /* Consume + clear the error status; the resync parser recovers
93	             * frame alignment on the next valid start/end pair. */
94	            (void)FLEXCOM1_USART_ErrorGet();
95	            (void)xSemaphoreGiveFromISR(s_rx_notify, &hpw);
96	            break;
97	        default:
98	            break;
99	    }
100	
101	    portYIELD_FROM_ISR(hpw);
102	}
103	
104	static bool send_one_byte(uint8_t mask)
105	{
106	    if (!s_link_up) { return false; }
107	
108	    uint8_t tx_byte = (uint8_t)(mask & 0x7F);
109	
110	    /* Ring-buffer Write copies the byte into the TX ring and returns the
111	     * count accepted; for a single byte this only fails if the TX ring is
112	     * full, which shouldn't happen at command rates. */
113	    if (FLEXCOM1_USART_Write(&tx_byte, 1u) != 1u)
114	    {
115	        LOG_WARN("FBL: TX ring full, byte dropped\r\n");
116	        return false;
117	    }
118	    PerfLog_EmitStamp(PERF_STAGE_FBL_SEND, 0u, (uint32_t)tx_byte);
119	
120	    s_last_sent_byte      = tx_byte;
121	    s_last_ack_result     = 0;
122	    s_last_ack_ts_counter = SYS_TIME_Counter64Get();
123	    PerfLog_EmitStamp(PERF_STAGE_CDC_WRITE_COMPLETE, 0u, 0u);
124	    return true;
125	}
126	
127	static void fretboard_link_task(void *param)
128	{
129	    (void)param;
130	
131	    LOG_INFO("FBL: fretboard link started (FLEXCOM1)\r\n");
132	
133	    uint8_t last_mask = 0u;
134	
135	    for (;;)
136	    {
137	        uint8_t mask;
138	        if (xQueueReceive(s_cmd_queue, &mask, pdMS_TO_TICKS(FBL_HEARTBEAT_MS)) == pdTRUE)
139	        {
140	            last_mask = mask;
141	        }
142	        else
143	        {
144	            mask = last_mask;
145	        }
146	
147	        (void)send_one_byte(mask);
148	    }
149	}
150	
151	/* Drain the FLEXCOM1 RX ring and emit one PERF_REC_FRETBOARD_RAW per parsed
152	 * 17-byte frame. Resync logic mirrors tools/ds_monitor.py: a frame is valid
153	 * only when buf[0]==0x03 AND buf[16]==0xFC; otherwise drop the leading byte
154	 * and retry alignment. The FSM-free buffered approach is easier to reason
155	 * about than a state machine and the frame is short. */
156	static void fretboard_rx_task(void *param)
157	{
158	    (void)param;
159	
160	    uint8_t  frame[DS_FRAME_LEN];
161	    size_t   filled = 0u;
162	    uint32_t parsed = 0u;
163	    uint32_t skipped_bytes = 0u;
164	
165	    for (;;)
166	    {
167	        if (FLEXCOM1_USART_ReadCountGet() == 0u)
168	        {
169	            (void)xSemaphoreTake(s_rx_notify, pdMS_TO_TICKS(FBL_RX_WAIT_MS));
170	            continue;
171	        }
172	
173	        size_t want = DS_FRAME_LEN - filled;
174	        size_t got  = FLEXCOM1_USART_Read(&frame[filled], want);
175	        if (got == 0u) { continue; }
176	        filled += got;
177	        if (filled < DS_FRAME_LEN) { continue; }
178	
179	        if (frame[0] != DS_START_BYTE || frame[DS_FRAME_LEN - 1u] != DS_END_BYTE)
180	        {
181	            /* Misaligned: drop one byte and shift, then loop to refill. */
182	            memmove(&frame[0], &frame[1], DS_FRAME_LEN - 1u);
183	            filled = DS_FRAME_LEN - 1u;
184	            skipped_bytes++;
185	            continue;
186	        }
187	
188	        uint16_t adc[FRET_COUNT];
189	        for (uint8_t i = 0u; i < FRET_COUNT; i++)
190	        {
191	            adc[i] = (uint16_t)frame[1u + i * 2u]
192	                   | (uint16_t)((uint16_t)frame[2u + i * 2u] << 8);
193	        }
194	
195	        /* seq: u32 LE at bytes 11-14, applied_mask: u8 at byte 15. */
196	        uint32_t fb_seq = (uint32_t)frame[11]
197	                        | ((uint32_t)frame[12] << 8)
198	                        | ((uint32_t)frame[13] << 16)
199	                        | ((uint32_t)frame[14] << 24);
200	        uint8_t  applied_mask = frame[15];
201	
202	        Video_FrameInfo info;
203	        Video_GetFrameInfo(&info);
204	        PerfLog_EmitFretboardRaw(adc, info.frame_count, fb_seq, applied_mask);
205	
206	        parsed++;
207	        if (parsed == 1u || (parsed % 240u) == 0u)
208	        {
209	            LOG_DEBUG("FBL: rx parsed=%u skipped=%u G=%u R=%u Y=%u B=%u O=%u\r\n",
210	                      (unsigned)parsed, (unsigned)skipped_bytes,
211	                      (unsigned)adc[0], (unsigned)adc[1], (unsigned)adc[2],
212	                      (unsigned)adc[3], (unsigned)adc[4]);
213	        }
214	
215	        filled = 0u;
216	    }
217	}
218	
219	void FretboardLink_Initialize(void)
220	{
221	    s_cmd_queue = xQueueCreateStatic(FBL_CMD_QUEUE_DEPTH,
222	                                     sizeof(uint8_t),
223	                                     s_cmd_queue_storage,
224	                                     &s_cmd_queue_buf);
225	    configASSERT(s_cmd_queue != NULL);
226	
227	    s_rx_notify = xSemaphoreCreateBinaryStatic(&s_rx_notify_buf);
228	    configASSERT(s_rx_notify != NULL);
229	
230	    /* Arm continuous RX: the ring fills from the FLEXCOM1 ISR; persistent
231	     * threshold notification wakes fretboard_rx_task each time a frame's
232	     * worth of bytes is available. */
233	    FLEXCOM1_USART_ReadCallbackRegister(rx_event_handler, 0u);
234	    FLEXCOM1_USART_ReadThresholdSet(FBL_RX_THRESHOLD);
235	    (void)FLEXCOM1_USART_ReadNotificationEnable(true, true);
236	
237	    s_link_up = true;
238	
239	    TaskHandle_t h = xTaskCreateStatic(fretboard_link_task,
240	                                       "FretLink",
241	                                       FBL_TASK_STACK_WORDS,
242	                                       NULL,
243	                                       FBL_TASK_PRIORITY,
244	                                       s_task_stack,
245	                                       &s_task_tcb);
246	    PerfLog_RegisterTaskForHighwater(PERF_TASK_FRETBOARD_LINK, h);
247	
248	    TaskHandle_t hr = xTaskCreateStatic(fretboard_rx_task,
249	                                        "FretRx",
250	                                        FBL_RX_TASK_STACK_WORDS,
251	                                        NULL,
252	                                        FBL_TASK_PRIORITY,
253	                                        s_rx_task_stack,
254	                                        &s_rx_task_tcb);
255	    PerfLog_RegisterTaskForHighwater(PERF_TASK_FRETBOARD_RX, hr);
256	}
257	
258	bool FretboardLink_IsConnected(void)
259	{
260	    return s_link_up;
261	}
262	
263	void FretboardLink_Send(uint8_t mask, uint8_t producer_id)
264	{
265	    if (s_cmd_queue == NULL) { return; }
266	    uint8_t v = (uint8_t)(mask & TIMING_BIT_VALID_MASK);
267	    /* Overwrite is strictly latest-wins: a newer producer's mask replaces
268	     * any unsent older one — keeps a stalled write from accumulating
269	     * stale chord state. */
270	    (void)xQueueOverwrite(s_cmd_queue, &v);
271	
272	    uint8_t strum_dir = 0u;
273	    if      (v & TIMING_BIT_STRUM_DOWN) { strum_dir = 1u; }
274	    else if (v & TIMING_BIT_STRUM_UP)   { strum_dir = 2u; }
275	
276	    PerfLog_EmitActuator(v, s_last_sent_byte, strum_dir, producer_id,
277	                         s_last_ack_result, s_last_ack_ts_counter);
278	}
```

```text
9	/* Fretboard link — FLEXCOM1 USART (ring-buffer) writer that ferries a 7-bit
10	 * GPIO bitmask to the fretboard MCU as a stream of single-byte messages, and
11	 * a parse task that drains the fretboard's 17-byte ADC frames off the RX ring
12	 * into PERF_REC_FRETBOARD_RAW records. Spec §4.4 actuator transport.
13	 * Initialize first among the actuator modules so the submit queue exists by
14	 * the time any producer task starts running. Call after SYS_Initialize so the
15	 * FLEXCOM1 peripheral is up.
16	 *
17	 * Producers — timing_pipeline today, manual_control during operator UI
18	 * mode, future game menu controller (spec §4.8) — all submit through
19	 * FretboardLink_Send and tag themselves with a perf_actuator_producer_t
20	 * id. The id rides on the PERF_REC_ACTUATOR record emitted per Send so
21	 * the host can see which producer owns the wire at any moment (mode-level
22	 * arbitration is invisible from the wire byte alone).
23	 *
24	 * Latest-wins semantics: a newer mask overwrites an unsent older one,
25	 * so a stalled USB write can't accumulate stale state. Mode-level
26	 * arbitration (which producer is allowed to submit when) lives one
27	 * layer up; the link stays dumb. */
28	
29	void FretboardLink_Initialize(void);
30	void FretboardLink_Send(uint8_t mask, uint8_t producer_id);
31	bool FretboardLink_IsConnected(void);
32	
33	#endif
```

```text
11	 * a parse task that drains the fretboard's 17-byte ADC frames off the RX ring
12	 * into PERF_REC_FRETBOARD_RAW records. Spec §4.4 actuator transport.
13	 * Initialize first among the actuator modules so the submit queue exists by
14	 * the time any producer task starts running. Call after SYS_Initialize so the
15	 * FLEXCOM1 peripheral is up.
16	 *
17	 * Producers — timing_pipeline today, manual_control during operator UI
18	 * mode, future game menu controller (spec §4.8) — all submit through
19	 * FretboardLink_Send and tag themselves with a perf_actuator_producer_t
20	 * id. The id rides on the PERF_REC_ACTUATOR record emitted per Send so
21	 * the host can see which producer owns the wire at any moment (mode-level
22	 * arbitration is invisible from the wire byte alone).
23	 *
24	 * Latest-wins semantics: a newer mask overwrites an unsent older one,
25	 * so a stalled USB write can't accumulate stale state. Mode-level
26	 * arbitration (which producer is allowed to submit when) lives one
27	 * layer up; the link stays dumb. */
28	
29	void FretboardLink_Initialize(void);
30	void FretboardLink_Send(uint8_t mask, uint8_t producer_id);
31	bool FretboardLink_IsConnected(void);

33	#endif
```

```text
104	static bool send_one_byte(uint8_t mask)
105	{
106	    if (!s_link_up) { return false; }
107	
108	    uint8_t tx_byte = (uint8_t)(mask & 0x7F);
109	
110	    /* Ring-buffer Write copies the byte into the TX ring and returns the
111	     * count accepted; for a single byte this only fails if the TX ring is
112	     * full, which shouldn't happen at command rates. */
113	    if (FLEXCOM1_USART_Write(&tx_byte, 1u) != 1u)
114	    {
115	        LOG_WARN("FBL: TX ring full, byte dropped\r\n");
116	        return false;
117	    }
118	    PerfLog_EmitStamp(PERF_STAGE_FBL_SEND, 0u, (uint32_t)tx_byte);
119	
120	    s_last_sent_byte      = tx_byte;
121	    s_last_ack_result     = 0;
122	    s_last_ack_ts_counter = SYS_TIME_Counter64Get();
123	    PerfLog_EmitStamp(PERF_STAGE_CDC_WRITE_COMPLETE, 0u, 0u);
124	    return true;
125	}
126	
127	static void fretboard_link_task(void *param)
128	{
129	    (void)param;
130	
131	    LOG_INFO("FBL: fretboard link started (FLEXCOM1)\r\n");
132	
133	    uint8_t last_mask = 0u;
134	
135	    for (;;)
136	    {
137	        uint8_t mask;
138	        if (xQueueReceive(s_cmd_queue, &mask, pdMS_TO_TICKS(FBL_HEARTBEAT_MS)) == pdTRUE)
139	        {
140	            last_mask = mask;
141	        }
142	        else
143	        {
144	            mask = last_mask;
145	        }
146	
147	        (void)send_one_byte(mask);
148	    }
149	}
150	
151	/* Drain the FLEXCOM1 RX ring and emit one PERF_REC_FRETBOARD_RAW per parsed
152	 * 17-byte frame. Resync logic mirrors tools/ds_monitor.py: a frame is valid
153	 * only when buf[0]==0x03 AND buf[16]==0xFC; otherwise drop the leading byte
154	 * and retry alignment. The FSM-free buffered approach is easier to reason
155	 * about than a state machine and the frame is short. */
156	static void fretboard_rx_task(void *param)
157	{
158	    (void)param;
159	
160	    uint8_t  frame[DS_FRAME_LEN];
161	    size_t   filled = 0u;
162	    uint32_t parsed = 0u;
163	    uint32_t skipped_bytes = 0u;
164	
165	    for (;;)
166	    {
167	        if (FLEXCOM1_USART_ReadCountGet() == 0u)
168	        {
169	            (void)xSemaphoreTake(s_rx_notify, pdMS_TO_TICKS(FBL_RX_WAIT_MS));
170	            continue;
171	        }
172	
173	        size_t want = DS_FRAME_LEN - filled;
174	        size_t got  = FLEXCOM1_USART_Read(&frame[filled], want);
175	        if (got == 0u) { continue; }
176	        filled += got;
177	        if (filled < DS_FRAME_LEN) { continue; }
178	
179	        if (frame[0] != DS_START_BYTE || frame[DS_FRAME_LEN - 1u] != DS_END_BYTE)
180	        {
181	            /* Misaligned: drop one byte and shift, then loop to refill. */
182	            memmove(&frame[0], &frame[1], DS_FRAME_LEN - 1u);
183	            filled = DS_FRAME_LEN - 1u;
184	            skipped_bytes++;
185	            continue;
186	        }
187	
188	        uint16_t adc[FRET_COUNT];
189	        for (uint8_t i = 0u; i < FRET_COUNT; i++)
190	        {
191	            adc[i] = (uint16_t)frame[1u + i * 2u]
192	                   | (uint16_t)((uint16_t)frame[2u + i * 2u] << 8);
193	        }
194	
195	        /* seq: u32 LE at bytes 11-14, applied_mask: u8 at byte 15. */
196	        uint32_t fb_seq = (uint32_t)frame[11]
197	                        | ((uint32_t)frame[12] << 8)
198	                        | ((uint32_t)frame[13] << 16)
199	                        | ((uint32_t)frame[14] << 24);
200	        uint8_t  applied_mask = frame[15];
201	
202	        Video_FrameInfo info;
203	        Video_GetFrameInfo(&info);
204	        PerfLog_EmitFretboardRaw(adc, info.frame_count, fb_seq, applied_mask);
205	
206	        parsed++;
207	        if (parsed == 1u || (parsed % 240u) == 0u)
208	        {
209	            LOG_DEBUG("FBL: rx parsed=%u skipped=%u G=%u R=%u Y=%u B=%u O=%u\r\n",
210	                      (unsigned)parsed, (unsigned)skipped_bytes,
211	                      (unsigned)adc[0], (unsigned)adc[1], (unsigned)adc[2],
212	                      (unsigned)adc[3], (unsigned)adc[4]);
213	        }
214	
215	        filled = 0u;
216	    }
217	}
218	
219	void FretboardLink_Initialize(void)
220	{
221	    s_cmd_queue = xQueueCreateStatic(FBL_CMD_QUEUE_DEPTH,
222	                                     sizeof(uint8_t),
223	                                     s_cmd_queue_storage,
224	                                     &s_cmd_queue_buf);
225	    configASSERT(s_cmd_queue != NULL);
226	
227	    s_rx_notify = xSemaphoreCreateBinaryStatic(&s_rx_notify_buf);
228	    configASSERT(s_rx_notify != NULL);
229	
230	    /* Arm continuous RX: the ring fills from the FLEXCOM1 ISR; persistent
231	     * threshold notification wakes fretboard_rx_task each time a frame's
232	     * worth of bytes is available. */
233	    FLEXCOM1_USART_ReadCallbackRegister(rx_event_handler, 0u);
234	    FLEXCOM1_USART_ReadThresholdSet(FBL_RX_THRESHOLD);
235	    (void)FLEXCOM1_USART_ReadNotificationEnable(true, true);
236	
237	    s_link_up = true;
238	
239	    TaskHandle_t h = xTaskCreateStatic(fretboard_link_task,
240	                                       "FretLink",
241	                                       FBL_TASK_STACK_WORDS,
242	                                       NULL,
243	                                       FBL_TASK_PRIORITY,
244	                                       s_task_stack,
245	                                       &s_task_tcb);
246	    PerfLog_RegisterTaskForHighwater(PERF_TASK_FRETBOARD_LINK, h);
247	
248	    TaskHandle_t hr = xTaskCreateStatic(fretboard_rx_task,
249	                                        "FretRx",
250	                                        FBL_RX_TASK_STACK_WORDS,
251	                                        NULL,
252	                                        FBL_TASK_PRIORITY,
253	                                        s_rx_task_stack,
254	                                        &s_rx_task_tcb);
255	    PerfLog_RegisterTaskForHighwater(PERF_TASK_FRETBOARD_RX, hr);
256	}
257	
258	bool FretboardLink_IsConnected(void)
259	{
260	    return s_link_up;
261	}
262	
263	void FretboardLink_Send(uint8_t mask, uint8_t producer_id)
264	{
265	    if (s_cmd_queue == NULL) { return; }
266	    uint8_t v = (uint8_t)(mask & TIMING_BIT_VALID_MASK);
267	    /* Overwrite is strictly latest-wins: a newer producer's mask replaces
268	     * any unsent older one — keeps a stalled write from accumulating
269	     * stale chord state. */
270	    (void)xQueueOverwrite(s_cmd_queue, &v);
271	
272	    uint8_t strum_dir = 0u;
273	    if      (v & TIMING_BIT_STRUM_DOWN) { strum_dir = 1u; }
274	    else if (v & TIMING_BIT_STRUM_UP)   { strum_dir = 2u; }
275	
276	    PerfLog_EmitActuator(v, s_last_sent_byte, strum_dir, producer_id,
277	                         s_last_ack_result, s_last_ack_ts_counter);
278	}
```

```text
205	/* PERF_REC_STRIP — variable-size BGR888 region of interest, kind-tagged.
206	 * Today's producers emit SENSING (row through the sensor patches) and
207	 * STRIKE (row through the strum trigger zone), each 240×32 once per ISC
208	 * frame; SNAPSHOT carries a full frame as a top-to-bottom sequence of
209	 * full-width bands sharing one frame_epoch (last band flags LAST).
210	 * Future kinds (SCORE, MINIMAP, etc.) plug into the same record type —
211	 * adding one is an enum entry plus a producer; no schema bump.
212	 *
213	 * Wire payload size is HDR + 12 B body + w*h*PERF_STRIP_BPP bytes,
214	 * tightly packed. The queue slot is sized to PERF_STRIP_MAX_BYTES; the
215	 * drain task computes the on-wire length from (w, h) and frames only
216	 * what's used. */
217	typedef enum
218	{
219	    PERF_STRIP_SENSING  = 0,
220	    PERF_STRIP_STRIKE   = 1,
221	    PERF_STRIP_SNAPSHOT = 2,
222	} perf_strip_kind_t;
223	
224	/* Strip flags byte (perf_rec_strip_t.flags). SNAPSHOT producers set LAST on
225	 * the final (bottom) band so the host knows the frame is complete without a
226	 * separate end marker. Zero for SENSING/STRIKE. */
227	#define PERF_STRIP_FLAG_LAST  0x01u
228	
229	#define PERF_STRIP_BPP        3u
230	
231	/* Wire-bound on the strip pixel-data size. Two stacked caps determine
232	 * the maximum payload a strip can carry:
233	 *
234	 *   1. Wire LEN field is u16 → max payload 65535 bytes
235	 *      → max pixel = 65535 − HDR(16) − BODY(12) = 65507
236	 *   2. UDPHS DMA single-transfer cap is
237	 *      DRV_USB_UDPHS_DMA_MAX_TRANSFER_SIZE × 64 KB
238	 *      (currently 2 × 64 KB = 128 KB; well above the LEN cap)
239	 *
240	 * The u16 LEN field is the binding constraint. Set at 65000 to land just
241	 * under it with a small margin. Producers may use any (w, h) shape as
242	 * long as w * h * PERF_STRIP_BPP <= PERF_STRIP_MAX_BYTES.
243	 *
244	 * Practical strip-size envelope (pixel area = w*h ≤ ~21666):
245	 *   720×30  640×33  480×45  320×64  290×72
246	 *
247	 * Buffer footprint scales with this:
248	 *   pool      = PL_STRIP_POOL_SIZE × (28 + PERF_STRIP_MAX_BYTES)
249	 *   sink ring = SINK_TX_RING_DEPTH × round_up_64(36 + PERF_STRIP_MAX_BYTES)
250	 * Together ~585 KB BSS at 65000; trivially fits in the 240 MB cached DDR.
251	 *
252	 * To go beyond u16 LEN, the wire format itself needs a schema break (LEN
253	 * → u32). Don't do that lightly — at 60 fps × 65 KB = ~3.9 MB/s, this cap
254	 * already lines up with what the wire can sustainably carry. */
255	#define PERF_STRIP_MAX_BYTES  65000u
```

```text
 * record-emit time) disambiguates within the frame.

 * fb_sample_seq and applied_mask are stamped by the fretboard itself and
 * carried on the wire: the sequence counter (one per fretboard tick) lets the
 * host reconstruct true sample order and detect frames dropped in transit,

 * this very scan — so sensor and actuator state are paired atomically at the
```

```text
10	/* Video pipeline: HDMI source → TC358743 bridge → CSI-2 → CSI2DC → ISC →
11	 * DDR → XLCDC HEO. The module owns its own FreeRTOS task; everything below
12	 * (tc358743, isc_capture, HEO bind/unbind, capture/display state machine)
13	 * runs inside that task except the frame-arrival notification which fires
14	 * from the ISC IRQ via xQueueSendFromISR.
15	 *
16	 * Capture and display are independent. CaptureEnable arms the bridge +
17	 * ISC chain when the source is locked; DisplayShow makes the HEO layer
18	 * visible at the configured window. You can run capture without display
19	 * (frames flow into DDR, BASE/UI fills the panel) or display without
20	 * capture (HEO shows whatever is in the framebuffer — possibly stale).
21	 *
22	 * Defaults at Initialize: capture disabled, display hidden, window
23	 * unset. Layout is app policy — DisplayShow is a no-op until the
24	 * caller has set a window with Video_SetWindow. */
25	
26	void Video_Initialize(void);
27	
28	/* Capture chain control. ENABLE: arm ISC + bridge stream when source
29	 * is locked, re-arm on every lost/regain cycle. DISABLE: stop ISC +
30	 * stream and stay off regardless of lock state. */
31	void Video_CaptureEnable(void);
32	void Video_CaptureDisable(void);
33	
34	/* Display layer control. SHOW: HEO visible, BASE DISCEN cleared under
35	 * the HEO rect (saves DDR read bandwidth). HIDE: HEO disabled, BASE
36	 * owns full panel. Independent of capture state. */
37	void Video_DisplayShow(void);
38	void Video_DisplayHide(void);
39	
40	/* Destination rect on the 1280×800 panel. dst_w/dst_h matching the
41	 * source frame size → 1:1, scaler bypassed. Otherwise HEO bilinear
42	 * scaler engages and stretches to fill the rect. The rect must fit
43	 * within the panel. Takes effect on the next display bind (next
44	 * DisplayShow call, or when capture/lock state changes). */
45	void Video_SetWindow(uint32_t x, uint32_t y, uint32_t dst_w, uint32_t dst_h);
46	
47	/* Frame metadata delivered to subscribers on every captured frame. */
48	typedef struct
49	{
50	    void    *buffer;          /* pointer to most-recent complete frame in DDR */
51	    uint32_t frame_count;     /* monotonic since last ISC start */
52	    uint16_t width;
53	    uint16_t height;
54	    uint16_t bytes_per_pixel;
55	} Video_FrameInfo;
56	
57	/* Subscribe a queue to frame-ready events. The video module sends a
58	 * Video_FrameInfo from the ISC frame-done IRQ via xQueueSendFromISR
59	 * each time a frame completes to DDR — fanned out to every subscribed
60	 * queue. Create the queue with:
61	 *   QueueHandle_t q = xQueueCreate(N, sizeof(Video_FrameInfo));
62	 *
63	 * Per-subscriber depth chooses the back-pressure policy. Depth 1 means
64	 * "process most recent frame, drop the rest" — when a frame arrives and
65	 * the queue is full, the IRQ's xQueueSendFromISR returns errQUEUE_FULL
66	 * and the frame is dropped for that subscriber. Deeper queues preserve
67	 * frames at the cost of memory and added latency. Each subscriber chooses
68	 * independently.
69	 *
70	 * The Video_FrameInfo.buffer pointer reflects the buffer that *just*
71	 * completed (one of the descriptor-ring slots). With NUM_BUFFERS > 2 a
72	 * subscriber can hold the pointer for multiple frame-times before the
73	 * ring laps it; with NUM_BUFFERS = 2 the buffer is overwritten on the
74	 * second-next frame.
75	 *
76	 * Returns false if the subscriber table is full. Calling with a queue
77	 * already in the table is a no-op success. Up to VIDEO_MAX_SUBSCRIBERS
78	 * concurrent subscribers (currently 4). */
79	bool Video_SubscribeFrames(QueueHandle_t q);
80	
81	/* Remove a queue from the subscriber list. Returns false if not found. */
82	bool Video_UnsubscribeFrames(QueueHandle_t q);
```

```text
12	/* Detector subsystem — see firmware/marvin/docs/spec.md §4.2.
13	 *
14	 * A detector is anything that turns observation data into a detector_state_t
15	 * event: cv_marvin_v1 reads captured video frames; adc_fretboard (future)
16	 * reads UART-streamed ADC samples from the fretboard MCU; off-board detectors
17	 * may feed state in over UART/Ethernet.
18	 *
19	 * Every detector publishes detector_state_t records onto a single FreeRTOS
20	 * queue (the "detector-state bus"). The timing pipeline (§4.4) is the sole
21	 * consumer in steady state; until it lands a stub task drains the queue so
22	 * producers don't block. */
23	
24	typedef enum
25	{
26	    DETECTOR_CV_MARVIN_V1  = 0,
27	    DETECTOR_ADC_FRETBOARD = 1,
28	} detector_id_t;
29	
30	/* Canonical record. Layout is fixed-width / naturally aligned / little-endian
31	 * because this is also the on-disk format for state.bin (spec §4.6.5). Do not
32	 * reorder fields without bumping the recording schema version. */
33	typedef struct
34	{
35	    uint32_t frame_epoch;     /* master sync token, spec §4.6.4 */
36	    uint64_t timestamp_us;    /* monotonic, marvin-local */
37	    uint8_t  detector_id;     /* detector_id_t */
38	    uint8_t  reserved[3];
39	    struct
40	    {
41	        uint8_t  pressed;     /* 0/1 hard call */
42	        uint16_t confidence;  /* 0..65535, detector-defined */
43	        uint16_t raw_value;   /* detector-defined: ADC sample, pixel mean, etc. */
44	    } fret[FRET_COUNT];
45	} detector_state_t;
46	
47	/* Brings up the detector-state bus queue, the cv_marvin_v1 detector task,
48	 * and (for now) a stub consumer. All detectors start disabled; the app
49	 * must Detector_Enable() each one it wants publishing. Active selection
50	 * defaults to DETECTOR_CV_MARVIN_V1 for symmetry but is independent of
51	 * enabled-state. Call after Video_Initialize so the video frame queue
52	 * can be subscribed to from inside cv_marvin_v1. */
53	void Detector_Initialize(void);
54	
55	/* Producers post records here; consumers (timing pipeline, eventually) read
56	 * them. Returns NULL until Detector_Initialize has run. */
57	QueueHandle_t Detector_BusQueue(void);
58	
59	/* Per-detector enable: controls whether a detector publishes records onto
60	 * the bus. Multiple detectors may be enabled simultaneously — recording
61	 * (§4.6) snoops everything for side-by-side training data. Disabled
62	 * detectors still consume their input (frames, ADC samples) so input
63	 * queues don't back up; they just don't emit. Bit operations are atomic
64	 * on aligned 32-bit reads; writes use a critical section. */
65	void Detector_Enable(detector_id_t id);
66	void Detector_Disable(detector_id_t id);
67	bool Detector_IsEnabled(detector_id_t id);
68	
69	/* Active selector: which detector's records the timing pipeline (§4.4)

71	 * enabled. The timing pipeline is responsible for filtering by
72	 * detector_id when it lands; for M1 this is a held setting only. */
73	void          Detector_SetActive(detector_id_t id);
```

```text
} perf_rec_type_t;
/* PERF_REC_ACTUATOR — emitted on every FretboardLink_Send call (i.e. on
 * intent), one record per call. Closes the gap between TIMING.publish_mask
 * (intent on the timing pipeline side) and FBL_SEND STAMP (a byte hit the
 * USB DMA): with multiple producers (timing_pipeline, manual_control, future
 * game_state_controller per spec §4.8), the wire byte alone doesn't say
 * who asserted what.
 *
 * intended_mask: what the producer asked for this Send (low 7 bits).
 * asserted_mask: what's currently held on the link (last byte queued).
 * strum_dir: from the bit pattern (0=none, 1=down, 2=up).
 * producer_id: perf_actuator_producer_t — the arbitration signal that's
 *              invisible on the wire today.
 * last_ack_*:  most recent CDC_WRITE_COMPLETE result and timestamp,
 *              snapshotted at Send-time so the host can compute transport-
 *              side latency without joining FBL_SEND/CDC_WRITE_COMPLETE
 *              stamps (still useful, but redundant for the common case). */
typedef enum
{
    PERF_ACTUATOR_PRODUCER_NONE   = 0,
    PERF_ACTUATOR_PRODUCER_TIMING = 1,
    PERF_ACTUATOR_PRODUCER_MANUAL = 2,
} perf_actuator_producer_t;
```

```text
4	#include <stdint.h>
5	#include <stdbool.h>
6	
7	/* Timing pipeline — spec §4.4. Consumes detector_state_t records from the
8	 * detector-state bus (filtered by Detector_GetActive()), runs the chord-
9	 * window + strum-scheduling state machine ported from
10	 * tools/fret-tuner/actuator.py, and submits a 7-bit GPIO bitmask via
11	 * FretboardLink_Send. One of several possible producers — game menu
12	 * control (spec §4.8) and manual test inputs share the same submit API.
13	 *
14	 * Bit layout matches firmware/fretboard/cmd_receive.h:
15	 *   bit 0 = green   bit 1 = red    bit 2 = yellow
16	 *   bit 3 = blue    bit 4 = orange bit 5 = strum-down bit 6 = strum-up
17	 *
18	 * Time base is detector frame timestamps, not wall clock — replay-
19	 * deterministic and frees the task to advance only when state changes
20	 * (with a periodic timeout for between-frame strum-pulse expiries). */
21	
22	#define TIMING_BIT_GREEN       (1u << 0)
23	#define TIMING_BIT_RED         (1u << 1)
24	#define TIMING_BIT_YELLOW      (1u << 2)
25	#define TIMING_BIT_BLUE        (1u << 3)
26	#define TIMING_BIT_ORANGE      (1u << 4)
27	#define TIMING_BIT_STRUM_DOWN  (1u << 5)
28	#define TIMING_BIT_STRUM_UP    (1u << 6)
29	#define TIMING_BIT_FRET_MASK   0x1Fu
30	#define TIMING_BIT_VALID_MASK  0x7Fu
31	
32	void TimingPipeline_Initialize(void);
33	
34	/* Output gate. Default: true. When false, the pipeline still advances
35	 * internal state but suppresses the FretboardLink_Send call so a peer
36	 * producer (manual_control today, future game-state controller §4.8) can
37	 * own the wire. Internal state stays current so the next advance() after
38	 * re-enable republishes the right mask without a stale frame. */
39	void TimingPipeline_SetEnabled(bool enabled);

41	#endif
```

30	| 2026-06-14 | **Full-frame snapshot capture = on-demand host→device perf-log command (`PERF_CMD_SNAPSHOT`, id 0x02) that streams the current frame back as banded `STRIP` records (new kind `PERF_STRIP_SNAPSHOT`=2).** First step toward the M9 gameplay engine (spec §4.8): get real GH3 screens off the device so screen/number/letter detection can be prototyped offline. `perf_log_rx.c` latches the request; the perf-drain task copies the live frame once into a static 1280×720×3 staging buffer (coherent — the 4-deep nocache ring laps in ~50 ms, less than the ~0.4–1 s emit), then writes full-width horizontal bands (≤ `PERF_STRIP_MAX_BYTES`, ~30 rows @480p / ~16 @720p) **directly via `PerfLogSinkCdc_WriteFramed`, bypassing the 6-slot strip pool** (which would drop most of 16–45 bands) and naturally paced by the wire. The final band sets `PERF_STRIP_FLAG_LAST` (a repurposed strip `reserved[0]`); host groups bands by `frame_epoch` and finalizes on LAST. Snapshot emit is **not** gated by the STRIP type mask — the command is the request. Schema bumped 4 → 5 (firmware + `tools/marvin-perf` in lockstep). Host: `marvin-perf snapshot --port … --out …` reassembles and saves `.bgr` + `.json` sidecar (+ `.png` via Pillow). **Detection library to be built host-side in Python first, then proven algorithms ported to a firmware C `gameplay_engine` module — neither built yet (out of scope here).** | Reused the existing `STRIP` wire path + host→device command channel rather than inventing a new transport or waiting on M4 SD recording (not started): a snapshot is just a full frame sliced into bands the host decoder already understands `(x,y,w,h,kind)`. One USB cable, scriptable. Drain-task + staging-copy chosen over the strip pool to guarantee a tear-free frame and zero drops without resizing the pool. Full-resolution (not downsampled) because the point is OCR/glyph analysis of fixed GH3 assets. Brief (~0.4–1 s) drain-task monopolization is acceptable for an on-demand debug capture; a dedicated low-prio task is a possible later refinement. |

32	| 2026-06-11 | **NAND programming from macOS = u-boot RAM-loaded over JTAG, as a PMECC-aware flasher; the boot region needs a hand-prepended PMECC header.** New flow in [`openocd/program-nand.{sh,cfg,md}`](../openocd/program-nand.md): the init-and-stop at91bootstrap brings up DDR (as `load-ram`), then we `load_image` the at91bootstrap + `harmony.bin` + `u-boot.bin` into DDR and jump to u-boot; u-boot's `atmel_nand` (`nand erase`/`nand write`) burns NAND with PMECC. Built `u-boot.bin` from `sam9x75_curiosity_pro_nandflash_defconfig` (macOS: `gmake`, OpenSSL via the **environment** so dtc's bundled-libfdt include isn't clobbered). **Validated on hardware: marvin boots standalone from NAND** (RomBOOT → at91bootstrap copies `0x100000` from `0x40000` → marvin runs, HDMI captured). | Closes the 2026-06-09 "macOS-native NAND is Phase-2 R&D" item. OpenOCD's `at91sam9` NAND driver can't do PMECC, so it can't write a bootable boot region; u-boot's driver uses the same PMECC IP and its DT (hw ECC, **8-bit/512, eccOffset 152** = `oobsize − 8·13`) matches both the chip's ONFI (`nand info`: 4096/256/8/512) and the at91bootstrap header generator — so `nand write` is RomBOOT-correct. **Two non-obvious gotchas, both bench-found:** (1) The SAM9X7 ROM reads page 0 *without ECC* expecting a NAND header — 52 copies of a 32-bit word, code at offset `0xD0` (DS60001813D p.159/162). SAM-BA's `writeboot` synthesizes this; a plain `nand write` does not, so headerless writes give RomBOOT-only (no boot). Fix: prepend the header with `binaries/make-pmecchead.sh` (wraps at91bootstrap `addpmecchead.py`) using the **real** chip params → word `0xc2605007`; *not* that script's SAM9X7 defaults (2048/64/4), which don't match this board. (2) u-boot's default `bootcmd` reads the empty kernel partition into `0x22000000`/`0x21000000`; a 3 s autoboot overwrites staged blobs with `0xff` before you can program. Fix: stage into `0x21100000`/`0x21200000` (outside its read windows) and stop autoboot on connect. QSPI path still SAM-BA (no OpenOCD driver). |

46	| 2026-05-29 | Strip queue uses 1-byte slot indices into a static `s_strip_pool[depth+2]` instead of pass-by-value `perf_rec_strip_t` items. | FreeRTOS queues are pass-by-value: every `xQueueSend`/`xQueueReceive` does `memcpy(slot, src, item_size)` inside a critical section (interrupts disabled). At `sizeof(perf_rec_strip_t) = 23-61 KB`, that was 38-100 µs of interrupts-off time per queue op × ~240 ops/s. Pool-and-index pattern moves the pixel data into a static pool indexed by 1-byte handles; queue ops drop to 1 µs critical sections. Same total BSS footprint (eliminates the producer's `static r;` and drain's `static s_strip_drain;` — pool size matches old "queue + 2 staging" footprint). Distinct from the gameplay note-detection path: a video-frame consumer (not a detector) emits typed game-state events on `xGameStateQueue`, and a controller layer translates verbs ("start single-player song X") into fret/strum sequences sent over the same fretboard link | Want marvin to drive whole-session play, not just notes once gameplay starts. Separating its bus from `xDetectorStateQueue` keeps `detector_state_t` narrow per the 2026-05-20 multi-detector decision. Per-game catalog (menu graph + song list) is metadata kept on marvin. Default arbitration with timing pipeline: mutually exclusive — controller runs only outside `gameplay` state. Phasing: M9 observer-only, M10 control. Open: recognizer algorithm (Q10), arbitration boundary (Q11). |

Likely momentary (active-packet indicator, not stream-on flag). CSI_ERR=0 and HLT=0 consistently. Phase 5 frames-in-memory confirmed the chain works regardless.

107	**Carried into future sessions:**

109	- **`vApplicationStackOverflowHook` is a silent infinite-loop.** ([freertos_hooks.c:62-76](../default/src/config/default/freertos_hooks.c#L62-L76)) MCC's default is `taskDISABLE_INTERRUPTS()` then `for (;;)`. An actual overflow is indistinguishable from any other freeze on hardware. Patch the hook to emit a `LOG_ERR` line naming the offending task before the spin (carefully — the stack is already corrupt, so the hook should avoid using locals or large stack frames). Already nearly bit us once: 2026-05-21 freeze in `open_cdc()` was first misdiagnosed as a stack overflow because we had no visibility into actual stack usage of the FBL task. (HWM/RUNTIME records reach the host now post-2026-05-29 work, so we have *steady-state* stack visibility — but a real overflow still freezes silently.)
110	
111	- **Legato `LE_MEMORY_MANAGER_SIZE` adequacy.** Legato has its own internal pool (`LE_MALLOC` per touch event in `leInput_InjectTouchDown`). With the manual-control surface adding 8 buttons and frequent press/release events during menu nav, confirm `legato_config.h` `LE_MEMORY_MANAGER_SIZE` has headroom for typical event bursts. Watch for Legato heap-exhaustion symptoms (silent dropped events, widget redraw glitches) once the UI is exercised on hardware.
112	
113	- **Single-screen attach assumption for `ui/manual_input`.** `screenHide_Screen0` deletes the root widget tree, taking the Composer-generated `Screen0_*` widget pointers with it. We bind callbacks once after the first `screenShow_Screen0`. If a second Legato screen is ever added, `ManualInput_Bind` must re-run inside that screen's show path (or whichever screen owns the manual-control widgets). Not an issue today — flagged for whenever the operator UI grows beyond Screen0.
114	
115	- ~~**Spec ↔ implementation drift on capture format.**~~ **Resolved 2026-06-01** in doc sweep: spec.md, capture_pipeline.md, and display_path.md all updated to reflect BGR888 packed (3 B/pixel, CSI2DC RMS=1), HEO layer (not OVR1), RGB\_888\_PACKED color mode, and `.region_nocache` framebuffer. Keyframe size corrected to 1.04 MB (720×480 × 3). README.md updated with project intro.
116	
117	- **MCC-file modifications maintenance risk.** A from-scratch MCC regen on 2026-05-15 confirmed **four** local modifications get clobbered. The 2026-05-20 USB-host regen added a fifth. Re-apply after every regen:
118	
119	  1. **`plib_csi.c` — `CSI_Analog_Init` refactor.** MCC emits per-lane HS-RX init inline with three bugs: Lane 1 in the 2-lane branch is missing the bit-rate write, Lane 2's lane-select code is `0x24` instead of `0x64`, and the 4-lane else-if branch skips Lane 1 entirely. Replace with the `csi_phy_hs_rx_init(lane_code, bit_rate)` helper and call it for lanes 0/1/2/3 from a flat `if (nlanes >= …)` chain.
120	
121	  2. **`plib_xlcdc.c` `XLCDC_EnableClocks` — `PMC_PLL_ACR`.** Set to datasheet-optimal `0x12023010` for the LVDSPLL with our 24 MHz reference (in the `fIN ∈ [20 MHz, 32 MHz]` band). Specifically: `LOOP_FILTER=0x12, LOCK_THR=0x2, UTMIBG=1, UTMIVR=1, CONTROL=0x10`. MCC's default emits a different (less-optimal) analog config (`LOOP_FILTER=0x1B, LOCK_THR=0x4, no UTMI bits`). Doesn't affect functional behavior in our use (50 Hz refresh works either way), but is the manufacturer-recommended jitter/lock optimum.
122	
123	  3. **`plib_csi2dc.c` `CSI2DC_Configure_VideoPipe` — `| CSI2DC_VPCFGR_RMS_1`.** Required by the RGB888-packed capture path: byte-stream packs 4 BGR pixels across 12 bytes per CSI-2 RMS spec (Table 49.27). Without it, capture writes wrong-format bytes and the display shows garbage. *(Earlier journal note claimed this was now MCC's default — incorrect; this regen confirmed MCC still emits without RMS_1.)*
124	
125	  4. **`drv_image_sensor.h` enum shim.** MCC's regen *deletes* this file when the image-sensor component is disabled. Restore the 30-line shim at `default/src/config/default/vision/drivers/image_sensor/drv_image_sensor.h` defining `DRV_IMAGE_SENSOR_RAW_BAYER…JPEG` and `DRV_IMAGE_SENSOR_8_BIT…40_BIT` enums (numeric values must match the original — `drv_isc.c` derives `bits_per_pixel = 4 - inputBits`). Without it, `drv_isc.c` and `configuration.h` won't compile.
126	
127	  5. **`initialization.c` `SYS_Initialize` — peripheral init order.** **(Hybrid board: the peripheral is now `FLEXCOM8_TWI_Initialize` (not FLEXCOM6) and there's no USB-host regen, but the MMU/AIC-before-peripherals concern still stands — verified intact on 2026-06-08: MMU/AIC run before TC0/FLEXCOM2/FLEXCOM8/XLCDC.)** The USB-host MCC regen (2026-05-20) reordered SYS_Initialize so that `TC0_CH0_TimerInitialize`, `FLEXCOM6_TWI_Initialize`, and `XLCDC_Initialize` run *before* `MMU_Initialize` and `AIC_INT_Initialize`. Symptom on hardware: TC358743 probe wedges on its first I²C write — `OSAL_SEM_Pend(transferDone, WAIT_FOREVER)` never returns because the FLEXCOM6 ISR never fires. (Display + capture totally dead; FBL heartbeat keeps printing because it doesn't depend on a peripheral interrupt.) Fix: move the `MMU_Initialize → AIC_INT_Initialize → WDT-disable` block back to *before* the TC0/FLEXCOM6/XLCDC inits, matching the pre-USB-regen order. After this revert, video came back immediately. Resolved on 2026-05-20.
128	
129	  6. **`FreeRTOSConfig.h` — `portCONFIGURE_TIMER_FOR_RUN_TIME_STATS` / `portGET_RUN_TIME_COUNTER_VALUE` macros + 64-bit counter type.** With `configGENERATE_RUN_TIME_STATS = 1` (set via `FREERTOS_GENERATE_RUN_TIME_STATS` MCC symbol), FreeRTOS expects the application to provide a free-running counter. MCC's FreeRTOS Harmony component does not expose a knob for an app-specific counter source. Append at the end of `FreeRTOSConfig.h` (just before `#endif`):
130	     ```c
131	     extern uint64_t SYS_TIME_Counter64Get(void);
132	     #define configRUN_TIME_COUNTER_TYPE             uint64_t
133	     #define portCONFIGURE_TIMER_FOR_RUN_TIME_STATS()
134	     #define portGET_RUN_TIME_COUNTER_VALUE()        SYS_TIME_Counter64Get()
135	     ```
136	     `SYS_TIME` is already initialised by Harmony before the scheduler starts, so the configure macro is a no-op. `SYS_TIME_Counter64Get` returns the full 64-bit TC0 CH0 counter; the matching `configRUN_TIME_COUNTER_TYPE = uint64_t` overrides FreeRTOS's `uint32_t` default so cumulative `ulRunTimeCounter` values don't wrap (uint32_t at 266 MHz wraps after ~16 s of accumulated CPU time across all tasks, which made percentages garbage almost immediately). Bare `extern` (rather than including a Harmony header) keeps `FreeRTOSConfig.h` consumable by low-level kernel sources that don't pull in `definitions.h`.
137	
138	  7. **`drv_usb_udphs_device.c` — multi-IRP DMA arming in completion ISRs.** Stock UDPHS device driver only programs the DMA channel in `IRPSubmit`'s queue-empty branch (line 1604+); IRPs appended to a non-empty queue link in (line 2273-2284 of patched file via `iterator->next = irp_t`) but never get armed for transmission. `Tasks_ISR_DMA` advances `irpQueue = irp->next` after firing the callback but does not re-program DMA hardware. Result: only one IRP per "queue idle" sequence ever transmits — the rest sit `STATUS_PENDING` forever.
139	
140	      Fix is additive (no refactor of working code): add a static helper `F_DRV_USB_UDPHS_DEVICE_ArmDmaForIrp` just before `DRV_USB_UDPHS_DEVICE_IRPSubmit`, mirroring the existing inline DMA-program block (~80 lines covering both DEVICE_TO_HOST and HOST_TO_DEVICE directions). Then add a call after the queue advance in **two** places:
141	
142	      - `Tasks_ISR_DMA` immediately after `endpointObj->irpQueue = irp->next; irp->callback(...)` — the normal DMA-completion path.
143	      - The ZLP-completion path inside `Tasks_ISR` (under "endpoint interrupt on a DMA capable endpoint, so it should be a ZLP"), same place: after queue advance.
144	
145	      Both call sites guarded by `if (endpointObj->irpQueue != NULL)`. Patch markers `/* PATCH: */` make the change findable after MCC regen. Helper carries the same cache-clean and DMA-program shape as the inline original, including the `__DSB(); __ISB();` barriers and the `SYS_CACHE_CleanDCache_by_Addr` for the IRP data buffer.
146	
147	      Without this patch, the lever-1 multi-IRP work (`queueSizeWrite=3`, `USB_DEVICE_CDC_QUEUE_DEPTH_COMBINED=5`) accepts writes but only ever transmits the first of any batch. With it, multi-IRP pipelining works as designed at the driver level. Patch is specific to Harmony USB v3.16.0 device driver; check whether future versions wire the post-completion arm and obviate the patch.
148	
149	  8. **`driver/input/drv_maxtouch.c` — bounded maXTouch init so an absent touch panel can't hang the whole system.** Stock `mxt_initialize()` does `while (1) { mxt_read_info_block(); if (!error) break; }`. With the display/maXTouch panel disconnected the info-block read never succeeds, so it spins forever — and because each `mxt_read_info_block()` allocates from the FreeRTOS heap (heap_1, no free), the retries leak until the heap is exhausted and the system hangs in `vApplicationMallocFailedHook`. This is exactly what blocked the JTAG load-to-RAM bring-up (fault landed in `DRV_MAXTOUCH_Tasks`, `xNextFreeByte`=40,944/40,960). Three-part fix: (a) `__mxt_read_reg` now propagates the real `DRV_I2C_WriteReadTransfer` result (`? 0 : -EIO`) instead of hardcoding `ret = 0`, so a NAK from an absent controller is detected at the *first* read and bails before the second, garbage-sized `OSAL_Malloc`; (b) `mxt_initialize` retries at most `MXT_INIT_MAX_ATTEMPTS` (10, 20 ms apart) then returns the error; (c) `DRV_MAXTOUCH_Tasks` `DEVICE_STATE_MXT_INITIALIZE` parks the driver in `DEVICE_STATE_ERROR` (not READY) on failure, so the rest of the system runs headless without touch. Syntax-checked clean with XC32 v4.60, then **validated on hardware (2026-06-08)**: with the display/maXTouch panel disconnected, marvin loaded via the JTAG load-to-RAM flow now boots *past* maXTouch init (driver → `DEVICE_STATE_ERROR`) and runs headless — PC samples land in `DRV_USB_UDPHS_DEVICE_IRPSubmit` / `USB_DEVICE_CDC_Read` (perf-log USB-CDC path) and advance across the codebase, instead of hanging at `vApplicationMallocFailedHook`. Re-apply after every maXTouch MCC regen.

152	  - ~~`plib_xlcdc.c` LVDSPLL multiplier~~ — MCC now emits the chosen `MUL/FRACR/DIVPMC` for our 50 Hz target once the XLCDC driver MCC config was set correctly. Manual override no longer needed.
153	  - ~~`plib_lvdsc.c` `LVDSC_CFGR.DEN_POL`~~ — Latest Harmony gfx library intentionally omits the DEN_POL field. File reverted to MCC default; not load-bearing.
154	  - ~~`initialization.c` `DRV_USB_VBUSPowerEnable` per-pin VBUS calls~~ — USB host removed on the Curiosity Hybrid (2026-06-08); VBUS enables deleted from `app.c`.
155	  - ~~`usb_host_cdc.c` `bInterfaceProtocol == 0`~~ — USB host stack removed on the Curiosity Hybrid (`598d370`); only applies to a host-capable board.
156	
157	  Recovery plan: re-apply all eight (small, self-contained diffs). Long-term options are (a) file MCC bugs, (b) shim into our own files, (c) live with periodic re-application.
158	
159	- **`log_csi_status` was removed** (Phase 5 restructure — tc358743 no longer auto-enables stream). If we ever want to re-query TC358743 CSI_STATUS/CSI_ERR bits, re-add the helper. The register addresses and masks are still defined in the file.

161	- **ISC_Capture framebuffer sized for max 1920×1080 × 2 (~16 MB)** — wastes DDR at our current 720×480 use, but trivial at 256 MB total DDR and gives headroom for different sources. Reconsider if DDR becomes tight later.
162	
163	- **Retry semantics on source loss.** `app_coordinate_capture` uses a `capture_attempted` flag to prevent retry spam. On unlock it resets, so the next lock triggers a fresh Configure+Start. Untested for fast lock/unlock cycles — if the Wii toggles power, watch for state-machine glitches.
164	
165	- **Frame counter wraps at UINT32_MAX.** `g_frame_count` is 32-bit; at 60 fps it wraps after ~2.3 years continuous run. Not an immediate issue.
166	
167	- **`TP_STRUM_DELAY_MS` likely needs to vary by difficulty.** 300 ms is the current default. Easy/Medium/Hard place notes higher up the highway with longer travel time, so the same delay may strike too early on slower difficulties. Open: per-difficulty preset, runtime-tunable from the manual-control surface, or auto-tuned from observed note-velocity. Defer until the game-state controller (spec §4.8) lands and difficulty is known to marvin.
168	
169	- **`derive_edges` press_count path not implemented.** Rising-edge detection currently uses `pressed` transitions (falling edge of `pressed` → release mask; rising edge → press mask). A more reliable approach would use a per-fret press_count exposed by the detector as a side channel — a press_count increment is unambiguous even on frames where `pressed` was already high. Blocked on the detector exposing press_count; wire it into `derive_edges` in `timing_pipeline.c` when available.
170	
171	- **T1S link transport — direction, not yet built.** Plan to replace the FLEXCOM2 USART fretboard link with **10BASE-T1S single-pair Ethernet + dumb PoDL** (LAN8651B1 MAC-PHY each end). System spec §6 + [`../../../docs/t1s-podl-link.md`](../../../docs/t1s-podl-link.md). marvin runs **bare-metal**, so it gets *no free netdev* — it needs its own OA TC6 SPI driver. Plan: a single portable `oa_tc6` layer shared with fretboard (Cortex-A5 + Cortex-M0+). `FretboardLink_{Initialize,Send,IsConnected}` stays the public API; only the transport beneath it swaps (SPI + TC6 chunk protocol + a 14-byte L2 header wrapping the existing 17-byte/1-byte frames). marvin resources are not a concern. PoDL is dumb (fixed voltage, no SCCP) and transparent to the MCU. Decide topology (PLCA vs p2p), ethertype/MACs, and UART-fallback-during-bring-up before code lands.

```text
1	# edge-ai — Design Specification
2	
3	> **Status:** running on hardware (2026-06-04). A 16-channel int8 StrumNet, distilled from marvin's hard-mode play across 5 songs, runs standalone on the fretboard PIC32CM — reads its own photosensors, drives the controller, plays hard reasonably well on the bench with marvin disconnected. Offline phases (data pipeline, training, int8 quantisation) and the on-device port are done; remaining work is play-quality polish and difficulty/timing coverage. See [rollout.md](rollout.md) for phase status, the [journal](journal.md) for current focus, and [review.md](review.md) for open questions, risks, and rejected alternatives.
4	
5	## 1. Purpose & scope
6	
7	A development effort to build a small ML model that takes the fretboard's 5-channel phototransistor ADC stream and emits the same 1-byte fret + strum bitmask that marvin's timing pipeline produces today. Once trained, validated, and deployed, it removes marvin from the runtime gameplay loop.
8	
9	This is intentionally an **offline-first development effort**. Almost all of the work — capture, label, train, validate, debug — happens on a dev PC against recorded marvin self-play data. The on-device deployment is the *last* phase, after the model has been proven offline.
10	
11	**In scope:**
12	
13	- Training-data plumbing: a new export mode in [tools/marvin-perf](../../marvin-perf/) that turns marvin self-play perf-log captures into labelled CSV.
14	- Host-side training, validation, and model artifacts.
15	- On-device runtime integration (**built**). The deployment target is the fretboard MCU (PIC32CM6408PL10048, M0+ @ 24 MHz) — see [runtime.md](runtime.md); the offline phases were MCU-agnostic and the target could have been revisited if the model size/shape demanded it, but the int8 model fits with large margin.
16	
17	**Out of scope:**
18	
19	- Replacing marvin as the *reference* detector. Marvin remains the source of truth for training and diagnostics.
20	- Game-state / menu navigation. The edge AI plays gameplay only; whole-session control still belongs to marvin (system [SPEC.md §4.8 of marvin spec](../../../firmware/marvin/docs/spec.md)).
21	- The fretboard-takeover fallback ([fretboard journal](../../../firmware/fretboard/docs/journal.md), 2026-06-02 entry). That mode runs `fret_button.c` standalone; the edge AI is a separate operating mode if/when it deploys to fretboard.
22	
23	## 2. Why now
24	
25	Two concrete pressures came out of the recent training-data work:
26	
27	### 2.1 Spatial mismatch between current label and ADC
28	
29	The current SensiML CSV exporter ([tools/marvin-perf/marvin_perf/exporters/sensiml_csv.py](../../marvin-perf/marvin_perf/exporters/sensiml_csv.py)) labels each fretboard ADC sample with `cv_marvin_v1`'s `pressed_mask`, broadcast forward by `frame_epoch`. But the two sensors look at different points on the screen:
30	
31	- `cv_marvin_v1` samples at `y = 311` ([detector/cv_marvin_v1.c](../../../firmware/marvin/default/src/detector/cv_marvin_v1.c)), above the strike line.
32	- The five phototransistors physically sit "above the TV strike line" ([fretboard SPEC.md](../../../firmware/fretboard/SPEC.md)), at a different (unverified) row than `y = 311`.
33	
34	Same falling note, different sensors, different times. Aligning them on `frame_epoch` bakes in a fixed offset that is only correct at one scroll speed. Fixing this in hardware is finicky and locks the system to a single mechanical layout.
35	
36	### 2.2 Strum timing missing from the AI's job
37	
38	Today's training pipeline emits per-fret pressed labels only. The chord window + +220 ms strum scheduler ([actuator/timing_pipeline.c:21,198,199](../../../firmware/marvin/default/src/actuator/timing_pipeline.c)) is real, non-trivial work that the AI is not being asked to learn. Whatever the AI replaces, the timing pipeline still has to live somewhere.
39	
40	The simplifying observation is that the model only needs to learn *when* to strum — not *which direction* — because alternating up/down is a human ergonomics constraint the controller doesn't enforce. That collapses 2 strum bits into 1 and halves the rare-class label density problem.
41	
42	## 3. Decisions locked
43	
44	| Decision | Why (one line) |
45	|---|---|
46	| **Output:** 6 bits — 5 fret bits + 1 collapsed strum bit. At the wire it's emitted as strum-down (bit 5) only; bit 6 is always 0. | Pulls strum timing into the AI; alternating up/down is a human ergonomic constraint the controller doesn't enforce. The collapse happens *at export time*, not in the recording — `PERF_REC_ACTUATOR` keeps both strum bits as captured so a future human-trainer corpus can preserve direction information for other uses. |
47	| **Supervision:** distillation against `PERF_REC_ACTUATOR.intended_mask` from marvin self-play. | Sidesteps spatial mismatch — labels are marvin's chosen byte, not a CV intermediate. |
48	| **Intended deployment target:** fretboard PIC32CM6408PL10048, M0+ @ 24 MHz. | Removes marvin from the gameplay loop; truly "edge". Offline phases are MCU-agnostic, so this can be revisited if the model demands more compute. |
49	| **Inputs at inference (v1):** the existing 5 ADC channels only. | Cheapest start; per-fret HW expansion deferred (see [review.md](review.md) Q1). |
50	| **Training corpus:** marvin self-play recordings only. | Simplest closure. AI inherits marvin's behavior — good and bad — see [review.md §risks](review.md#risks). |
51	
52	The key insight that makes this work: **distilling against marvin's commands dissolves the spatial-mismatch problem.** The label is the byte marvin chose with the +220 ms strum delay already baked in. The model just needs a wide enough causal window of ADC to learn whatever delay maps photo dip → strum, regardless of where the photoxistors physically sit. Mechanical alignment becomes a non-requirement.
53	
54	## 4. Document map
55	
56	| Doc | What's in it |
57	|---|---|
58	| [architecture.md](architecture.md) | Training-time and inference-time data flow; cadence; sanity-check that the shape addresses §2 |
59	| [training.md](training.md) | Exporter changes, CSV schema, capture protocol, model architecture |
60	| [model.md](model.md) | The actual network (StrumNet) layer by layer — design rationale, receptive field, params, int8 deploy path, limitations |
61	| [runtime.md](runtime.md) | On-device deployment (as built) — the two int8 inference modules (streaming / recompute), callback wiring, mode toggle, memory budget |
62	| [rollout.md](rollout.md) | Phased plan with explicit offline/hardware split, plus per-phase verification (offline + on-device port done) |
63	| [review.md](review.md) | Risks, open questions surfaced for reviewer pushback, and alternatives considered |
64
```

## Summary: T1S/10BASE-T1S Single-Pair Ethernet Planning — Complete Capture

I've conducted a thorough search across the repository. Here's what has been captured about T1S / single-pair Ethernet for the marvin ↔ fretboard link:

### **Primary Documentation**

**File: `/Users/gregmrozek/Projects/microchip/guitar-pic/docs/t1s-podl-link.md`**

This is the authoritative low-level engineering document (140 lines). Key sections:

- **Lines 1–11:** Status statement — "direction, not yet built." The link today is FLEXCOM2 UART (system spec M2). Nothing here is flashed yet.

- **Lines 13–26:** Why T1S here
  - Primary motivation: **PoDL** (Power-over-Data-Lines) — one twisted pair carries both data and the fretboard's power, eliminating separate power feed
  - Secondary: robustness/reach vs TTL UART on noisy/long cable runs
  - Multidrop headroom: 10BASE-T1S/PLCA supports up to 8 nodes on one pair
  - Demonstration goal: showcasing 10BASE-T1S + PoDL inside a larger Microchip system (SAM9X7 + LAN8651 + PIC32CM)
  - Bandwidth is **not** a motivation — existing 500 kbaud UART already carries ~4 KB/s payload with ~12× headroom

- **Lines 27–42:** Hardware choice: **LAN8651B1** (MAC-PHY integrating IEEE 802.3 Clause 4 MAC and 10BASE-T1S PHY)
  - Talks to host MCU over **SPI** using **OPEN Alliance TC6** ("10BASE-T1x MAC-PHY Serial Interface", v1.1) protocol
  - Hardware handles: line coding, PLCA/CSMA-CD media access, preamble/SFD, FCS (CRC32) generation/checking, on-wire framing, minimum-frame padding
  - SPI: LAN8651 is SPI client, SCLK up to 25 MHz. Pins: SDI, SDO, CS_N, SCLK, IRQ_N (active-low interrupt), reset

- **Lines 44–69:** Host MCU implementation layers (no TCP/IP stack needed):
  1. **SPI transport** — one SERCOM in SPI-master mode + GPIO for CS_N, IRQ_N (external interrupt), reset
  2. **OA TC6 chunk protocol** — only real "driver." Fixed-size chunks (default 64-byte payload + 4-byte header on TX / 4-byte footer on RX), credit-based flow control, separate control-transaction format for register read/writes
     - Reference driver: **[`MicrochipTech/oa-tc6-lib`](https://github.com/MicrochipTech/oa-tc6-lib)** (open-source, small enough for Arduino — candidate base for both fretboard and marvin)
  3. **Minimal L2 framing** — 14-byte Ethernet header (dest MAC, src MAC, ethertype)
     - Custom ethertype carries existing frame formats verbatim inside payload
     - fretboard → marvin: 17-byte data-stream frame
     - marvin → fretboard: 1-byte button bitmask
     - **17 B + 14 B header = 31 B → single chunk**

- **Lines 71–86:** Resource budget for **fretboard (PIC32CM6408PL10048, 64 KB flash / 8 KB SRAM)**
  - Flash: ~6–10 KB (OA TC6 lib + SPI glue + L2 framing; can reclaim UART data path if fully retired)
  - SRAM: ~1–2 KB (couple chunk buffers + one TX/RX frame buffer)
  - SERCOM: 1 (SPI master, separate from SERCOM1 which currently handles UART)
  - GPIO: 2–3 (CS_N, IRQ_N, reset)
  - CPU: negligible (one chunk per 240 Hz tick, interrupt-driven off IRQ_N)
  - SPI clock: SERCOM SPI master maxes at GCLK/2 ≈ 12 MHz on 24 MHz part (irrelevant for this data rate)

- **Lines 88–94:** marvin side
  - Runs **bare-metal** (no Linux), so **no free netdev** — needs its own TC6 driver
  - Plan: **single portable `oa_tc6` layer shared between marvin (Cortex-A5) and fretboard (Cortex-M0+)** — demonstrates the OPEN Alliance SPI driver scales across the family
  - marvin resources are not a concern

- **Lines 96–108:** PoDL — "dumb" (no negotiation)
  - **PoDL is NOT in the LAN8651** — MAC-PHY only moves data
  - PoDL is external coupling circuitry around the pair, transparent to both MCUs (zero firmware footprint)
  - PSE side (marvin): fixed-voltage source + coupling inductors inject DC onto pair
  - PD side (fretboard): coupling inductors extract DC + regulator down to PIC32CM rail
  - Dumb/unmanaged: no SCCP classification/negotiation, fixed supply voltage, fixed point-to-point pair, decided at design time
  - Microchip has PoDL reference designs that pair with LAN865x EVBs

- **Lines 113–118:** Topology decision: PLCA multidrop vs point-to-point
  - **Recommended: enable PLCA from the start** rather than strict point-to-point
  - 2-node PLCA bus demonstrates headline T1S feature (collision-free multidrop on one pair) at no extra cost
  - Leaves door open to second node sharing same pair and power
  - Open until decided

- **Lines 120–127:** Open items needing decision before implementation
  - PLCA vs pure point-to-point (§7)
  - PoDL supply voltage and PD-side regulator topology (BOM, not firmware)
  - Custom ethertype value and two hardcoded MAC addresses
  - Whether to keep UART link as fallback during bring-up or cut over outright
  - Magnetics-free coupling component selection on Sensor-LCD5 PCB

- **Lines 129–140:** References
  - OA TC6 driver: [`MicrochipTech/oa-tc6-lib`](https://github.com/MicrochipTech/oa-tc6-lib)
  - LAN8650/1 datasheet on Microchip online docs
  - OPEN Alliance *10BASE-T1x MAC-PHY Serial Interface* specification (TC6), v1.1

### **Protocol/Stack Decisions Made**

1. **Transport layer:** IEEE 802.3 Clause 4 MAC + 10BASE-T1S PHY via **LAN8651B1 MAC-PHY** (integrates both on one chip)
2. **Host↔MAC-PHY interface:** **OPEN Alliance TC6** v1.1 protocol over **SPI**
3. **Chunk format:** Default 64-byte payload + 4-byte header on TX / 4-byte footer on RX, credit-based flow control
4. **MAC-layer framing:** **Minimal L2** — 14-byte Ethernet header with hardcoded source/destination MACs and custom ethertype
5. **Application payload:** Existing frame formats ride unchanged (17-byte sensor stream + 1-byte command bitmask)
6. **Media access:** **PLCA** (Physical Layer Collision Avoidance) multidrop recommended over strict point-to-point

### **Hardware Chosen**

| Component | Spec |
|-----------|------|
| MAC-PHY IC | **LAN8651B1** — 10BASE-T1S, SPI interface, up to 25 MHz SCLK |
| fretboard side | 1 SERCOM in SPI-master mode, GPIO for CS_N / IRQ_N / reset |
| marvin side | 1 SERCOM in SPI-master mode, GPIO for CS_N / IRQ_N / reset |
| Power coupling | Fixed-voltage PSE on marvin side, capacitive/inductive coupling, PD regulator on fretboard side (transparent to MCU) |
| Single pair cable | TBD: magnetics-free coupling component on Sensor-LCD5 PCB |

### **Driver Repository Referenced**

**`MicrochipTech/oa-tc6-lib`** — https://github.com/MicrochipTech/oa-tc6-lib
- Open-source reference driver for OPEN Alliance TC6 SPI protocol
- Small enough for Arduino; candidate base for shared portable layer on both marvin (Cortex-A5) and fretboard (Cortex-M0+)

### **Node Addressing / Topology Planned**

- **Current:**  Point-to-point UART (marvin ↔ fretboard only)
- **Planned:** **2-node PLCA bus** (fretboard + future second sensor/guitar node sharing one twisted pair + PoDL power)
- **Hardcoded MACs:** Source/destination MAC addresses TBD (custom, not standard unicast)
- **Custom ethertype:** Value TBD (carries proprietary frame formats)
- **No DHCP/ARP/IP.** Static Layer 2 only.

```text
7	/* Timing pipeline — spec §4.4. Consumes detector_state_t records from the
8	 * detector-state bus (filtered by Detector_GetActive()), runs the chord-
9	 * window + strum-scheduling state machine ported from
10	 * tools/fret-tuner/actuator.py, and submits a 7-bit GPIO bitmask via

14	 * Bit layout matches firmware/fretboard/cmd_receive.h:
15	 *   bit 0 = green   bit 1 = red    bit 2 = yellow
16	 *   bit 3 = blue    bit 4 = orange bit 5 = strum-down bit 6 = strum-up
17	 *
18	 * Time base is detector frame timestamps, not wall clock — replay-
19	 * deterministic and frees the task to advance only when state changes
20	 * (with a periodic timeout for between-frame strum-pulse expiries). */
21	
22	#define TIMING_BIT_GREEN       (1u << 0)
23	#define TIMING_BIT_RED         (1u << 1)
24	#define TIMING_BIT_YELLOW      (1u << 2)
25	#define TIMING_BIT_BLUE        (1u << 3)
26	#define TIMING_BIT_ORANGE      (1u << 4)
27	#define TIMING_BIT_STRUM_DOWN  (1u << 5)
28	#define TIMING_BIT_STRUM_UP    (1u << 6)
29	#define TIMING_BIT_FRET_MASK   0x1Fu
30	#define TIMING_BIT_VALID_MASK  0x7Fu
31	
32	void TimingPipeline_Initialize(void);
33	
34	/* Output gate. Default: true. When false, the pipeline still advances
35	 * internal state but suppresses the FretboardLink_Send call so a peer
36	 * producer (manual_control today, future game-state controller §4.8) can
37	 * own the wire. Internal state stays current so the next advance() after
38	 * re-enable republishes the right mask without a stale frame. */
```

1	# marvin — System Specification
2	
3	> **Read this first** for any non-trivial marvin task. The journal ([`journal.md`](journal.md)) is the running diary of decisions and work-in-progress; this spec is the durable description of *what marvin is*. When the two disagree, fix the spec.
4	
5	**Status:** in-progress draft. Sections that are settled are marked ✅; sections that depend on open architectural questions are marked 🚧 and link to the relevant entries in §9.
6	
7	---
8	
9	## 1. Purpose & scope
10	
11	### 1.1 What marvin is
12	
13	marvin is the firmware running on a **SAM9X75 Curiosity** board. Its job, in the guitar-playing-robot system, is to:
14	
15	1. Capture live HDMI video of a Guitar Hero / Rock Band game from a Nintendo Wii.
16	2. Run computer-vision note detection on the captured frames.
17	3. Decide *what* to play and *when* (chord grouping, fret-early timing, strum scheduling).
18	4. Send the corresponding fret/strum commands to the actuator controller (the **fretboard** MCU).
19	5. Provide an on-device operator UI (10.1″ LVDS panel + maxtouch capacitive touch) for live view, calibration, mode selection, logs.
20	6. Produce **reference data** — annotated frames + detector state — for off-board use (training low-fidelity detectors, side-by-side detector comparison, replay).
21	7. **Observe game state from the screen** — recognize current menu / song-select / gameplay / pause / score-summary contexts via CV, expose high-level control verbs ("start single-player playthrough of song X", "advance menu", "exit to main menu") that translate into fret/strum command sequences sent through the same fretboard link.
22	
23	In short: marvin is the runtime brain *and* the reference-detector data source for the project.
24	
25	### 1.2 What marvin is *not*
26	
27	- **Not the actuator.** Physical fret/strum GPIO drive lives on the fretboard MCU. marvin sends bitmask commands; fretboard converts them to button presses.
28	- **Not a sensor / detection-only device.** marvin owns timing and command emission. It is not a passive vision peripheral that some other host orchestrates.
29	- **Not a router for a PC.** The previous PC-based architecture (Elgato + OpenCV + USB to a Pi) is retired. marvin replaces the PC in the runtime path.
30	- **Not a generic camera platform.** The video source is a fixed HDMI signal from a game console. Suggestions like "just use a USB webcam" or "output to HDMI directly" miss the point.
31	
32	### 1.3 North-star one-paragraph summary
33	
34	A SAM9X75 captures Wii HDMI video at 720×480 / 1280×720 @ 60 Hz over a TC358743 → MIPI CSI-2 → ISC path into DDR (BGR888 packed, 3 B/pixel). It runs reference-quality CV note detection on those frames, fuses with ADC-based detection ingested from a fretboard MCU over a FLEXCOM2 UART link, schedules chord/strum commands through a low-latency timing pipeline, sends commands back to the fretboard, drives an operator UI on a 10.1″ LVDS panel, and exports a compressed reference-data stream so that lighter-weight detectors (today: fretboard's phototransistors; future: an Edge AI MCU) can be trained against marvin's ground truth.
35	
36	### 1.4 What's done, what's next
37	
38	| Subsystem | Status |
39	|---|---|
40	| HDMI capture (TC358743 → CSI-2 → ISC → DDR, BGR888 packed) | ✅ working at 480p60 and 720p60. See [`capture_pipeline.md`](capture_pipeline.md). |
41	| Display path (DDR → XLCDC HEO → LVDSC → panel) | ✅ working, pillarboxed/letterboxed, per-frame pointer swap. See [`display_path.md`](display_path.md). |
42	| FreeRTOS scheduler, video task, OSAL I²C | ✅ landed. |
43	| Lightweight log shim, FreeRTOS analytics, task priorities | ✅ done. |
44	| CV detection pipeline | 🚧 M1 complete: `cv_marvin_v1` running on captured frames, `detector_state_t` bus active. No actuation path through detector yet. §4.2. |
45	| Fretboard link (FLEXCOM2 USART) | ✅ working; gameplay tested over the original USB CDC host link. Link rewired to a direct FLEXCOM2 UART for the Curiosity Hybrid board (no host-capable USB port); pending on-hardware re-validation. §4.3. |
46	| Timing pipeline (chord FIFO, strum) | ✅ working; end-to-end gameplay tested on Expert and Easy. §4.4. |
47	| Operator UI (Legato) | 🚧 Manual-control surface (8 buttons, Legato Composer) done; full calibration/log UI not started. §4.5, open Q5. |
48	| Reference-data recording & export (SD) | 🚧 SD recording not started. Perf-log USB CDC export (separate dev-tooling path) complete at 2.77 MB/s. §4.6, open Q1/Q2. |
49	| System services (config, time, watchdog) | 🚧 Partial: logging, FreeRTOS analytics, static task priorities done; config persistence and watchdog not started. §4.7. |
50	| Game-state awareness & high-level game control | 🚧 M9 Phases 1+2 firmware-complete (screen classifier + section-select/song readers; MPLAB build confirmed, pending hardware test). M9 Phase 3 (number/score readers) and M10 (controller/navigator) not yet started in firmware. §4.8. |

123	### 2.2 Who owns what
124	
125	| Concern | Owner | Notes |
126	|---|---|---|
127	| HDMI capture into memory | marvin | TC358743 + CSI-2 + ISC; 720×480 / 1280×720 @ 60 Hz, BGR888 packed (3 B/pixel). |
128	| Reference-quality CV note detection | marvin | Ground truth; multiple algorithms may coexist on the bus. |
129	| ADC-based note detection | fretboard → marvin | fretboard scans 5 phototransistors @ 240 Hz, streams raw values; marvin runs the detector logic. |
130	| Detector-state fusion / arbitration | marvin | One canonical detector-state bus; the active source feeds the timing pipeline. |
131	| Chord-window FIFO + strum scheduling | marvin | Open Q4: stays on marvin (centralized) vs migrates to fretboard. Default: marvin. |
132	| Fret/strum GPIO output | fretboard | Open-drain pin drive only; receives a bitmask over UART. |
133	| Operator UI (live view, calibration, modes, logs) | marvin | 10.1″ LVDS + maxtouch. Open Q5: Legato vs custom. |
134	| Reference-data recording & export | marvin | Compressed/derived format; transport TBD (open Q1/Q2). |
135	| Game-state observation (menu / song-select / gameplay / pause / score) | marvin | CV on captured frames; emits typed game-state events on its own bus. §4.8. |
136	| Game catalog + menu metadata (song list, menu graph, recognized icons) | marvin | Compile-time tables and/or SD-card JSON. Drives the recognizer and the navigator. §4.8. |
137	| High-level game control (e.g., "start single-player song X") | marvin | Translates verbs into fret/strum sequences sent over the same fretboard link as gameplay commands. §4.8. |
138	| Calibration / tuning UI authoring | dev PC (fret-tuner) | Optional; not required at runtime. Open Q7: long-term fate. |
139	| Training data ingest / replay analysis | dev PC | Off-band consumer of marvin's reference-data export. |
140	
141	### 2.3 Data flow at a glance
142	
143	1. **Frame ready** — ISC writes a BGR888 packed frame to DDR; the video task notifies subscribers.
144	2. **CV detect** — one or more CV detectors read the frame and emit detector-state events.
145	3. **ADC ingest** — a UART task receives raw ADC samples from the fretboard and runs an ADC detector that emits detector-state events on the same bus.
146	4. **Arbitrate** — the timing pipeline picks the active detector (or fuses), maintains the chord-accumulation window, and pushes finished chords onto its FIFO.
147	5. **Schedule** — the FIFO emits fret-assert and strum-pulse commands at the correct ticks.
148	6. **Send** — commands are encoded and transmitted to the fretboard over UART.
149	7. **Display** — the captured frame is composited with overlays (sensor crosshairs, detector outputs, chord state, latency markers) and shown on the LVDS panel.
150	8. **Record** (optional) — when recording is enabled, a derived/compressed reference-data record (frame epoch + detector state + raw ADC + emitted commands) is buffered and exported via the chosen transport.
151	
152	### 2.4 Latency budget (target, end-to-end)
153	
154	| Stage | Budget | Notes |
155	|---|---|---|
156	| HDMI source → DDR (capture) | ≤ 16.7 ms | One frame @ 60 Hz; bounded by capture pipeline. |
157	| Detect on frame | ≤ 16.7 ms | One frame budget for CV; ADC path is separate and faster. |
158	| Timing pipeline → command emit | latency dominated by `STRUM_DELAY_MS` (≈ 200 ms) — intentional, not waste; compensates for sensor placement above strike line. |
159	| UART command → fretboard GPIO | ≤ 5 ms | Short fixed-format frame at ≥ 115 200 Bd. |
160	| Total user-visible latency | ≈ 200–250 ms | Tunable via `STRUM_DELAY_MS`, set per-game by calibration. |
161	
162	The dominant fixed delay (`STRUM_DELAY_MS`) exists by design — the camera sees notes before they reach the strike line. Capture + detect + UART jitter is what we actually budget against.
