202	
203	## 4. Subsystems
204	
205	### 4.1 Video capture & display ✅
206	
207	Working end-to-end. See [`capture_pipeline.md`](capture_pipeline.md) and [`display_path.md`](display_path.md) for register-level detail. The video task (`video.c`, FreeRTOS) owns the capture pipeline and a frame queue that other tasks subscribe to. Display intent and capture intent are decoupled (commit `e28c497`); a software scaler can be inserted between capture and display when source ≠ panel native.
208	
209	**What this subsystem owns:**
210	- TC358743 init, source detection, EDID, format negotiation.
211	- ISC DMA configuration and frame buffer rotation in DDR.
212	- XLCDC overlay window placement (pillarbox/letterbox) for the active source.
213	- Frame-ready notification to subscribers (CV detect, recording, UI overlay).
214	
215	**What it doesn't own:**
216	- CV processing (§4.2).
217	- Recording / export (§4.6).
218	- UI widgets / chrome (§4.5) — only the pixel composition for the live-view layer.
219	
220	### 4.2 CV detection pipeline + detector-state bus 🚧
221	
222	#### 4.2.1 Role
223	
224	This is what makes marvin the *reference detector*. It runs computer-vision note detection on captured frames and publishes a structured detector-state record per frame onto a shared bus. Other detectors (fretboard ADC; future Edge-AI unit) publish onto the same bus. The timing pipeline (§4.4) consumes the bus.
225	
226	#### 4.2.2 Detector model
227	
228	A **detector** is anything that turns observation data into a `detector_state_t` event. marvin will host at least:
229	
230	- `cv_marvin_v1` — the reference vision detector. Reads RGB888-packed (3 B/pixel) frames from the video frame queue; emits one `detector_state_t` per frame.
231	- `adc_fretboard` — runs on top of raw ADC samples streamed from the fretboard MCU (§4.3); emits `detector_state_t` events at the fretboard's 240 Hz rate.
232	
233	Future detectors may include alternate CV algorithms running in parallel for comparison, or off-board detectors (Edge-AI MCU) feeding state in over UART/Ethernet.
234	
235	#### 4.2.3 detector_state record (canonical shape)
236	
237	```
238	typedef struct {
239	    uint32_t frame_epoch;     // master sync token (§4.6.4)
240	    uint64_t timestamp_us;    // monotonic, marvin-local
241	    uint8_t  detector_id;     // 0=cv_marvin_v1, 1=adc_fretboard, ...
242	    uint8_t  reserved[3];
243	    struct {
244	        uint8_t  pressed;     // 0/1 hard call
245	        uint16_t confidence;  // 0..65535, detector-defined
246	        uint16_t raw_value;   // detector-defined: ADC sample, pixel mean, etc.
247	    } fret[5];                // FRET_GREEN..FRET_ORANGE
248	} detector_state_t;
249	```
250	
251	Fields are fixed-width, naturally aligned, little-endian — this is also the on-disk record layout for the state log (§4.6.5). `frame_epoch` is the master clock for cross-detector and cross-recording sync.
252	
253	#### 4.2.4 Bus mechanics
254	
255	- A single FreeRTOS queue (`xDetectorStateQueue`) carries `detector_state_t` records, one entry per detector emit.
256	- The timing pipeline task (§4.4) is the sole consumer.
257	- The recording task (§4.6) snoops the queue via a side-channel: each producer publishes simultaneously to the timing-pipeline queue and to a recording stream buffer. (Single producer→multiple consumers is implemented by tee'ing inside each detector, not by a broker; keeps queue semantics blocking and simple.)
258	- Detectors run on their own FreeRTOS tasks (one per detector instance) so a slow detector cannot stall the frame pipeline.
259	
260	#### 4.2.5 Reference-detector responsibilities
261	
262	`cv_marvin_v1` is a *first-class* subsystem, not a debug aid. Its detector state is the ground-truth label for any reference-data recording (§4.6). Implications:
263	
264	- Algorithm changes are versioned (`cv_marvin_v1`, `cv_marvin_v2`, …). The version is stamped into recordings so training data stays attributable.
265	- Calibration (sensor/strike-line ROIs in pixel space) is stored in the system config (§4.7) and reproducibly applied at startup.
266	- The detector must run within one frame-time (≤ 16.7 ms) on Cortex-A5 — concrete algorithm choice is a future decision, but the budget is set.
267	
268	#### 4.2.6 Open questions surfaced here
269	
270	- Initial CV algorithm — pixel-mean threshold per ROI, edge-trough, optical-flow-based, or learned. (Defer; bring up the simplest first to validate end-to-end.)
271	- ADC-detector logic location — port `fretboard/fret_button.c`'s detection (hysteresis edges) into marvin (`adc_fretboard` runs on raw samples), or have fretboard pre-process and stream edges. (Default: marvin runs the detector on raw samples; fretboard stays dumb.)
272	
273	### 4.3 Fretboard link ✅
274	
275	Direct **FLEXCOM1 USART** link between marvin and the fretboard MCU — a plain UART wire, no USB. marvin's `PA28` (FLEXCOM1_IO0, `GUITAR_TX`) and `PA29` (FLEXCOM1_IO1, `GUITAR_RX`) connect to the fretboard's SERCOM1 (`PB01` RX / `PB00` TX). Both ends run **500 000 baud, 8N1**. The FLEXCOM1 USART runs in Harmony ring-buffer mode so RX never drops bytes between reads. (Was FLEXCOM2 until the console moved onto FLEXCOM2 — see §4.9.)
276	
277	- **Marvin → fretboard:** command bitmask (which frets to assert + strum direction). 1-byte bitmask, no framing. `fretboard_link_task` writes the latest mask via `FLEXCOM1_USART_Write`.
278	- **Fretboard → marvin:** raw ADC stream (5 channels × 16-bit) at 240 Hz, in a 17-byte start/end-bracketed frame (`0x03 … 0xFC`, with `sample_seq` + `applied_mask`). The FLEXCOM1 RX ring fills continuously from its ISR; a persistent read-threshold notification wakes `fretboard_rx_task`, which drains the ring, resyncs on the frame markers, and republishes each valid frame as a `PERF_REC_FRETBOARD_RAW` perf-log record (default-disabled, host enables via `PERF_CMD_SET_TYPE_MASK`). This is the on-board capture path until the SD-card recorder lands; it's also the substrate for the future `adc_fretboard` detector (§4.2).
279	- **Standalone fallback:** when marvin's timing pipeline is disabled (see §4.4 and §6), the fretboard runs its own existing chord FIFO (`fret_button.c`) and continues to stream ADC + emitted-command telemetry to marvin for capture/display.
280	
281	### 4.4 Timing pipeline 🚧
282	
283	Centralized on marvin by default. Owns:
284	
285	- Chord-accumulation window (`CHORD_WINDOW_MS` ≈ 20–40 ms).
286	- Pending-chord FIFO with per-chord `press_at` / `strum_at` ticks.
287	- Per-fret release scheduling.
288	- Strum direction alternation and pulse generation.
289	- `STRUM_DELAY_MS` / `FRET_EARLY_MS` / `STRUM_PULSE_MS` constants — initial values port from `tools/fret-tuner/SPEC.md` and `firmware/fretboard/SPEC.md`.
290	
291	**Disable / handoff mode:** an operator-mode toggle (§6) deactivates marvin's pipeline. fretboard then runs its own existing pipeline; marvin still ingests ADC + emitted-command telemetry for recording/display, but does not emit commands.
292	
293	### 4.5 UI / operator surface 🚧
294	
295	10.1″ 1280×800 LVDS panel + maxtouch capacitive touch. Functional surfaces required:
296	
297	- Live game view (capture composited with detector overlays — sensor crosshairs, detection events, latency markers).
298	- Calibration / tuning (per-fret ROI placement, threshold values, timing constants).
299	- Mode + run controls (idle, calibrate, dry-run, play, replay, record).
300	- Logs / history / stats (recent commands, miss/hit counts, dropped frames).
```

Motivation, in order: PoDL carries power *and* data on one pair to the guitar; better noise/cable tolerance; PLCA multidrop headroom; and demonstrating 10BASE-T1S + PoDL inside a larger Microchip system (SAM9X7 + LAN8651 + PIC32CM). 12	/* Per-frame performance log. Producers post records onto two static
13	 * queues (small / patch); a low-priority drain task frames them
14	 * (SOF + length + payload + CRC-16/CCITT) and pushes the bytes out the
15	 * USB-device CDC sink. Drop-on-full, never block. The pipeline must
16	 * remain unaffected if perf-log vanishes.
17	 *
18	 * All emit calls take ≈O(memcpy) and never lock. The ISR variants use
19	 * xQueueSendFromISR; the task variants use xQueueSend with zero block
20	 * time. Choose by call site — passing the wrong one will not corrupt
21	 * state but may misuse the higher_priority_task_woken pathway. */
22

143	 * via the host→device PERF_CMD_SET_TYPE_MASK command; default is all-on.

1	#ifndef MARVIN_CONSOLE_H
2	#define MARVIN_CONSOLE_H
3	
4	/* Interactive operator console — FLEXCOM2 USART (ring-buffer), 115200 8N1.
5	 *
6	 * A human-facing command line (embedded-cli) on a channel separate from the
7	 * DBGU log/printf chatter: log output stays on DBGU, console I/O stays on
8	 * FLEXCOM2. Commands set the operating-mode toggles (detect / timing / manual),
9	 * select the active detector, drive manual fret/strum actuation, and print a
10	 * status snapshot — see the binding table in console.c.
11	 *
12	 * One FreeRTOS task owns the link: it drains the FLEXCOM2 RX ring (woken by a
13	 * read-threshold notification), feeds bytes to embedded-cli, and runs the line
14	 * editor / dispatcher. All state is statically allocated; embedded-cli is given
15	 * a fixed buffer so no malloc is exercised.
16	 *
17	 * Call after SYS_Initialize so the FLEXCOM2 peripheral is up, and after the
18	 * actuator/detector modules so their setters are ready to be driven. */
19	
20	void Console_Initialize(void);
21	
22	#endif
23

```text
1	# fretboard ↔ marvin link — 10BASE-T1S + PoDL
2	
3	Low-level design for moving the fretboard ↔ marvin link from a FLEXCOM2/SERCOM
4	UART pair to **10BASE-T1S single-pair Ethernet with "dumb" Power-over-Data-Lines
5	(PoDL)**. System-level summary and rationale live in [`../SPEC.md`](../SPEC.md)
6	§6; this document holds the engineering detail.
7	
8	Status: **direction, not yet built.** The link today is FLEXCOM2 UART (system
9	spec M2). Nothing here is flashed.
10	
11	---
12	
13	## 1. Why T1S here
14	
15	- **PoDL** — one twisted pair carries both data *and* the fretboard's power, so
16	  the cable to the guitar is a single 2-wire link instead of a data pair plus a
17	  separate power feed. This is the primary motivation.
18	- **Robustness / reach** — differential single-pair Ethernet tolerates a long,
19	  electrically noisy run to a moving instrument better than a TTL UART pair.
20	- **Multidrop headroom** — 10BASE-T1S/PLCA puts up to 8 nodes on one pair, so a
21	  second sensor node or fretboard can share the same pair *and* the same power.
22	- **Demonstration** — showcasing 10BASE-T1S + PoDL doing real work inside a
23	  larger Microchip system (SAM9X7 + LAN8651 + PIC32CM) is an explicit goal, not
24	  just an incidental benefit. Bandwidth is *not* a motivation — the existing
25	  500 kbaud UART already carries the ~4 KB/s payload with ~12× headroom.
26	
27	## 2. The part: LAN8651B1
28	
29	A **MAC-PHY**: integrates the full IEEE 802.3 Clause 4 MAC *and* the 10BASE-T1S
30	PHY on one chip, and talks to the host MCU over **SPI** using the OPEN Alliance
31	TC6 ("10BASE-T1x MAC-PHY Serial Interface", v1.1) protocol. It exists precisely
32	to give a small MCU with no built-in Ethernet MAC a single-pair Ethernet link
33	over ~5 pins.
34	
35	Done in hardware by the LAN8651 (the MCU never touches these):
36	
37	- Line coding, PLCA / CSMA-CD media access, preamble/SFD.
38	- **FCS (CRC32) generation on TX and checking on RX.**
39	- On-wire framing and minimum-frame padding.
40	
41	SPI: LAN8651 is an SPI client, SCLK up to 25 MHz. Pins: `SDI`, `SDO`, `CS_N`,
42	`SCLK`, `IRQ_N` (active-low interrupt), plus a reset.
43	
44	## 3. What the host MCU must implement
45	
46	No TCP/IP, ARP, DHCP, or any IP stack. Three layers, none large:
47	
48	1. **SPI transport** — one SERCOM in SPI-master mode + GPIO for `CS_N`,
49	   `IRQ_N` (external interrupt), and reset.
50	2. **OA TC6 chunk protocol** — the only real "driver." Unlike a UART, the SPI
51	   link is *not* byte-transparent: it exchanges fixed-size **chunks** (default
52	   64-byte data payload + a 4-byte header on TX / 4-byte footer on RX), with
53	   credit-based flow control (TX credits and RX-chunks-available are reported in
54	   each footer), plus a separate control-transaction format for register
55	   read/writes during init. Microchip publishes an open-source reference driver
56	   ([`MicrochipTech/oa-tc6-lib`](https://github.com/MicrochipTech/oa-tc6-lib),
57	   §References) small enough to run on an Arduino — the candidate base for both
58	   ends here.
59	3. **Minimal L2 framing** — the MAC-PHY only transmits *valid Ethernet frames*,
60	   so the host prepends a fixed 14-byte Ethernet header (dest MAC, src MAC,
61	   ethertype) to the payload. For this link the MACs are hardcoded and a custom
62	   ethertype carries the existing frame formats verbatim:
63	   - fretboard → marvin: the 17-byte data-stream frame (see fretboard SPEC).
64	   - marvin → fretboard: the 1-byte button bitmask.
65	
66	   17 B + 14 B header = 31 B → a single chunk. The 1-byte command likewise. The
67	   existing UART framing (`0x03 … 0xFC`, `sample_seq`, etc.) can ride unchanged
68	   inside the Ethernet payload, so higher layers don't need to know the
69	   transport changed.
70	
71	## 4. Resource budget — fretboard (PIC32CM6408PL10048, 64 KB flash / 8 KB SRAM)
72	
73	Estimates; static allocation only (no malloc), per project rule.
74	
75	| Resource | Estimate | Notes |
76	|---|---|---|
77	| Flash | ~6–10 KB | OA TC6 lib (~4–8 KB) + SPI glue + L2 framing. Reclaim the UART data path if the UART link is fully retired. |
78	| SRAM | ~1–2 KB | A couple of chunk buffers + one TX/RX frame buffer. |
79	| SERCOM | 1 (SPI master) | A free SERCOM alongside SERCOM1 (still UART for now). |
80	| GPIO | 2–3 | `CS_N`, `IRQ_N` (ext-int), reset. |
81	| CPU | negligible | One chunk per 240 Hz tick, interrupt-driven off `IRQ_N`; the TC0 ISR stays lean. |
82	
83	SPI clock: SERCOM SPI master maxes at GCLK/2 ≈ **12 MHz** on the 24 MHz part
84	(not the chip's 25 MHz ceiling) — irrelevant for this data rate.
85	
86	Everything fits comfortably inside 64 KB / 8 KB.
87	
88	## 5. marvin side
89	
90	marvin runs **bare-metal (no Linux)**, so it does *not* get a free netdev — it
91	needs its own TC6 driver. The upside: a **single portable `oa_tc6` layer shared
92	between marvin (Cortex-A5) and fretboard (Cortex-M0+)**, which is itself a tidy
93	demonstration that the OPEN Alliance SPI driver scales across the family. marvin
94	resources are not a concern.
95	
96	## 6. PoDL — "dumb" (no negotiation)
97	
98	PoDL is **not in the LAN8651** — the MAC-PHY only moves data. PoDL is external
99	coupling circuitry around the pair, and it is **transparent to both MCUs** (zero
100	firmware footprint, the §4 budget is unaffected):
101	
102	- **PSE side (marvin):** a fixed-voltage source + coupling inductors that inject
103	  DC onto the pair.
104	- **PD side (fretboard):** coupling inductors to extract DC + a regulator down to
105	  the PIC32CM rail.
106	- **Dumb / unmanaged:** no SCCP classification or negotiation handshake. Fixed
107	  supply voltage, fixed point-to-point pair, decided at design time. Simplest
108	  PoDL form; appropriate because the topology is fixed and both ends are ours.
109	
110	Microchip has PoDL reference designs that pair with the LAN865x EVBs, which also
111	helps the demonstration story.
112	
113	## 7. Topology: point-to-point vs PLCA multidrop
114	
115	Recommended direction: **enable PLCA from the start** rather than strict
116	point-to-point. A 2-node PLCA bus already demonstrates the headline T1S feature
117	(collision-free multidrop on one pair) at no extra cost, and leaves the door
118	open to a second node sharing the same pair and power. Open until decided.
119	
120	## 8. Open items
121	
122	- PLCA vs pure point-to-point (see §7) — lean PLCA.
123	- PoDL supply voltage and the PD-side regulator topology (BOM, not firmware).
124	- Custom ethertype value and the two hardcoded MAC addresses.
125	- Whether to keep the UART link as a fallback during bring-up or cut over
126	  outright (affects whether SERCOM1's data path is reclaimed — §4).
127	- Magnetics-free coupling component selection on the Sensor-LCD5 PCB.
128	
129	## References
130	
131	- **OA TC6 driver (candidate base, both ends):**
132	  [`MicrochipTech/oa-tc6-lib`](https://github.com/MicrochipTech/oa-tc6-lib) —
133	  Microchip's open-source OPEN Alliance TC6 (10BASE-T1x MAC-PHY Serial
134	  Interface) library: SPI chunk protocol + control transactions, used as the
135	  shared portable layer (§3, §5).
136	- LAN8650/1 (LAN8651B1) datasheet — 10BASE-T1S MAC-PHY Ethernet Controller with
137	  SPI, on [Microchip online docs](https://onlinedocs.microchip.com/) /
138	  the LAN8651 product page.
139	- OPEN Alliance *10BASE-T1x MAC-PHY Serial Interface* specification (TC6), v1.1.
140
```

I've thoroughly explored the repo to understand the current fretboard ↔ marvin link, node topology, and payload requirements for your T1S multidrop design. Here are the key findings:

### 1. **Current Node Architecture & Hardware Platforms**

**marvin (SAM9X75 Curiosity / Hybrid) — Cortex-A5, bare-metal:**
- Runtime brain: HDMI capture → CV detection → timing pipeline → actuator commands
- Reference detector source for training data
- Currently linked to fretboard via:
  - **Original:** USB CDC host bridge (EDBG)
  - **Current (2026-06-08 port):** FLEXCOM1 USART @ 500 000 Bd, 8N1, ring-buffer mode (direct GPIO over FLEXCOM)
  - **File:** `/Users/gregmrozek/Projects/microchip/guitar-pic/firmware/marvin/default/src/actuator/fretboard_link.c` (lines 1–279)
  - **Roles:** TX = 7-bit command bitmask (1 byte/tick), RX = 17-byte ADC frames (240 Hz)

**fretboard (PIC32CM6408PL10048) — Cortex-M0+, 24 MHz, 64 KB flash / 8 KB SRAM:**
- I/O bridge: reads 5-channel phototransistor ADC, outputs button presses to Wii controller
- Two modes (compile-time `FRETBOARD_MODE`):
  - `MARVIN_DRIVEN` (current alternate): I/O bridge only, no game logic
  - `MODEL_DRIVEN` (current default): on-device int8 inference, standalone play with marvin optional
- Currently linked via:
  - SERCOM1 UART @ 500 000 Bd, 8N1, ring-buffer mode
  - **Files:** `/Users/gregmrozek/Projects/microchip/guitar-pic/firmware/fretboard/data_stream.c`, `cmd_receive.c`, `main.c`
  - TC0 timer callback @ 240 Hz ISR: `fret_scan_all()` → `data_stream_send()` → `cmd_receive_update()`

---

### 2. **Current Data Payloads**

#### **fretboard → marvin: 17-byte ADC frame (240 Hz)**

**Structure** (`data_stream.c` lines 9–40):
```c
typedef struct __attribute__((packed)) {
    uint8_t  start;          // 0x03
    uint16_t green;          // ADC[FRET_GREEN], u16 LE
    uint16_t red;            // ADC[FRET_RED], u16 LE
    uint16_t yellow;         // ADC[FRET_YELLOW], u16 LE
    uint16_t blue;           // ADC[FRET_BLUE], u16 LE
    uint16_t orange;         // ADC[FRET_ORANGE], u16 LE
    uint32_t sample_seq;     // Monotonic counter, one per tick (u32 LE) — for gap detection
    uint8_t  applied_mask;   // Actuator bitmask driven during *this* scan
    uint8_t  end;            // 0xFC
} ds_frame_t;  // 17 bytes total
```

**ADC Channels** (fretboard SPEC.md lines 35–49):
- 5 phototransistors at the TV strike line, 12-bit unsigned (0–4095)
- Lower ADC value = brighter (note present)
- Channel mapping: Green/Red/Yellow/Blue/Orange → PA28/PA16/PA19/PA27/PA26 (FRET_* enum)

**Rate:** 17 B × 240 Hz = **4.08 KB/s** (well under 500 kbaud @ ~50 KB/s budget, ~12× headroom)

**Key feature (fretboard journal 2026-06-03):** `sample_seq` and `applied_mask` are stamped *by the fretboard* atomically at the same tick, pairing sensor and actuator state at the source for training-data labeling.

#### **marvin → fretboard: 1-byte command (variable rate)**

**Structure** (`cmd_receive.h` lines 4–15):
```c
#define CMD_BIT_GREEN       (1U << 0)  // Bit 0
#define CMD_BIT_RED         (1U << 1)  // Bit 1
#define CMD_BIT_YELLOW      (1U << 2)  // Bit 2
#define CMD_BIT_BLUE        (1U << 3)  // Bit 3
#define CMD_BIT_ORANGE      (1U << 4)  // Bit 4
#define CMD_BIT_STRUM_DOWN  (1U << 5)  // Bit 5
#define CMD_BIT_STRUM_UP    (1U << 6)  // Bit 6
```

**Behavior** (`cmd_receive.c` lines 54–65):
- Drain RX ring each tick, apply only the **last byte** as bitmask (latest-wins)
- Bit set → drive GPIO low (assert button press)
- Bit clear → tri-state GPIO (release button, pull-up restores idle)

**Rate:** Timing pipeline submits at game-dependent rates (~60 Hz typical gameplay, up to 240 Hz in strum scheduling). fretboard link uses a **latest-wins depth-1 queue** (`xQueueOverwrite`) so stalled writes don't accumulate stale commands.

### 3. **Multidrop Topology & PLCA Considerations**

From `/Users/gregmrozek/Projects/microchip/guitar-pic/docs/t1s-podl-link.md` (sections 1, 7):

**Current plan:**
- Move from FLEXCOM UART to **10BASE-T1S single-pair Ethernet + dumb PoDL** via **LAN8651B1 MAC-PHY** (each end)
- **PLCA multidrop lean direction** (not strict point-to-point): enables up to 8 nodes on one pair
- **Open decision** (not yet resolved): formal topology (PLCA vs p2p), but "lean PLCA" indicates intent to enable a second node (e.g., additional fretboard or sensor)
- **PoDL:** Transparent to MCU (zero firmware footprint), couples power + data on the single twisted pair

**Resource budget on fretboard (lines 71–87):**
- Flash: ~6–10 KB (OA TC6 SPI driver + L2 framing)
- SRAM: ~1–2 KB (couple chunk buffers + TX/RX frame)
- GPIO: 2–3 (CS_N, IRQ_N, reset)
- SERCOM: 1 (SPI master, ~12 MHz feasible on the 24 MHz part)
- **17-byte + 1-byte payloads ride unchanged inside the Ethernet payload** — no logic change to `data_stream.c`/`cmd_receive.c`

**marvin side:** Bare-metal (no free netdev), so it needs its own portable `oa_tc6` SPI driver — shared across both SAM9X75 (Cortex-A5) and fretboard (Cortex-M0+).

### 4. **Data Flow Context: marvin's Detector-State Bus & Edge-AI**

From `/Users/gregmrozek/Projects/microchip/guitar-pic/firmware/marvin/default/src/perf_log/perf_log_records.h`:

**marvin also ingests fretboard ADC as a parallel detector** (PERF_REC_FRETBOARD_RAW, record type 0x0B):
- Records one per valid 17-byte fretboard frame, tagged with the same `frame_epoch` as video frames
- Carries the 5×u16 ADC values, `fb_sample_seq`, and `applied_mask` (from the fretboard itself)
- Used by edge-ai training pipeline to label (marvin's distilled commands) with raw ADC inputs

**edge-ai system** (tools/edge-ai):
- Distillation against `PERF_REC_ACTUATOR.intended_mask` (marvin's command byte)
- Output: 6 bits (5 frets + 1 collapsed strum) — deployed to fretboard PIC32CM
- Already running on hardware (2026-06-04) in `MODEL_DRIVEN` mode
- Removes marvin from the gameplay loop for standalone fretboard operation

### 5. **Timing Pipeline Command Rates & Arbitration**

From `/Users/gregmrozek/Projects/microchip/guitar-pic/firmware/marvin/default/src/actuator/timing_pipeline.h`:

**Timing pipeline (primary command producer):**
- Maintains chord-accumulation window + strum scheduling state machine
- Emits 7-bit bitmask (bits 0–4 frets, bit 5 strum-down, bit 6 strum-up)
- Submits via `FretboardLink_Send(mask, producer_id)` with `producer_id = PERF_ACTUATOR_PRODUCER_TIMING`

**Multiple producers** (latest-wins arbitration):
- `timing_pipeline` (primary, gameplay notes)
- `manual_control` (operator UI buttons) — mutual-exclusion mode gating (marvin disables timing during manual mode)
- Future `game_state_controller` (M10, menu navigation) — same API, mutual-exclusion gating

**fretboard_link queue:** Depth 1, `xQueueOverwrite` semantics
- If marvin can't TX faster than fretboard can consume, the newest mask wins
- No accumulation of stale commands

| **marvin perf-log records** | `/firmware/marvin/default/src/perf_log/perf_log_records.h` | 38–40, ~200–230 | PERF_REC_FRETBOARD_RAW (ADC ingest) + PERF_REC_ACTUATOR (command tracking) |
| **edge-ai distillation** | `/tools/edge-ai/docs/SPEC.md` | §3 | Supervision against `PERF_REC_ACTUATOR.intended_mask` |
| **T1S link design** | `/docs/t1s-podl-link.md` | §1–8 | LAN8651B1, OA TC6 SPI, dumb PoDL, PLCA topology direction |
| **fretboard SPEC** | `/firmware/fretboard/SPEC.md` | Lines 35–75 | ADC channel map, button output map, 17-byte frame format |
| **system SPEC** | `/SPEC.md` | §2, §6 | Architecture, T1S direction, fretboard role |

---

### 7. **Minimal Protocol Payload Summary for T1S Design**

**Steady-state wire rates (marvin ↔ fretboard):**

| Direction | Payload | Period | Rate |
|-----------|---------|--------|------|
| fretboard → marvin | 17 B (ADC + seq + mask) | 4.17 ms (240 Hz) | 4.08 KB/s |
| marvin → fretboard | 1 B (7-bit bitmask) | Variable (~60–240 Hz) | ~0.5–2 KB/s |
| **Total** | **18 B/tick** | **4.17 ms** | **~4.5 KB/s** |

**Within T1S/Ethernet:**
- 17-byte ADC frame → wrapped in 14-byte Ethernet header (dest MAC, src MAC, custom ethertype) = **31 B** (single OA TC6 chunk at default 64-byte payload)
- 1-byte command → wrapped in Ethernet header = **15 B** (fits in single chunk)
- **No IP stack, no TCP/IP overhead** — OPEN Alliance TC6 chunk protocol only

**10BASE-T1S baseline:** 10 Mbps = 1.25 MB/s raw throughput. Your 4–5 KB/s payload is ~0.4% of link capacity, leaving **massive headroom for:**
- PLCA overhead (collision arbitration, inter-frame spacing)
- A second or third node on the same pair (sensor node, second fretboard MCU, etc.)
- Future protocol evolution

---

### 8. **Open Decisions (from docs/t1s-podl-link.md §8)**

Before T1S code lands, settle:
1. **PLCA topology** — Full PLCA (up to 8 nodes), lean PLCA (2–3 nodes), or strict point-to-point?
   - Current direction: "lean PLCA" (allows future expansion without re-routing)
2. **Custom ethertype value** — Proposed (not yet hardcoded)
3. **Two hardcoded MAC addresses** — fretboard ↔ marvin MACs (fixed, not dynamic discovery)
4. **UART fallback during bring-up** — Keep SERCOM1 as a parallel debug path, or cut over outright?

---

This exploration shows you have a well-structured, payload-light system with ample T1S capacity and clear extensibility for multidrop nodes. The 17-byte ADC frame + 1-byte command format is minimalist, deterministic, and ready to live unchanged inside Ethernet payloads.

- **`main.c`** — Minimal: calls `SYS_Initialize()` then loops `SYS_Tasks()`.
- **`log.c/h`** — Logging shim with FreeRTOS-aware locking.

**Subsystems (all task-based FreeRTOS):**
- **`video/`** — HDMI capture (TC358743 → CSI-2 → ISC → DDR). Owns frame queue subscriptions. Files: `video.c/h`, `isc_capture.c/h`, `tc358743.c/h` (35 KB — comprehensive bridging logic).
- **`detector/`** — CV note detection (cv_marvin_v1) + detector-state bus. Files: `detector.c/h`, `cv_marvin_v1.c/h`. Detector-state records are fixed-width `detector_state_t` (line 33–45 in detector.h), published onto `xDetectorStateQueue`.
- **`actuator/`** — Timing pipeline + fretboard link. Files: `timing_pipeline.c/h`, `fretboard_link.c/h`, `manual_control.c/h`.

- **`game/`** — Gameplay engine (screen classification, menu navigation).
- **`console/`** — Operator CLI on FLEXCOM2 (115200 8N1, embedded-cli). Files: `console.c/h` (1000 lines).
- **`ui/`** — Legato graphics UI.
- **`perf_log/`** — Performance telemetry + USB-CDC export. Multi-producer (ISR-safe queues), single drain task. Records tagged with frame_epoch for cross-detector sync.

  - **`peripheral/flexcom/usart/plib_flexcom1_usart.h`** — PLIB interface for FLEXCOM1 (ring-buffer mode, callbacks, threshold notifications).

  - **`definitions.h`** — System includes all plib headers, drivers, USB, graphics stack.

---

### 2. **Existing Peripheral/Driver Structure**

**Naming conventions:**
- **PLib (peripheral library):** `plib_<peripheral>.h`, functions like `FLEXCOM1_USART_Initialize()`, `FLEXCOM1_USART_Read()`, `FLEXCOM1_USART_Write()`. Located in `peripheral/<type>/<name>/`.
- **HAL driver:** `drv_<name>.c/h`, functions like `DRV_I2C_Open()`, `DRV_I2C_ReadTransferAdd()`. Located in `driver/<name>/src/`. Uses init structs like `DRV_I2C_INIT` populated in `initialization.c`.

**Init patterns:**
1. **Peripheral init (SYS_Initialize):** Call PLib `_Initialize()` (e.g., `FLEXCOM1_USART_Initialize()` at line 335 in initialization.c).
2. **Driver init (SYS_Initialize):** Create init struct, call `DRV_*_Initialize()` returning a handle, store in `SYSTEM_OBJECTS sysObj` (line 140 in initialization.c). Example: `sysObj.drvI2C0 = DRV_I2C_Initialize(…)` at line 353.
3. **Module init (APP_Initialize):** Higher-level task/subsystem setup. Example: `Video_Initialize()` at line 111 in app.c — creates FreeRTOS task, subscribes to frame queue.

**Ring-buffer USART pattern (used by fretboard_link):**
- **Register callback:** `FLEXCOM1_USART_ReadCallbackRegister(rx_event_handler, context)` (line 233 in fretboard_link.c).
- **Set threshold:** `FLEXCOM1_USART_ReadThresholdSet(framesize)` (line 234).
- **Enable notification:** `FLEXCOM1_USART_ReadNotificationEnable(true, true)` (line 235).
- **Callback woken on threshold/full:** callback fires from ISR, posts to binary semaphore via `xSemaphoreGiveFromISR`.
- **Task drains:** `FLEXCOM1_USART_ReadCountGet()` checks pending bytes, `FLEXCOM1_USART_Read(&buf, want)` drains, resync on markers.
- **TX:** `FLEXCOM1_USART_Write(buf, 1)` enqueues to TX ring, returns immediately.

**Task pattern (FreeRTOS static allocation):**
```c
static StackType_t s_task_stack[STACK_WORDS];
static StaticTask_t s_task_tcb;
TaskHandle_t h = xTaskCreateStatic(task_func, "Name", STACK_WORDS, NULL, PRIORITY, s_task_stack, &s_task_tcb);
```
Example: lines 239–246 in fretboard_link.c. Priorities: timing_pipeline = 5, fretboard_link = 5 (same tier).

**CMake-based (not Makefile):**
- **Root:** `/firmware/marvin/cmake/marvin/default/CMakeLists.txt` (13–22). Minimal: includes `.generated/main.cmake` + optional `user.cmake`.
- **Generated file list:** `/cmake/marvin/default/.generated/file.cmake` (1+). Exhaustive list of source files (over 500 entries from Legato, USB CDC, GFX, peripherals, FreeRTOS).
- **Toolchain:** `/cmake/marvin/default/.generated/toolchain.cmake` — XC32 compiler config.
- **User customization:** Create `/cmake/marvin/default/user.cmake` to inject custom sources/flags (never committed by MCC, safe to version-control).

**Adding a new driver module:**
1. Create `.c` + `.h` files in `default/src/config/default/driver/<name>/src/`.
2. Add sources to `.generated/file.cmake` (or create a `user.cmake` to append for development).
3. Wrap init in a struct (e.g., `DRV_T1S_INIT`) and call `DRV_T1S_Initialize()` from `initialization.c` or a task.
4. Register tasks via `PerfLog_RegisterTaskForHighwater()` if task-based.

**Build artifacts:** `out/` directory (final binaries).

### 4. **Existing Networking, Message-Passing, Command/Event Interfaces**

**Fretboard link (current M2, FLEXCOM1 USART):**
- **Marvin → fretboard:** 1-byte bitmask (7 bits: 5 frets + 2 strum). Latest-wins via `xQueueOverwrite` (queue depth 1). Sent every 50 ms (line 39 in fretboard_link.c) + on state change.
- **Fretboard → marvin:** 17-byte frames at 240 Hz (lines 26–34 in fretboard_link.c). Format: `[0x03, 5×ADC_u16, seq_u32, applied_mask_u8, 0xFC]`. Resync on markers. Ring-buffer RX.
- **Perf-log snoop:** Fretboard raw frames also emit `PERF_REC_FRETBOARD_RAW` records (line 204 in fretboard_link.c).

**Detector-state bus (internal event bus):**
- **Queue:** `xDetectorStateQueue` (single FreeRTOS queue, detector.h line 57).
- **Record:** `detector_state_t` (fixed-width, detector.h lines 33–45):
  ```c
  struct {
    uint32_t frame_epoch;     // master sync (frame counter)
    uint64_t timestamp_us;    // local monotonic
    uint8_t detector_id;      // 0=cv_marvin_v1, 1=adc_fretboard
    uint8_t reserved[3];
    struct { uint8_t pressed; uint16_t confidence; uint16_t raw_value; } fret[5];
  }
  ```
- **Producers:** cv_marvin_v1 task (reads frames, emits per-frame), adc_fretboard (future, reads UART stream).
- **Consumer:** timing_pipeline task (reads bus, runs chord FIFO, calls `FretboardLink_Send()`).
- **Recording:** perf_log snoops via side-channel (no broker, each detector posts to both bus + recording stream).

**Console (operator CLI):**
- **FLEXCOM2 USART** (lines 3–4 in console.h). 115200 8N1, ring-buffer mode.
- **Embedded-cli** (third-party embedded-cli library, lines 5–10 in console.h).
- **Commands:** Set detector enable/active, manual fret/strum input, status print, timing constants (all defined in console.c).
- **Entirely separate from DBGU log channel** (DBGU = printf retarget, FLEXCOM2 = interactive console).

- **Records:** Stamped with `perf_rec_*_t` types (perf_log_records.h). Multi-producer (ISR-safe + task-safe queues), single drain task.
- **Format:** SOF + length + payload + CRC-16/CCITT (lines 13–15 in perf_log.h).

### 5. **RTOS vs Bare-Metal, Task Structure, Static-Allocation Patterns**

**FreeRTOS (not bare-metal):**
- Scheduler active at power-on (SYS_Initialize → initialization.c line 388 → APP_Initialize).
- Tasks created pre-scheduler with `xTaskCreateStatic` in APP_Initialize (app.c lines 111–174).
- APP_Tasks itself (app.c lines 186–193) calls `vTaskDelete(NULL)` to self-exit post-launch.

**Task hierarchy (in start order):**
1. **Video task** (app.c line 111): `Video_Initialize()` — captures frames, notifies subscribers.
2. **PerfLog queues** (app.c line 117): Subscribers set up before video task posts.
3. **Detector task** (app.c line 134): `Detector_Initialize()` + `Detector_SetActive()` — cv_marvin_v1 subscribes to frame queue inside its task.
4. **FretboardLink tasks** (app.c line 142): TX task (cmdqueue + 50 ms heartbeat), RX task (ring-buffer drain).
5. **TimingPipeline task** (app.c line 147): Consumes detector bus, emits fretboard commands.
6. **ManualControl task** (app.c line 154): UI-driven actuator producer.
7. **GameplayEngine task** (app.c line 161): Game-state observer (optional, toggled).
8. **Console task** (app.c line 167): Operator CLI (FLEXCOM2).
9. **PerfLog drain task** (app.c line 174): Last, so all producer queues valid when it starts.

**Static allocation patterns:**
- **Queues:** `xQueueCreateStatic(depth, item_size, storage, &buf)` (fretboard_link.c lines 221–225).
- **Semaphores:** `xSemaphoreCreateBinaryStatic(&buf)` (fretboard_link.c lines 227–228).
- **Tasks:** `xTaskCreateStatic(func, name, stack_words, param, priority, &stack, &tcb)` (fretboard_link.c lines 239–246, 248–255).
- **Storage:** All `static` at module scope (no heap).

**Priorities:**
- Fretboard link tasks: priority 5 (app.c line 42 in fretboard_link.c, though priorities defined in fretboard_link.c line 20).
- Typical convention: higher priority for hard real-time (video ISR → frame subscription), mid for timing pipeline, low for UI/logging.

**ISR callback patterns:**
- Peripheral ISR fires callback (e.g., FLEXCOM1 RX threshold), callback posts to semaphore via `xSemaphoreGiveFromISR()` (fretboard_link.c line 89).
- Task woken by semaphore, drains ring buffer, processes payload.
- Error handling: On RX error, clear error state + re-arm semaphore (lines 94–95).

**Example: Fretboard RX path (fretboard_link.c lines 156–217):**
1. FLEXCOM1 ISR fires when RX crosses threshold (line 234).
2. ISR callback wakes `fretboard_rx_task` via semaphore (line 89).
3. Task checks `FLEXCOM1_USART_ReadCountGet()` (line 167), reads until frame full (line 174).
4. Validates markers, parses ADC + seq + mask (lines 179–200).
5. Emits perf record (line 204).
6. Loops indefinitely (for-ever at line 165).

```

Payload:                 17 B (fretboard RX) or 1 B (marvin TX)
Total:                   31 B or 15 B → fits in single OA TC6 chunk (64 B data payload)
```

---

## Summary

The marvin firmware is **well-structured, FreeRTOS-based, and ready for T1S integration.** The existing `FretboardLink_{Initialize,Send,IsConnected}` API provides a clean abstraction layer; the new T1S driver plugs in beneath it without touching timing pipeline, console, or application logic. Key entry points for modification:

1. **initialization.c** (line ~335) — wire up SPI PLib + T1S driver.
2. **definitions.h** (includes section) — add driver headers.
3. **app.c** (line ~142) — swap init call (FretboardLink → T1SLink, same signature).
4. **CMakeLists.txt** or **user.cmake** — register source files.

The OA TC6 protocol layer can be ported from the open-source Microchip reference (`oa-tc6-lib`) and shared with the fretboard side (PIC32CM), keeping both ends of the bus aligned and maintainable.

1	# fretboard ↔ marvin link — 10BASE-T1S + PoDL
2	
3	Low-level design for moving the fretboard ↔ marvin link from a FLEXCOM2/SERCOM
4	UART pair to **10BASE-T1S single-pair Ethernet with "dumb" Power-over-Data-Lines
5	(PoDL)**. System-level summary and rationale live in [`../SPEC.md`](../SPEC.md)
6	§6; this document holds the engineering detail.

10	
11	---
12	
13	## 1. Why T1S here
14	
15	- **PoDL** — one twisted pair carries both data *and* the fretboard's power, so
16	  the cable to the guitar is a single 2-wire link instead of a data pair plus a
17	  separate power feed. This is the primary motivation.
18	- **Robustness / reach** — differential single-pair Ethernet tolerates a long,
19	  electrically noisy run to a moving instrument better than a TTL UART pair.
20	- **Multidrop headroom** — 10BASE-T1S/PLCA puts up to 8 nodes on one pair, so a
21	  second sensor node or fretboard can share the same pair *and* the same power.
22	- **Demonstration** — showcasing 10BASE-T1S + PoDL doing real work inside a
23	  larger Microchip system (SAM9X7 + LAN8651 + PIC32CM) is an explicit goal, not
24	  just an incidental benefit. Bandwidth is *not* a motivation — the existing
25	  500 kbaud UART already carries the ~4 KB/s payload with ~12× headroom.
26	
27	## 2. The part: LAN8651B1
28	
29	A **MAC-PHY**: integrates the full IEEE 802.3 Clause 4 MAC *and* the 10BASE-T1S
30	PHY on one chip, and talks to the host MCU over **SPI** using the OPEN Alliance
31	TC6 ("10BASE-T1x MAC-PHY Serial Interface", v1.1) protocol. It exists precisely
32	to give a small MCU with no built-in Ethernet MAC a single-pair Ethernet link
33	over ~5 pins.
34	
35	Done in hardware by the LAN8651 (the MCU never touches these):
36	
37	- Line coding, PLCA / CSMA-CD media access, preamble/SFD.
38	- **FCS (CRC32) generation on TX and checking on RX.**
39	- On-wire framing and minimum-frame padding.
40	
41	SPI: LAN8651 is an SPI client, SCLK up to 25 MHz. Pins: `SDI`, `SDO`, `CS_N`,
42	`SCLK`, `IRQ_N` (active-low interrupt), plus a reset.
43	
44	## 3. What the host MCU must implement
45	
46	No TCP/IP, ARP, DHCP, or any IP stack. Three layers, none large:
47	
48	1. **SPI transport** — one SERCOM in SPI-master mode + GPIO for `CS_N`,
49	   `IRQ_N` (external interrupt), and reset.
50	2. **OA TC6 chunk protocol** — the only real "driver." Unlike a UART, the SPI
51	   link is *not* byte-transparent: it exchanges fixed-size **chunks** (default
52	   64-byte data payload + a 4-byte header on TX / 4-byte footer on RX), with
53	   credit-based flow control (TX credits and RX-chunks-available are reported in
54	   each footer), plus a separate control-transaction format for register
55	   read/writes during init. Microchip publishes an open-source reference driver
56	   ([`MicrochipTech/oa-tc6-lib`](https://github.com/MicrochipTech/oa-tc6-lib),
57	   §References) small enough to run on an Arduino — the candidate base for both
58	   ends here.
59	3. **Minimal L2 framing** — the MAC-PHY only transmits *valid Ethernet frames*,
60	   so the host prepends a fixed 14-byte Ethernet header (dest MAC, src MAC,
61	   ethertype) to the payload. For this link the MACs are hardcoded and a custom
62	   ethertype carries the existing frame formats verbatim:
63	   - fretboard → marvin: the 17-byte data-stream frame (see fretboard SPEC).
64	   - marvin → fretboard: the 1-byte button bitmask.
65	
66	   17 B + 14 B header = 31 B → a single chunk. The 1-byte command likewise. The
67	   existing UART framing (`0x03 … 0xFC`, `sample_seq`, etc.) can ride unchanged
68	   inside the Ethernet payload, so higher layers don't need to know the
69	   transport changed.
70	
71	## 4. Resource budget — fretboard (PIC32CM6408PL10048, 64 KB flash / 8 KB SRAM)
72	
73	Estimates; static allocation only (no malloc), per project rule.
74	
75	| Resource | Estimate | Notes |
76	|---|---|---|
77	| Flash | ~6–10 KB | OA TC6 lib (~4–8 KB) + SPI glue + L2 framing. Reclaim the UART data path if the UART link is fully retired. |
78	| SRAM | ~1–2 KB | A couple of chunk buffers + one TX/RX frame buffer. |
79	| SERCOM | 1 (SPI master) | A free SERCOM alongside SERCOM1 (still UART for now). |
80	| GPIO | 2–3 | `CS_N`, `IRQ_N` (ext-int), reset. |
81	| CPU | negligible | One chunk per 240 Hz tick, interrupt-driven off `IRQ_N`; the TC0 ISR stays lean. |
82	
83	SPI clock: SERCOM SPI master maxes at GCLK/2 ≈ **12 MHz** on the 24 MHz part
84	(not the chip's 25 MHz ceiling) — irrelevant for this data rate.
85	
86	Everything fits comfortably inside 64 KB / 8 KB.

88	## 5. marvin side
89	
90	marvin runs **bare-metal (no Linux)**, so it does *not* get a free netdev — it
91	needs its own TC6 driver. The upside: a **single portable `oa_tc6` layer shared
92	between marvin (Cortex-A5) and fretboard (Cortex-M0+)**, which is itself a tidy
93	demonstration that the OPEN Alliance SPI driver scales across the family. marvin
94	resources are not a concern.
95	
96	## 6. PoDL — "dumb" (no negotiation)
97	
98	PoDL is **not in the LAN8651** — the MAC-PHY only moves data. PoDL is external
99	coupling circuitry around the pair, and it is **transparent to both MCUs** (zero
100	firmware footprint, the §4 budget is unaffected):
101	
102	- **PSE side (marvin):** a fixed-voltage source + coupling inductors that inject
103	  DC onto the pair.
104	- **PD side (fretboard):** coupling inductors to extract DC + a regulator down to
105	  the PIC32CM rail.
106	- **Dumb / unmanaged:** no SCCP classification or negotiation handshake. Fixed
107	  supply voltage, fixed point-to-point pair, decided at design time. Simplest
108	  PoDL form; appropriate because the topology is fixed and both ends are ours.
109	
110	Microchip has PoDL reference designs that pair with the LAN865x EVBs, which also
111	helps the demonstration story.
112	
113	## 7. Topology: point-to-point vs PLCA multidrop
114	
115	Recommended direction: **enable PLCA from the start** rather than strict
116	point-to-point. A 2-node PLCA bus already demonstrates the headline T1S feature
117	(collision-free multidrop on one pair) at no extra cost, and leaves the door
118	open to a second node sharing the same pair and power. Open until decided.
119	
120	## 8. Open items
121	
122	- PLCA vs pure point-to-point (see §7) — lean PLCA.
123	- PoDL supply voltage and the PD-side regulator topology (BOM, not firmware).
124	- Custom ethertype value and the two hardcoded MAC addresses.
125	- Whether to keep the UART link as a fallback during bring-up or cut over
126	  outright (affects whether SERCOM1's data path is reclaimed — §4).
127	- Magnetics-free coupling component selection on the Sensor-LCD5 PCB.
128	
129	## References
130	
131	- **OA TC6 driver (candidate base, both ends):**
132	  [`MicrochipTech/oa-tc6-lib`](https://github.com/MicrochipTech/oa-tc6-lib) —
133	  Microchip's open-source OPEN Alliance TC6 (10BASE-T1x MAC-PHY Serial
134	  Interface) library: SPI chunk protocol + control transactions, used as the
135	  shared portable layer (§3, §5).
136	- LAN8650/1 (LAN8651B1) datasheet — 10BASE-T1S MAC-PHY Ethernet Controller with
137	  SPI, on [Microchip online docs](https://onlinedocs.microchip.com/) /
138	  the LAN8651 product page.
139	- OPEN Alliance *10BASE-T1x MAC-PHY Serial Interface* specification (TC6), v1.1.

# Marvin T1S inter-node interface — first implementation pass

## Context

The fretboard ↔ marvin link is FLEXCOM1 UART today. [docs/t1s-podl-link.md](docs/t1s-podl-link.md)
already captures the direction — move to 10BASE-T1S single-pair Ethernet + dumb PoDL via a
**LAN8651B1 MAC-PHY** at each end, talking OPEN Alliance TC6 over SPI, with a minimal L2
header and no IP stack. That doc, however, was written for a **2-node** link (two hardcoded
MACs, one payload pair).

The new requirement: marvin must support **multiple simultaneous nodes** — several guitars,
several phototransistor fretboard detectors — on one PLCA multidrop pair. We focus on the
**marvin side** now, but the comm stack stays minimal so the same portable layer runs on a
low-end Cortex-M0+ (PIC32CM PL10) node.

**Decisions locked (this session):**
- Hardware: a **LAN8651 EVB/Click is wired to the SAM9X75 Curiosity now** → target runnable, testable code.
- Scope: **design the node-addressing/PLCA-coordinator abstraction for N nodes now, bring up the single marvin↔fretboard link** physically.
- Driver: **adapt [`MicrochipTech/oa-tc6-lib`](https://github.com/MicrochipTech/oa-tc6-lib)** with thin Harmony/FreeRTOS glue (not a from-scratch TC6).
- UART: **keep FLEXCOM1 UART in parallel**, select transport by build flag; cut over once T1S is proven.

**Gaps this pass closes (beyond what the doc has):** node-ID/addressing scheme, src→`detector_id`
demux, PLCA-coordinator role + ID map, FreeRTOS (not "bare-metal") integration model, and a
node-addressed evolution of the single-peer `FretboardLink_*` API.

## Architecture — layering on marvin (bottom → top)

1. **SPI transport (MCC-generated PLib).** Enable a free FLEXCOM in SPI-master mode (FLEXCOM0/3–7 are free; 1=fretboard UART, 2=console, 8=I2C). GPIO for `CS_N`, `IRQ_N` (PIO ext-interrupt), `RST`. Wire init in `config/default/initialization.c` alongside the existing FLEXCOM/driver setup.
2. **OA TC6 chunk driver (vendored + glue).** Vendor `oa-tc6-lib`'s hardware-agnostic core. Implement its SPI-transaction callback against the FLEXCOM SPI PLib and raise its RX path from an `IRQ_N` PIO interrupt → FreeRTOS task notification (reuse the `xSemaphoreGiveFromISR` pattern from `fretboard_link.c:89`). Control transactions used for register init. *Confirm the lib's exact callback/API names against the repo during step 1.*
3. **MAC-PHY init (LAN8651).** Reset, read device-ID register (first SPI sanity check), set MAC address, configure **PLCA as coordinator** (this node = PLCA ID 0, node-count = max nodes), enable TX/RX, unmask `IRQ_N`.
4. **L2 framing + node addressing.** Prepend/parse the 14-byte Ethernet header. Static **node directory** maps `{PLCA ID, MAC, node_type} → detector_id / actuator target`. RX demuxes by src MAC → node; TX addresses a specific node. No discovery protocol (keeps the M0+ side dumb) — static table now, design-for-N.
5. **Transport abstraction under the link API.** Generalize the link so a node dimension is first-class, and select UART vs T1S by compile flag (default UART; T1S opt-in for bring-up).

### Addressing scheme (proposed; design-for-N, static)
- marvin = PLCA **coordinator, ID 0**, locally-administered MAC `02:00:00:00:00:00`.
- node *k* = PLCA **ID k**, MAC `02:00:00:00:00:0k`; `node_type` (guitar/fretboard vs photo-detector) in the node table.
- One **custom ethertype** (propose a local/experimental value, e.g. `0x88B5`); existing 17-byte ADC frame and 1-byte bitmask ride inside the payload **unchanged**.
- `detector_state_t.detector_id` (already `uint8_t`, `detector.h:33`) is the bus-side identity; the node table maps node→`detector_id`. The single physical fretboard stays `detector_id = 1` as today.

## Files

**New (hand-authored, kept OUT of the MCC-generated `config/default/` tree to avoid project-file regeneration — see memory `project_mplab_build`):**
- `firmware/marvin/default/src/net/t1s/` — vendored `oa-tc6-lib` core + SPI/IRQ glue, MAC-PHY init, L2 framing, node table. Written portably so the fretboard reuses the TC6 + L2 layer.

**Modified (marvin):**
- `config/default/initialization.c` — FLEXCOM SPI PLib init + `CS_N`/`IRQ_N`/`RST` GPIO + T1S driver init.
- `config/default/definitions.h` — driver/PLib includes.
- `default/src/actuator/fretboard_link.c` / `.h` — add T1S transport behind the existing submit-queue + RX-to-bus structure; introduce node dimension; `MARVIN_FRETBOARD_TRANSPORT={UART,T1S}` build flag (default UART). Keep `FretboardLink_{Initialize,Send,IsConnected}` working; `Send` gains a node target (default node for the single link).
- `app.c` — unchanged call site if the flag lives inside the module; otherwise swap init.
- `cmake/marvin/default/user.cmake` — append the new `src/net/t1s/` sources.

**Docs (update, don't restate plans in chat — per project rule):**
- `docs/t1s-podl-link.md` — add multi-node addressing/PLCA-ID map; correct "bare-metal" → FreeRTOS+Harmony (no netdev, so own TC6 still required); resolve the topology open item to "PLCA coordinator on marvin."
- `firmware/marvin/docs/journal.md` + `spec.md` (§4.4 transport, §6) — decisions + phased progress.
- `firmware/fretboard/docs/journal.md` — note the shared portable TC6/L2 layer and node-ID scheme for the M0+ side.

## Phased steps

1. **SPI + GPIO bring-up:** enable FLEXCOM SPI PLib + pins; vendor `oa-tc6-lib`; first control transaction reads LAN8651 device ID. *Gate: correct ID over SPI.*
2. **MAC-PHY + PLCA init:** reset/config sequence, MAC address, PLCA coordinator (ID 0), enable TX/RX, `IRQ_N` → task. *Gate: PLCA status reads healthy.*
3. **L2 framing + node table:** TX a hand-built Ethernet frame; RX-demux by src MAC. *Gate: loopback / single-node frame round-trips.*
4. **Wire under the link API:** route the 17-byte RX → `PERF_REC_FRETBOARD_RAW`/detector bus and 1-byte TX exactly as the UART path does, selected by the build flag. *Gate: T1S path matches UART path behavior end-to-end.*
5. **Docs + journals** updated as each gate lands.

## Verification

- **SPI/TC6:** control-transaction read of LAN8651 device-ID and PLCA status registers (step 1–2 gates). Surface a `t1s` status command via the existing console CLI (`console/console.c`).
- **End-to-end vs UART baseline:** with `MARVIN_FRETBOARD_TRANSPORT=T1S`, confirm fretboard's 17-byte ADC frames arrive, parse, and emit `PERF_REC_FRETBOARD_RAW` on the same `frame_epoch` cadence as the UART path; confirm marvin's 1-byte bitmask drives the fretboard. Compare perf-log streams UART vs T1S — records should be indistinguishable above the transport.
- **Multidrop sanity:** verify PLCA beacon/ID 0 coordinator behavior on the 2-node bus (scope/PLCA status) so adding node *k* later needs only a node-table entry, no transport changes.

74	/* Last send result + timestamp, snapshotted into the ACTUATOR record so the

77	static volatile int32_t  s_last_ack_result;

80	static void rx_event_handler(FLEXCOM_USART_EVENT event, uintptr_t context)
81	{
82	    (void)context;
83	    BaseType_t hpw = pdFALSE;
84	
85	    switch (event)
86	    {
87	        case FLEXCOM_USART_EVENT_READ_THRESHOLD_REACHED:
88	        case FLEXCOM_USART_EVENT_READ_BUFFER_FULL:
89	            (void)xSemaphoreGiveFromISR(s_rx_notify, &hpw);
90	            break;
91	        case FLEXCOM_USART_EVENT_READ_ERROR:
92	            /* Consume + clear the error status; the resync parser recovers
93	             * frame alignment on the next valid start/end pair. */
94	            (void)FLEXCOM1_USART_ErrorGet();
95	            (void)xSemaphoreGiveFromISR(s_rx_notify, &hpw);
96	            break;
97	        default:
98	            break;
99	    }
100	
101	    portYIELD_FROM_ISR(hpw);
102	}

104	static bool send_one_byte(uint8_t mask)
105	{
106	    if (!s_link_up) { return false; }
107	
108	    uint8_t tx_byte = (uint8_t)(mask & 0x7F);
109	
110	    /* Ring-buffer Write copies the byte into the TX ring and returns the
111	     * count accepted; for a single byte this only fails if the TX ring is
112	     * full, which shouldn't happen at command rates. */
113	    if (FLEXCOM1_USART_Write(&tx_byte, 1u) != 1u)

123	    PerfLog_EmitStamp(PERF_STAGE_CDC_WRITE_COMPLETE, 0u, 0u);
124	    return true;
125	}

127	static void fretboard_link_task(void *param)
128	{
129	    (void)param;
130	
131	    LOG_INFO("FBL: fretboard link started (FLEXCOM1)\r\n");
132	
133	    uint8_t last_mask = 0u;
134	
135	    for (;;)
136	    {
137	        uint8_t mask;
138	        if (xQueueReceive(s_cmd_queue, &mask, pdMS_TO_TICKS(FBL_HEARTBEAT_MS)) == pdTRUE)
139	        {
140	            last_mask = mask;
141	        }
142	        else
143	        {
144	            mask = last_mask;
145	        }
146	
147	        (void)send_one_byte(mask);
148	    }
149	}
150	
151	/* Drain the FLEXCOM1 RX ring and emit one PERF_REC_FRETBOARD_RAW per parsed
152	 * 17-byte frame. Resync logic mirrors tools/ds_monitor.py: a frame is valid
153	 * only when buf[0]==0x03 AND buf[16]==0xFC; otherwise drop the leading byte
154	 * and retry alignment. The FSM-free buffered approach is easier to reason
155	 * about than a state machine and the frame is short. */
156	static void fretboard_rx_task(void *param)
157	{
158	    (void)param;
159	
160	    uint8_t  frame[DS_FRAME_LEN];
161	    size_t   filled = 0u;
162	    uint32_t parsed = 0u;
163	    uint32_t skipped_bytes = 0u;
164	
165	    for (;;)
166	    {
167	        if (FLEXCOM1_USART_ReadCountGet() == 0u)
168	        {
169	            (void)xSemaphoreTake(s_rx_notify, pdMS_TO_TICKS(FBL_RX_WAIT_MS));
170	            continue;
171	        }
172	
173	        size_t want = DS_FRAME_LEN - filled;
174	        size_t got  = FLEXCOM1_USART_Read(&frame[filled], want);
175	        if (got == 0u) { continue; }
176	        filled += got;
177	        if (filled < DS_FRAME_LEN) { continue; }
178	
179	        if (frame[0] != DS_START_BYTE || frame[DS_FRAME_LEN - 1u] != DS_END_BYTE)
180	        {
181	            /* Misaligned: drop one byte and shift, then loop to refill. */
182	            memmove(&frame[0], &frame[1], DS_FRAME_LEN - 1u);
183	            filled = DS_FRAME_LEN - 1u;
184	            skipped_bytes++;
185	            continue;
186	        }
187	
188	        uint16_t adc[FRET_COUNT];
189	        for (uint8_t i = 0u; i < FRET_COUNT; i++)
190	        {
191	            adc[i] = (uint16_t)frame[1u + i * 2u]
192	                   | (uint16_t)((uint16_t)frame[2u + i * 2u] << 8);
193	        }
194	
195	        /* seq: u32 LE at bytes 11-14, applied_mask: u8 at byte 15. */
196	        uint32_t fb_seq = (uint32_t)frame[11]
197	                        | ((uint32_t)frame[12] << 8)
198	                        | ((uint32_t)frame[13] << 16)
199	                        | ((uint32_t)frame[14] << 24);
200	        uint8_t  applied_mask = frame[15];
201	
202	        Video_FrameInfo info;
203	        Video_GetFrameInfo(&info);
204	        PerfLog_EmitFretboardRaw(adc, info.frame_count, fb_seq, applied_mask);
205	
206	        parsed++;
207	        if (parsed == 1u || (parsed % 240u) == 0u)
208	        {
209	            LOG_DEBUG("FBL: rx parsed=%u skipped=%u G=%u R=%u Y=%u B=%u O=%u\r\n",
210	                      (unsigned)parsed, (unsigned)skipped_bytes,
211	                      (unsigned)adc[0], (unsigned)adc[1], (unsigned)adc[2],
212	                      (unsigned)adc[3], (unsigned)adc[4]);
213	        }
214	
215	        filled = 0u;
216	    }
217	}

219	void FretboardLink_Initialize(void)
220	{
221	    s_cmd_queue = xQueueCreateStatic(FBL_CMD_QUEUE_DEPTH,
222	                                     sizeof(uint8_t),
223	                                     s_cmd_queue_storage,
224	                                     &s_cmd_queue_buf);
225	    configASSERT(s_cmd_queue != NULL);
226	
227	    s_rx_notify = xSemaphoreCreateBinaryStatic(&s_rx_notify_buf);
228	    configASSERT(s_rx_notify != NULL);
229	
230	    /* Arm continuous RX: the ring fills from the FLEXCOM1 ISR; persistent
231	     * threshold notification wakes fretboard_rx_task each time a frame's
232	     * worth of bytes is available. */
233	    FLEXCOM1_USART_ReadCallbackRegister(rx_event_handler, 0u);
234	    FLEXCOM1_USART_ReadThresholdSet(FBL_RX_THRESHOLD);
235	    (void)FLEXCOM1_USART_ReadNotificationEnable(true, true);
236	
237	    s_link_up = true;
238	
239	    TaskHandle_t h = xTaskCreateStatic(fretboard_link_task,
240	                                       "FretLink",
241	                                       FBL_TASK_STACK_WORDS,
242	                                       NULL,
243	                                       FBL_TASK_PRIORITY,
244	                                       s_task_stack,
245	                                       &s_task_tcb);
246	    PerfLog_RegisterTaskForHighwater(PERF_TASK_FRETBOARD_LINK, h);
247	
248	    TaskHandle_t hr = xTaskCreateStatic(fretboard_rx_task,
249	                                        "FretRx",
250	                                        FBL_RX_TASK_STACK_WORDS,
251	                                        NULL,
252	                                        FBL_TASK_PRIORITY,
253	                                        s_rx_task_stack,
254	                                        &s_rx_task_tcb);
255	    PerfLog_RegisterTaskForHighwater(PERF_TASK_FRETBOARD_RX, hr);
256	}
257	
258	bool FretboardLink_IsConnected(void)
259	{
260	    return s_link_up;
261	}
262	
263	void FretboardLink_Send(uint8_t mask, uint8_t producer_id)
264	{
265	    if (s_cmd_queue == NULL) { return; }
266	    uint8_t v = (uint8_t)(mask & TIMING_BIT_VALID_MASK);
267	    /* Overwrite is strictly latest-wins: a newer producer's mask replaces
268	     * any unsent older one — keeps a stalled write from accumulating
269	     * stale chord state. */
270	    (void)xQueueOverwrite(s_cmd_queue, &v);
271	
272	    uint8_t strum_dir = 0u;
273	    if      (v & TIMING_BIT_STRUM_DOWN) { strum_dir = 1u; }
274	    else if (v & TIMING_BIT_STRUM_UP)   { strum_dir = 2u; }
275	
276	    PerfLog_EmitActuator(v, s_last_sent_byte, strum_dir, producer_id,
277	                         s_last_ack_result, s_last_ack_ts_counter);
278	}

Fix is additive (new helper, two new call sites, no refactor of existing IRPSubmit body), making it easy to find/maintain after MCC regen. Future Harmony versions may obviate this if upstream wires it up. |
46	| 2026-05-29 | Strip queue uses 1-byte slot indices into a static `s_strip_pool[depth+2]` instead of pass-by-value `perf_rec_strip_t` items. | FreeRTOS queues are pass-by-value: every `xQueueSend`/`xQueueReceive` does `memcpy(slot, src, item_size)` inside a critical section (interrupts disabled). At `sizeof(perf_rec_strip_t) = 23-61 KB`, that was 38-100 µs of interrupts-off time per queue op × ~240 ops/s. Pool-and-index pattern moves the pixel data into a static pool indexed by 1-byte handles; queue ops drop to 1 µs critical sections. Same total BSS footprint (eliminates the producer's `static r;` and drain's `static s_strip_drain;` — pool size matches old "queue + 2 staging" footprint). Pool size `depth + 2` covers "1 slot in producer's hand + 1 in drain's hand" while preserving drop-on-full semantics. |
47	| 2026-05-29 | Fletcher-16 (mod 255, init 0xFFFF) replaces CRC-16/CCITT-FALSE in the framing layer. `crc_*` field names renamed to `fcs_*` end-to-end. | USB hardware already CRCs every bulk packet on the wire; our framing-layer checksum's job is *firmware-side framing-bug detection* and *resync alignment* (false SOF in the middle of a corrupt stream). Fletcher-16 catches single-byte changes, adjacent swaps, and most non-adjacent swaps with ~1/65536 false-positive rate against random byte streams — sufficient for that job at ~2 cycles/byte (vs ~25 cycles for the bit-by-bit CRC, ~6 cycles for table-driven). SAM9X75 has no CRCCU peripheral (verified against `packs/SAM9X75D2G_DFP/component/`), so DMA-driven CRC isn't available. Wire format unchanged (still SOF+LEN+payload+16-bit checksum). One-shot wire-format break — old `.bin` captures aren't readable with new code; fine for dev. |
48	| 2026-05-29 | Single `PERF_STRIP_MAX_BYTES = 65000u` constant; `PERF_STRIP_MAX_W`/`MAX_H` removed. | The W×H pair was arbitrary — producer code only ever checks total bytes (`w * h * BPP <= PERF_STRIP_MAX_BYTES`). Real binding constraint is the wire LEN field, which is `uint16_t` → max 65535 byte payload → max ~65 KB pixel per strip. Tighter than the UDPHS DMA cap (128 KB at `DRV_USB_UDPHS_DMA_MAX_TRANSFER_SIZE = 2`). Picking 65000 lands just under the LEN cap with margin. Producer accepts any (w, h) shape under that — practical envelope at 60 fps: 720×30, 480×45, 320×64, 290×72. Going beyond requires bumping LEN to u32, which is a wire-format break and not worth doing casually since wire bandwidth caps out around the same point at 60 fps. |
49	| 2026-05-29 | Default-disable high-rate perf-log record types at firmware boot — start mask is `DROP | TASK_HIGHWATER | TASK_RUNTIME` only; STAMP, DETECTOR, TIMING, STRIP off until host enables. | Avoids the unattended-firmware case where boot generates multi-MB/s of strip records that all get dropped at the sink (no DTR), burning producer-side CPU on framing/Fletcher work that goes nowhere. Host viewer enables higher-rate types via `PERF_CMD_SET_TYPE_MASK` on attach (the live mode's mask UI). SESSION is always emitted regardless of mask so the host gets `timer_freq_hz` on attach. |
50	| 2026-05-21 | `configMAX_PRIORITIES` bumped 5 → 8; tasks re-tiered into 4 active bands (UI=2, diagnostic+perf-wire=3, vision=4, strum-critical+host-wire=5) plus 3 reserve bands (1, 6, 7) and idle (0). MCC tasks re-prioritised via the per-component yml files so future regens preserve the layout. | Pre-change layout had 11 tasks bunched at priority 1 (9 MCC pollers + VideoTask + DetectorDrain) and 4 at priority 2, with no headroom. Two concrete problems: (a) VideoTask was *below* its consumer CvMarvinV1, a classic priority inversion that would bite during any priority-2 busy spell; (b) Legato (UI rendering) at the same priority as USB host driver tasks meant a heavy frame redraw could stall fretboard wire transit. The new layout puts strum-critical output above vision-real-time above diagnostic-I/O above UI, which matches the failure-cost ordering: a late strum is a missed note, a late detector tick recovers next frame, a late UI paint is jitter only. Reserve bands cost ~60 B BSS each, leave room for future watchdog or fault-recovery work to land without re-shuffling. Setting priorities in MCC yml (rather than patching `tasks.c` post-regen) avoids a re-apply patch — the source of truth and the emitted code now agree. |
51	| 2026-05-21 | `manual_control` lands as the second producer of `fretboard_link`, alongside `timing_pipeline`. Mode-level arbitration is two-mode (`timing_pipeline` vs `manual_control`) and embedded in `ManualControl_SetEnabled`: entering manual mode calls `TimingPipeline_SetEnabled(false)` then takes the wire; exiting reverses. | First concrete validation of the 2026-05-20 multi-producer `fretboard_link` design — `FretboardLink_Send` stays the only entry point; arbitration lives one layer up. Embedded toggle is enough for two producers; refactor to a dedicated `actuator_mode` arbiter when a third producer (game-state controller §4.8) arrives. `timing_pipeline.publish_mask` keeps updating internal state when gated so the next ≤5 ms tick after re-enable republishes a correct mask without a stale frame. |
52	| 2026-05-21 | Legato chosen for the manual-control surface; widgets authored in Microchip Graphics Composer (regenerated into `le_gen_screen_Screen0.{h,c}`); marvin-side code is a thin event-binding shim (`ui/manual_input.c`) | Composer makes the layout iterable in a tool rather than C source, and keeps our code out of MCC-clobbered files: only the binding shim references the Composer-generated widget pointers. **Does not commit spec Q5 for the full operator UI** — that's still M5's call. The thin-shim shape works equally well behind a future custom GFX2D UI by swapping the bind module. |
53	| 2026-05-21 | Manual-control input model is single-finger momentary; multi-finger chord input is out of scope for this surface | Legato's input pipeline (`legato_input.c:340/429`) routes each touch to a single focus widget, so a second simultaneous touch cancels the first button's release and strands its `pressed` state. Workarounds (custom maxtouch dispatcher; toggle-style frets) are real but not worth the complexity here — primary use case is game-menu navigation, which is single-finger by nature. Revisit only if a user-facing flow needs held chords. |
54	| 2026-05-21 | `fret_t` lives in `game/fret.h`, a top-level domain header. Detector / actuator / UI all include it directly; detector.h re-includes it so `detector_state_t` still compiles cleanly. | The fret colors (G/R/Y/B/O) are a Guitar Hero / Rock Band domain primitive, not a detector concept — the actuator and UI shouldn't reach into `detector/` for them. `game/` also stakes out the directory the future game-state controller (spec §4.8) will land in, so we don't have a transient home. Header-only, no cmake change. |
55	| 2026-05-20 | Relax Microchip's host CDC-ACM Communications-interface protocol check to accept `bInterfaceProtocol == 0x00 (None)` in addition to `0x01 (AT_V250)` | The fretboard hardware exposes its UART to marvin via the on-board EDBG debugger's CDC ACM (composite VID=0x03EB PID=0x2175: HID + CDC ACM IAD + vendor + MSC). EDBG declares the comm interface with `bInterfaceProtocol=0x00` rather than the AT-command protocol Microchip hardcodes. The TPL/IAD match accepts the device (host stack does call `interfaceAssign`), but the per-interface check inside `F_USB_HOST_CDC_InterfaceAssign` then rejects the comm interface, the interrupt pipe never opens, the CDC instance flips to STATE_ERROR, and our attach handler never fires. Both are CDC ACM in practice and Linux/macOS accept either. Two-line OR per check in `usb_host_cdc.c`; logged as patch #7 in the re-apply list. |
56	| 2026-05-20 | `USB_HOST_Initialize` ordering relative to `DRV_USB_EHCI/OHCI_Initialize` and `Legato_Initialize` is **not** load-bearing — keep MCC's emitted order | A prior session hand-edited `initialization.c` to move `USB_HOST_Initialize` *after* the EHCI/OHCI driver inits on the theory that the host layer needed the HCD interfaces present at init time. Empirical retest with the CDC diagnostic logging in place: MCC's original order (`USB_HOST_Initialize` → `Legato_Initialize` → driver inits) enumerates and binds the CDC IAD just as well. The host layer evidently looks up HCD interfaces lazily at `USB_HOST_BusEnable` time, not at `USB_HOST_Initialize`. Reverted the hand-edit; one fewer re-apply patch to maintain. (This is unrelated to patch #6, which is the *peripheral* init order — MMU/AIC ahead of TC0/FLEXCOM6/XLCDC — that one is still a real regression and stays in the list.) |
57	| 2026-05-20 | Marvin replaces the fret-tuner PC as the runtime brain | One-host architecture. fret-tuner persists as an off-band dev/calibration tool. fretboard stays a dumb relay (ADC out, bitmask in). |
58	| 2026-05-20 | Marvin is the *reference detector* — not a debug aid | HDMI-direct CV is ground-truth for the system. Fretboard's photo-detection and any future Edge-AI MCU are trained against marvin's output. Recording reference data is therefore a first-class subsystem (spec §4.6), not an afterthought. |
59	| 2026-05-20 | Multiple coexisting detectors are in scope; one canonical detector-state bus | At minimum `cv_marvin_v1` (CV) and `adc_fretboard` (over UART ingest). Bus shape: typed `detector_state_t` records on a FreeRTOS queue, single-consumer (timing pipeline). Recording snoops via tee from each producer. Spec §4.2. |

Latency budget allows a few ms of UART jitter. Fallback mode disables marvin's pipeline; fretboard runs its own existing `fret_button.c` and feeds emitted-command telemetry up to marvin for capture/display. Spec §4.4 + §6. |

Device Operation\nThe AT25512 is controlled by a set of instructions that are sent from a host controller, commonly referred to as the SPI Host. The SPI Host communicates with the AT25512 via the SPI bus which is comprised of four signal lines: Chip Select (CS), Serial Data Clock (SCK), Serial Data Input (SI) and Serial Data Output (SO).\n\nThe SPI protocol defines a total of four modes of operation (Mode 0, 1, 2 or 3) with each mode differing in respect to the SCK polarity and phase and how the polarity and phase control the flow of data on the SPI bus. The AT25512 supports the two most common modes, SPI Modes 0 and 3. With SPI Modes 0 and 3, data is always latched in on the rising edge of SCK and always output on the falling edge of SCK. The only difference between SPI Modes 0 and 3 is the polarity of the SCK signal when in the Inactive state (when the SPI Host is in Standby mode and not transferring any data). SPI Mode 0 is defined as a low SCK while CS is not asserted (at VCC) and SPI Mode 3 has SCK high in the Inactive state. The SCK Idle state must match when the CS is deasserted both before and after the communication sequence in SPI Mode 0 and 3. The figures in this document depict Mode 0 with a solid line on SCK while CS is inactive and Mode 3 with a dotted line.\n\nFigure 5-1. SPI Mode 0 and Mode 3\n\n5.1 Interfacing the AT25512 on the SPI Bus\nCommunication to and from the AT25512 must be initiated by the SPI Host device, such as a microcontroller. The SPI Host device must generate the serial clock for the AT25512 on the Serial Data Clock (SCK) pin. The AT25512 always operates as a client due to the fact that the SCK is always an input.\n\n5.1.1 Selecting the Device\nThe AT25512 is selected when the Chip Select (CS) pin is low. When the device is not selected, data will not be accepted via the Serial Data Input (SI) pin, and the Serial Data Output (SO) pin will remain in a high-impedance state.\n\n5.1.2 Sending Data to the Device\nThe AT25512 uses the SI pin to receive information. All instructions, addresses and data input bytes are clocked into the device with the Most Significant bit (MSb) first. The SI pin samples on the first rising edge of the SCK line after the CS has been asserted.\n\n5.1.3 Receiving Data from the Device\nData output from the device is transmitted on the SO pin, with the MSb output first. The SO data is latched on the first falling edge of SCK after the instruction has been clocked into the device, such as the Read from Memory Array (READ) and Read STATUS Register (RDSR) instructions. See Read Sequence for more details.\n\n\u00A9 2019-2021 Microchip Technology Inc. The clock polarity is specified by the CPOL control bit, which selects an active high or active low clock. The clock phase (CPHA) control bit selects one of the two fundamentally different transfer formats. To ensure a proper communication between master and slave both devices have to run in the same mode. This might require a reconfiguration of the master to match the requirements of different peripheral slaves. The settings of CPOL and CPHA that specify the different SPI modes are shown in the following table. | SPI mode | CPOL | CPHA | Shift SCK-Edge | Capture SCK-Edge | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 0 | 0 | 0 | Falling | Rising | | 1 | 0 | 1 | Rising | Falling | | 2 | 1 | 0 | Rising | Falling | | 3 | 1 | 1 | Falling | Rising | The clock polarity has no significant effect on the transfer format. Switching this bit causes the clock signal to be inverted (active high becomes active low and idle low becomes idle high). When CKP is clear (CKP = 0), the idle state is low as seen in modes 0 and 1. This means that when CKP is set (CKP = 1), the idle state is high as seen in modes 2 and 3. \r\n\r\nCKE is the clock phase, or in our definition, clock edge. This determines the clock edge that is used for transmission, or in other words, the edge that the module will transmit data. When CKE is clear (CKE = 0), the module will transmit data on the clock edge that occurs when the clock is switching from the active to the idle state, shown in modes 0 and 2. When CKE is set (CKE = 1), data is transmitted on the clock edge as it transitions from idle to active, as seen in modes 1 and 3. \r\n\r\nBelow is an excerpt from the SPI Block Guide V03.06 from Motorola, who developed the SPI protocol: \r\n\r\nCPOL \u2014 SPI Clock Polarity Bit \r\nThis bit selects an inverted or non-inverted SPI clock. To transmit data between SPI modules, the SPI modules must have identical CPOL values. In master mode, a change of this bit will abort a transmission in progress and force the SPI system into idle state.\r\n\r\n1 = Active-low clocks selected. In idle state SCK is high. \r\n0 = Active-high clocks selected. In idle state SCK is low.\r\n\r\nCPHA \u2014 SPI Clock Phase Bit \r\nThis bit is used to select the SPI clock format. In master mode, a change of this bit will abort a transmission in progress and force the SPI system into idle state.\r\n\r\n**1 = Sampling of data occurs at even edges (2,4,6,...,16) of the SCK clock 0 = Sampling of data occurs at odd edges (1,3,5,...,15) of the SCK clock**\r\n\r\nSo if you examine the waveforms, they appear to match the definitions specified in the Motorola protocol. The problem is that the data sheet does in fact incorrectly describe the CKE: \r\n\r\nbit 6 CKE: SPI Clock Select bit(1) \r\n1 = Transmit occurs on transition from active to Idle clock state \r\n0 = Transmit occurs on transition from Idle to active clock state \r\n\r\nTake mode 0 for example \u2013 the idle state for the clock is low, and the third clock edge shown is the one that is sampled. The sampling edge is the edge that the master samples the MISO line.\r\n\r\n**Note:**\r\nthe datasheets will be reviewed and corrected with the CKE description. Other datasheets with the same module will be also reviewed and corrected.\n\n## Root Cause\n\n\n## Summary\n\n\n## Symptoms\n\n\n## Workaround\n","url":"https://support.microchip.com/s/article/SPI-Mode-clock-polarity-and-phase-reword-for-PIC18F-microcontrollers?utm_source=mchpmcp","keywords":[],"relevancyScore":104.938896},{"title":"25CSM04 4-Mbit SPI Serial EEPROM with 128-Bit Serial Number and Enhanced Write Protection - page13.md","content":"4.0 FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION\n\n4.1 Device Operation\n\nThe 25CSM04 is controlled by a set of instructions that are sent from a host controller, commonly referred to as the SPI host. The SPI host communicates with the 25CSM04 via the SPI bus which is comprised of four signal lines:\n\u2022 Chip Select (CS)\n\u2022 Serial Clock (SCK)\n\u2022 Serial Input (SI)\n\u2022 Serial Output (SO)\n\nThe SPI protocol defines a total of four modes of operation (Mode 0, 1, 2, or 3) with each mode differing in respect to the SCK polarity and phase and how the polarity and phase control the flow of data on the SPI bus. The 25CSM04 supports the two most common modes, SPI Mode 0 and 3. With SPI Modes 0 and 3, data are always latched in on the rising edge of SCK and always output on the falling edge of SCK. The only difference between SPI Modes 0 and 3 is the polarity of the SCK signal when in the inactive state (when the SPI host is in Standby mode and not transferring any data). SPI Mode 0 is defined as a low SCK while CS is not asserted (high) and SPI Mode 3 has SCK high in the inactive state. The SCK idle state must match when the CS is deasserted both before and after the communication sequence in SPI Mode 0 and 3.\n\nThe figures in this document depict Mode 0 with a solid line on SCK while CS is inactive and Mode 3 with a dotted line.\n\nFIGURE 4-1: SPI MODE 0 AND MODE 3\n\nCS\nMode 3\nMode 0\nSCK\nMode 3\nMode 0\nSI\nMSb\nLSb\nSO\nMSb\nLSb\n\n4.2 Interfacing the 25CSM04 on the SPI Bus\n\nCommunication to and from the 25CSM04 must be initiated by the SPI host device. The SPI host device must generate the serial clock for the 25CSM04 on the SCK pin. The 25CSM04 always operates as a client due to the fact that the Serial Clock pin (SCK) is always an input.\n\n4.2.1 SELECTING THE DEVICE\n\nThe 25CSM04 is selected when the CS pin is low. When the device is not selected, data will not be accepted via the SI pin and the SO pin will remain in a high-impedance state.\n\n4.2.2 SENDING DATA TO THE DEVICE\n\nThe 25CSM04 uses the Serial Data Input (SI) pin to receive information. All instructions, addresses and data input bytes are clocked into the device with the Most Significant bit (MSb) first. The SI pin begins sampling on the first rising edge of the SCK line after the CS has been asserted.\n\n4.2.3 RECEIVING DATA FROM THE DEVICE\n\nData output from the device is transmitted on the Serial Data Output (SO) pin with the MSb output first. The SO data are latched on the falling edge of the first SCK clock cycle after the instruction and address bytes, if necessary, have been clocked into the device.\n\n\u00A9 2019-2022 Microchip Technology Inc. and its subsidiaries\n\nDS20005817D-page 13","url":"https://ww1.microchip.com/downloads/aemDocuments/documents/MPD/ProductDocuments/DataSheets/25CSM04-4-Mbit-SPI-Serial-EEPROM-with-128-Bit-Serial-Number-and-Enhanced-Write-Protection-20005817D.pdf?utm_source=mchpmcp#page=13","keywords":["25CSM04 4-Mbit SPI Serial EEPROM with 128-Bit Serial Number and Enhanced Write Protection","25CSM04","page13.md"],"relevancyScore":68.68167}]},"timestamp":"2026-06-16T18:19:51Z"}

Serial Peripheral Interface (SPI)
The LAN8650/1 is designed to conform to the OPEN Alliance 10BASE‑T1x MAC‑PHY Serial Interface

integration within the microcontroller.

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-16 18:21:14Z)**_

Yes — confirmed straight from the LAN8650/1 datasheet (DS60001734, §5.1 *SPI Format* + §9 timing), not from memory:

## SPI Mode 0 — CPOL = 0, CPHA = 0

The datasheet states:

> "On the rising edge of SCLK the data is **captured**, while on the falling edge of SCLK the data will **change**. The data on SDI and SDO is always transferred **most significant bit/byte first**."

And the AC timing table lists **`tcss` — "CS_N low to SCLK rising"**, i.e. the first clock edge after chip-select asserts is a *rising* edge → **SCLK idles low**. Idle-low (CPOL=0) + sample-on-leading-rising-edge (CPHA=0) is unambiguously **SPI Mode 0**.

This isn't LAN8651-specific — it's mandated by the **OPEN Alliance 10BASE-T1x MAC-PHY Serial Interface spec v1.1** that the part conforms to, so the fretboard PIC32CM side uses the same mode.

**Concrete settings for the marvin FLEXCOM SPI config (and the fretboard SERCOM later):**

| Parameter | Value |
|---|---|
| Clock polarity (CPOL) | **0** — SCLK idle low |
| Clock phase (CPHA) | **0** — sample on leading (rising) edge, shift on falling |
| Bit order | **MSB first** |
| Max SCLK | **25 MHz** (datasheet ceiling; marvin's FLEXCOM SPI master tops out around GCLK/2 anyway) |
| CS | active-low, **CS_N idles high** |
| Word size | 8-bit |

In MPLAB Harmony terms when you set up the FLEXCOM SPI: **Clock Polarity = Idle Low**, **Clock Phase = Valid Leading Edge** (Harmony's wording for the "leading edge" capture used by `SPI_CLOCK_PHASE_VALID_LEADING_EDGE`). A couple of Harmony SPI PLibs label the phase the opposite way in the dropdown, so if the device-ID read comes back as `0x00`/`0xFF` during Phase-1 bring-up, flipping the phase setting is the first thing to try — but per the datasheet the target is **Mode 0**.

One bring-up note worth flagging now: a few SPI-master peripherals also need **CS held low across the whole multi-byte TC6 chunk transaction** (header + 64-byte data), so if the FLEXCOM SPI PLib's hardware-controlled CS toggles per byte, we'll drive CS_N as a plain GPIO instead — something to watch when the PLib lands.

Want me to record the SPI-mode finding in the T1S doc (§2, the LAN8651 hardware section) so it's captured before bring-up? It's a small, factual addition to the engineering detail.

69	void FLEXCOM4_SPI_Initialize ( void )
70	{

72	    FLEXCOM4_REGS->FLEX_MR = FLEX_MR_OPMODE_SPI;
73	
74	    /* Disable and Reset the FLEXCOM SPI */
75	    FLEXCOM4_REGS->FLEX_SPI_CR = FLEX_SPI_CR_SPIDIS_Msk | FLEX_SPI_CR_SWRST_Msk;
76	
77	    FLEXCOM4_REGS->FLEX_SPI_CR = FLEX_SPI_CR_FIFOEN_Msk;
