80	    FLEXCOM4_REGS->FLEX_SPI_MR = FLEX_SPI_MR_MSTR_Msk | FLEX_SPI_MR_BRSRCCLK_PERIPH_CLK | FLEX_SPI_MR_DLYBCS(0U) | FLEX_SPI_MR_PCS((uint32_t)FLEXCOM_SPI_CHIP_SELECT_NPCS0) | FLEX_SPI_MR_MODFDIS_Msk;
81	
82	    /* Set up clock Polarity, data phase, Communication Width, Baud Rate */
83	    FLEXCOM4_REGS->FLEX_SPI_CSR[0]= FLEX_SPI_CSR_CPOL(0U) | FLEX_SPI_CSR_NCPHA(1U) | FLEX_SPI_CSR_BITS_8_BIT | FLEX_SPI_CSR_SCBR(255U) | FLEX_SPI_CSR_DLYBS(0U) | FLEX_SPI_CSR_DLYBCT(0U)  | FLEX_SPI_CSR_CSAAT_Msk ;
84	
85	
86	
87	
88	    /* Initialize global variables */
89	    flexcom4SpiObj.transferIsBusy = false;
90	    flexcom4SpiObj.callback = NULL;
91	
92	    /* Enable FLEXCOM4 SPI */
93	    FLEXCOM4_REGS->FLEX_SPI_CR = FLEX_SPI_CR_SPIEN_Msk;
94	    return;

100	static uint8_t FLEXCOM4_SPI_FIFO_Fill(void)
101	{
102	    uint8_t nDataCopiedToFIFO = 0;
103	    uint32_t dataBits = FLEXCOM4_REGS->FLEX_SPI_CSR[0] & FLEX_SPI_CSR_BITS_Msk;
104	
105	    size_t txCount = flexcom4SpiObj.txCount;
106	
107	    while ((nDataCopiedToFIFO < 16U) && ((FLEXCOM4_REGS->FLEX_SPI_SR & FLEX_SPI_SR_TDRE_Msk) != 0U))
108	    {
109	        if(dataBits == FLEX_SPI_CSR_BITS_8_BIT)
110	        {
111	            if (txCount < flexcom4SpiObj.txSize)
112	            {
113	                FLEXCOM_SPI_TDR_8BIT_REG =  ((uint8_t*)flexcom4SpiObj.txBuffer)[txCount];
114	                txCount++;
115	            }
116	            else if (flexcom4SpiObj.dummySize > 0U)
117	            {
118	                FLEXCOM_SPI_TDR_8BIT_REG = (uint8_t)(0xff);
119	                flexcom4SpiObj.dummySize--;
120	            }
121	            else
122	            {
123	                break;
124	            }
125	        }
126	        else
127	        {
128	            if (txCount < flexcom4SpiObj.txSize)
129	            {
130	                FLEXCOM_SPI_TDR_9BIT_REG =  ((uint16_t*)flexcom4SpiObj.txBuffer)[txCount];
131	                txCount++;
132	            }
133	            else if (flexcom4SpiObj.dummySize > 0U)
134	            {
135	                FLEXCOM_SPI_TDR_9BIT_REG = (uint16_t)(0xffff);
136	                flexcom4SpiObj.dummySize--;
137	            }
138	            else
139	            {
140	                break;
141	            }
142	        }
143	
144	        nDataCopiedToFIFO++;
145	    }
146	
147	    flexcom4SpiObj.txCount = txCount;
148	
149	    return nDataCopiedToFIFO;
150	}
151	
152	bool FLEXCOM4_SPI_WriteRead (void* pTransmitData, size_t txSize, void* pReceiveData, size_t rxSize)
153	{
154	    bool isRequestAccepted = false;
155	    uint32_t nTxPending = 0;
156	    uint8_t rxThreshold = 0;
157	    /* Verify the request */
158	    if((flexcom4SpiObj.transferIsBusy == false) && (((txSize > 0U) && (pTransmitData != NULL)) || ((rxSize > 0U) && (pReceiveData != NULL))))
159	    {
160	        isRequestAccepted = true;
161	        flexcom4SpiObj.txBuffer = pTransmitData;
162	        flexcom4SpiObj.rxBuffer = pReceiveData;
163	        flexcom4SpiObj.rxCount = 0;
164	        flexcom4SpiObj.txCount = 0;
165	        flexcom4SpiObj.dummySize = 0;
166	
167	        if (pTransmitData != NULL)
168	        {
169	            flexcom4SpiObj.txSize = txSize;
170	        }
171	        else
172	        {
173	            flexcom4SpiObj.txSize = 0;
174	        }
175	
176	        if (pReceiveData != NULL)
177	        {
178	            flexcom4SpiObj.rxSize = rxSize;
179	        }
180	        else
181	        {
182	            flexcom4SpiObj.rxSize = 0;
183	        }
184	
185	        flexcom4SpiObj.transferIsBusy = true;
186	
187	        size_t txSz = flexcom4SpiObj.txSize;
188	
189	        if (flexcom4SpiObj.rxSize > txSz)
190	        {
191	            flexcom4SpiObj.dummySize = flexcom4SpiObj.rxSize - txSz;
192	        }
193	
194	        if((FLEXCOM4_REGS->FLEX_SPI_CSR[0] & FLEX_SPI_CSR_BITS_Msk) != FLEX_SPI_CSR_BITS_8_BIT)
195	        {
196	            flexcom4SpiObj.txSize >>= 1;
197	            flexcom4SpiObj.dummySize >>= 1;
198	            flexcom4SpiObj.rxSize >>= 1;
199	
200	            txSz = flexcom4SpiObj.txSize;
201	        }
202	
203	        /* Clear TX and RX FIFO */
204	        FLEXCOM4_REGS->FLEX_SPI_CR = (FLEX_SPI_CR_RXFCLR_Msk | FLEX_SPI_CR_TXFCLR_Msk);
205	
206	        nTxPending = (txSz - flexcom4SpiObj.txCount);
207	        nTxPending += flexcom4SpiObj.dummySize;
208	
209	        if (nTxPending < 16U)
210	        {
211	            rxThreshold = (uint8_t)nTxPending;
212	        }
213	        else
214	        {
215	            rxThreshold = 16;
216	        }
217	
218	        /* Set RX FIFO level so as to generate interrupt after all bytes are transmitted and response from slave is received for all the bytes */
219	        /* RX FIFO level must be set first or else FIFO may be filled before RX threshold is set and hardware may not recognize threshold crossover and not generate threshold interrupt */
220	        FLEXCOM4_REGS->FLEX_SPI_FMR = (FLEXCOM4_REGS->FLEX_SPI_FMR & ~FLEX_SPI_FMR_RXFTHRES_Msk) | FLEX_SPI_FMR_RXFTHRES(rxThreshold);
221	
222	        (void) FLEXCOM4_SPI_FIFO_Fill();
223	
224	        /* Enable RX FIFO Threshold interrupt */
225	        FLEXCOM4_REGS->FLEX_SPI_IER = FLEX_SPI_IER_RXFTHF_Msk;
226	    }
227	
228	    return isRequestAccepted;
229	}

231	bool FLEXCOM4_SPI_TransferSetup (FLEXCOM_SPI_TRANSFER_SETUP * setup, uint32_t spiSourceClock )
232	{
233	    uint32_t scbr;
234	    bool setupStatus = false;
235	    if ((setup != NULL) && (setup->clockFrequency != 0U))
236	    {

238	        {
239	            // Fetch Master Clock Frequency directly
240	            spiSourceClock = 266666666;
241	        }
242	
243	        scbr = spiSourceClock/setup->clockFrequency;
244	
245	        if(scbr == 0U)
246	        {
247	            scbr = 1;
248	        }
249	        else if(scbr > 255U)
250	        {
251	            scbr = 255;
252	        }
253	        else
254	        {
255	            /* Do nothing */
256	        }
257	
258	        FLEXCOM4_REGS->FLEX_SPI_CSR[0]= (FLEXCOM4_REGS->FLEX_SPI_CSR[0] & ~(FLEX_SPI_CSR_CPOL_Msk | FLEX_SPI_CSR_NCPHA_Msk | FLEX_SPI_CSR_BITS_Msk | FLEX_SPI_CSR_SCBR_Msk)) | ((uint32_t)setup->clockPolarity | (uint32_t)setup->clockPhase | (uint32_t)setup->dataBits | FLEX_SPI_CSR_SCBR(scbr));
259	
260	        setupStatus = true;
261	    }
262	    return setupStatus;
263	}

Reviewed all the staged FLEXCOM4 files. Here's the verdict.

## ✅ The SPI master itself has everything the TC6 driver needs

| Requirement | Status | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| **SPI Mode 0** (CPOL=0/CPHA=0) | ✅ correct | `plib_flexcom4_spi_master.c:83` — `CPOL(0)` idle-low + `NCPHA(1)` = leading-edge capture (SAM's NCPHA is inverted CPHA, so NCPHA=1 → Mode 0) |
| **Full-duplex transfer** | ✅ | `FLEXCOM4_SPI_WriteRead(tx, txSize, rx, rxSize)` — TC6 clocks a TX chunk out and an RX chunk in simultaneously |
| **CS held across the whole chunk** | ✅ | `CSAAT` set (`:83`) + `LASTXFER` only on completion (`:345`) → NPCS0 stays low for the full header+payload transfer, deasserts at end. **Hardware CS works — no GPIO bit-bang needed**, which resolves the watch-item I flagged earlier |
| **Interrupt-driven + completion callback** | ✅ | `FLEXCOM4_SPI_CallbackRegister`; ISR fires callback at end (`:352`). Wrap with a FreeRTOS semaphore (give-from-ISR, same pattern as `fretboard_link.c`) |
| **Runtime clock/mode setup** | ✅ | `FLEXCOM4_SPI_TransferSetup()` lets us set frequency at init |
| **Init called + interrupt routed** | ✅ | `initialization.c:339` `FLEXCOM4_SPI_Initialize()`; AIC entry `plib_aic.c:73` (periph ID 13, level-sensitive) → `FLEXCOM4_InterruptHandler` |
| **Pins** | ✅ | PA10 MOSI / PA9 MISO / PA11 SCK / PA12 nCS (NPCS0) |

## ⚠️ Two required control GPIOs are missing from the config

The SPI link is complete, but the LAN8651 needs two side-band signals that aren't assigned anywhere in `pin_configurations.csv` (only the 4 SPI pins exist):

1. **`IRQ_N` (LAN8651 → host interrupt)** — the MAC-PHY asserts this active-low when it has received data or a status change. This is how the TC6 service task knows to clock in an RX chunk. Needs a **PIO input**; we can enable the PIO edge/level interrupt in our glue at runtime, so in MCC it just needs to be assigned as a GPIO input (a PIO-interrupt-capable pin).
   - *Fallback if you'd rather not wire it:* poll the `RCA` (receive-chunks-available) field that TC6 returns in every data footer — works, but wakes/polls needlessly and adds latency. IRQ_N is the proper design and what `oa-tc6-lib` expects.

2. **`RST` (host → LAN8651 reset)** — a **GPIO output** to hard-reset the MAC-PHY at init.
   - *Fallback:* TC6 has a software reset (write the `RESET` register / SYNC sequence), which `oa-tc6-lib` does anyway — but a hardware reset line is more robust against power-up glitches. Worth wiring if your board (e.g. the Two-Wire ETH Click `RST` on mikroBUS) exposes it.

Free PIOA pins near the SPI block from the staged CSV include **PA15, PA16, PA17, PA24, PA25, PA30, PA31** (currently "Available, In") if you want IRQ_N/RST adjacent to the rest.

## One non-blocking note

`FLEXCOM4_SPI_Initialize()` hardcodes `SCBR(255)` → ~1 MHz at the 266.7 MHz peripheral clock (`:83`/`:240`). That's fine — actually nice and safe for bring-up — and our glue will call `FLEXCOM4_SPI_TransferSetup()` to raise it (toward the LAN8651's 25 MHz ceiling) once the device-ID read is solid. No MCC change required.

## Recommendation

The SPI peripheral is **good to go**. To fully unblock Phase 1, **assign IRQ_N and RST in MCC** (or explicitly tell me to use the software-reset + footer-poll fallbacks and skip them). Tell me which pins you pick for IRQ_N/RST and I'll wire the PIO interrupt + reset sequence into the glue.

Reviewed. Both pins are correctly defined and the GPIO macros are generated:

- **`T1S_IRQ_N` = PB25** — input; `T1S_IRQ_N_Get()` reads it (`plib_pio.h:194`).
- **`T1S_RST` = PB3** — output, **Latch = High** → reset de-asserted at boot (correct for an active-low reset); `T1S_RST_Set()/_Clear()` at `:396-397`. Our init will pulse it low then release. ✓

## One thing still missing: IRQ_N can't actually interrupt yet

The pin has **PIO Interrupt = Disabled**, and I confirmed the consequence:
- `plib_pio.h/.c` contain **no PIO interrupt API** (no `PIO_PinInterruptCallbackRegister`, no handler) — MCC only generates that infrastructure when at least one pin enables PIO Interrupt.
- The **AIC table has no PIO controller entry** (`plib_aic.c:69-78` — only SYSC/FLEXCOMs/TC0/XDMAC/USB/ISC/CSI2DC; no PIOA/PIOB).

So right now PB25 is just a readable GPIO — the LAN8651 asserting `IRQ_N` won't wake the CPU. That defeats the interrupt-driven RX design (the whole point of `IRQ_N`: the MAC-PHY tells us when an RX chunk is waiting).

**The one remaining MCC change:** set **`T1S_IRQ_N` → PIO Interrupt = Falling Edge** (my recommendation) and regenerate. That makes MCC emit the PIOB interrupt handler, the `PIO_PinInterruptCallbackRegister` API, and the PIOB AIC entry — then the glue registers a callback → gives a FreeRTOS semaphore → TC6 service task drains.

- **Falling Edge** (recommended): fires on the high→low assertion; simple, no re-fire. Safe because TC6's footer reports `RCA` (RX chunks available), so the service task drains in a loop until `RCA==0` and re-checks the IRQ level — can't lose an event.
- **Low Level** (alternative): the most faithful to a level-held IRQ, but the ISR must mask-then-unmask-after-servicing or it re-fires continuously. More fiddly; only needed if edge detection proves lossy.
- **Polling fallback** (no MCC change): skip the interrupt entirely and poll `RCA` from every footer. Works, but adds latency and wakes needlessly — not recommended.

## Two small suggestions while you're in MCC

1. **Enable the internal pull-up on `T1S_IRQ_N` (PB25)** — currently Pull Up = No. While `RST` is asserted or before the PHY drives the line, `IRQ_N` can float and produce a spurious interrupt. A pull-up is cheap insurance (and *mandatory* if the LAN8651's `IRQ_N` is open-drain — worth confirming against the datasheet, but the pull-up is safe either way).
2. `RST` (PB3) as push-pull output (Open Drain = No) is correct for a dedicated reset line — no change needed.

| IRQ_N | PB25 | ⚠️ pin OK, but **needs PIO Interrupt = Falling Edge** + pull-up to be usable |

That's correct — the PIO interrupt path is now **fully wired**:

- **`T1S_IRQ_N` = PB25, Falling Edge** ✓
- **AIC routes PIOB** — `plib_aic.c:70` `{ 3U, PIOB_InterruptHandler, ... }` (periph ID 3) ✓
- **PIOB peripheral clock enabled** — `plib_clk.c:119` `{ ID_PIOB, 1, ... }` ✓
- **PIO interrupt API generated** — `PIO_PinInterruptCallbackRegister`, `PIO_PinInterruptEnable/Disable`, and `PIOB_InterruptHandler → PIO_Interrupt_Handler(PIO_PORT_B)` (reads `PIO_ISR`, dispatches per-pin callbacks) ✓

So the glue will do exactly: `PIO_PinInterruptCallbackRegister(T1S_IRQ_N_PIN, cb, ctx)` → `PIO_PinInterruptEnable(T1S_IRQ_N_PIN)` → callback fires on the falling edge → `xSemaphoreGiveFromISR` → TC6 service task drains until `RCA==0`.

**The MCC hardware layer is now complete** — SPI (Mode 0, CSAAT, IRQ-driven), RST output, and IRQ_N falling-edge interrupt all generated and routed. Nothing else needed there.

(The pull-up on IRQ_N is now genuinely optional rather than recommended: with falling-edge + the RCA backstop, a spurious edge during reset is harmless — the service task reads the footer, sees `RCA==0`, and does nothing. Leave it off unless bring-up shows phantom interrupts.)

# OPEN Alliance TC6 Protocol Driver for LAN8650/1

This repository contains the Microchip OPEN Alliance TC6 Protocol Driver for LAN8650/1 source code and example applications.

The driver is fully OPEN Alliance TC6 V1.1 compliant.
Quickly incorporate connectivity to your designs with 10BASE-T1S
ICs, modules, software and development kits that make connecting effortless
for your customers. Our comprehensive 10BASE-T1S portfolio has the technology
to meet your range, data rate, interoperability, frequency and topology needs.
Please contact the Microchip support in case of issues and questions.

- [10BASE-T1S Support](https://www.microchip.com/support)
- [OPEN Alliance TC6 - 10BASE-T1x MAC-PHY Serial Interface specification](https://www.opensig.org/Automotive-Ethernet-Specifications)
- [10Base-T1x MAC-PHY Serial Interface Protocol Analyzer for Saleae Logic](https://github.com/MicrochipTech/oa-tc6-saleae-extension)

303	 * \param offset - 0, if this is the start of a new Ethernet frame. Otherwise the offset to which this slide of payload belongs to.
304	 * \param len - Length of the byte array.
305	 * \param pGlobalTag - The exact same pointer, which was given along with the TC6_Init() function.
306	 */
307	extern void TC6_CB_OnRxEthernetSlice(TC6_t *pInst, const uint8_t *pRx, uint16_t offset, uint16_t len, void *pGlobalTag);
308	
309	/**
310	 * \brief Callback when ever an Ethernet packet was received. This will notify the integrator, that now all chunks very reported by TC6_CB_OnRxEthernetPacket and the data can be processed.
311	 * \note This function must be implemented by the integrator.
312	 * \param pInst - The pointer returned by TC6_Init.
313	 * \param success - true, if the received Ethernet frame was received without errors. false, if there were errors.
314	 * \param len - Length of the entire Ethernet frame. This is all length reported TC6_CB_OnRxEthernetPacket combined.
315	 * \param rxTimestamp - Pointer to the receive timestamp, if there was any. NULL, otherwise. Pointer will be invalid after returning out of the callback!
316	 * \param pGlobalTag - The exact same pointer, which was given along with the TC6_Init() function.
317	 */
318	extern void TC6_CB_OnRxEthernetPacket(TC6_t *pInst, bool success, uint16_t len, uint64_t *rxTimestamp, void *pGlobalTag);
319	
320	/**
321	 * \brief Callback when ever an error occurred.
322	 * \note This function must be implemented by the integrator.
323	 * \param pInst - The pointer returned by TC6_Init.
324	 * \param err - Enumeration value holding the actual error condition.
325	 * \param pGlobalTag - The exact same pointer, which was given along with the TC6_Init() function.
326	 */
327	extern void TC6_CB_OnError(TC6_t *pInst, TC6_Error_t err, void *pGlobalTag);
328	
329	/**
330	 * \brief Callback when ever TC6 packet was received, which had the extended flag set. This means, that the user should read (and clear) at least Status0 and Status1 registers.
331	 * \note The integrator MUST call TC6_UnlockExtendedStatus() whenever he is ready to process the next extended status flag. Reenabling it to early may trigger thousands of events per second.
332	 * \note This function must be implemented by the integrator.
333	 * \param pInst - The pointer returned by TC6_Init.
334	 * \param pGlobalTag - The exact same pointer, which was given along with the TC6_Init() function.
335	 */
336	extern void TC6_CB_OnExtendedStatus(TC6_t *pInst, void *pGlobalTag);
337	
338	/**
339	 * \brief Users implementation of SPI transfer function.
340	 * \note The implementation may be synchronous or asynchronous. But in any case the TC6_SpiBufferDone() must be called, when the SPI transaction is over!
341	 * \param tc6instance - The instance number of the hardware. Starting with 0 for the first.
342	 * \param pTx - Pointer to the MOSI data. The pointer stays valid until user calls TC6_SpiBufferDone()
343	 * \param pRx - Pointer to the MISO Buffer. The pointer stays valid until user calls TC6_SpiBufferDone()
344	 * \param len - The length of both buffers (pTx and pRx). The entire length must be transfered via SPI.
345	 * \param pGlobalTag - The exact same pointer, which was given along with the TC6_Init() function.
346	 * \return true, if the SPI data was enqueued/transfered. false, there was an error.
347	 */
348	extern bool TC6_CB_OnSpiTransaction(uint8_t tc6instance, uint8_t *pTx, uint8_t *pRx, uint16_t len, void *pGlobalTag);
349	
350	#ifdef __cplusplus
351	}
352	#endif
353	#endif /* TC6_H_ */

84	    volatile bool busy;
85	    volatile uint8_t macValid;
86	} Stub_Local_t;

107	bool TC6Stub_Init(uint8_t idx, uint8_t pMac[6])
108	{
109	    bool success = false;
110	    if (idx >= TC6_MAX_INSTANCES) {
111	        ASSERT(false);
112	    } else {
113	        Stub_Local_t *ps = &d[idx];
114	        ps->idx = idx;
115	        if (GetMacAddress(ps)) {
116	            memcpy(pMac, ps->mac, 6u);
117	        } else {
118	            PRINT("Using fallback MAC address, instance=%d\r\n", idx);
119	            memcpy(pMac, FALLBACK_MAC, 6u);
120	        }
121	        switch (idx) {
122	        case FIRST_TC6_INSTANCE:
123	            EIC_CallbackRegister(EIC_PIN_14, IntHandler, (uintptr_t)ps);
124	            TC6_RESET_1_Clear();
125	            SYSTICK_DelayMs(10);
126	            TC6_RESET_1_Set();
127	            SYSTICK_DelayMs(10);
128	            break;
129	        default:
130	            ASSERT(false);
131	            break;
132	        }
133	        if (!ps->opened) {
134	            ps->opened = true;
135	            ASSERT((idx + SPI_OFFSET) < DRV_SPI_INSTANCES_NUMBER);
136	            ps->handle = DRV_SPI_Open((idx + SPI_OFFSET), DRV_IO_INTENT_EXCLUSIVE);
137	            switch (idx) {
138	            case FIRST_TC6_INSTANCE:
139	                ps->spiSetup.chipSelect = SYS_PORT_PIN_PC15;
140	                break;
141	            default:
142	                ASSERT(false);
143	                break;
144	            }
145	        }
146	        ps->spiSetup.baudRateInHz = DEFAULT_SPI_SPEED;
147	        ps->spiSetup.clockPhase = DRV_SPI_CLOCK_PHASE_VALID_LEADING_EDGE;
148	        ps->spiSetup.clockPolarity = DRV_SPI_CLOCK_POLARITY_IDLE_LOW;
149	        ps->spiSetup.dataBits = DRV_SPI_DATA_BITS_8;
150	        ps->spiSetup.csPolarity = DRV_SPI_CS_POLARITY_ACTIVE_LOW;
151	        DRV_SPI_TransferEventHandlerSet(ps->handle, EventHandlerSPI, (uintptr_t)ps);
152	        success = DRV_SPI_TransferSetup(ps->handle, &ps->spiSetup);
153	    }
154	    return success;
155	}

160	    ASSERT(idx < TC6_MAX_INSTANCES);

179	bool TC6Stub_SpiTransaction(uint8_t idx, uint8_t *pTx, uint8_t *pRx, uint16_t len)
180	{
181	    DRV_SPI_TRANSFER_HANDLE transferHandle;
182	    Stub_Local_t *ps = &d[idx];
183	    bool success = false;
184	    ASSERT(idx < TC6_MAX_INSTANCES);
185	
186	    if (ps->opened && !ps->busy) {
187	        ps->busy = true;
188	        DRV_SPI_WriteReadTransferAdd(ps->handle, pTx, len, pRx, len, &transferHandle);
189	        if (transferHandle == DRV_SPI_TRANSFER_HANDLE_INVALID) {
190	            ps->busy = false;
191	        } else {
192	            success = true;
193	        }
194	    }
195	    return success;
196	}

201	
202	static bool GetMacAddress(Stub_Local_t *ps)
203	{
204	    uint8_t MAC_EEPROM_I2C_SLAVE_ADDR = 0x58;
205	    uint8_t MAC_EEPROM_EUI_REG_ADDR = 0x9A;
206	    bool success = false;
207	    if (NULL != ps) {
208	        DRV_HANDLE i2c_handle = DRV_I2C_Open(ps->idx, DRV_IO_INTENT_EXCLUSIVE);
209	        if (DRV_HANDLE_INVALID == i2c_handle) {
210	            ASSERT(false);
211	            return false;
212	        }
213	        ps->macValid = 0;
214	        DRV_I2C_TransferEventHandlerSet(i2c_handle, EventHandlerI2C, (uintptr_t)ps);
215	        DRV_I2C_WriteReadTransferAdd(i2c_handle, MAC_EEPROM_I2C_SLAVE_ADDR, &MAC_EEPROM_EUI_REG_ADDR, sizeof(MAC_EEPROM_EUI_REG_ADDR), ps->mac, 6, &ps->i2cHandle);
216	        if (DRV_I2C_TRANSFER_HANDLE_INVALID == ps->i2cHandle) {
217	            PRINT("Failed to enqueue read MAC address from EEPROM\r\n");
218	            return false;
219	        }
220	        while (!ps->macValid) {}
221	        ps->i2cHandle = DRV_I2C_TRANSFER_HANDLE_INVALID;
222	        if (2 == ps->macValid) {
223	            PRINT("Failed to obtain MAC address from EEPROM\r\n");
224	            return false;
225	        }
226	        DRV_I2C_Close(i2c_handle);
227	        success = true;
228	    }
229	    return success;
230	}
231	
232	static void EventHandlerI2C(DRV_I2C_TRANSFER_EVENT event, DRV_I2C_TRANSFER_HANDLE transferHandle, uintptr_t context)
233	{
234	    Stub_Local_t *ps = (Stub_Local_t *)context;
235	    (void)transferHandle;
236	    ASSERT((NULL != ps) && (ps->idx < TC6_MAX_INSTANCES));
237	    switch (event) {
238	    case DRV_I2C_TRANSFER_EVENT_PENDING:
239	        /* Not yet ready*/
240	        break;
241	    case DRV_I2C_TRANSFER_EVENT_COMPLETE:
242	        ps->macValid = 1;
243	        break;
244	    case DRV_I2C_TRANSFER_EVENT_ERROR:
245	    default:
246	        ps->macValid = 2;
247	        break;
248	    }
249	}
250	
251	static void EventHandlerSPI(DRV_SPI_TRANSFER_EVENT event, DRV_SPI_TRANSFER_HANDLE transferHandle, uintptr_t context)
252	{
253	    Stub_Local_t *ps = (Stub_Local_t *)context;
254	    (void)transferHandle;
255	    ASSERT((NULL != ps) && (ps->idx < TC6_MAX_INSTANCES));
256	    if (event == DRV_SPI_TRANSFER_EVENT_ERROR) {
257	        ASSERT(false);
258	    }
259	    if (event == DRV_SPI_TRANSFER_EVENT_PENDING) {
260	        return;
261	    }
262	    ps->busy = false;
263	    TC6_SpiBufferDone(ps->idx, (event == DRV_SPI_TRANSFER_EVENT_COMPLETE));
264	}
265	
266	static void IntHandler(uintptr_t context)
267	{
268	    Stub_Local_t *ps = (Stub_Local_t *)context;
269	    ps->intIn++;
270	}

103	int8_t TC6NoIP_Init(bool enablePlca, uint8_t nodeId, uint8_t nodeCount, uint8_t burstCount, uint8_t burstTimer, bool promiscuous, bool txCutThrough, bool rxCutThrough)
104	{
105	    TC6NoIP_t *lw = NULL;
106	    uint8_t i;
107	    bool success = false;
108	    /* Search for empty entry */
109	    for (i = 0; i < TC6_MAX_INSTANCES; i++) {
110	        if (NOIP_TC6_MAGIC != mlw[i].magic) {
111	            lw = &mlw[i];
112	            lw->idx = i;
113	            success = true;
114	            break;
115	        }
116	    }
117	    if (success) {
118	        success = TC6Stub_Init(lw->idx, lw->tc.mac);
119	        if (!success) {
120	            PRINT_FORCE(ESC_RED "[%d]TC6Stub_Init() failed" ESC_RESETCOLOR "\r\n", lw->idx);
121	        }
122	    }
123	    if (success) {
124	        lw->tc.tc6 = TC6_Init(lw);
125	        success = (NULL != lw->tc.tc6);
126	        if (!success) {
127	            PRINT_FORCE(ESC_RED "[%d]TC6_Init() failed" ESC_RESETCOLOR "\r\n", lw->idx);
128	        }
129	    }
130	    if (success) {
131	        success = TC6Regs_Init(lw->tc.tc6, lw, lw->tc.mac, enablePlca, nodeId, nodeCount, burstCount, burstTimer, promiscuous, txCutThrough, rxCutThrough);
132	        if (!success) {
133	            PRINT_FORCE(ESC_RED "[%d]TC6Regs_Init() failed" ESC_RESETCOLOR "\r\n", lw->idx);
134	        }
135	    }
136	    if (success) {
137	        uint8_t *mac = lw->tc.mac;
138	        PRINT_FORCE("NoIP-Init [MAC=%02X:%02X:%02X:%02X:%02X:%02X, ChipRev=%d", mac[0], mac[1], mac[2], mac[3], mac[4], mac[5], TC6Regs_GetChipRevision(lw->tc.tc6));
139	        if (enablePlca) {
140	            PRINT(", PLCA-NodeId=%d]\r\n", nodeId);
141	        } else {
142	            PRINT(", CSMA/CD]\r\n");
143	        }
144	        lw->magic = NOIP_TC6_MAGIC;
145	    } else {
146	        TC6_Destroy(lw->tc.tc6);
147	    }
148	    return (success ? (int8_t)lw->idx : -1);
149	}

151	void TC6NoIP_Service(void)
152	{
153	    uint8_t idx;
154	    for (idx = 0; idx < TC6_MAX_INSTANCES; idx++) {
155	        TC6NoIP_t *lw = &mlw[idx];
156	        if (NOIP_TC6_MAGIC == lw->magic) {
157	            if (TC6Stub_IntActive(lw->idx)) {
158	                if (TC6_Service(lw->tc.tc6, false)) {
159	                    TC6Stub_ReleaseInt(lw->idx);
160	                }
161	            } else {
162	                TC6_Service(lw->tc.tc6, true);
163	            }
164	        }
165	    }
166	    TC6Regs_CheckTimers();
167	}

236	            break;
237	        case TC6Error_UnexpectedDvEv:
238	            PRINT(ESC_CLEAR_LINE ESC_RED "[%d]Unexpected Data Valid or End Valid Flag" ESC_RESETCOLOR "\r\n", lw->idx);
239	            break;
240	        case TC6Error_BadChecksum:
241	            PRINT(ESC_CLEAR_LINE ESC_RED "[%d]Checksum in footer is wrong" ESC_RESETCOLOR "\r\n", lw->idx);
242	            reinit = true;
243	            break;
244	        case TC6Error_UnexpectedCtrl:
245	            PRINT(ESC_CLEAR_LINE ESC_RED "[%d]Unexpected control packet received" ESC_RESETCOLOR "\r\n", lw->idx);
246	            reinit = true;
247	            break;
248	        case TC6Error_BadTxData:
249	            PRINT(ESC_CLEAR_LINE ESC_RED "[%d]Header Bad Flag received" ESC_RESETCOLOR "\r\n", lw->idx);
250	            reinit = true;
251	            break;
252	        case TC6Error_SyncLost:
253	            PRINT(ESC_CLEAR_LINE ESC_RED "[%d]Sync Flag is no longer set" ESC_RESETCOLOR "\r\n", lw->idx);
254	            reinit = true;
255	            break;
256	        case TC6Error_SpiError:
257	            PRINT(ESC_CLEAR_LINE ESC_RED "[%d]TC6 SPI Error" ESC_RESETCOLOR "\r\n", lw->idx);
258	            reinit = true;
259	            break;
260	        case TC6Error_ControlTxFail:
261	            PRINT(ESC_CLEAR_LINE ESC_RED "[%d]TC6 Control Message Error" ESC_RESETCOLOR "\r\n", lw->idx);
262	            break;
263	        default:
264	            PRINT(ESC_CLEAR_LINE ESC_RED "[%d]Unknown TC6 error occurred" ESC_RESETCOLOR "\r\n", lw->idx);
265	            break;
266	    }

399	static void PrintRateLimited(const char *statement, ...)
400	{
401	    static uint32_t cnt_ = 0;
402	    static uint32_t t0_;
403	    uint32_t now = TC6Stub_GetTick();
404	
405	    if (t0_ && ((now - t0_) >= PRINT_RATE_TIMEOUT)) {
406	        if (cnt_ > PRINT_RATE_THRESHOLD) {
407	            printf(ESC_CLEAR_LINE ESC_YELLOW "[skipped %lu]" ESC_RESETCOLOR "\r\n", (cnt_ - PRINT_RATE_THRESHOLD));
408	        }
409	        t0_ = 0;
410	        cnt_ = 0;
411	    }
412	    ++cnt_;
413	    if (cnt_ <= PRINT_RATE_THRESHOLD) {
414	        va_list args;
415	        va_start( args, statement );
416	        (void)vfprintf(stdout, statement, args);
417	        va_end( args );
418	        t0_ = now;
419	    }
420	}

98	{

104	     * INFO; flip to DEBUG via log_set_level() to enable verbose. */
105	    log_init(LOG_LEVEL_INFO);
106	
107	    /* Spawn the video task. xTaskCreate is safe before vTaskStartScheduler;
108	     * the task runs once the scheduler picks it up. The video module owns
109	     * its capture-pipeline init (ISC, TC358743, backlight, HEO unbind),
110	     * the capture/display state machine, and the bridge-status polling. */
111	    Video_Initialize();
112	
113	    /* Per-frame performance log: producer-side queues + drain task.
114	     * Init the queues here so any producer that posts before the
115	     * scheduler starts will not crash; the drain task is launched
116	     * separately by PerfLog_Start once the scheduler is up. */
117	    PerfLog_Initialize();
118

120	     * panel — 1:1 with the bridge's typical 480p source, leaves a UI

122	     * default window of its own. */
123	    Video_SetWindow(280u, 76u, 720u, 480u);
124	
125	    /* Default: arm the capture chain when source locks, and show video. */
126	    Video_CaptureEnable();
127	    Video_DisplayShow();
128

132	     * queue from inside its task. Detectors default disabled; explicitly
133	     * enable + select the active one for the timing pipeline. */
134	    Detector_Initialize();
135	    Detector_Enable(DETECTOR_CV_MARVIN_V1);
136	    Detector_SetActive(DETECTOR_CV_MARVIN_V1);
137

139	     * USART writer and the RX parse task. The FLEXCOM1 peripheral is brought
140	     * up by SYS_Initialize (FLEXCOM1_USART_Initialize), so this just arms the
141	     * ring-buffer RX notification and starts the link tasks. */
142	    FretboardLink_Initialize();
143	
144	    /* timing_pipeline runs the chord-window + strum scheduler against the
145	     * active detector and pushes the resulting 7-bit mask through
146	     * FretboardLink_Send. */
147	    TimingPipeline_Initialize();

154	    ManualControl_Initialize();

159	     * from inside its task, so it follows Video_Initialize. Enable observation

173	     * is the standard FreeRTOS pattern. */

#ifndef TC6_CONFIG_H_
#define TC6_CONFIG_H_

/* Build-time configuration for the vendored OPEN Alliance TC6 driver
 * (third_party/oa-tc6-lib). The library #includes "tc6-conf.h" from the
 * include path; this is marvin's copy. Values mirror the library's
 * cfg-example defaults; only TC6_MAX_INSTANCES is pinned (one LAN8651). */

#ifdef __cplusplus
extern "C" {
#endif

#define TC6_ASSERT(condition)

/* One MAC-PHY on the marvin side. */
#define TC6_MAX_INSTANCES       (1u)

/* OPEN Alliance fixed protocol values — do not modify. */
#define TC6_HEADER_SIZE         (4u)
#define TC6_CHUNK_SIZE          (64u)
#define TC6_CHUNK_BUF_SIZE      (TC6_CHUNK_SIZE + TC6_HEADER_SIZE)

/* Control-data queue length (power of 2). */
#define REG_OP_ARRAY_SIZE       (4u)

/* Max TC6 chunks per SPI transaction, and concat threshold. */
#define TC6_CHUNKS_XACT         (31u)
#define TC6_CONCAT_THRESHOLD    (1024u)

#define TC6_TX_ETH_QSIZE        (4u)
#define TC6_TX_ETH_MAX_SEGMENTS (8u)
#define TC6_MAX_CNTRL_VARS      (1u)

#ifdef __cplusplus
}
#endif

#endif /* TC6_CONFIG_H_ */

#ifndef T1S_LINK_H
#define T1S_LINK_H

#include <stdbool.h>
#include <stdint.h>

/* 10BASE-T1S inter-node link (marvin side, LAN8651 MAC-PHY over FLEXCOM4 SPI).
 *
 * marvin is the PLCA coordinator (node ID 0). The transport is the vendored
 * OPEN Alliance TC6 driver (third_party/oa-tc6-lib): SPI chunk protocol +
 * register control, wrapped here with the FLEXCOM4 SPI PLib, the T1S_RST /
 * T1S_IRQ_N GPIOs, and a FreeRTOS service task. See docs/t1s-podl-link.md.
 *
 * Phase 1/2 scope: bring the MAC-PHY up (reset, TC6_Init + TC6Regs_Init with
 * PLCA enabled) and confirm the link by reading the chip revision. L2 framing,
 * node-table demux, and the fretboard data path land in later phases.
 *
 * Initialize after SYS_Initialize (FLEXCOM4_SPI_Initialize must have run). The
 * call only creates the service task + semaphore; the reset pulse and TC6 init
 * run inside the task once the scheduler is up (TC6 init is asynchronous and
 * needs the SPI ISR + service loop). */

void T1SLink_Initialize(void);

/* True once the MAC-PHY has been configured and data path enabled. */
bool T1SLink_IsConnected(void);

#endif /* T1S_LINK_H */

```

```c
#include "t1s_link.h"

#include <stdint.h>
#include <stdbool.h>
#include <string.h>

#include "FreeRTOS.h"
#include "task.h"
#include "semphr.h"

#include "definitions.h"   /* FLEXCOM4_SPI_*, PIO_*, T1S_* pin macros */
#include "log.h"

#include "tc6.h"
#include "tc6-regs.h"

/* marvin is the PLCA coordinator. Node IDs and MACs follow the addressing
 * scheme in docs/t1s-podl-link.md §7.1: coordinator = ID 0, MAC ...00. */
#define T1S_NODE_ID         (0u)
#define T1S_NODE_COUNT      (8u)     /* PLCA cycle length; headroom for nodes 1..7 */
#define T1S_PLCA_ENABLE     (true)
#define T1S_SPI_HZ          (15000000u)
#define T1S_INSTANCE        (0u)

#define T1S_TASK_STACK_WORDS (1024u)
#define T1S_TASK_PRIORITY    (5u)

/* Locally administered coordinator MAC (02:00:00:00:00:00). */
static uint8_t s_mac[6] = { 0x02u, 0x00u, 0x00u, 0x00u, 0x00u, (uint8_t)T1S_NODE_ID };

static TC6_t            *s_tc6;
static volatile bool     s_need_service;
static volatile bool     s_link_up;

static SemaphoreHandle_t s_svc_sem;
static StaticSemaphore_t s_svc_sem_buf;

static StackType_t       s_task_stack[T1S_TASK_STACK_WORDS];
static StaticTask_t      s_task_tcb;

/* RX reassembly: TC6 delivers an Ethernet frame as slices; collect them here
 * and process on the OnRxEthernetPacket completion callback. */
static uint8_t           s_rx_buf[1518];

/* FLEXCOM4 SPI completion ISR callback: the chunk transfer is done, hand the
 * buffer back to the TC6 driver and wake the service task. */
static void spi_done_cb(uintptr_t context)
{
    (void)context;
    BaseType_t hpw = pdFALSE;
    TC6_SpiBufferDone(T1S_INSTANCE, true);
    (void)xSemaphoreGiveFromISR(s_svc_sem, &hpw);
    portYIELD_FROM_ISR(hpw);
}

/* T1S_IRQ_N falling-edge PIO ISR callback: the MAC-PHY needs servicing. */
static void irq_cb(PIO_PIN pin, uintptr_t context)
{
    (void)pin;
    (void)context;
    BaseType_t hpw = pdFALSE;
    s_need_service = true;
    (void)xSemaphoreGiveFromISR(s_svc_sem, &hpw);
    portYIELD_FROM_ISR(hpw);
}

/* Run the protocol stack until it has no immediately pending work. IRQ_N is
 * active-low; TC6_Service treats a false interruptLevel as "interrupt active". */
static void service_pump(void)
{
    do {
        s_need_service = false;
        bool no_int = (T1S_IRQ_N_Get() != 0u);
        (void)TC6_Service(s_tc6, no_int);
    } while (s_need_service);
    TC6Regs_CheckTimers();
}

static void t1s_task(void *param)
{
    (void)param;

    /* Hardware reset pulse (T1S_RST is active-low, idle high). */
    T1S_RST_Clear();
    vTaskDelay(pdMS_TO_TICKS(10));
    T1S_RST_Set();
    vTaskDelay(pdMS_TO_TICKS(10));

    /* SPI: Mode 0 (CPOL=0 idle low, CPHA=0 leading edge), 8-bit, 15 MHz.
     * Source clock 0 => PLib uses the FLEXCOM4 peripheral clock. */
    FLEXCOM_SPI_TRANSFER_SETUP setup = {
        .clockFrequency = T1S_SPI_HZ,
        .clockPhase     = FLEXCOM_SPI_CLOCK_PHASE_LEADING_EDGE,
        .clockPolarity  = FLEXCOM_SPI_CLOCK_POLARITY_IDLE_LOW,
        .dataBits       = FLEXCOM_SPI_DATA_BITS_8,
    };
    (void)FLEXCOM4_SPI_TransferSetup(&setup, 0u);
    FLEXCOM4_SPI_CallbackRegister(spi_done_cb, 0u);

    s_tc6 = TC6_Init(NULL);
    if (s_tc6 == NULL) {
        LOG_ERROR("T1S: TC6_Init failed\r\n");
        vTaskDelete(NULL);
        return;
    }

    (void)PIO_PinInterruptCallbackRegister(T1S_IRQ_N_PIN, irq_cb, 0u);
    PIO_PinInterruptEnable(T1S_IRQ_N_PIN);

    /* Configure the LAN8651 registers + PLCA (coordinator, id 0). promiscuous
     * during bring-up so RX isn't filtered before the node table exists. */
    while (!TC6Regs_Init(s_tc6, NULL, s_mac, T1S_PLCA_ENABLE, T1S_NODE_ID,
                         T1S_NODE_COUNT, 0u, 0u, true, false, false)) {
        LOG_WARN("T1S: TC6Regs_Init busy, retrying\r\n");
        vTaskDelay(pdMS_TO_TICKS(50));
    }

    /* Drive the async register writes to completion (bounded for the up log). */
    TickType_t deadline = xTaskGetTickCount() + pdMS_TO_TICKS(3000);
    while (!TC6Regs_GetInitDone(s_tc6) &&
           ((int32_t)(deadline - xTaskGetTickCount()) > 0)) {
        (void)xSemaphoreTake(s_svc_sem, pdMS_TO_TICKS(2));
        service_pump();
    }

    if (TC6Regs_GetInitDone(s_tc6)) {
        s_link_up = true;
        TC6_EnableData(s_tc6, true);
        LOG_INFO("T1S: LAN8651 up — chipRev=%u, MAC=%02X:%02X:%02X:%02X:%02X:%02X, "
                 "PLCA coord id=%u/%u\r\n",
                 (unsigned)TC6Regs_GetChipRevision(s_tc6),
                 s_mac[0], s_mac[1], s_mac[2], s_mac[3], s_mac[4], s_mac[5],
                 (unsigned)T1S_NODE_ID, (unsigned)T1S_NODE_COUNT);
    } else {
        LOG_WARN("T1S: MAC-PHY not responding (check EVB/wiring); still servicing\r\n");
    }

    for (;;) {
        (void)xSemaphoreTake(s_svc_sem, pdMS_TO_TICKS(1));
        service_pump();
        if (!s_link_up && TC6Regs_GetInitDone(s_tc6)) {
            s_link_up = true;
            TC6_EnableData(s_tc6, true);
            LOG_INFO("T1S: LAN8651 up (late) — chipRev=%u\r\n",
                     (unsigned)TC6Regs_GetChipRevision(s_tc6));
        }
    }
}

void T1SLink_Initialize(void)
{
    s_svc_sem = xSemaphoreCreateBinaryStatic(&s_svc_sem_buf);
    configASSERT(s_svc_sem != NULL);

    (void)xTaskCreateStatic(t1s_task, "T1SLink", T1S_TASK_STACK_WORDS, NULL,
                            T1S_TASK_PRIORITY, s_task_stack, &s_task_tcb);
}

bool T1SLink_IsConnected(void)
{
    return s_link_up;
}

/*>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>  TC6 driver callbacks (integrator)  >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>*/

bool TC6_CB_OnSpiTransaction(uint8_t tc6instance, uint8_t *pTx, uint8_t *pRx,
                             uint16_t len, void *pGlobalTag)
{
    (void)tc6instance;
    (void)pGlobalTag;
    /* Non-blocking full-duplex transfer; spi_done_cb calls TC6_SpiBufferDone.
     * Returns false if the PLib is busy — the driver retries. */
    return FLEXCOM4_SPI_WriteRead(pTx, len, pRx, len);
}

void TC6_CB_OnNeedService(TC6_t *pInst, void *pGlobalTag)
{
    (void)pInst;
    (void)pGlobalTag;
    /* May be called from task or ISR context; just flag. ISR sources also give
     * the semaphore, so the service task always wakes. */
    s_need_service = true;
}

void TC6_CB_OnRxEthernetSlice(TC6_t *pInst, const uint8_t *pRx, uint16_t offset,
                              uint16_t len, void *pGlobalTag)
{
    (void)pInst;
    (void)pGlobalTag;
    if (((uint32_t)offset + len) <= sizeof(s_rx_buf)) {
        memcpy(&s_rx_buf[offset], pRx, len);
    }
}

void TC6_CB_OnRxEthernetPacket(TC6_t *pInst, bool success, uint16_t len,
                               uint64_t *rxTimestamp, void *pGlobalTag)
{
    (void)pInst;
    (void)rxTimestamp;
    (void)pGlobalTag;
    /* Phase 1: log only. L2 demux + fretboard data path land in later phases. */
    if (success && (len >= 14u)) {
        LOG_DEBUG("T1S: rx %u B, src=%02X:%02X:%02X:%02X:%02X:%02X type=%04X\r\n",
                  (unsigned)len,
                  s_rx_buf[6], s_rx_buf[7], s_rx_buf[8],
                  s_rx_buf[9], s_rx_buf[10], s_rx_buf[11],
                  (unsigned)((s_rx_buf[12] << 8) | s_rx_buf[13]));
    }
}

void TC6_CB_OnError(TC6_t *pInst, TC6_Error_t err, void *pGlobalTag)
{
    (void)pGlobalTag;
    LOG_WARN("T1S: error: %s\r\n", TC6_GetErrorStr(err));
    switch (err) {
        case TC6Error_NoHardware:
        case TC6Error_BadChecksum:
        case TC6Error_UnexpectedCtrl:
        case TC6Error_BadTxData:
        case TC6Error_SyncLost:
        case TC6Error_SpiError:
            TC6Regs_Reinit(pInst);
            break;
        default:
            break;
    }
}

/*>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>  TC6Regs callbacks (integrator)  >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>*/

uint32_t TC6Regs_CB_GetTicksMs(void)
{
    /* configTICK_RATE_HZ is 1000, so one tick is one millisecond. */
    return (uint32_t)xTaskGetTickCount();
}

void TC6Regs_CB_OnEvent(TC6_t *pInst, TC6Regs_Event_t event, void *pTag)
{
    (void)pTag;
    LOG_INFO("T1S: event: %s\r\n", TC6Regs_GetEventStr(event));
    switch (event) {
        case TC6Regs_Event_Loss_of_Framing_Error:
        case TC6Regs_Event_RX_Non_Recoverable_Error:
        case TC6Regs_Event_TX_Non_Recoverable_Error:
            TC6Regs_Reinit(pInst);
            break;
        default:
            break;
    }
}

```

Phase 1 is **code-complete**. Because `TC6Regs_Init()` configures the LAN8651 registers *and* PLCA in one call, Phases 1 and 2 naturally collapsed into a single bring-up step.

## What I wrote (new `default/src/net/t1s/`)

- **`tc6-conf.h`** — marvin's build config for the vendored driver (one instance, OA default chunk/queue sizes).
- **`t1s_link.{c,h}`** — `T1SLink_Initialize()` spins up a FreeRTOS service task that:
  1. pulses `T1S_RST`, sets FLEXCOM4 to **Mode 0 @ 15 MHz**,
  2. `TC6_Init()` + `TC6Regs_Init()` as **PLCA coordinator (node id 0 / count 8, MAC `02:00:00:00:00:00`)**, promiscuous during bring-up,
  3. services to init-done and logs **`T1S: LAN8651 up — chipRev=…`** (the Phase 1/2 gate),
  4. then runs the steady service loop.
  - SPI-completion ISR → `TC6_SpiBufferDone` + semaphore; `T1S_IRQ_N` falling-edge → semaphore; `OnNeedService` → flag. RX callbacks log only for now (L2 demux is Phase 3).

## Wiring

- **`user.cmake`** — added `t1s_link.c` + `libtc6/src/tc6.c` + `tc6-regs.c`, and include dirs (`net/t1s`, `libtc6/inc`, `libtc6/src`).
- **`app.c`** — `T1SLink_Initialize()` runs alongside `FretboardLink_Initialize()`; T1S comes up in parallel with the UART link (no transport arbitration yet — that's Phase 4).

A couple of deliberate choices: the library's mandatory callbacks live in `t1s_link.c`, except `TC6_CB_OnExtendedStatus` which `tc6-regs.c` provides (defining it would clash); and the example sources aren't compiled, so no duplicate symbols.

64	    out[2] = 0x00u;

72	{
73	    if ((mac[0] != 0x02u) || (mac[1] | mac[2] | mac[3] | mac[4])) {
74	        return NULL;
75	    }
76	    for (uint8_t i = 0u; i < (sizeof(s_nodes) / sizeof(s_nodes[0])); i++) {

78	            return &s_nodes[i];
79	        }
80	    }
81	    return NULL;

109	    (void)context;

121	    BaseType_t hpw = pdFALSE;
122	    s_need_service = true;

125	}

127	/* TX completion: the staged frame buffer is free for reuse. */
128	static void tx_done_cb(TC6_t *pInst, const uint8_t *pTx, uint16_t len,
129	                       void *pTag, void *pGlobalTag)
130	{
131	    (void)pInst;
132	    (void)pTx;
133	    (void)len;
134	    (void)pTag;
135	    (void)pGlobalTag;
136	    s_tx_busy = false;

139	/* Frame a payload to a node (dst = 02:00:00:00:00:<node_id>) and queue it.
140	 * Returns false if a TX is already in flight or the driver rejected it. */
141	static bool send_to_node(uint8_t node_id, const uint8_t *payload, uint16_t payload_len)
142	{
143	    if (s_tx_busy || !s_link_up) {
144	        return false;
145	    }
146	    if (payload_len > (sizeof(s_tx_frame) - T1S_ETH_HDR_LEN)) {
147	        return false;
148	    }
149	    node_mac(&s_tx_frame[0], node_id);          /* dest MAC */
150	    memcpy(&s_tx_frame[6], s_mac, T1S_MAC_LEN);  /* src MAC  */
151	    s_tx_frame[12] = (uint8_t)(T1S_ETHERTYPE >> 8);
152	    s_tx_frame[13] = (uint8_t)(T1S_ETHERTYPE & 0xFFu);
153	    memcpy(&s_tx_frame[T1S_ETH_HDR_LEN], payload, payload_len);
154	
155	    s_tx_busy = true;
156	    bool ok = TC6_SendRawEthernetPacket(s_tc6, s_tx_frame,
157	                                        (uint16_t)(T1S_ETH_HDR_LEN + payload_len),
158	                                        0u, tx_done_cb, NULL);
159	    if (!ok) {
160	        s_tx_busy = false;
161	    }
162	    return ok;
163	}

165	/* Run the protocol stack until it has no immediately pending work. IRQ_N is
166	 * active-low; TC6_Service treats a false interruptLevel as "interrupt active". */
167	static void service_pump(void)
168	{
169	    do {
170	        s_need_service = false;
171	        bool no_int = (T1S_IRQ_N_Get() != 0u);
172	        (void)TC6_Service(s_tc6, no_int);
173	    } while (s_need_service);
174	    TC6Regs_CheckTimers();
175	}
176	
177	static void t1s_task(void *param)
178	{
179	    (void)param;
180	
181	    /* Hardware reset pulse (T1S_RST is active-low, idle high). */
182	    T1S_RST_Clear();
183	    vTaskDelay(pdMS_TO_TICKS(10));
184	    T1S_RST_Set();
185	    vTaskDelay(pdMS_TO_TICKS(10));
186	
187	    /* SPI: Mode 0 (CPOL=0 idle low, CPHA=0 leading edge), 8-bit, 15 MHz.
188	     * Source clock 0 => PLib uses the FLEXCOM4 peripheral clock. */
189	    FLEXCOM_SPI_TRANSFER_SETUP setup = {
190	        .clockFrequency = T1S_SPI_HZ,
191	        .clockPhase     = FLEXCOM_SPI_CLOCK_PHASE_LEADING_EDGE,
192	        .clockPolarity  = FLEXCOM_SPI_CLOCK_POLARITY_IDLE_LOW,
193	        .dataBits       = FLEXCOM_SPI_DATA_BITS_8,
194	    };
195	    (void)FLEXCOM4_SPI_TransferSetup(&setup, 0u);
196	    FLEXCOM4_SPI_CallbackRegister(spi_done_cb, 0u);
197	
198	    s_tc6 = TC6_Init(NULL);
199	    if (s_tc6 == NULL) {
200	        LOG_ERROR("T1S: TC6_Init failed\r\n");
201	        vTaskDelete(NULL);
202	        return;
203	    }
204	
205	    (void)PIO_PinInterruptCallbackRegister(T1S_IRQ_N_PIN, irq_cb, 0u);
206	    PIO_PinInterruptEnable(T1S_IRQ_N_PIN);
207	
208	    /* Configure the LAN8651 registers + PLCA (coordinator, id 0). promiscuous
209	     * during bring-up so RX isn't filtered before the node table exists. */
210	    while (!TC6Regs_Init(s_tc6, NULL, s_mac, T1S_PLCA_ENABLE, T1S_NODE_ID,
211	                         T1S_NODE_COUNT, 0u, 0u, true, false, false)) {
212	        LOG_WARN("T1S: TC6Regs_Init busy, retrying\r\n");
213	        vTaskDelay(pdMS_TO_TICKS(50));
214	    }
215	
216	    /* Drive the async register writes to completion (bounded for the up log). */
217	    TickType_t deadline = xTaskGetTickCount() + pdMS_TO_TICKS(3000);
218	    while (!TC6Regs_GetInitDone(s_tc6) &&
219	           ((int32_t)(deadline - xTaskGetTickCount()) > 0)) {
220	        (void)xSemaphoreTake(s_svc_sem, pdMS_TO_TICKS(2));
221	        service_pump();
222	    }
223	
224	    if (TC6Regs_GetInitDone(s_tc6)) {
225	        s_link_up = true;
226	        TC6_EnableData(s_tc6, true);
227	        LOG_INFO("T1S: LAN8651 up — chipRev=%u, MAC=%02X:%02X:%02X:%02X:%02X:%02X, "
228	                 "PLCA coord id=%u/%u\r\n",
229	                 (unsigned)TC6Regs_GetChipRevision(s_tc6),
230	                 s_mac[0], s_mac[1], s_mac[2], s_mac[3], s_mac[4], s_mac[5],
231	                 (unsigned)T1S_NODE_ID, (unsigned)T1S_NODE_COUNT);
232	    } else {
233	        LOG_WARN("T1S: MAC-PHY not responding (check EVB/wiring); still servicing\r\n");
234	    }
235	
236	    TickType_t last_hb = xTaskGetTickCount();
237	    for (;;) {
238	        (void)xSemaphoreTake(s_svc_sem, pdMS_TO_TICKS(1));
239	        service_pump();
240	        if (!s_link_up && TC6Regs_GetInitDone(s_tc6)) {
241	            s_link_up = true;
242	            TC6_EnableData(s_tc6, true);
243	            LOG_INFO("T1S: LAN8651 up (late) — chipRev=%u\r\n",
244	                     (unsigned)TC6Regs_GetChipRevision(s_tc6));
245	        }
246	
247	        /* Periodic 1-byte heartbeat to the fretboard node — exercises the TX
248	         * framing path on the bus. Phase 4 carries the real command byte. */
249	        if (s_link_up &&
250	            ((xTaskGetTickCount() - last_hb) >= pdMS_TO_TICKS(T1S_HEARTBEAT_MS))) {
251	            last_hb = xTaskGetTickCount();
252	            uint8_t hb = 0u;
253	            (void)send_to_node(s_nodes[0].node_id, &hb, 1u);
254	        }
255	    }
256	}

274	bool TC6_CB_OnSpiTransaction(uint8_t tc6instance, uint8_t *pTx, uint8_t *pRx,
275	                             uint16_t len, void *pGlobalTag)
276	{
277	    (void)tc6instance;
278	    (void)pGlobalTag;
279	    /* Non-blocking full-duplex transfer; spi_done_cb calls TC6_SpiBufferDone.
280	     * Returns false if the PLib is busy — the driver retries. */
281	    return FLEXCOM4_SPI_WriteRead(pTx, len, pRx, len);
282	}

284	void TC6_CB_OnNeedService(TC6_t *pInst, void *pGlobalTag)
285	{
286	    (void)pInst;
287	    (void)pGlobalTag;
288	    /* May be called from task or ISR context; just flag. ISR sources also give
289	     * the semaphore, so the service task always wakes. */
290	    s_need_service = true;
291	}

296	    (void)pInst;
297	    (void)pGlobalTag;
298	    if (((uint32_t)offset + len) <= sizeof(s_rx_buf)) {
299	        memcpy(&s_rx_buf[offset], pRx, len);
300	    }
301	}
302	
303	void TC6_CB_OnRxEthernetPacket(TC6_t *pInst, bool success, uint16_t len,
304	                               uint64_t *rxTimestamp, void *pGlobalTag)
305	{
306	    (void)pInst;
307	    (void)rxTimestamp;
308	    (void)pGlobalTag;
309	
310	    if (!success || (len < T1S_ETH_HDR_LEN)) {
311	        return;
312	    }
313	
314	    uint16_t ethertype = (uint16_t)((s_rx_buf[12] << 8) | s_rx_buf[13]);
315	    if (ethertype != T1S_ETHERTYPE) {
316	        return;  /* not ours (promiscuous RX during bring-up) */
317	    }
318	
319	    const uint8_t *src = &s_rx_buf[6];
320	    const t1s_node_t *node = node_for_mac(src);
321	    if (node == NULL) {
322	        LOG_DEBUG("T1S: rx from unknown node %02X:%02X:%02X:%02X:%02X:%02X\r\n",
323	                  src[0], src[1], src[2], src[3], src[4], src[5]);
324	        return;
325	    }
326	
327	    const uint8_t *payload = &s_rx_buf[T1S_ETH_HDR_LEN];
328	    uint16_t       payload_len = (uint16_t)(len - T1S_ETH_HDR_LEN);
329	    (void)payload;
330	
331	    /* Phase 3: demux only. Phase 4 routes the payload (e.g. the 17-byte
332	     * fretboard frame) to the detector-state bus / PERF_REC_FRETBOARD_RAW. */
333	    LOG_DEBUG("T1S: rx node=%u det=%u %u B\r\n",
334	              (unsigned)node->node_id, (unsigned)node->detector_id,
335	              (unsigned)payload_len);
336	}
337	
338	void TC6_CB_OnError(TC6_t *pInst, TC6_Error_t err, void *pGlobalTag)
339	{
340	    (void)pGlobalTag;
341	    LOG_WARN("T1S: error: %s\r\n", TC6_GetErrorStr(err));
342	    switch (err) {
343	        case TC6Error_NoHardware:
344	        case TC6Error_BadChecksum:
345	        case TC6Error_UnexpectedCtrl:
346	        case TC6Error_BadTxData:
347	        case TC6Error_SyncLost:
348	        case TC6Error_SpiError:
349	            TC6Regs_Reinit(pInst);
350	            break;
351	        default:
352	            break;
353	    }
354	}
355	
356	/*>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>  TC6Regs callbacks (integrator)  >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>*/
357	
358	uint32_t TC6Regs_CB_GetTicksMs(void)
359	{
360	    /* configTICK_RATE_HZ is 1000, so one tick is one millisecond. */
361	    return (uint32_t)xTaskGetTickCount();
362	}
363	
364	void TC6Regs_CB_OnEvent(TC6_t *pInst, TC6Regs_Event_t event, void *pTag)
365	{
366	    (void)pTag;
367	    LOG_INFO("T1S: event: %s\r\n", TC6Regs_GetEventStr(event));
368	    switch (event) {
369	        case TC6Regs_Event_Loss_of_Framing_Error:
370	        case TC6Regs_Event_RX_Non_Recoverable_Error:
371	        case TC6Regs_Event_TX_Non_Recoverable_Error:
372	            TC6Regs_Reinit(pInst);
373	            break;
374	        default:
375	            break;
376	    }
377	}
378

## What's left

**Phase 4 — wire it under the `FretboardLink` API.** This is where T1S stops running as a parallel bring-up exercise and actually carries the fretboard data, selectable against the UART path:
- A `MARVIN_FRETBOARD_TRANSPORT={UART,T1S}` build flag so `FretboardLink_Send()` routes the 1-byte command over T1S (`send_to_node`) instead of FLEXCOM1 — replacing the heartbeat with the real command byte.
- RX: route a node's incoming 17-byte payload to `PerfLog_EmitFretboardRaw` / the detector-state bus, exactly as the UART RX parser does today — so everything above the transport is unchanged.

One thing worth noting before Phase 4: it can be written and built, but **end-to-end validation needs the fretboard talking T1S** (a second node). Today the fretboard is still on its SERCOM1 UART. So Phase 4 on marvin gets us code-complete + the transport flag, but the real round-trip test arrives when we bring up the fretboard's T1S side (the shared portable layer reuse) or wire a test peer.

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-16 22:17:57Z)**_

Phase 4 — wire T1S under the `FretboardLink` API behind a transport flag. Key design decisions:

- **Keep all TC6 access in the t1s service task** (TC6 isn't reentrant): `FretboardLink_Send` → T1S stashes a latest-wins command that the service loop flushes, rather than calling TC6 from another task. This also retires the Phase 3 heartbeat.
- **RX runs in the service task too** — `OnRxEthernetPacket` → registered frame handler → the same `emit_fretboard_frame` that the UART RX path uses, so `PERF_REC_FRETBOARD_RAW` is identical above the transport.
- **`fretboard_link.c` owns transport selection** via `MARVIN_FRETBOARD_TRANSPORT={UART,T1S}` and brings up the chosen backend, so `app.c` just calls `FretboardLink_Initialize()`.

```c
#include "fretboard_link.h"

#include <stdint.h>
#include <stdbool.h>
#include <string.h>

#include "FreeRTOS.h"
#include "task.h"
#include "queue.h"
#include "semphr.h"

#include "definitions.h"
#include "log.h"
#include "timing_pipeline.h"
#include "perf_log/perf_log.h"
#include "video/video.h"
#include "game/fret.h"

#if (MARVIN_FRETBOARD_TRANSPORT == FRETBOARD_TRANSPORT_T1S)
#include "net/t1s/t1s_link.h"
#include "detector/detector.h"  /* DETECTOR_ADC_FRETBOARD */
#endif

#define FBL_TASK_STACK_WORDS    768u
#define FBL_TASK_PRIORITY       5u

#define FBL_CMD_QUEUE_DEPTH     1u   /* latest-wins via xQueueOverwrite */

#define DS_FRAME_LEN            17u
#define DS_START_BYTE           0x03u
#define DS_END_BYTE             0xFCu

/* Idle heartbeat: re-send last mask if the timing pipeline goes quiet, so
 * a stalled detector or paused game can't leave a stale frets-active
 * pattern stuck on the wire. 50 ms is well below human-perceptible. */
#define FBL_HEARTBEAT_MS        50u

static QueueHandle_t s_cmd_queue;
static StaticQueue_t s_cmd_queue_buf;
static uint8_t       s_cmd_queue_storage[FBL_CMD_QUEUE_DEPTH * sizeof(uint8_t)];

static StackType_t   s_task_stack[FBL_TASK_STACK_WORDS];
static StaticTask_t  s_task_tcb;

/* Asserted-mask snapshot + last send result, snapshotted into the
 * PERF_REC_ACTUATOR record so the host can read which byte went out and when.
 * Transport-independent. */
static volatile uint8_t  s_last_sent_byte;
static volatile int32_t  s_last_ack_result;
static volatile uint64_t s_last_ack_ts_counter;

/* Parse a validated 17-byte fretboard frame and emit a PERF_REC_FRETBOARD_RAW
 * record. Shared by both transports; the caller guarantees the frame markers.
 * Frame: [0x03, 5×ADC_u16 LE, seq_u32 LE, applied_mask_u8, 0xFC]. */
static void emit_fretboard_frame(const uint8_t *frame)
{
    static uint32_t parsed;

    uint16_t adc[FRET_COUNT];
    for (uint8_t i = 0u; i < FRET_COUNT; i++)
    {
        adc[i] = (uint16_t)frame[1u + i * 2u]
               | (uint16_t)((uint16_t)frame[2u + i * 2u] << 8);
    }

    uint32_t fb_seq = (uint32_t)frame[11]
                    | ((uint32_t)frame[12] << 8)
                    | ((uint32_t)frame[13] << 16)
                    | ((uint32_t)frame[14] << 24);
    uint8_t  applied_mask = frame[15];

    Video_FrameInfo info;
    Video_GetFrameInfo(&info);
    PerfLog_EmitFretboardRaw(adc, info.frame_count, fb_seq, applied_mask);

    parsed++;
    if (parsed == 1u || (parsed % 240u) == 0u)
    {
        LOG_DEBUG("FBL: rx parsed=%u G=%u R=%u Y=%u B=%u O=%u\r\n",
                  (unsigned)parsed,
                  (unsigned)adc[0], (unsigned)adc[1], (unsigned)adc[2],
                  (unsigned)adc[3], (unsigned)adc[4]);
    }
}

#if (MARVIN_FRETBOARD_TRANSPORT == FRETBOARD_TRANSPORT_T1S)

/* T1S RX: the fretboard's 17-byte frame arrives as the Ethernet payload,
 * already deframed by the MAC-PHY + TC6, so only the markers are checked. */
static void t1s_frame_handler(uint8_t detector_id, const uint8_t *payload, uint16_t len)
{
    if ((detector_id == (uint8_t)DETECTOR_ADC_FRETBOARD) &&
        (len >= DS_FRAME_LEN) &&
        (payload[0] == DS_START_BYTE) &&
        (payload[DS_FRAME_LEN - 1u] == DS_END_BYTE))
    {
        emit_fretboard_frame(payload);
    }
}

static bool send_one_byte(uint8_t mask)
{
    uint8_t tx_byte = (uint8_t)(mask & 0x7F);
    if (!T1SLink_SendToFretboard(tx_byte))
    {
        return false;
    }
    PerfLog_EmitStamp(PERF_STAGE_FBL_SEND, 0u, (uint32_t)tx_byte);
    s_last_sent_byte      = tx_byte;
    s_last_ack_result     = 0;
    s_last_ack_ts_counter = SYS_TIME_Counter64Get();
    PerfLog_EmitStamp(PERF_STAGE_CDC_WRITE_COMPLETE, 0u, 0u);
    return true;
}

#else  /* FRETBOARD_TRANSPORT_UART */

#define FBL_RX_TASK_STACK_WORDS 512u

/* RX notification threshold: wake the parse task once a full frame's worth of
 * bytes has landed in the FLEXCOM1 RX ring. The ring (sized in MCC) keeps
 * receiving continuously, so there is no per-read re-arm gap to lose bytes
 * across. */
#define FBL_RX_THRESHOLD        DS_FRAME_LEN

/* Bound the RX wait so a missed notification can't wedge the parser; the
 * stream is continuous at 240 Hz so a wake normally arrives every ~4 ms. */
#define FBL_RX_WAIT_MS          100u

/* Link runs at 500 000 baud, 8N1 — configured by the MCC FLEXCOM1 USART
 * component (FLEXCOM1_USART_Initialize). Must match the fretboard SERCOM1
 * setting or every byte arrives corrupt. */

static StackType_t   s_rx_task_stack[FBL_RX_TASK_STACK_WORDS];
static StaticTask_t  s_rx_task_tcb;

/* Given from the FLEXCOM1 read callback (ISR) when the RX ring crosses the
 * frame threshold; woken thread drains and parses. */
static SemaphoreHandle_t s_rx_notify;
static StaticSemaphore_t s_rx_notify_buf;

/* A UART has no enumeration step — the link is up once Initialize has armed
 * the peripheral. Kept so producers and the heartbeat path can gate sends. */
static volatile bool s_link_up;

static void rx_event_handler(FLEXCOM_USART_EVENT event, uintptr_t context)
{
    (void)context;
    BaseType_t hpw = pdFALSE;

    switch (event)
    {
        case FLEXCOM_USART_EVENT_READ_THRESHOLD_REACHED:
        case FLEXCOM_USART_EVENT_READ_BUFFER_FULL:
            (void)xSemaphoreGiveFromISR(s_rx_notify, &hpw);
            break;
        case FLEXCOM_USART_EVENT_READ_ERROR:
            /* Consume + clear the error status; the resync parser recovers
             * frame alignment on the next valid start/end pair. */
            (void)FLEXCOM1_USART_ErrorGet();
            (void)xSemaphoreGiveFromISR(s_rx_notify, &hpw);
            break;
        default:
            break;
    }

    portYIELD_FROM_ISR(hpw);
}

static bool send_one_byte(uint8_t mask)
{
    if (!s_link_up) { return false; }

    uint8_t tx_byte = (uint8_t)(mask & 0x7F);

    /* Ring-buffer Write copies the byte into the TX ring and returns the
     * count accepted; for a single byte this only fails if the TX ring is
     * full, which shouldn't happen at command rates. */
    if (FLEXCOM1_USART_Write(&tx_byte, 1u) != 1u)
    {
        LOG_WARN("FBL: TX ring full, byte dropped\r\n");
        return false;
    }
    PerfLog_EmitStamp(PERF_STAGE_FBL_SEND, 0u, (uint32_t)tx_byte);

    s_last_sent_byte      = tx_byte;
    s_last_ack_result     = 0;
    s_last_ack_ts_counter = SYS_TIME_Counter64Get();
    PerfLog_EmitStamp(PERF_STAGE_CDC_WRITE_COMPLETE, 0u, 0u);
    return true;
}

/* Drain the FLEXCOM1 RX ring and emit one PERF_REC_FRETBOARD_RAW per parsed
 * 17-byte frame. Resync: a frame is valid only when buf[0]==0x03 AND
 * buf[16]==0xFC; otherwise drop the leading byte and retry alignment. */
static void fretboard_rx_task(void *param)
{
    (void)param;

    uint8_t  frame[DS_FRAME_LEN];
    size_t   filled = 0u;
    uint32_t skipped_bytes = 0u;

    for (;;)
    {
        if (FLEXCOM1_USART_ReadCountGet() == 0u)
        {
            (void)xSemaphoreTake(s_rx_notify, pdMS_TO_TICKS(FBL_RX_WAIT_MS));
            continue;
        }

        size_t want = DS_FRAME_LEN - filled;
        size_t got  = FLEXCOM1_USART_Read(&frame[filled], want);
        if (got == 0u) { continue; }
        filled += got;
        if (filled < DS_FRAME_LEN) { continue; }

        if (frame[0] != DS_START_BYTE || frame[DS_FRAME_LEN - 1u] != DS_END_BYTE)
        {
            /* Misaligned: drop one byte and shift, then loop to refill. */
            memmove(&frame[0], &frame[1], DS_FRAME_LEN - 1u);
            filled = DS_FRAME_LEN - 1u;
            skipped_bytes++;
            continue;
        }

        emit_fretboard_frame(frame);
        filled = 0u;
    }
}

#endif  /* MARVIN_FRETBOARD_TRANSPORT */

static void fretboard_link_task(void *param)
{
    (void)param;

    LOG_INFO("FBL: fretboard link started\r\n");

    uint8_t last_mask = 0u;

    for (;;)
    {
        uint8_t mask;
        if (xQueueReceive(s_cmd_queue, &mask, pdMS_TO_TICKS(FBL_HEARTBEAT_MS)) == pdTRUE)
        {
            last_mask = mask;
        }
        else
        {
            mask = last_mask;
        }

        (void)send_one_byte(mask);
    }
}

void FretboardLink_Initialize(void)
{
    s_cmd_queue = xQueueCreateStatic(FBL_CMD_QUEUE_DEPTH,
                                     sizeof(uint8_t),
                                     s_cmd_queue_storage,
                                     &s_cmd_queue_buf);
    configASSERT(s_cmd_queue != NULL);

#if (MARVIN_FRETBOARD_TRANSPORT == FRETBOARD_TRANSPORT_T1S)
    /* T1S transport owns the MAC-PHY/service task; RX frames arrive via the
     * registered handler, TX commands flow through T1SLink_SendToFretboard. */
    T1SLink_Initialize();
    T1SLink_SetFrameHandler(t1s_frame_handler);
#else
    s_rx_notify = xSemaphoreCreateBinaryStatic(&s_rx_notify_buf);
    configASSERT(s_rx_notify != NULL);

    /* Arm continuous RX: the ring fills from the FLEXCOM1 ISR; persistent
     * threshold notification wakes fretboard_rx_task each frame's worth. */
    FLEXCOM1_USART_ReadCallbackRegister(rx_event_handler, 0u);
    FLEXCOM1_USART_ReadThresholdSet(FBL_RX_THRESHOLD);
    (void)FLEXCOM1_USART_ReadNotificationEnable(true, true);

    s_link_up = true;
#endif

    TaskHandle_t h = xTaskCreateStatic(fretboard_link_task,
                                       "FretLink",
                                       FBL_TASK_STACK_WORDS,
                                       NULL,
                                       FBL_TASK_PRIORITY,
                                       s_task_stack,
                                       &s_task_tcb);
    PerfLog_RegisterTaskForHighwater(PERF_TASK_FRETBOARD_LINK, h);

#if (MARVIN_FRETBOARD_TRANSPORT != FRETBOARD_TRANSPORT_T1S)
    TaskHandle_t hr = xTaskCreateStatic(fretboard_rx_task,
                                        "FretRx",
                                        FBL_RX_TASK_STACK_WORDS,
                                        NULL,
                                        FBL_TASK_PRIORITY,
                                        s_rx_task_stack,
                                        &s_rx_task_tcb);
    PerfLog_RegisterTaskForHighwater(PERF_TASK_FRETBOARD_RX, hr);
#endif
}

bool FretboardLink_IsConnected(void)
{
#if (MARVIN_FRETBOARD_TRANSPORT == FRETBOARD_TRANSPORT_T1S)
    return T1SLink_IsConnected();
#else
    return s_link_up;
#endif
}

void FretboardLink_Send(uint8_t mask, uint8_t producer_id)
{
    if (s_cmd_queue == NULL) { return; }
    uint8_t v = (uint8_t)(mask & TIMING_BIT_VALID_MASK);
    /* Overwrite is strictly latest-wins: a newer producer's mask replaces
     * any unsent older one — keeps a stalled write from accumulating
     * stale chord state. */
    (void)xQueueOverwrite(s_cmd_queue, &v);

    uint8_t strum_dir = 0u;
    if      (v & TIMING_BIT_STRUM_DOWN) { strum_dir = 1u; }
    else if (v & TIMING_BIT_STRUM_UP)   { strum_dir = 2u; }

    PerfLog_EmitActuator(v, s_last_sent_byte, strum_dir, producer_id,
                         s_last_ack_result, s_last_ack_ts_counter);
}

```

Phase 4 marvin-side is **code-complete**. T1S now lives behind the `FretboardLink` API:

**Transport flag** — `MARVIN_FRETBOARD_TRANSPORT` in `fretboard_link.h` (default `UART`), flipped with one line in `user.cmake`. `fretboard_link.c` owns bring-up of the chosen backend; `app.c` is back to a single `FretboardLink_Initialize()` call.

**TX** — `send_one_byte()` is now per-transport. The T1S path calls `T1SLink_SendToFretboard(mask)`, which **stashes a latest-wins command and wakes the service task** to flush it via `send_to_node` — so all TC6 access stays single-threaded. Same `PERF_STAGE_FBL_SEND`/`ACTUATOR` telemetry as UART. (This retired the Phase 3 heartbeat.)

**RX** — factored `emit_fretboard_frame()` (validated 17-byte frame → `PERF_REC_FRETBOARD_RAW`) shared by both paths. T1S registers `t1s_frame_handler` via `T1SLink_SetFrameHandler`; since the MAC-PHY already deframes, it just checks markers → emit. So `PERF_REC_FRETBOARD_RAW` is byte-identical regardless of transport.

**Key property:** producers, perf records, and `app.c` are all unchanged — only the bytes' path swaps.

I **haven't committed**. Two build checks before I do:
1. **Default (UART) build** — regression: the fretboard link behaves exactly as before (this is the important one, since it's the committed default).
2. *Optional* **`MARVIN_FRETBOARD_TRANSPORT=1` build** — confirms the T1S path compiles and the link still comes up (commands will TX to node 1 with no receiver; full RX validation needs the fretboard peer).

Could you build #1 (and #2 if convenient)? Once it's clean I'll commit Phase 4.

Then we're set up for the **fretboard PIC32CM PL10 side** — that's where the shared `oa-tc6-lib` + L2 layer gets reused on the M0+, and it's what unlocks the real end-to-end round-trip. One thing to flag for that subproject: the PL10's SERCOM SPI tops out around ~12 MHz (vs marvin's 15), and it'll be a PLCA *follower* (node id 1), so the fretboard glue is the mirror of marvin's with `enablePlca=true, nodeId=1` and no coordinator role — we'll plan it properly when we get there.

That's the natural stopping point you flagged. What's left for end-to-end is the **fretboard PIC32CM PL10 T1S side**, which is the mirror of marvin's glue and reuses the same `oa-tc6-lib` + L2 framing (the shared-portable-layer payoff). When you start it, the key deltas from marvin to plan for:

- **No FreeRTOS** on the fretboard (bare-metal + TC0 240 Hz ISR today) — the TC6 service loop integrates into the main loop / tick instead of a task; the `IRQ_N` wiring is a SERCOM-EIC pin, not PIOB.
- **The existing `data_stream.c`/`cmd_receive.c` keep their frame formats** — only the transport under them swaps, same as marvin.

## Comprehensive Fretboard Firmware Exploration Report

I have thoroughly analyzed the fretboard firmware (`PIC32CM6408PL10048`) and can provide you with a complete picture for planning the detector/guitar split.

### Executive Summary

The firmware has **two build-time modes** controlled by `FRETBOARD_MODE` in `fretboard_config.h`:
1. **`MARVIN_DRIVEN` (I/O bridge mode)** — pure detector: scan ADCs, emit frames, apply remote commands
2. **`MODEL_DRIVEN` (current default)** — hybrid: detector + local inference (on-device ML model)

The code cleanly separates **detector** (sensor reading & UART output) from **actuator** (GPIO button control). Model inference is a **third, independent concern**.

---

### 1. HARDWARE CONFIGURATION

**Device:** PIC32CM6408PL10048 (ARM Cortex-M0+, 24 MHz, 8 KB SRAM, 64 KB Flash)

#### ADC Inputs (Phototransistor Detector — **STAY in fretboard**)
- **Green:** AIN28 (PA28)
- **Red:** AIN16 (PA16)  
- **Yellow:** AIN19 (PA19)
- **Blue:** AIN27 (PA27)
- **Orange:** AIN26 (PA26)

Read in `/firmware/fretboard/fret_scan.c:4-9` (channel mapping).

#### GPIO Outputs (Wii Guitar Button Actuator — **MOVE to new guitar project**)
Open-drain tri-state GPIOs (assert=drive low, release=input+pull-up):
- **PA06** (bit 0) — Green fret
- **PA05** (bit 1) — Red fret
- **PA07** (bit 2) — Yellow fret
- **PA04** (bit 3) — Blue fret
- **PA01** (bit 4) — Orange fret
- **PA03** (bit 5) — Strum down
- **PA00** (bit 6) — Strum up

All driven via `BUTTON_*` macros in MCC-generated `/firmware/fretboard/fretboard-mcc/src/config/default/peripheral/port/plib_port.h`.

#### UART (SERCOM1 — Transport layer)
- **TX (PB00)** — data stream out (17 or 21 bytes/frame @ 240 Hz)
- **RX (PB01)** — command in (1 byte/tick, bitmask)
- **Baud:** 500,000 (8N1)

#### Timer (TC0 — ISR Backbone)
240 Hz callback drives the sampling/apply/send loop.

### 4. BUILD-TIME MODES & CODE BRANCHING

#### Mode A: `MARVIN_DRIVEN` (Default fallback; I/O bridge)
- **Purpose:** Pure detector. No game logic, no inference. Sends raw ADCs; applies remote bitmask commands.
- **TC0 ISR:** `fret_scan_all()` → `data_stream_send()` → `cmd_receive_update()`
- **Main loop:** Empty while(true) loop
- **Orphaned files:** Still compiled (`fret_detect.c`, `fret_button.c` in fileset), but not called
- **Flash footprint:** ~8–10 KB (core + MCC)
- **SRAM:** ~1 KB

#### Mode B: `MODEL_DRIVEN` (Current default; standalone inference)
- **Purpose:** Detector + on-device ML inference. Marvin disconnected (except for initial commissioning/fallback).
- **TC0 ISR:** `fret_scan_all()` → push to model's ring/queue → apply `s_latest_cmd` → `data_stream_send_model()`
- **Main loop:** Drain sample queue/recompute inference, publish `s_latest_cmd`
- **SW0 (PB03, active-low momentary):** Toggles model on/off (debounced, ~50 ms window)
- **LED0 (PB02, active-low):** Lit when model enabled; off at boot
- **Model selection:** Runtime pointer swap via `model_infer_set_model()` (per-difficulty)
- **Flash footprint:** ~18–22 KB (core + MCC + model weights)
- **SRAM:** ~4–5 KB (input ring + layer activations + scratch)
- **Compilation guard:** Both `model_infer.c` and `model_infer_stream.c` included; `MODEL_INFER_STREAMING` selects which compiles its static buffers

---

### 5. WIRE PROTOCOL (SERCOM1, 500 kbaud)

#### MARVIN_DRIVEN data frame (17 bytes, sent every 4.17 ms @ 240 Hz):
```
Offset  Size  Field
0       1     start = 0x03
1–2     2×u16 green (LE)
3–4     2×u16 red (LE)
5–6     2×u16 yellow (LE)
7–8     2×u16 blue (LE)
9–10    2×u16 orange (LE)
11–14   1×u32 sample_seq (LE, monotonic; gaps = dropped frames)
15      1×u8  applied_mask (bitmask currently driving GPIO)
16      1     end = 0xFC
```

**Applied mask:** Bits [0–6] = frets [0–4], strum-down, strum-up. Snapshot at send time (from `cmd_receive_current_mask()`).

#### MODEL_DRIVEN data frame (21 bytes):
```
Offset  Size  Field
0–16    (as above)
17–20   1×u32 infer_count (total inferences run in main loop)
16      1     end = 0xFC (shifted to offset 20)
```

**Total bandwidth:** 17 B × 240 Hz = 4.08 KB/s (12× headroom at 500 kbaud).

#### RX command (single byte):
```
Bit  Function
0    Green fret
1    Red fret
2    Yellow fret
3    Blue fret
4    Orange fret
5    Strum down
6    Strum up
7    (unused)
```

**Coalescing:** Only the **last byte in the current tick** is applied (older bytes in the same tick are discarded).

**Direction (2026-06-09, not yet built):**
- Replace SERCOM1 UART (500 kbaud) with **10BASE-T1S Ethernet** (LAN8651B1 MAC-PHY + TC6 SPI driver).

- **Frame formats unchanged:** 17-byte data + 1-byte command ride inside Ethernet payload; `data_stream.c` / `cmd_receive.c` logic unaffected.
- **PLCA multi-node bus:** Marvin = ID 0; fretboard = ID 1, MAC `02:00:00:00:00:01`.

### 12. SPECIFICATION EXCERPT (from SPEC.md)

**Current stated purpose (lines 3–10):**
> Firmware for PIC32CM6408PL10048 (Cortex-M0+, 24 MHz) that acts as an **I/O bridge** between a Guitar Hero controller and an off-board host. Five phototransistors above the TV strike line are sampled and streamed out continuously; the host runs detection / chord / strum logic and sends back a single-byte bitmask that drives the controller's button GPIOs directly.

**Two build-time modes (lines 12–20):**
> - `MARVIN_DRIVEN`: firmware contains **no game logic** — it only scans ADCs, emits frames, and applies received bitmasks.
> - `MODEL_DRIVEN` (current default): on-device int8 neural net maps ADC window to button bitmask, standalone (marvin disconnected).

---

| Component | File(s) | Role | Destination | Dependencies | Notes |

You now have the complete anatomy of the fretboard firmware. The **detector → UART output** and **UART input → actuator GPIO** flows are cleanly isolated; model inference is orthogonal and currently runs standalone on the detector hardware. 1	# Fretboard Firmware Specification
2	
3	## Overview
4	
5	Firmware for PIC32CM6408PL10048 (Cortex-M0+, 24 MHz) that acts as an
6	**I/O bridge** between a Guitar Hero controller and an off-board host.
7	Five phototransistors above the TV strike line are sampled and streamed
8	out continuously; the host runs detection / chord / strum logic and
9	sends back a single-byte bitmask that drives the controller's button
10	GPIOs directly.
11	
12	In its `MARVIN_DRIVEN` mode the firmware contains **no game logic** — it only
13	scans ADCs, emits frames, and applies received bitmasks. A second build-time
14	mode, **`MODEL_DRIVEN`** (`FRETBOARD_MODE` in `main.c`, the current default),
15	makes the board standalone: an on-device int8 neural net (`model_infer.c`,
16	weights in the generated `model_weights.h`) maps the ADC window to the button
17	bitmask itself, no host required. SW0 toggles it; LED0 shows the state.
18	Inference runs in the main loop; the 240 Hz TC0 ISR only samples and applies.
19	See [`docs/journal.md`](docs/journal.md) and edge-ai
20	[`runtime.md`](../../tools/edge-ai/docs/runtime.md).
21	
22	## Hardware
23	
24	### Target
25	
26	| Spec | Value |
27	|------|-------|
28	| Device | PIC32CM6408PL10048 |
29	| Core | ARM Cortex-M0+ |
30	| Clock | 24 MHz |
31	| Toolchain | XC32 5.10 |
32	| Programmer | PKOB nano |
33	
34	### Pin Map
35	
36	#### Sensor Inputs (ADC)
37	
38	Five phototransistors positioned above the TV strike line. Each
39	produces an analog voltage that drops when a note passes the sensor.
40	ADC reads 12-bit unsigned (0–4095); lower values indicate note
41	presence.
42	
43	| Channel | ADC Input | Pin |
44	|---------|-----------|-----|
45	| Green | AIN28 | PA28 |
46	| Red | AIN16 | PA16 |
47	| Yellow | AIN19 | PA19 |
48	| Blue | AIN27 | PA27 |
49	| Orange | AIN26 | PA26 |
50	
51	#### Button Outputs (Open-Drain GPIO)
52	
53	Each button output is normally tri-stated (input mode). To "press" a
54	button the pin is driven low (clear + output-enable). To "release" it
55	the pin returns to input mode, which floats the line and lets the
56	guitar controller's own pull-up restore the idle state.
57	
58	| Function | Pin | Cmd bit |
59	|----------|-----|---------|
60	| Green fret | PA06 | 0 |
61	| Red fret | PA05 | 1 |
62	| Yellow fret | PA07 | 2 |
63	| Blue fret | PA04 | 3 |
64	| Orange fret | PA01 | 4 |
65	| Strum down | PA03 | 5 |
66	| Strum up | PA00 | 6 |
67	
68	#### UART (SERCOM1)
69	
70	| Function | Pin |
71	|----------|-----|
72	| TX (data stream out) | PB00 |
73	| RX (command in) | PB01 |
74	
75	Baud: **500 000**, 8N1.
76	
77	## Software Architecture
78	
79	### Processing Loop
80	
81	`TC0` is configured to fire a periodic callback at **240 Hz**
82	(≈4.17 ms period). Each tick runs three stages in sequence from the
83	timer ISR:
84	
85	```
86	TC0 callback (240 Hz)
87	    |
88	    v
89	fret_scan_all()          Blocking ADC read of all 5 channels
90	    |
91	    v
92	data_stream_send()       17-byte frame over SERCOM1 TX
93	    |
94	    v
95	cmd_receive_update()     Drains SERCOM1 RX, applies latest bitmask
96	```
97	
98	`main()` is just init + idle loop; all work happens in the TC0 ISR.
99	
100	### Module Descriptions
101	
102	#### fret_scan ([fret_scan.c](fret_scan.c) / [fret_scan.h](fret_scan.h))
103	
104	Reads all five ADC channels sequentially using blocking polling.
105	Results are stored in a static array and accessed via
106	`fret_scan_result(channel)`.
107	
108	The channel enum defines the canonical fret ordering used throughout
109	the firmware:
110	
111	```
112	FRET_GREEN = 0, FRET_RED = 1, FRET_YELLOW = 2, FRET_BLUE = 3, FRET_ORANGE = 4
113	```
114	
115	#### data_stream ([data_stream.c](data_stream.c) / [data_stream.h](data_stream.h))
116	
117	Emits one 17-byte little-endian frame per tick over SERCOM1 TX:
118	
119	| Offset | Size | Field |
120	|-------:|-----:|-------|
121	| 0 | 1 | start = `0x03` |
122	| 1 | 2 | green (uint16) |
123	| 3 | 2 | red |
124	| 5 | 2 | yellow |
125	| 7 | 2 | blue |
126	| 9 | 2 | orange |
127	| 11 | 4 | sample_seq (uint32) — monotonic, one per tick |
128	| 15 | 1 | applied_mask — actuator bitmask driven this scan |
129	| 16 | 1 | end = `0xFC` (`~start`) |
130	
131	`sample_seq` lets the host reconstruct true sample order and detect frames
132	dropped in transit (it advances per tick even when a send is skipped).
133	`applied_mask` is the bitmask `cmd_receive` currently drives, captured in the
134	same tick as the scan so sensor and actuator state are paired at the source
135	(used by edge-ai training-data export). The frame is dropped silently if the
136	TX free-buffer count is below the frame size. At 240 Hz this is 4 080 B/s —
137	well within the 50 000 B/s budget at 500 000 baud.
138	
139	#### cmd_receive ([cmd_receive.c](cmd_receive.c) / [cmd_receive.h](cmd_receive.h))
140	
141	Drains the SERCOM1 RX buffer each tick. The **last byte received** in
142	the tick is interpreted as a button bitmask and applied directly:
143	
144	| Bit | Output |
145	|----:|--------|
146	| 0 | Green fret |
147	| 1 | Red fret |
148	| 2 | Yellow fret |
149	| 3 | Blue fret |
150	| 4 | Orange fret |
151	| 5 | Strum down |
152	| 6 | Strum up |
153	
154	Bit set → drive low (assert). Bit clear → tri-state (release).
155	
156	Note: only the most recent byte each tick is honoured. The host is
157	expected to send commands at a rate ≤ the loop rate; older bytes in
158	the same tick are coalesced away.
159	
160	## Tools
161	
162	### Host-side data-stream monitor
163	
164	[`tools/ds_monitor.py`](tools/ds_monitor.py) opens the serial port,
165	resyncs on `0x03 … 0xFC` framing, and reports actual frame rate, byte
166	rate, framing-error count, and current ADC values once per second.
167	
168	The script declares its dependencies inline (PEP 723) and is run via
169	[`uv`](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) — no manual venv or `pip install`
170	needed:
171	
172	```
173	./tools/ds_monitor.py /dev/tty.usbmodem<...>
174	# or, equivalently:
175	uv run tools/ds_monitor.py /dev/tty.usbmodem<...>
176	```
177	
178	Defaults: `--baud 500000 --expect-hz 240`.
179	
180	## Build System
181	
182	MPLAB Extensions for VS Code. Project config is in
183	`.vscode/fretboard.mplab.json`. Source files are listed in the
184	`fileSets[0].files` array. MCC/Harmony-generated code lives under
185	`fretboard-mcc/` and should not be edited.
186	
187	## File Map
188	
189	| File | Purpose |
190	|------|---------|
191	| [main.c](main.c) | Init + TC0 callback wiring |
192	| [fret_scan.c](fret_scan.c) / [.h](fret_scan.h) | ADC channel scanning |
193	| [data_stream.c](data_stream.c) / [.h](data_stream.h) | UART output frame |
194	| [cmd_receive.c](cmd_receive.c) / [.h](cmd_receive.h) | UART input bitmask |
195	| [tools/ds_monitor.py](tools/ds_monitor.py) | Host-side frame-rate / content check |
196	| `fret_detect.c` / `.h` | **Orphaned** (see [docs/journal.md](docs/journal.md)) |
197	| `fret_button.c` / `.h` | **Orphaned** (see [docs/journal.md](docs/journal.md)) |
198	| `fretboard-mcc/` | MCC Harmony peripheral libraries (generated) |
199
```
