1	# fretboard — Working Journal
2	
3	Running log of planning, decisions, open questions, and work-in-progress for the fretboard firmware. Newest entries at the top. For *what fretboard is* (purpose, hardware, modules, frame format), read [`../SPEC.md`](../SPEC.md) — this journal does not duplicate it.
4	
5	---
6	
7	## Current focus
8	
9	**Two build-time modes (`FRETBOARD_MODE` in `main.c`):**
10	
11	- **`MARVIN_DRIVEN`** (I/O bridge) — 240 Hz TC0 callback: scan five ADCs, emit a 17-byte frame on SERCOM1 TX, drain RX and apply the latest button bitmask. Frame carries `sample_seq` + the applied actuator bitmask (edge-ai training-data sync). Chord/strum logic off-board.
12	- **`MODEL_DRIVEN`** (new, current default — standalone edge-ai inference) — the on-device int8 model ([`model_infer.c`](../model_infer.c), weights in [`model_weights.h`](../model_weights.h)) reads the ADC window and drives the buttons itself; marvin disconnected. **SW0 (PB03)** toggles model control, **LED0 (PB02)** shows enabled (boots disabled). The 240 Hz TC0 ISR only samples + applies the latest command + streams; `model_infer_run()` runs in the **main loop** (it overruns the tick if put in the ISR — see decision log + edge-ai `runtime.md` §3). Build at `-O2`/`-O3`.
13	
14	Baud is 500 000. Host checks: [`tools/ds_monitor.py`](../tools/ds_monitor.py) (framing) and [`../../../tools/marvin-perf/fretboard_rate.py`](../../../tools/marvin-perf/fretboard_rate.py) (true tick rate from `sample_seq` + strums/s).
15	
16	---
17	
18	## Decision log
19	
20	| Date | Decision | Rationale |
21	|------|----------|-----------|
22	| 2026-06-04 | **Added `MODEL_DRIVEN` mode: on-device int8 inference (`model_infer.c/.h` + generated `model_weights.h`), SW0/LED0 enable toggle, and inference run in the main loop — NOT the TC0 ISR.** Active model is a swappable `model_def_t` pointer (`model_infer_set_model`). Build at `-O2`/`-O3`. | Standalone bring-up of the edge-ai model (edge-ai journal 2026-06-04). **Inference must not run in the 240 Hz ISR**: measured on hardware, doing so dropped the callback rate to ~150–190 Hz (so the model's 250 ms window/lag went wrong) *and* starved the interrupt-driven SERCOM TX (recv ~22 fps, heavy drops). Moving `model_infer_run()` to the main loop and having the ISR only sample + apply a `volatile uint8_t` latest-command restored clean 240/240 Hz. The pointer-swap model_def lets per-difficulty weights be selected at runtime and keeps the door open for serial-loaded weights (RAM headroom confirmed; 8 KB SRAM). SW0 (PB03 active-low momentary, debounced) toggles control; LED0 (PB02) shows state; boots disabled (outputs released). `MARVIN_DRIVEN` stays the alternate build for the I/O-bridge path. |
23	| 2026-06-03 | Data-stream frame grows 12→17 bytes: `0x03 \| g r y b o (5×u16 LE) \| sample_seq (u32 LE) \| applied_mask (u8) \| 0xFC`. `sample_seq` is a monotonic counter incremented once per tick in `data_stream_send` (before the TX-buffer check, so a dropped send shows as a gap); `applied_mask` comes from a new `cmd_receive_current_mask()` getter. Resolves open-questions #3 and #4. | Closes the edge-ai data-sync hole (edge-ai journal 2026-06-03). Pairing the actuator state with the ADC scan *in the same frame* makes label↔feature alignment atomic at the source, instead of marvin reconstructing it across its bursty USB RX and separate TX clocks — which Phase-2 training showed floored strum timing at ~20 ms. The seq counter lets the host reconstruct true 240 Hz ordering and detect dropped frames. Callback order is scan→send→receive, so `current_mask` at send time is exactly the state driven *during* this scan. Wire-format break: requires marvin's RX parser + `perf_rec_fretboard_raw_t` (schema v4) to update in lockstep. 17 B × 240 Hz = 4.08 KB/s, still ~12× under the 500 000-baud budget. |
24	| 2026-06-02 | Leave the orphaned `fret_detect.*` and `fret_button.*` modules in place (still in MPLAB fileSet, still building, no callers). Don't delete, don't move to a `fallback/` directory. | Marvin's 2026-05-20 decision keeps a "fretboard-takeover" fallback mode in scope — `fret_button.c` is the existing implementation of that mode and is cheap to keep around. Cost is small (a few KB of flash + the stale `#include "fret_detect.h"` in `data_stream.c`). Revisit if the takeover mode is formally dropped or if these files start drifting against a refactor. |

32	## Open questions
33	
34	1. **No corruption signalling on the wire.** A bit-flip inside the 5 uint16 payload bytes is silently accepted — only out-of-range start/end bytes are caught. At 500 000 baud over EDBG-CDC this is probably fine, but if we ever see suspect detector behaviour, adding a Fletcher-16 byte (matching marvin's wire format) is a one-byte frame growth.
35	
36	2. **No host→firmware framing.** Command stream is raw bitmask bytes with no start byte. A spurious byte (e.g. line glitch on RX) becomes a button command. Acceptable for now because the line is short and runs over the same EDBG-CDC pair as TX, but worth revisiting if we see ghost presses.
37	
38	3. **T1S link transport — direction, not yet built.** Plan to move the marvin link from the SERCOM1 UART to **10BASE-T1S single-pair Ethernet + dumb PoDL** via a LAN8651B1 MAC-PHY (system spec §6 + [`../../../docs/t1s-podl-link.md`](../../../docs/t1s-podl-link.md)). Fretboard-side cost is an OA TC6 SPI driver + minimal L2 framing (~6–10 KB flash / ~1–2 KB SRAM, one free SERCOM in SPI mode + CS_N/IRQ_N/reset GPIO); the 17-byte data frame + 1-byte command formats ride unchanged inside the Ethernet payload, so `data_stream.c`/`cmd_receive.c` need no logic change — only the transport under them swaps. Scope settled on the marvin side 2026-06-16 (marvin journal): a **multi-node PLCA bus** (marvin = coordinator ID 0; fretboard = ID 1, MAC `02:00:00:00:00:01`), adapt `oa-tc6-lib` as a **shared portable TC6 + L2 layer** (the M0+ side reuses what marvin builds), one custom ethertype (~`0x88B5`, TBC), and the UART kept in parallel behind a build flag. The PIC32CM-side work follows once marvin's link is proven; `data_stream.c`/`cmd_receive.c` still need no logic change. PoDL is transparent to the MCU (zero firmware footprint). Remaining open: final ethertype/MAC values, PoDL BOM.
39	
40	> Resolved 2026-06-03 (see decision log): #3 "no sample timestamp" and #4 "no applied actuator state" — both fixed by growing the frame to 17 bytes with `sample_seq` + `applied_mask`.

void Detector_Enable(detector_id_t id)
{
    taskENTER_CRITICAL();
    s_enabled_mask |= (1u << (uint32_t)id);
    taskEXIT_CRITICAL();
}

void Detector_Disable(detector_id_t id)
{
    taskENTER_CRITICAL();
    s_enabled_mask &= ~(1u << (uint32_t)id);
    taskEXIT_CRITICAL();
}

{

}

### 6. TIMING PIPELINE ACTIVE DETECTOR FILTERING

**File:** `/Users/gregmrozek/Projects/microchip/guitar-pic/firmware/marvin/default/src/actuator/timing_pipeline.c`

The timing pipeline reads detector_state_t records from the detector-state bus queue and filters by active detector (line snippet from the task loop):

```c
for (;;)
{
    detector_state_t state;
    if (xQueueReceive(bus, &state, pdMS_TO_TICKS(TP_TICK_MS)) == pdTRUE)
    {
        if ((detector_id_t)state.detector_id != Detector_GetActive())
        {
            continue;  /* Skip records from inactive detectors */
        }
        process_frame(&state);
    }
    else
    {
        /* No new frame; advance the clock so deadlines that fell
         * between frames (strum pulses, release timers) still fire. */
        s_now_ms += TP_TICK_MS;
    }
}
```

**Console command (console.c):** The active detector can be toggled via console command `active <cv|adc>`:
```c
Detector_SetActive((detector_id_t)id);
console_printf("active = %s", (id == DETECTOR_CV_MARVIN_V1) ? "cv" : "adc");
```

**Status display (console.c):**
```c
detector_id_t act = Detector_GetActive();
console_printf("active:     %s", (act == DETECTOR_CV_MARVIN_V1) ? "cv" : "adc");
console_printf("detect cv:  %s", Detector_IsEnabled(DETECTOR_CV_MARVIN_V1)  ? "on" : "off");
console_printf("detect adc: %s", Detector_IsEnabled(DETECTOR_ADC_FRETBOARD) ? "on" : "off");
```

### 7. T1S-PODL LINK SPEC (docs/t1s-podl-link.md)

**File:** `/Users/gregmrozek/Projects/microchip/guitar-pic/docs/t1s-podl-link.md`

**Key sections:**
- §2: LAN8651B1 MAC-PHY part description
- §3: Host MCU implementation requirements (SPI, OA TC6 chunk protocol, minimal L2 framing)
- §4: Resource budget for fretboard (6–10 KB flash / 1–2 KB SRAM)
- §5: marvin side (FreeRTOS + Harmony, adapts oa-tc6-lib)
- §6: PoDL (dumb, transparent to firmware)
- **§7.1: Addressing scheme** — Locally administered MACs, static node table with no discovery
- §8: Transport coexistence (UART + T1S behind build flag)

**Node table excerpt (§7.1, lines 152–167):**
> "| Node | PLCA ID | MAC (locally administered) | Notes |
> |---|---|---|---|
> | marvin | 0 (coordinator) | `02:00:00:00:00:00` | beacons the PLCA cycle |
> | node *k* | *k* | `02:00:00:00:00:0k` | e.g. fretboard = ID 1 |
> 
> - One **custom ethertype** `0x88B5` (IEEE local/experimental range; no registration needed for a private bus) carries the existing payloads verbatim.
> - A static **node table** on marvin maps `{PLCA ID, MAC, node_type}` → the bus `detector_id` (and the actuator target for TX). The single fretboard keeps `detector_id = 1`, matching today's `adc_fretboard` bus slot."

## CRITICAL DESIGN POINTS ALREADY IN PLACE

1. **Multi-node model is already architected** — the T1S link design (lines 41–56 of t1s_link.c) defines `t1s_node_type_t` enum and `s_nodes[]` table with lookup functions (`node_for_type`, `node_for_mac`) ready for N nodes.

2. **Detector ID is decoupled from node** — a node has a `type` (T1S_NODE_FRETBOARD, etc.) but feeds its data to a `detector_id` (e.g., DETECTOR_ADC_FRETBOARD). A new guitar node type gets a new detector ID slot and registers in the node table by node_id, MAC, and type.

3. **Timing pipeline filters by `Detector_GetActive()`** — independent of how many detectors/nodes are enabled, only one is active for the timing pipeline at a time (console command `active <cv|adc>` switches). Adding a third detector ID requires only a new enum value and console command enhancement.

4. **Frame format is transport-agnostic** — the 17-byte fretboard ADC stream rides inside the Ethernet payload unchanged (docs/t1s-podl-link.md §3). A new guitar node stream can follow the same pattern.

11	 *
12	 *   Bit 0 = Green fret
13	 *   Bit 1 = Red fret
14	 *   Bit 2 = Yellow fret

17	 *   Bit 5 = Strum down
18	 *   Bit 6 = Strum up
19	 *
20	 * Bit = 1 → assert (drive low), Bit = 0 → release (tri-state).

24	#define CMD_BIT_RED         (1U << 1)

39

3	> Top-level overview. For implementation detail of any single subproject, follow the pointers in §3. Each subproject owns its own spec; this document does not duplicate them.
4	
5	---
6	
7	## 1. Mission
8	
9	Build an autonomous robot that plays Guitar Hero / Rock Band on a real Wii guitar controller by watching the game video, detecting notes in real time, and pressing physical buttons in sync with the music. The system must run end-to-end without a host PC in the runtime path, produce reference-quality detector output that lighter detectors can be trained against, and provide an on-device operator UI for calibration, mode control, and replay.
10	
11	## 2. Current architecture
12	
13	Three pieces, one runtime brain:
14	
15	```
16	Wii ──HDMI──► ElectronWarp ──HDMI──► TC358743 ──CSI-2──┐
17	                                                       ▼
18	   ┌──────────────────────  marvin (SAM9X75)  ────────────┐
19	   │  HDMI capture → CV detect → timing pipeline → cmds   │
20	   │           ↑              detector-state bus          │
21	   │           │                       ▲                  │
22	   │           │  10.1″ LVDS + maxtouch │                  │
23	   │           │       (operator UI)    │                  │
24	   │           └────────── SD card ─────┘  (recording)    │
25	   └────────┬──────────────────────────┬───────────────────┘
26	            │ FLEXCOM2 UART (cmds)     │ FLEXCOM2 UART (ADC)
27	            ▼                          │
28	   ┌──────────────────────────────────┐│
29	   │   fretboard (PIC32CM6408)        │┘
30	   │   ADC scan ↔ open-drain GPIO     │
31	   └────────┬─────────────────────────┘
32	            │ GPIO
33	            ▼
34	   Wii guitar controller ──► Wii (closes the loop)
35	
36	                ◇ off-band: dev PC running fret-tuner
37	                  (calibration / detector tuning / replay)
38	```
39	
40	**Per-tier role summary:**
41	
42	- **marvin** — SAM9X75 Curiosity host. Owns HDMI capture, the *reference* CV note detector, ingest of fretboard ADC samples, the chord/strum timing pipeline, command emission to fretboard, the on-device LVDS+touch operator UI, and reference-data recording to SD. The runtime brain.
43	- **fretboard** — PIC32CM6408PL10048 MCU on a sensor/actuator board. Streams 5-channel phototransistor ADC up to marvin and converts incoming bitmask commands into open-drain GPIO presses on a Wii guitar controller. Has a standalone fallback mode where it runs its own chord FIFO without marvin in the loop.
44	- **fret-tuner** — Off-band Python tool (FastAPI + browser UI, Linux/macOS PC). Used at the bench for sensor calibration, detector-algorithm tuning, and replay analysis of recordings produced by marvin. Not in the runtime path.
45

101	## 6. Cross-cutting decisions
102	
103	- **Architecture pivot.** The original PC-hosted / Elgato-USB-capture / PS2 / single-PIC-actuator design is retired. Source documents are preserved at [`docs/archive/`](docs/archive/) for design-rationale reference; they are *not* maintained.
104	- **`frame_epoch` is the master sync token.** A 32-bit counter incremented by marvin's video task on every captured ISC frame. Every detector-state record, emitted command, and recording artifact — including data from off-board observers — keys off this token so multi-source data can be aligned post-hoc. Detail in [marvin spec §4.6](firmware/marvin/docs/spec.md).
105	- **Reference data persists on marvin's SD card.** Detector-state + sparse raw BGR888 keyframes (default 1 keyframe/sec) + raw ADC stream + emitted commands. Off-board detectors record their own data keyed by `frame_epoch` and align offline.
106	- **Centralized timing on marvin, with a fretboard-takeover fallback.** marvin runs the chord-window FIFO and strum scheduler by default; an operator-mode toggle hands timing back to fretboard's standalone `fret_button.c` while marvin still records observations.
107	- **Operating modes are independent toggles**, not a global state machine: `detect_enable`, `marvin_timing_enable`, `actuate_enable`, `record_enable`. Named modes (idle / calibrate / dry-run / play / replay / record) are presets over them.
108	- **Planned: fretboard ↔ marvin link moves to 10BASE-T1S + dumb PoDL.** Replace the FLEXCOM2/SERCOM UART pair with single-pair Ethernet via a LAN8651B1 MAC-PHY on each end. Motivation, in order: PoDL carries power *and* data on one pair to the guitar; better noise/cable tolerance; PLCA multidrop headroom; and demonstrating 10BASE-T1S + PoDL inside a larger Microchip system (SAM9X7 + LAN8651 + PIC32CM). Bandwidth is not a driver — the existing UART has ~12× headroom. PoDL is **dumb** (fixed voltage, no SCCP negotiation) and transparent to both MCUs. No IP stack — the host implements only SPI + the OPEN Alliance TC6 chunk protocol + minimal L2 framing, with the existing frame formats riding unchanged inside the Ethernet payload. Fits comfortably on the PIC32CM (est. ~6–10 KB flash / ~1–2 KB SRAM); marvin is bare-metal so it gets a shared portable `oa_tc6` driver, not a free netdev. Detail in [`docs/t1s-podl-link.md`](docs/t1s-podl-link.md).
109

129	
130	Detail (definitions of done, demos) in [marvin spec §8](firmware/marvin/docs/spec.md).
131	
132	## 8. What this is *not*
133	
134	To anchor against the original architecture (preserved in `docs/archive/`):
135	
136	- **Not PC-hosted.** marvin is the runtime brain; no host PC is required for play.
137	- **Not USB-capture / Elgato.** Video is captured directly off HDMI via a TC358743 → MIPI CSI-2 path into the SAM9X75's ISC.
138	- **Not PS2.** The supported console is the Nintendo Wii (with an ElectronWarp component → HDMI converter).
139	- **Not a single-MCU actuator.** Sensing and timing live on marvin; fretboard is a sensor/actuator MCU, not a solo controller (with the explicit exception of the standalone-fallback mode).
140	- **Not OpenCV / Python at runtime.** CV runs natively on the SAM9X75 (Cortex-A5). Python (`fret-tuner`) is a bench tool only.
141

2	
3	These rules apply to every session on this repo. Follow them without being reminded.
4	
5	## Git commits require explicit approval
6	
7	Never run `git commit` on your own initiative. Always ask first and wait for explicit confirmation before committing — even when wrapping up a session or completing a doc sweep.
8	
9	## Specs orient you; journals track progress
10	
11	The repo has three subprojects (marvin, fretboard, fret-tuner) plus a top-level system spec.
12	
13	- **[`SPEC.md`](SPEC.md) is the cross-subproject overview** — read it first if a task spans subprojects or if you're new to the repo. It points at each subproject's spec and journal.
14	- For non-trivial work inside a single subproject, read that subproject's spec **and** journal first (see below).
15	
16	## Journals are the source of truth for planning and progress
17	
18	This repo uses working journals to track planning, decisions, open questions, and work-in-progress *outside* the chat context so they survive across sessions, compactions, and restarts.
19	
20	Current journals:
21	
22	- `firmware/marvin/docs/journal.md` — marvin firmware (SAM9X75 vision-based guitar-playing robot)
23	  - System-level spec for marvin lives at `firmware/marvin/docs/spec.md` — **read it first** alongside the journal on any non-trivial marvin task. The spec is the durable description of what marvin is (purpose, subsystems, interfaces, milestones); the journal is the running diary.
24	- `firmware/fretboard/docs/journal.md` — fretboard firmware (PIC32CM I/O bridge: ADC stream out + button-bitmask in)
25	  - Spec for fretboard lives at `firmware/fretboard/SPEC.md` — read it alongside the journal on any non-trivial fretboard task.
26	- `tools/edge-ai/docs/journal.md` — edge-ai (distill marvin's gameplay commands into a small ML model for the fretboard MCU)
27	  - Specs for edge-ai live under `tools/edge-ai/docs/` (`SPEC.md` + the doc map there) — read them alongside the journal on any non-trivial edge-ai task.
28	- `firmware/fauxmote/docs/journal.md` — fauxmote (ESP32 firmware emulating a Wiimote + guitar extension to a real Wii; parallel proof-of-concept)
29	  - Spec for fauxmote lives at `firmware/fauxmote/SPEC.md` — read it alongside the journal on any non-trivial fauxmote task.
30	- `tools/gameplay/docs/journal.md` — gameplay (offline host-side prototype for marvin's GH3 game-state observer/controller; algorithms proven against the screen corpus, then ported to a firmware `gameplay_engine`)
31	  - Orienting docs: marvin `spec.md` §4.8 and `firmware/marvin/docs/gh3_navigation.md` — read them alongside the journal on any non-trivial gameplay task.
32	
33	When working on a subproject that has a journal:
34	
35	1. **Read the journal first.** Before responding to any non-trivial request, read the journal for that subproject. It contains the current focus, phased plan, open questions, decision log, and session log — the state you need to be useful.
36	2. **Update the journal as you go.** When we make a decision, resolve an open question, finish a plan phase, or finish a session, reflect that in the journal. Newest entries at the top within each section.
37	   - Decisions → append to the decision log with date and rationale.
38	   - Resolved open questions → remove from "Open questions" and add to the decision log with the answer and rationale.
39	   - Plan progress → check off phase items; add sub-bullets for anything learned during implementation.
40	   - Session close → add a dated session-log entry summarizing what happened.
41	3. **Prefer updating the journal over restating plans in chat.** If I'd otherwise write a multi-paragraph plan in chat, it belongs in the journal — the chat is ephemeral, the journal isn't.
42	4. **If a new subproject needs a journal, create one** using the same structure as `firmware/marvin/docs/journal.md`, and add it to the list above in this file.
43	
44	## Code comments describe current code only
45	
46	Comments in source files explain **what the code currently does and why**, when that's non-obvious. They are not a development diary.
47	
48	Do not put any of the following in source comments — they belong in the journal, commit messages, or PR descriptions:
49	
50	- Narrative of how the code evolved ("previously we did X, now we do Y", "this replaces the old …")
51	- Debug notes, troubleshooting history, or why something *doesn't* work
52	- TODO lists for future features (use the journal or an issue tracker)
53	- References to tasks, tickets, or past conversations ("fix for Greg's bug", "see chat from 2026-05-01")
54	- Extensive block comments explaining design rationale — a one-line "why" is fine; multi-paragraph prose goes in the journal
55	
56	**Default to no comment.** Only add one when removing it would confuse a future reader. If you catch yourself wanting to write a paragraph, write it in the journal instead and link from the code if needed (e.g. `// see firmware/marvin/docs/journal.md`).

52	void model_infer_set_model(const model_def_t *m)
53	{
54	    s_model = m;
55	    if (m == NULL) { return; }
56	
57	    /* Back-propagate the needed positions: the top layer needs only the last
58	     * timestep; each lower layer needs the taps its consumer reads. */
59	    memset(s_need, 0, sizeof(s_need));

67	            for (int j = 0; j < MODEL_KERNEL; j++)

69	                int pos = p - j * dil;

81	    s_hold_until = 0;
82	    s_block_until = 0;
83	    s_prev_strum = 0;
84	    model_infer_set_model(MODEL_DEFAULT);
85	}
86	
87	void model_infer_push(const uint16_t adc[5])
88	{
89	    for (int c = 0; c < MODEL_N_IN; c++)
90	    {
91	        s_ring[s_pos][c] = adc[c];
92	    }
93	    s_pos = (uint16_t)((s_pos + 1u) % MODEL_WINDOW);
94	    if (s_count < MODEL_WINDOW) { s_count++; }
95	}
96	
97	/* Causal int8 conv at output position p: out[o] = requant(relu(bias + Σ w·in)).
98	 * Tap k reads input at p-(K-1-k)*dil (the PyTorch causal-left-pad convention).
99	 * `in` is row-major [position][in_stride]. */
100	static void conv_at(const int8_t *w, const int32_t *b, int cin, int dil,
101	                    int32_t mult, int shift, const int8_t *in, int in_stride,
102	                    int p, int8_t out[MODEL_CHANNELS])
103	{
104	    for (int o = 0; o < MODEL_CHANNELS; o++)
105	    {
106	        int32_t acc = b[o];
107	        for (int i = 0; i < cin; i++)
108	        {
109	            const int8_t *wo = &w[(o * cin + i) * MODEL_KERNEL];
110	            for (int k = 0; k < MODEL_KERNEL; k++)
111	            {
112	                int pos = p - (MODEL_KERNEL - 1 - k) * dil;
113	                if (pos < 0) { continue; }
114	                acc += (int32_t)wo[k] * (int32_t)in[pos * in_stride + i];
115	            }
116	        }
117	        if (acc < 0) { acc = 0; }   /* ReLU */
118	        int64_t q = ((int64_t)acc * mult + ((int64_t)1 << (shift - 1))) >> shift;
119	        if (q > QMAX) { q = QMAX; }
120	        out[o] = (int8_t)q;
121	    }
122	}
123	
124	uint8_t model_infer_run(void)
125	{
126	    const model_def_t *m = s_model;
127	    /* Snapshot the ring cursor: when inference runs in the main loop the TC0 ISR
128	     * may push() concurrently. Using a fixed `pos` keeps the window mapping
129	     * stable for this inference; at worst the oldest slot is overwritten mid-run
130	     * (60 samples back — negligible). */
131	    uint16_t pos = s_pos;
132	    if (m == NULL || s_count < MODEL_WINDOW) { return 0u; }
133	
134	    /* Standardise the whole window into int8 (folded mean/std + input scale). */
135	    for (int wpos = 0; wpos < MODEL_WINDOW; wpos++)
136	    {
137	        int ring_idx = (pos + wpos) % MODEL_WINDOW;
138	        for (int c = 0; c < MODEL_N_IN; c++)
139	        {
140	            int64_t v = (int64_t)s_ring[ring_idx][c] * m->m_in[c] - m->b_in[c];
141	            int64_t q = (v + ((int64_t)1 << (m->s_in_shift - 1))) >> m->s_in_shift;
142	            s_qin[wpos][c] = clamp_i8(q);
143	        }
144	    }
145	
146	    /* Conv layers, only at the needed positions. */
147	    for (int l = 0; l < MODEL_N_LAYERS; l++)
148	    {
149	        const int8_t *in = (l == 0) ? &s_qin[0][0] : &s_act[l - 1][0][0];
150	        int in_stride = (l == 0) ? MODEL_N_IN : MODEL_CHANNELS;
151	        for (int p = 0; p < MODEL_WINDOW; p++)
152	        {
153	            if (!s_need[l][p]) { continue; }
154	            conv_at(m->w[l], m->b[l], m->cin[l], m->dilation[l],
155	                    m->req_mult[l], m->req_shift[l], in, in_stride,
156	                    p, s_act[l][p]);
157	        }
158	    }
159	
160	    /* Head on the last timestep: bit = (logit >= threshold), no sigmoid. */
161	    const int8_t *last = &s_act[MODEL_N_LAYERS - 1][MODEL_WINDOW - 1][0];
162	    uint8_t mask = 0u;
163	    int raw_strum = 0;
164	    for (int o = 0; o < MODEL_N_OUT; o++)
165	    {
166	        int32_t acc = m->head_b[o];
167	        for (int i = 0; i < MODEL_CHANNELS; i++)
168	        {
169	            acc += (int32_t)m->head_w[o * MODEL_CHANNELS + i] * (int32_t)last[i];
170	        }
171	        int bit = (acc >= m->head_tq[o]) ? 1 : 0;
172	        if (o < 5) { if (bit) { mask |= (uint8_t)(1u << o); } }
173	        else       { raw_strum = bit; }
174	    }
175	
176	    /* Strum monostable: one pulse per rising edge, model->strum_hold ticks. */
177	    int strum_out;
178	    if (m->strum_hold > 0)
179	    {
180	        uint32_t i = s_tick;
181	        if (raw_strum && !s_prev_strum && i >= s_block_until)
182	        {
183	            s_hold_until  = i + m->strum_hold;
184	            s_block_until = i + m->strum_hold + m->strum_refractory;
185	        }
186	        strum_out = (i < s_hold_until) ? 1 : 0;
187	        s_prev_strum = (uint8_t)raw_strum;
188	        s_tick++;
189	    }
190	    else
191	    {
192	        strum_out = raw_strum;
193	    }
194	    if (strum_out) { mask |= (uint8_t)(1u << 5); }
195	
196	    return mask;
197	}
198	
199	#endif /* !MODEL_INFER_STREAMING */

7	/*

9	 * receptive field every tick (model_infer.c), it caches each layer's output
10	 * column in a small ring and advances ONE new column per sample — ~1 conv column
11	 * per layer per tick (~4x fewer MACs), so inference clears 240 Hz.
12	 *
13	 * Stateful and per-sample: call model_infer_stream_step() exactly once per ADC
14	 * scan, in order. It computes a CONTINUOUS causal conv, which is bit-exact with a
15	 * model TRAINED AT window >= receptive field (85) — at a shorter window the
16	 * windowed model's moving zero-pad boundary would not match (see runtime.md /
17	 * edge-ai journal). Output is 0 until the receptive field has filled.
18	 *
19	 * Output bitmask matches CMD_BIT_* (bits 0..4 frets, bit 5 strum-down).
20	 */
21	
22	void model_infer_stream_init(void);

28	 * one sample (do not skip or repeat samples). */

16	static pending_note_t note_q[NOTE_Q_CAP];
17	static uint8_t nq_head;
18	static uint8_t nq_count;
19	
20	/* ---- pending strum FIFO ---- */
21	
22	typedef struct {
23	    uint8_t  fret_mask;
24	    uint32_t strum_at;
25	} pending_strum_t;
26	
27	#define STRUM_Q_CAP 8
28	static pending_strum_t strum_q[STRUM_Q_CAP];
29	static uint8_t sq_head;
30	static uint8_t sq_count;
31	
32	/* ---- per-fret release scheduling ---- */
33	
34	static uint32_t release_at[FRET_COUNT];
35	static bool     release_pending[FRET_COUNT];
36	
37	/* ---- chord accumulation window ---- */
38	
39	static bool     chord_open;
40	static uint32_t chord_start_ms;
41	static uint8_t  chord_mask;
42	
43	/* ---- fret output tracking ---- */
44	
45	static uint8_t frets_active;
46	
47	/* ---- strum state ---- */
48	
49	static uint32_t strum_release_at;
50	static bool     strum_active;
51	static bool     strum_direction;
52	
53	/* ---- enable / SW0 ---- */
54	
55	static bool     enabled;
56	static bool     sw0_prev;
57	static uint32_t sw0_change_ms;
58	static bool     sw0_pending;
59	
60	/* ---- button pin helpers ---- */
61	
62	static void button_assert(uint8_t i)
63	{
64	    switch ((fret_channel_t)i) {
65	    case FRET_GREEN:  BUTTON_GREEN_Clear();  BUTTON_GREEN_OutputEnable();  break;
66	    case FRET_RED:    BUTTON_RED_Clear();    BUTTON_RED_OutputEnable();    break;
67	    case FRET_YELLOW: BUTTON_YELLOW_Clear(); BUTTON_YELLOW_OutputEnable(); break;
68	    case FRET_BLUE:   BUTTON_BLUE_Clear();   BUTTON_BLUE_OutputEnable();   break;
69	    case FRET_ORANGE: BUTTON_ORANGE_Clear(); BUTTON_ORANGE_OutputEnable(); break;
70	    default: break;
71	    }
72	}
73	
74	static void button_release(uint8_t i)
75	{
76	    switch ((fret_channel_t)i) {
77	    case FRET_GREEN:  BUTTON_GREEN_InputEnable();  break;
78	    case FRET_RED:    BUTTON_RED_InputEnable();    break;
79	    case FRET_YELLOW: BUTTON_YELLOW_InputEnable(); break;
80	    case FRET_BLUE:   BUTTON_BLUE_InputEnable();   break;
81	    case FRET_ORANGE: BUTTON_ORANGE_InputEnable(); break;
82	    default: break;
83	    }
84	}
85	
86	static void strum_release(void)
87	{
88	    BUTTON_STRUM_DOWN_InputEnable();
89	    BUTTON_STRUM_UP_InputEnable();
90	    strum_active = false;
91	    LED0_Set();
92	    // button_release(FRET_ORANGE);
93	}
94	
95	static void strum_trigger(uint32_t now)
96	{
97	    strum_release();
98	    if (strum_direction) {
99	        BUTTON_STRUM_UP_Clear();
100	        BUTTON_STRUM_UP_OutputEnable();
101	    } else {
102	        BUTTON_STRUM_DOWN_Clear();
103	        BUTTON_STRUM_DOWN_OutputEnable();
104	    }
105	    strum_direction = !strum_direction;
106	    strum_active = true;
107	    strum_release_at = now + STRUM_PULSE_MS;
108	    LED0_Clear();
109	    // button_assert(FRET_ORANGE);
110	}
111	
112	static void release_all(void)
113	{
114	    for (uint8_t i = 0; i < FRET_COUNT; i++) {
115	        button_release(i);
116	        release_pending[i] = false;
117	    }
118	    frets_active = 0;
119	    strum_release();
120	    nq_head = 0;
121	    nq_count = 0;
122	    sq_head = 0;
123	    sq_count = 0;
124	    chord_open = false;
125	    chord_mask = 0;
126	}
127	
128	/* ---- enable / disable ---- */
129	
130	static void set_enabled(bool en)
131	{
132	    enabled = en;
133	    if (en)
134	        LED0_Clear();
135	    else {
136	        LED0_Set();
137	        release_all();
138	    }
139	}
140	
141	static void sw0_poll(uint32_t now)
142	{
143	    bool raw = !SW0_Get();
144	    if (raw == sw0_prev) {
145	        sw0_pending = false;
146	        return;
147	    }
148	    if (!sw0_pending) {
149	        sw0_pending = true;
150	        sw0_change_ms = now;
151	        return;
152	    }
153	    if ((now - sw0_change_ms) >= SW0_DEBOUNCE_MS) {
154	        sw0_prev = raw;
155	        sw0_pending = false;
156	        if (raw)
157	            set_enabled(!enabled);
158	    }
159	}
160	
161	/* ---- chord commit ---- */
162	
163	static void chord_commit(uint32_t now)
164	{
165	    if (nq_count >= NOTE_Q_CAP || sq_count >= STRUM_Q_CAP) {
166	        chord_open = false;
167	        chord_mask = 0;
168	        return;
169	    }
170	
171	    uint32_t assert_at = now + STRUM_DELAY_MS - FRET_EARLY_MS;
172	    uint32_t strum_at  = now + STRUM_DELAY_MS;
173	
174	    /* If previous strum pulse hasn't finished, push times forward so
175	       new frets don't interfere with the prior strum. */
176	    if (sq_count > 0) {
177	        uint8_t tail = (sq_head + sq_count - 1U) % STRUM_Q_CAP;
178	        uint32_t earliest = strum_q[tail].strum_at + STRUM_PULSE_MS;
179	        if ((int32_t)(assert_at - earliest) < 0) {
180	            assert_at = earliest;
181	            strum_at  = assert_at + FRET_EARLY_MS;
182	        }
183	    }
184	
185	    uint8_t nslot = (nq_head + nq_count) % NOTE_Q_CAP;
186	    note_q[nslot] = (pending_note_t){
187	        .fret_mask  = chord_mask,
188	        .assert_at  = assert_at,
189	    };
190	    nq_count++;
191	
192	    uint8_t sslot = (sq_head + sq_count) % STRUM_Q_CAP;
193	    strum_q[sslot] = (pending_strum_t){
194	        .fret_mask  = chord_mask,
195	        .strum_at   = strum_at,
196	    };
197	    sq_count++;
198	
199	    chord_open = false;
200	    chord_mask = 0;
201	}
202	
203	/* ---- process pending notes (FIFO order) ---- */
204	
205	static void process_notes(uint32_t now)
206	{
207	    while (nq_count > 0) {
208	        pending_note_t *n = &note_q[nq_head];
209	        if ((int32_t)(now - n->assert_at) < 0)
210	            break;
211	
212	        for (uint8_t i = 0; i < FRET_COUNT; i++) {
213	            bool need = (n->fret_mask >> i) & 1U;
214	            bool have = (frets_active >> i) & 1U;
215	            if (need && !have) {
216	                button_assert(i);
217	                frets_active |= (1U << i);
218	            } else if (!need && have) {
219	                button_release(i);
220	                frets_active &= ~(1U << i);
221	            }
222	        }
223	
224	        nq_head = (nq_head + 1U) % NOTE_Q_CAP;
225	        nq_count--;
226	    }
227	}
228	
229	/* ---- process pending strums (FIFO order) ---- */
230	
231	static void process_strums(uint32_t now)
232	{
233	    while (sq_count > 0) {
234	        pending_strum_t *s = &strum_q[sq_head];
235	        if ((int32_t)(now - s->strum_at) < 0)
236	            break;
237	
238	        strum_trigger(now);
239	        sq_head = (sq_head + 1U) % STRUM_Q_CAP;
240	        sq_count--;
241	    }
242	}
243	
244	/* ---- process per-fret releases ---- */
245	
246	static void process_releases(uint32_t now)
247	{
248	    for (uint8_t i = 0; i < FRET_COUNT; i++) {
249	        if (!release_pending[i])
250	            continue;
251	        if ((int32_t)(now - release_at[i]) < 0)
252	            continue;
253	
254	        if (fret_is_pressed((fret_channel_t)i))
255	            continue;
256	
257	        /* Don't release if any pending note or strum still needs this fret. */
258	        bool needed = false;
259	        for (uint8_t j = 0; j < nq_count && !needed; j++) {
260	            uint8_t slot = (nq_head + j) % NOTE_Q_CAP;
261	            if (note_q[slot].fret_mask & (1U << i))
262	                needed = true;
263	        }
264	        for (uint8_t j = 0; j < sq_count && !needed; j++) {
265	            uint8_t slot = (sq_head + j) % STRUM_Q_CAP;
266	            if (strum_q[slot].fret_mask & (1U << i))
267	                needed = true;
268	        }
269	        if (needed)
270	            continue;
271	
272	        button_release(i);
273	        frets_active &= ~(1U << i);
274	        release_pending[i] = false;
275	    }
276	}
277	
278	/* ---- main update ---- */
279	
280	void fret_button_init(void)
281	{
282	    nq_head = 0;
283	    nq_count = 0;
284	    sq_head = 0;
285	    sq_count = 0;
286	    frets_active = 0;
287	    chord_open = false;
288	    chord_mask = 0;
289	    strum_active = false;
290	    strum_direction = false;
291	    sw0_prev = !SW0_Get();
292	    sw0_pending = false;
293	
294	    for (uint8_t i = 0; i < FRET_COUNT; i++) {
295	        release_pending[i] = false;
296	        button_release(i);
297	    }
298	    strum_release();
299	    set_enabled(false);
300	}
301	
302	void fret_button_update(uint32_t now)
303	{
304	    sw0_poll(now);
305	
306	    if (!enabled)
307	        return;
308	
309	    uint8_t presses  = fret_detect_new_presses();
310	    uint8_t releases = fret_detect_new_releases();
311	
312	    /* New presses open / extend the chord window. */
313	    if (presses) {
314	        if (!chord_open) {
315	            chord_open = true;
316	            chord_start_ms = now;
317	            chord_mask = 0;
318	        }
319	        chord_mask |= presses;
320	    }
321	
322	    /* Schedule delayed releases for each fret that went up. */
323	    for (uint8_t i = 0; i < FRET_COUNT; i++) {
324	        if (releases & (1U << i)) {
325	            release_at[i] = now + STRUM_DELAY_MS;
326	            release_pending[i] = true;
327	        }
328	    }
329	
330	    if (chord_open && (now - chord_start_ms) >= CHORD_WINDOW_MS)
331	        chord_commit(now);
332	
333	    if (strum_active && (int32_t)(now - strum_release_at) >= 0)
334	        strum_release();
335	
336	    process_notes(now);
337	    process_strums(now);
338	    process_releases(now);
339	}
340	
341	bool fret_button_is_enabled(void)
342	{
343	    return enabled;
344	}
345

```text
1	# Fretboard Firmware Specification
2	
3	## Overview
4	
5	Firmware for PIC32CM6408PL10048 (Cortex-M0+, 24 MHz) that acts as an
6	**I/O bridge** between a Guitar Hero controller and an off-board host.
7	Five phototransistors above the TV strike line are sampled and streamed
8	out continuously; the host runs detection / chord / strum logic and
9	sends back a single-byte bitmask that drives the controller's button
10	GPIOs directly.
11	
12	In its `MARVIN_DRIVEN` mode the firmware contains **no game logic** — it only
13	scans ADCs, emits frames, and applies received bitmasks. A second build-time
14	mode, **`MODEL_DRIVEN`** (`FRETBOARD_MODE` in `main.c`, the current default),
15	makes the board standalone: an on-device int8 neural net (`model_infer.c`,
16	weights in the generated `model_weights.h`) maps the ADC window to the button
17	bitmask itself, no host required. SW0 toggles it; LED0 shows the state.
18	Inference runs in the main loop; the 240 Hz TC0 ISR only samples and applies.
19	See [`docs/journal.md`](docs/journal.md) and edge-ai
20	[`runtime.md`](../../tools/edge-ai/docs/runtime.md).
21	
22	## Hardware
23	
24	### Target
25	
26	| Spec | Value |
27	|------|-------|
28	| Device | PIC32CM6408PL10048 |
29	| Core | ARM Cortex-M0+ |
30	| Clock | 24 MHz |
31	| Toolchain | XC32 5.10 |
32	| Programmer | PKOB nano |
33	
34	### Pin Map
35	
36	#### Sensor Inputs (ADC)
37	
38	Five phototransistors positioned above the TV strike line. Each
39	produces an analog voltage that drops when a note passes the sensor.
40	ADC reads 12-bit unsigned (0–4095); lower values indicate note
41	presence.
42	
43	| Channel | ADC Input | Pin |
44	|---------|-----------|-----|
45	| Green | AIN28 | PA28 |
46	| Red | AIN16 | PA16 |
47	| Yellow | AIN19 | PA19 |
48	| Blue | AIN27 | PA27 |
49	| Orange | AIN26 | PA26 |
50	
51	#### Button Outputs (Open-Drain GPIO)
52	
53	Each button output is normally tri-stated (input mode). To "press" a
54	button the pin is driven low (clear + output-enable). To "release" it
55	the pin returns to input mode, which floats the line and lets the
56	guitar controller's own pull-up restore the idle state.
57	
58	| Function | Pin | Cmd bit |
59	|----------|-----|---------|
60	| Green fret | PA06 | 0 |
61	| Red fret | PA05 | 1 |
62	| Yellow fret | PA07 | 2 |
63	| Blue fret | PA04 | 3 |
64	| Orange fret | PA01 | 4 |
65	| Strum down | PA03 | 5 |
66	| Strum up | PA00 | 6 |
67	
68	#### UART (SERCOM1)
69	
70	| Function | Pin |
71	|----------|-----|
72	| TX (data stream out) | PB00 |
73	| RX (command in) | PB01 |
74	
75	Baud: **500 000**, 8N1.
76	
77	## Software Architecture
78	
79	### Processing Loop
80	
81	`TC0` is configured to fire a periodic callback at **240 Hz**
82	(≈4.17 ms period). Each tick runs three stages in sequence from the
83	timer ISR:
84	
85	```
86	TC0 callback (240 Hz)
87	    |
88	    v
89	fret_scan_all()          Blocking ADC read of all 5 channels
90	    |
91	    v
92	data_stream_send()       17-byte frame over SERCOM1 TX
93	    |
94	    v
95	cmd_receive_update()     Drains SERCOM1 RX, applies latest bitmask
96	```
97	
98	`main()` is just init + idle loop; all work happens in the TC0 ISR.
99	
100	### Module Descriptions
101	
102	#### fret_scan ([fret_scan.c](fret_scan.c) / [fret_scan.h](fret_scan.h))
103	
104	Reads all five ADC channels sequentially using blocking polling.
105	Results are stored in a static array and accessed via
106	`fret_scan_result(channel)`.
107	
108	The channel enum defines the canonical fret ordering used throughout
109	the firmware:
110	
111	```
112	FRET_GREEN = 0, FRET_RED = 1, FRET_YELLOW = 2, FRET_BLUE = 3, FRET_ORANGE = 4
113	```
114	
115	#### data_stream ([data_stream.c](data_stream.c) / [data_stream.h](data_stream.h))
116	
117	Emits one 17-byte little-endian frame per tick over SERCOM1 TX:
118	
119	| Offset | Size | Field |
120	|-------:|-----:|-------|
121	| 0 | 1 | start = `0x03` |
122	| 1 | 2 | green (uint16) |
123	| 3 | 2 | red |
124	| 5 | 2 | yellow |
125	| 7 | 2 | blue |
126	| 9 | 2 | orange |
127	| 11 | 4 | sample_seq (uint32) — monotonic, one per tick |
128	| 15 | 1 | applied_mask — actuator bitmask driven this scan |
129	| 16 | 1 | end = `0xFC` (`~start`) |
130	
131	`sample_seq` lets the host reconstruct true sample order and detect frames
132	dropped in transit (it advances per tick even when a send is skipped).
133	`applied_mask` is the bitmask `cmd_receive` currently drives, captured in the
134	same tick as the scan so sensor and actuator state are paired at the source
135	(used by edge-ai training-data export). The frame is dropped silently if the
136	TX free-buffer count is below the frame size. At 240 Hz this is 4 080 B/s —
137	well within the 50 000 B/s budget at 500 000 baud.
138	
139	#### cmd_receive ([cmd_receive.c](cmd_receive.c) / [cmd_receive.h](cmd_receive.h))
140	
141	Drains the SERCOM1 RX buffer each tick. The **last byte received** in
142	the tick is interpreted as a button bitmask and applied directly:
143	
144	| Bit | Output |
145	|----:|--------|
146	| 0 | Green fret |
147	| 1 | Red fret |
148	| 2 | Yellow fret |
149	| 3 | Blue fret |
150	| 4 | Orange fret |
151	| 5 | Strum down |
152	| 6 | Strum up |
153	
154	Bit set → drive low (assert). Bit clear → tri-state (release).
155	
156	Note: only the most recent byte each tick is honoured. The host is
157	expected to send commands at a rate ≤ the loop rate; older bytes in
158	the same tick are coalesced away.
159	
160	## Tools
161	
162	### Host-side data-stream monitor
163	
164	[`tools/ds_monitor.py`](tools/ds_monitor.py) opens the serial port,
165	resyncs on `0x03 … 0xFC` framing, and reports actual frame rate, byte
166	rate, framing-error count, and current ADC values once per second.
167	
168	The script declares its dependencies inline (PEP 723) and is run via
169	[`uv`](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) — no manual venv or `pip install`
170	needed:
171	
172	```
173	./tools/ds_monitor.py /dev/tty.usbmodem<...>
174	# or, equivalently:
175	uv run tools/ds_monitor.py /dev/tty.usbmodem<...>
176	```
177	
178	Defaults: `--baud 500000 --expect-hz 240`.
179	
180	## Build System
181	
182	MPLAB Extensions for VS Code. Project config is in
183	`.vscode/fretboard.mplab.json`. Source files are listed in the
184	`fileSets[0].files` array. MCC/Harmony-generated code lives under
185	`fretboard-mcc/` and should not be edited.
186	
187	## File Map
188	
189	| File | Purpose |
190	|------|---------|
191	| [main.c](main.c) | Init + TC0 callback wiring |
192	| [fret_scan.c](fret_scan.c) / [.h](fret_scan.h) | ADC channel scanning |
193	| [data_stream.c](data_stream.c) / [.h](data_stream.h) | UART output frame |
194	| [cmd_receive.c](cmd_receive.c) / [.h](cmd_receive.h) | UART input bitmask |
195	| [tools/ds_monitor.py](tools/ds_monitor.py) | Host-side frame-rate / content check |

16	 *       receptive field (85). (default)

19	 * guards its body on MODEL_INFER_STREAMING, so only the active one compiles its

18	/* marvin is the PLCA coordinator. Node IDs and MACs follow the addressing
19	 * scheme in docs/t1s-podl-link.md §7.1: coordinator = ID 0, MAC ...00. */
20	#define T1S_NODE_ID         (0u)
21	#define T1S_NODE_COUNT      (8u)     /* PLCA cycle length; headroom for nodes 1..7 */
22	#define T1S_PLCA_ENABLE     (true)
23	#define T1S_SPI_HZ          (15000000u)

26	#define T1S_TASK_STACK_WORDS (1024u)
27	#define T1S_TASK_PRIORITY    (5u)
28	
29	/* L2 framing (docs/t1s-podl-link.md §7.1): a custom ethertype carries the
30	 * existing fretboard payloads verbatim inside a 14-byte Ethernet header. */
31	#define T1S_ETHERTYPE        (0x88B5u)   /* local/experimental range */
32	#define T1S_ETH_HDR_LEN      (14u)
33	#define T1S_MAC_LEN          (6u)
34	
35	/* Locally administered coordinator MAC (02:00:00:00:00:00). */
36	static uint8_t s_mac[6] = { 0x02u, 0x00u, 0x00u, 0x00u, 0x00u, (uint8_t)T1S_NODE_ID };
37	
38	/* Static node directory: maps a follower's PLCA id / MAC to the detector-state
39	 * bus id it feeds. No discovery — adding a node is a table entry. The single
40	 * fretboard is node 1 -> DETECTOR_ADC_FRETBOARD, matching today's bus slot. */
41	typedef enum
42	{
43	    T1S_NODE_FRETBOARD,
44	    T1S_NODE_PHOTODETECTOR,
45	} t1s_node_type_t;
46	
47	typedef struct
48	{
49	    uint8_t         node_id;      /* PLCA id, also the MAC low byte */
50	    uint8_t         detector_id;  /* detector_state_t.detector_id */
51	    t1s_node_type_t type;
52	} t1s_node_t;
53	
54	static const t1s_node_t s_nodes[] = {
55	    { 1u, (uint8_t)DETECTOR_ADC_FRETBOARD, T1S_NODE_FRETBOARD },
56	};
57	
58	/* Fill a follower MAC for a node id: 02:00:00:00:00:<id>. */
59	static void node_mac(uint8_t out[T1S_MAC_LEN], uint8_t node_id)
60	{
61	    out[0] = 0x02u;
62	    out[1] = 0x00u;
63	    out[2] = 0x00u;
64	    out[3] = 0x00u;
65	    out[4] = 0x00u;
66	    out[5] = node_id;
67	}
68	
69	/* Look up a node by type (NULL if none of that type is configured). */
70	static const t1s_node_t *node_for_type(t1s_node_type_t type)
71	{
72	    for (uint8_t i = 0u; i < (sizeof(s_nodes) / sizeof(s_nodes[0])); i++) {
73	        if (s_nodes[i].type == type) {
74	            return &s_nodes[i];
75	        }
76	    }
77	    return NULL;
78	}
79	
80	/* Look up a node by its source MAC (NULL if unknown). */
81	static const t1s_node_t *node_for_mac(const uint8_t mac[T1S_MAC_LEN])
82	{
83	    if ((mac[0] != 0x02u) || (mac[1] | mac[2] | mac[3] | mac[4])) {
84	        return NULL;
85	    }
86	    for (uint8_t i = 0u; i < (sizeof(s_nodes) / sizeof(s_nodes[0])); i++) {
87	        if (s_nodes[i].node_id == mac[5]) {
88	            return &s_nodes[i];
89	        }
90	    }
91	    return NULL;
92	}
93	
94	/* TX frame staging: TC6_SendRawEthernetPacket keeps a pointer to the buffer
95	 * until its TX callback fires, so the buffer must stay valid meanwhile. One
96	 * in-flight frame at a time (guarded by s_tx_busy) suffices for the link's
97	 * rates. */
98	static uint8_t       s_tx_frame[T1S_ETH_HDR_LEN + 64u];
99	static volatile bool s_tx_busy;
100	
101	/* Latest-wins outbound command to the fretboard, flushed by the service task. */
102	static volatile uint8_t s_cmd;
103	static volatile bool    s_cmd_dirty;
104	
105	static T1SLink_FrameHandler s_frame_handler;
106	
107	static TC6_t            *s_tc6;
108	static volatile bool     s_need_service;
109	static volatile bool     s_link_up;
110	
111	static SemaphoreHandle_t s_svc_sem;
112	static StaticSemaphore_t s_svc_sem_buf;
113	
114	static StackType_t       s_task_stack[T1S_TASK_STACK_WORDS];
115	static StaticTask_t      s_task_tcb;
116	
117	/* RX reassembly: TC6 delivers an Ethernet frame as slices; collect them here
118	 * and process on the OnRxEthernetPacket completion callback. */
119	static uint8_t           s_rx_buf[1518];
120	
121	/* FLEXCOM4 SPI completion ISR callback: the chunk transfer is done, hand the
122	 * buffer back to the TC6 driver and wake the service task. */
123	static void spi_done_cb(uintptr_t context)
124	{
125	    (void)context;
126	    BaseType_t hpw = pdFALSE;
127	    TC6_SpiBufferDone(T1S_INSTANCE, true);
128	    (void)xSemaphoreGiveFromISR(s_svc_sem, &hpw);
129	    portYIELD_FROM_ISR(hpw);
130	}
131	
132	/* T1S_IRQ_N falling-edge PIO ISR callback: the MAC-PHY needs servicing. */
133	static void irq_cb(PIO_PIN pin, uintptr_t context)
134	{
135	    (void)pin;
136	    (void)context;
137	    BaseType_t hpw = pdFALSE;
138	    s_need_service = true;
139	    (void)xSemaphoreGiveFromISR(s_svc_sem, &hpw);
140	    portYIELD_FROM_ISR(hpw);
141	}
142	
143	/* TX completion: the staged frame buffer is free for reuse. */
144	static void tx_done_cb(TC6_t *pInst, const uint8_t *pTx, uint16_t len,
145	                       void *pTag, void *pGlobalTag)
146	{
147	    (void)pInst;
148	    (void)pTx;
149	    (void)len;
150	    (void)pTag;
151	    (void)pGlobalTag;
152	    s_tx_busy = false;
153	}
154	
155	/* Frame a payload to a node (dst = 02:00:00:00:00:<node_id>) and queue it.
156	 * Returns false if a TX is already in flight or the driver rejected it. */
157	static bool send_to_node(uint8_t node_id, const uint8_t *payload, uint16_t payload_len)
158	{
159	    if (s_tx_busy || !s_link_up) {
160	        return false;
161	    }
162	    if (payload_len > (sizeof(s_tx_frame) - T1S_ETH_HDR_LEN)) {
163	        return false;
164	    }
165	    node_mac(&s_tx_frame[0], node_id);          /* dest MAC */
166	    memcpy(&s_tx_frame[6], s_mac, T1S_MAC_LEN);  /* src MAC  */
167	    s_tx_frame[12] = (uint8_t)(T1S_ETHERTYPE >> 8);
168	    s_tx_frame[13] = (uint8_t)(T1S_ETHERTYPE & 0xFFu);
169	    memcpy(&s_tx_frame[T1S_ETH_HDR_LEN], payload, payload_len);
170	
171	    s_tx_busy = true;
172	    bool ok = TC6_SendRawEthernetPacket(s_tc6, s_tx_frame,
173	                                        (uint16_t)(T1S_ETH_HDR_LEN + payload_len),
174	                                        0u, tx_done_cb, NULL);
175	    if (!ok) {
176	        s_tx_busy = false;
177	    }
178	    return ok;
179	}
180	
181	/* Run the protocol stack until it has no immediately pending work. IRQ_N is
182	 * active-low; TC6_Service treats a false interruptLevel as "interrupt active". */
183	static void service_pump(void)
184	{
185	    do {
186	        s_need_service = false;
187	        bool no_int = (T1S_IRQ_N_Get() != 0u);
188	        (void)TC6_Service(s_tc6, no_int);
189	    } while (s_need_service);
190	    TC6Regs_CheckTimers();
191	}
192	
193	static void t1s_task(void *param)
194	{
195	    (void)param;
196	
197	    /* Hardware reset pulse (T1S_RST is active-low, idle high). */
198	    T1S_RST_Clear();
199	    vTaskDelay(pdMS_TO_TICKS(10));
200	    T1S_RST_Set();
201	    vTaskDelay(pdMS_TO_TICKS(10));
202	
203	    /* SPI: Mode 0 (CPOL=0 idle low, CPHA=0 leading edge), 8-bit, 15 MHz.
204	     * Source clock 0 => PLib uses the FLEXCOM4 peripheral clock. */
205	    FLEXCOM_SPI_TRANSFER_SETUP setup = {
206	        .clockFrequency = T1S_SPI_HZ,
207	        .clockPhase     = FLEXCOM_SPI_CLOCK_PHASE_LEADING_EDGE,
208	        .clockPolarity  = FLEXCOM_SPI_CLOCK_POLARITY_IDLE_LOW,
209	        .dataBits       = FLEXCOM_SPI_DATA_BITS_8,
210	    };
211	    (void)FLEXCOM4_SPI_TransferSetup(&setup, 0u);
212	    FLEXCOM4_SPI_CallbackRegister(spi_done_cb, 0u);
213	
214	    s_tc6 = TC6_Init(NULL);
215	    if (s_tc6 == NULL) {
216	        LOG_ERROR("T1S: TC6_Init failed\r\n");
217	        vTaskDelete(NULL);
218	        return;
219	    }
220	
221	    (void)PIO_PinInterruptCallbackRegister(T1S_IRQ_N_PIN, irq_cb, 0u);
222	    PIO_PinInterruptEnable(T1S_IRQ_N_PIN);
223	
224	    /* Configure the LAN8651 registers + PLCA (coordinator, id 0). promiscuous
225	     * during bring-up so RX isn't filtered before the node table exists. */
226	    while (!TC6Regs_Init(s_tc6, NULL, s_mac, T1S_PLCA_ENABLE, T1S_NODE_ID,
227	                         T1S_NODE_COUNT, 0u, 0u, true, false, false)) {
228	        LOG_WARN("T1S: TC6Regs_Init busy, retrying\r\n");
229	        vTaskDelay(pdMS_TO_TICKS(50));
230	    }
231	
232	    /* Drive the async register writes to completion (bounded for the up log). */
233	    TickType_t deadline = xTaskGetTickCount() + pdMS_TO_TICKS(3000);
234	    while (!TC6Regs_GetInitDone(s_tc6) &&
235	           ((int32_t)(deadline - xTaskGetTickCount()) > 0)) {
236	        (void)xSemaphoreTake(s_svc_sem, pdMS_TO_TICKS(2));
237	        service_pump();
238	    }
239	
240	    if (TC6Regs_GetInitDone(s_tc6)) {
241	        s_link_up = true;
242	        TC6_EnableData(s_tc6, true);
243	        LOG_INFO("T1S: LAN8651 up — chipRev=%u, MAC=%02X:%02X:%02X:%02X:%02X:%02X, "
244	                 "PLCA coord id=%u/%u\r\n",
245	                 (unsigned)TC6Regs_GetChipRevision(s_tc6),
246	                 s_mac[0], s_mac[1], s_mac[2], s_mac[3], s_mac[4], s_mac[5],
247	                 (unsigned)T1S_NODE_ID, (unsigned)T1S_NODE_COUNT);
248	    } else {
249	        LOG_WARN("T1S: MAC-PHY not responding (check EVB/wiring); still servicing\r\n");
250	    }
251	
252	    for (;;) {
253	        (void)xSemaphoreTake(s_svc_sem, pdMS_TO_TICKS(1));
254	        service_pump();
255	        if (!s_link_up && TC6Regs_GetInitDone(s_tc6)) {
256	            s_link_up = true;
257	            TC6_EnableData(s_tc6, true);
258	            LOG_INFO("T1S: LAN8651 up (late) — chipRev=%u\r\n",
259	                     (unsigned)TC6Regs_GetChipRevision(s_tc6));
260	        }
261	
262	        /* Flush the latest pending command to the fretboard node. All TC6
263	         * access stays in this task; producers only stash via the API. */
264	        if (s_link_up && s_cmd_dirty && !s_tx_busy) {
265	            const t1s_node_t *fb = node_for_type(T1S_NODE_FRETBOARD);
266	            if (fb != NULL) {
267	                /* Clear before reading so a concurrent update re-arms dirty
268	                 * rather than being dropped (latest-wins). */
269	                s_cmd_dirty = false;
270	                uint8_t mask = s_cmd;
271	                (void)send_to_node(fb->node_id, &mask, 1u);
272	            }
273	        }
274	    }
275	}

342	    (void)rxTimestamp;

345	    if (!success || (len < T1S_ETH_HDR_LEN)) {
346	        return;

358	                  src[0], src[1], src[2], src[3], src[4], src[5]);
359	        return;
360	    }
361	
362	    const uint8_t *payload = &s_rx_buf[T1S_ETH_HDR_LEN];
363	    uint16_t       payload_len = (uint16_t)(len - T1S_ETH_HDR_LEN);
364	
365	    if (s_frame_handler != NULL) {

  {

      apply_output(mask, CMD_BIT_RED,        red_assert,        red_release);
      apply_output(mask, CMD_BIT_YELLOW,     yellow_assert,     yellow_release);
      apply_output(mask, CMD_BIT_BLUE,       blue_assert,       blue_release);
      apply_output(mask, CMD_BIT_ORANGE,     orange_assert,     orange_release);
      apply_output(mask, CMD_BIT_STRUM_DOWN, strum_down_assert, strum_down_release);

      current_mask = mask;

### **Blast Radius Summary: What Breaks if You Split**

| **Layer** | **Coupling** | **Change Required** |
|-----------|-----------|---|
| **Edge AI** | Model deployed to `firmware/fretboard/` output path | Redirect quantizer output to new "guitar" path; model still runs on guitar MCU, not fretboard |
| **Edge AI Training** | Labels sourced from `applied_mask` bundled in fretboard ADC frame | Move applied_mask to guitar firmware's output frame; cross-stream join with fretboard ADC required for training |
| **fret-tuner** | Port config allows single device to own both ADC and actuator | Support two separate devices by default; single-device case becomes an explicit "dual-role" option |
| **fret-tuner Timing** | Strum delay/pulse timing constants shared between Python pipeline and fretboard firmware | Split constants: one set for Python→fretboard ADC scheduling, one set for fretboard→guitar actuator scheduling |
| **marvin: Detector Bus** | DETECTOR_ADC_FRETBOARD models the fretboard as an ADC event source | Keep detector; no change needed (fretboard is still the detector node) |
| **marvin: Actuator Bus** | FretboardLink_Send targets fretboard MCU for command TX | Create new "GuitarLink_Send" or rename to "ActuatorLink_Send" targeting guitar MCU; separate UART/Ethernet driver |
| **marvin: Timing Pipeline** | Consumes detector, sends via FretboardLink_Send | Unchanged consumer logic; decoupled from which physical node actuator targets via producer_id abstraction |
| **marvin: Telemetry** | PERF_REC_FRETBOARD_RAW includes applied_mask for edge-ai training sync | applied_mask becomes PERF_REC_GUITAR_RAW; fretboard_link must cross-stream-join detector ADC with guitar-reported actuator mask for training export |
| **marvin-perf Export** | `--labels=actuator-fb` sources labels from fretboard's in-frame applied_mask (atomic, zero-skew) | Fall back to cross-stream join mode for `--labels=actuator-fb` (re-introduces skew, potential frame drops) OR extend guitar frame to carry applied_mask (adds wire bandwidth) |

19	 * Every detector publishes detector_state_t records onto a single FreeRTOS
20	 * queue (the "detector-state bus"). The timing pipeline (§4.4) is the sole
21	 * consumer in steady state; until it lands a stub task drains the queue so
22	 * producers don't block. */
23

27	    DETECTOR_ADC_FRETBOARD = 1,

31	 * because this is also the on-disk format for state.bin (spec §4.6.5). Do not
32	 * reorder fields without bumping the recording schema version. */
33	typedef struct
34	{
35	    uint32_t frame_epoch;     /* master sync token, spec §4.6.4 */
36	    uint64_t timestamp_us;    /* monotonic, marvin-local */
37	    uint8_t  detector_id;     /* detector_id_t */
38	    uint8_t  reserved[3];
39	    struct
40	    {
41	        uint8_t  pressed;     /* 0/1 hard call */

44	    } fret[FRET_COUNT];
45	} detector_state_t;

52	 * can be subscribed to from inside cv_marvin_v1. */
53	void Detector_Initialize(void);

1	# architecture
2	
3	How the edge AI fits at training time and at inference time. For decisions and the document map, see [SPEC.md](SPEC.md).
4	
5	## 1. Training-time data flow (offline)
6	
7	```
8	Wii ──► marvin (cv_marvin_v1 + timing_pipeline)
9	          │   │
10	          │   ├── PERF_REC_ACTUATOR (intended_mask, strum_dir)   ──┐
11	          │   └── (commands over USB CDC to fretboard)              │
12	          │                                                          ▼
13	          │                                                  marvin-perf
14	          │                                                   (offline)
15	          │   ▲                                                      │
16	          │   │ PERF_REC_FRETBOARD_RAW (5×ADC @ 240 Hz)              │
17	          │   │                                                      │
18	          │   └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────►│
19	          │                                                          │
20	          │                                                          ▼
21	          │                                                   SensiML CSV
22	          │                                            (per-row: 5 ADC + 6 labels)
23	                                                                     │
24	                                                                     ▼
25	                                                        host training (PyTorch)
26	                                                                     │
27	                                                                     ▼
28	                                                          int8 quantised model
29	                                                            (model_weights.h)
30	```
31	
32	Both record streams already flow through perf-log keyed by `frame_epoch` + `ts_counter`. The exporter joins them offline. See [training.md](training.md) for the exporter change and CSV schema.
33	
34	## 2. Inference-time data flow (on-device, as built)
35	
36	```
37	fretboard TC0 ISR @ 240 Hz (short & bounded):
38	    fret_scan_all()                  ──► model_infer_stream_step(scan) ──► cmd
39	                                            │  (streaming: ~1 conv col/layer/tick,
40	                                            │   no full-window buffer)
41	                                            ▼
42	    cmd_receive_apply_mask(enabled ? cmd : 0)  (open-drain fret GPIOs + strum)
43	    data_stream_send()                          (applied_mask telemetry)
44	```
45	
46	The marvin command stream (`cmd_receive`) is bypassed when fretboard is in `MODEL_DRIVEN` mode; the model owns the wire. The deployed path is **streaming** inference (locks to 240 Hz, runs inline); a **recompute** fallback runs in the main loop for non-RF-width models. SW0 toggles model control at runtime. See [runtime.md](runtime.md) for the full integration shape and the two inference modules.
47	
48	## 3. Inference cadence
49	
50	One inference per 240 Hz tick (every 4.17 ms). Budget at 24 MHz with no FPU is ≈100 k cycles. The deployed 16-channel model costs ~3 k MACs/tick streaming (~16 k recompute) — comfortably inside budget; the dense `count_macs` figure (~252 k) is a loose upper bound (see [model.md §5](model.md)).
51	
52	## 4. Why this shape addresses both concerns
53	
54	- **Spatial mismatch dissolved.** No CV-row → photo-row alignment needed at training time. The causal window (RF 85 ≈ 354 ms) captures whatever upstream photoxistor signal preceded the strum, regardless of physical sensor placement on the screen.
55	- **Strum timing learned.** The strum bit is part of the output. Weighted BCE (the strum bit is sparse — see [review.md §risks](review.md#risks)) lets the model learn the photo→strum delay implicitly from the data — provided the receptive field reaches back far enough to see the cue ([model.md §4](model.md)).
56	- **Edge AI is end-to-end standalone.** Once deployed, fretboard runs the model on its own ADC stream; marvin can be off and gameplay still works. Marvin's role becomes "training-data source + reference detector for diagnostics + game-state controller".
57
```

1	#ifndef TIMING_PIPELINE_H
2	#define TIMING_PIPELINE_H
3	
4	#include <stdint.h>
5	#include <stdbool.h>
6	
7	/* Timing pipeline — spec §4.4. Consumes detector_state_t records from the
8	 * detector-state bus (filtered by Detector_GetActive()), runs the chord-
9	 * window + strum-scheduling state machine ported from
10	 * tools/fret-tuner/actuator.py, and submits a 7-bit GPIO bitmask via
11	 * FretboardLink_Send. One of several possible producers — game menu
12	 * control (spec §4.8) and manual test inputs share the same submit API.
13	 *
14	 * Bit layout matches firmware/fretboard/cmd_receive.h:
15	 *   bit 0 = green   bit 1 = red    bit 2 = yellow
16	 *   bit 3 = blue    bit 4 = orange bit 5 = strum-down bit 6 = strum-up
17	 *
18	 * Time base is detector frame timestamps, not wall clock — replay-
19	 * deterministic and frees the task to advance only when state changes
20	 * (with a periodic timeout for between-frame strum-pulse expiries). */
21	
22	#define TIMING_BIT_GREEN       (1u << 0)
23	#define TIMING_BIT_RED         (1u << 1)
24	#define TIMING_BIT_YELLOW      (1u << 2)
25	#define TIMING_BIT_BLUE        (1u << 3)
26	#define TIMING_BIT_ORANGE      (1u << 4)
27	#define TIMING_BIT_STRUM_DOWN  (1u << 5)
28	#define TIMING_BIT_STRUM_UP    (1u << 6)
29	#define TIMING_BIT_FRET_MASK   0x1Fu
30	#define TIMING_BIT_VALID_MASK  0x7Fu
31	
32	void TimingPipeline_Initialize(void);
33	
34	/* Output gate. Default: true. When false, the pipeline still advances
35	 * internal state but suppresses the FretboardLink_Send call so a peer
36	 * producer (manual_control today, future game-state controller §4.8) can
37	 * own the wire. Internal state stays current so the next advance() after
38	 * re-enable republishes the right mask without a stale frame. */
39	void TimingPipeline_SetEnabled(bool enabled);
40	
41	#endif
