```text
1	# Fret-Tuner Specification
2	
3	## Overview
4	
5	Web-based Python tool for developing and refining fret-press detection algorithms. Consumes the same raw ADC data the firmware sees -- either live from the board over UART or replayed from a captured CSV -- runs detection logic in Python, and visualizes everything in an interactive browser UI. Optionally sends actuation commands back to the microcontroller, moving the entire detection and strum-timing pipeline to the PC for rapid iteration.
6	
7	## Video reference (always-on)
8	
9	A first-class always-on subsystem. The UI exposes a video viewport at all times; behavior is independent of which detector is active.
10	
11	**Primary role**: time-aligned visual reference and recording against the ADC sample timeline and any derived signals (waveforms, detector state, fret/strum events). The question it answers: does what was on screen at time *t* match what the ADC and algorithms reported at *t*?
12	
13	**Secondary roles**: debugging alignment between capture and charts, reviewing a session after the fact, documenting false positives/negatives.
14	
15	### Requirements
16	
17	- **Primacy**: video reference is a first-class always-on subsystem, not gated on detector choice.
18	- **Source ownership**: the fret-tuner **backend** owns the camera. Exactly one source feeds the reference ring buffer at a time. The source is selectable in the UI from cameras enumerated by the backend, plus a "none" option, plus any video file supplied for replay.
19	- **Buffer**: server-side ring buffer with **≥30 s wall-clock coverage** at a **target 30 Hz** capture rate. The buffer accepts whatever rate the camera delivers, sized to retain ≥30 s even when the source runs as fast as 60 Hz.
20	- **Synchronization**: every buffered frame carries a sample-clock timestamp anchored to the ADC stream so that any time *t* in the chart timeline maps to the closest buffered frame.
21	- **Live behavior**: while playing, the browser shows the most recent server frame with overlays composed for that frame's *t*.
22	- **Paused / scrubbing**: when paused, or while panning/zooming the charts, the video display follows the chart cursor / center time, picking the closest buffered frame.
23	- **Overlays**: per-frame composition (live and paused) at the display path's natural rate. Required minimum set:
24	    - 5 fret **pressed-state** indicators (per ADC channel)
25	    - **strum state** indicators (down + up, sourced from the actuator pipeline)
26	    - **scrub-time** text cursor
27	  Detectors may register additional overlay layers via the extension hook (see [Detection Algorithm Contract → Overlay extension](#overlay-extension)).
28	- **Detector consumption**: detectors that need pixel data (e.g. `detect_video`) **read from the reference buffer**; they do not own a separate camera grab.
29	
30	## Actuation (always-on)
31	
32	A first-class always-on subsystem that owns the GPIO command serial link to the actuator microcontroller. Behavior is independent of which detector is active and of where the ADC data comes from (live serial, CSV replay, or none).
33	
34	**Primary role**: consume detector state each tick, run the strum timing pipeline (chord window, FIFO scheduling, fret early/late, strum pulse), and emit a 1-byte GPIO bitmask to the actuator board over UART.
35	
36	### Requirements
37	
38	- **Primacy**: actuation is a first-class always-on subsystem, not a side effect of opening a data port. It can be enabled with any detector and any data source (including CSV-only replay against a live actuator board).
39	- **Source ownership**: the actuator owns its own `serial.Serial` handle. The port is selectable in the UI from ports enumerated by the backend, plus a "none" option.
40	- **Port sharing**: the actuator port may name the same `/dev/cu.*` device as an ADC data port (single-board case). In that case the backend opens the device once and shares the handle between the data reader and the actuator writer; the writer never blocks on the reader and vice versa.
41	- **Reconnect**: when the actuator port is lost (unplug, USB sleep, etc.) the writer goes silent without raising; on reconnect, output resumes. Auto-reconnect runs at the same cadence as the data-port reconnect.
42	- **Enable gate**: a UI toggle gates output at the *bitmask* level. When disabled, the timing pipeline still runs (and reports `output_mask = 0`), but no bytes are written. Manual GPIO override (`manual_output`) still works when actuation is disabled, so individual buttons can be poked from the browser without engaging the full pipeline.
43	- **Always-on lifecycle**: created at server startup, persists across detector switches, never owned by a detector.
44	
45	## Architecture
46	
47	The backend is organized around two **always-on subsystems** (video reference, actuation) and one swappable **detector subsystem**. Always-on subsystems own their I/O and run regardless of which detector is active. The detector consumes whatever inputs it needs (ADC stream, video frames, etc.), produces detection state, and feeds it to the actuator.
48	
49	```
50	Browser (localhost:8080)
51	  ├── Video viewport (live or scrubbed frame + composited overlays)
52	  ├── uPlot charts (zoom, pan, pause)
53	  ├── Controls (camera source, actuator port, detector, params, recording)
54	  └── WebSocket  (sample data, detector state, sources, actuator status)
55	        ↕
56	FastAPI backend (Python)
57	  ├── camera.py          (OpenCV capture → shared ring buffer, ≥30 s @ ≥30 Hz)   [always-on]
58	  ├── actuator.py        (strum timing pipeline + GPIO serial TX)                 [always-on]
59	  ├── stream.py          (serial/CSV ADC source for ADC-based detectors)
60	  ├── detect_*.py        (consume samples and/or video frames; emit overlay layers)
61	  └── server.py          (WebSocket + HTTP video transport, subsystem wiring)
62	        ↕
63	Microcontrollers (PIC32CM)
64	  ├── Data board   →  fret_scan + data_stream     (17-byte ADC frames over UART)
65	  └── Actuator board → cmd_receive                (1-byte bitmask → GPIO assert/release)
66	                       The data board and actuator board may be the same physical
67	                       device sharing one UART, or two different devices.
68	```
69	
70	Browser and backend are deployed as a split / resizable layout: video viewport and ADC charts are co-equal, neither dominant by default. The shared video ring buffer lives in the backend; detector pixel consumers and the browser display both read from it.
71	
72	## File Layout
73	
74	```
75	tools/fret-tuner/
76	    fret-tuner.py          # CLI entry point (launches server, opens browser)
77	    server.py              # FastAPI app, WebSocket, data pipeline wiring
78	    camera.py              # OpenCV capture + shared video ring buffer
79	    index.html             # Browser UI (uPlot charts + video viewport, no build step)
80	    stream.py              # Serial + CSV data sources
81	    actuator.py            # Strum timing pipeline (port of fret_button.c)
82	    detect_threshold.py    # Detection: fixed per-channel hysteresis
83	    detect_trough.py       # Detection: baseline + trough FSM
84	    detect_slope.py        # Detection: EMA + slope FSM with re-press handling
85	    detect_video.py        # Detection: pixel sampling against the reference buffer
86	    video_calibrate.py     # Standalone helper for marking detect_video sensor coords
87	    requirements.txt       # Python dependencies
88	    SPEC.md                # This file
89	    .gitignore
90	
91	firmware/fretboard/
92	    cmd_receive.c          # UART RX command handler
93	    cmd_receive.h          # Header
94	```
95	
96	## Data Source
97	
98	### UART Binary Frame (micro → PC)
99	
100	The fretboard firmware streams 17-byte packed frames at **240 Hz** over SERCOM1 USART at **500000 baud** (8N1):
101	
102	```
103	Offset  Size   Field
104	------  -----  -----
105	0       1      Start byte (0x03)
106	1       2      Green   (uint16 LE, 12-bit ADC)
107	3       2      Red     (uint16 LE)
108	5       2      Yellow  (uint16 LE)
109	7       2      Blue    (uint16 LE)
110	9       2      Orange  (uint16 LE)
111	11      4      sample_seq (uint32 LE) — monotonic counter, one per tick; gaps indicate dropped frames
112	15      1      applied_mask — actuator bitmask driven during this scan (edge-ai training sync)
113	16      1      End byte (0xFC)
114	```
115	
116	### Command Byte (PC → micro)
117	
118	Single byte bitmask sent over the same serial connection (full-duplex). Each bit directly controls one GPIO output:
119	
120	```
121	Bit   Output
122	---   ------
123	0     Green fret
124	1     Red fret
125	2     Yellow fret
126	3     Blue fret
127	4     Orange fret
128	5     Strum down
129	6     Strum up
130	```
131	
132	Bit = 1 → assert (drive low). Bit = 0 → release (tri-state). The firmware applies the latest received byte each tick. When no bytes are received, outputs remain unchanged.
133	
134	### Serial Auto-Reconnect
135	
136	When the USB serial connection is lost (board unplugged, USB sleep, etc.), the feed loop catches the error, closes the stale serial handle, and retries opening the port every 2 seconds until the device reappears. On disconnect and reconnect, the server pushes `serial_status` messages over WebSocket so the browser UI can display the current state (amber "Serial disconnected -- reconnecting..." while down, green "Connected" on recovery). CSV replay sources are not affected.
137	
138	### CSV Replay Format
139	
140	CSV files captured from Microchip Data Visualizer. Expected columns:
141	
142	```
143	timestamp,BLUE RAW,BLUE,GREEN RAW,GREEN,ORANGE RAW,ORANGE,RED RAW,RED,YELLOW RAW,YELLOW
144	```
145	
146	Only the `timestamp` and `* RAW` columns are consumed.
147	
148	## Detection Algorithm Contract
149	
150	Each detector lives in its own `detect_*.py` file and exports a `Detector` class:
151	
152	```python
153	class Detector:
154	    @classmethod
155	    def default_params(cls) -> dict:
156	        """Return default parameter values."""
157	
158	    def __init__(self, **params):
159	        """Accept tunable parameters as keyword args."""
160	
161	    def update(self, sample: Sample) -> dict:
162	        """Process one sample. Return per-channel state dict:
163	        {
164	            "green":  {"pressed": bool, "baseline": int, ...},
165	            ...
166	        }
167	        """
168	```
169	
170	The `update()` return dict must include `"pressed"` (bool) and `"baseline"` (int) per channel. Additional keys are detector-specific and available for charting.
171	
172	The server auto-injects `"raw"` (the raw ADC reading for that channel) into each per-channel state dict before charting, so detectors do not need to copy it themselves.
173	
174	### Chart schema
175	
176	Detectors describe what their five chart slots should display via:
177	
178	```python
179	class Detector:
180	    def chart_schema(self) -> list[dict]:
181	        """Return 5 slot specs:
182	        {
183	            "id":      str,             # state-dict key (e.g. "green")
184	            "label":   str,             # axis label
185	            "color":   "#rrggbb",
186	            "y_range": [min, max],
187	            "series":  [
188	                {"key": str, "label": str, "color": "#rrggbb",
189	                 "width": float, "dash": [int, int] | None},
190	                ...
191	            ],
192	        }
193	        """
194	```
195	
196	Each `series.key` names a field inside that channel's state dict. `stream.adc_chart_schema(extra_series=[...])` builds the conventional `raw + <extras>` layout for ADC detectors. Detectors with no use for raw ADC (e.g. `detect_video`) simply omit the `"raw"` series.
197	
198	The browser rebuilds its chart slots whenever a new schema arrives, so switching detectors swaps the chart contents (labels, colors, y-range, plotted series) along with the algorithm.
199	
200	### Overlay extension
201	
202	Detectors may optionally contribute named overlay layers to the video viewport:
203	
204	```python
205	class Detector:
206	    def overlays(self) -> list[OverlayLayer]:
207	        """Optional. Return list of overlay layers to draw on the video.
208	        Each layer = {name: str, draw(ctx, frame_meta, sample_state) -> None}.
209	        Returning [] (or omitting the method) means no detector-specific overlays.
210	        """
211	        return []
212	```
213	
214	Layers compose on top of the always-on minimum set (fret pressed-state, strum state, scrub time). Transport for overlay drawcalls is implementation-defined: the server may bake them into delivered frames, or stream drawcall metadata (see [WebSocket Protocol](#websocket-protocol) `video_meta`) for client-side compositing.
215	
216	`detect_video`, for example, registers a layer that draws its sensor sample points and per-button signal levels.
217	
218	### Adding a new detector
219	
220	1. Create `tools/fret-tuner/detect_myalgo.py`
221	2. Implement a `Detector` class following the contract above
222	3. Select it from the dropdown in the browser UI (or `--detector detect_myalgo` on the CLI)
223	
224	The server hot-reloads detector modules on switch, so you can edit the file and switch to it without restarting.
225	
226	## Bundled Detector: detect_threshold
227	
228	Fixed per-channel hysteresis. Matches the current firmware `fret_detect.c`.
229	
230	| Parameter | Default | Description |
231	|-----------|---------|-------------|
232	| `GREEN_PRESS` | 2500 | Green press threshold |
233	| `GREEN_RELEASE` | 2800 | Green release threshold |
234	| `RED_PRESS` | 2500 | Red press threshold |
235	| `RED_RELEASE` | 2800 | Red release threshold |
236	| `YELLOW_PRESS` | 1500 | Yellow press threshold |
237	| `YELLOW_RELEASE` | 1700 | Yellow release threshold |
238	| `BLUE_PRESS` | 1500 | Blue press threshold |
239	| `BLUE_RELEASE` | 1700 | Blue release threshold |
240	| `ORANGE_PRESS` | 2000 | Orange press threshold |
241	| `ORANGE_RELEASE` | 2200 | Orange release threshold |
242	
243	## Bundled Detector: detect_trough
244	
245	Baseline + trough FSM. Three states: IDLE → DESCENDING → PRESSED.
246	
247	| Parameter | Default | Description |
248	|-----------|---------|-------------|
249	| `MIN_DROP` | 200 | ADC counts below baseline to begin descent tracking |
250	| `RISE_CONFIRM` | 50 | ADC counts above running minimum to confirm press |
251	| `RELEASE_MARGIN` | 300 | Counts within baseline to trigger release |
252	| `BASELINE_DECAY_RATE` | 250 | Samples between 1-count baseline decrements |
253	
254	## Actuator (actuator.py)
255	
256	Python port of `firmware/fretboard/fret_button.c`. Translates detector press/release edges into a timed sequence of fret assertions and strum pulses.
257	
258	### Timing Pipeline
259	
260	1. **Chord window** -- new presses within `CHORD_WINDOW_MS` are accumulated
261	2. **Chord commit** -- schedules note assert at `t + STRUM_DELAY_MS - FRET_EARLY_MS` and strum at `t + STRUM_DELAY_MS`
262	3. **Note FIFO** (cap 8) -- pending fret assertions, processed in order
263	4. **Strum FIFO** (cap 8) -- pending strum triggers, alternating up/down
264	5. **Strum pulse** -- held for `STRUM_PULSE_MS`, then released
265	6. **Delayed releases** -- each released fret is scheduled for release at `t + STRUM_DELAY_MS`, skipped if still needed by pending notes/strums
266	
267	### Timing Parameters
268	
269	| Parameter | Default | Description |
270	|-----------|---------|-------------|
271	| `STRUM_DELAY_MS` | 220 | Delay from chord commit to strum |
272	| `FRET_EARLY_MS` | 50 | How early frets assert before strum |
273	| `STRUM_PULSE_MS` | 50 | How long the strum output is held |
274	| `CHORD_WINDOW_MS` | 20 | Window for accumulating chord presses |
275	
276	All timing is driven by sample timestamps, not wall clock, so the pipeline behaves identically in live and CSV replay modes.
277	
278	### Output
279	
280	Computes a 7-bit bitmask each tick and writes it to the serial port. Actuation is disabled by default and toggled from the browser UI.
281	
282	## Firmware: cmd_receive
283	
284	Minimal command receiver added to the fretboard firmware. Replaces `fret_detect` and `fret_button` in `main.c` -- the microcontroller becomes a scan/stream/actuate relay.
285	
286	### Main loop (modified)
287	
288	```c
289	fret_scan_all();
290	data_stream_send();
291	cmd_receive_update();
292	```
293	
294	### cmd_receive_update()
295	
296	1. Checks `SERCOM1_USART_ReadCountGet()` for available bytes
297	2. Reads all available bytes, keeps the last one
298	3. Applies the bitmask: for each bit, asserts (drive low + output enable) or releases (input enable) the corresponding GPIO
299	
300	## Browser UI
301	
302	Single-file HTML served by the backend at `http://localhost:8080`. Loads uPlot from CDN (no build step).
303	
304	### Charts
305	
306	- 5 stacked uPlot time-series charts, one per fret slot (green, red, yellow, blue, orange)
307	- The active detector's `chart_schema()` defines the series, labels, colors, and y-range for each slot. ADC detectors plot raw ADC + their baseline / threshold lines; `detect_video` plots its hold + edge signals (no raw ADC). Switching detectors swaps the chart contents.
308	- Shaded press bands and (where the detector emits `press_count`) re-press tick marks are overlaid in the slot color
309	- Native mouse-drag zoom, scroll-wheel zoom, double-click to reset
310	
311	### Controls (sidebar)
312	
313	- **Pause / Resume** -- freezes chart updates; data continues to buffer server-side
314	- **Window width** -- slider controlling visible time range (0.5--30 seconds)
315	- **Detector dropdown** -- switch between available `detect_*.py` modules live
316	- **Parameter sliders** -- dynamically generated from the active detector's `default_params()`, changes take effect immediately
317	- **Camera source dropdown** -- enumerated cameras + "none"; controls the always-on video reference
318	- **Actuator port dropdown** -- enumerated `/dev/cu.*` (or platform equivalent) serial ports + "none"; controls the always-on actuator. Selecting the same device as a live ADC data port shares the handle.
319	- **Actuation toggle** -- enable/disable writing command bytes (the timing pipeline runs either way)
320	- **Timing sliders** -- strum delay, fret early, strum pulse, chord window
321	- **Connection status** indicators -- separate badges for the data port and the actuator port
322	
323	### Layout
324	
325	Split / resizable two-pane layout. The **video viewport** and the **ADC charts** are co-equal first-class panes; neither is dominant by default and the user can resize the split. Sidebar controls remain to one side.
326	
327	### Video viewport
328	
329	Backed by the always-on subsystem in [Video reference (always-on)](#video-reference-always-on). UI surface:
330	
331	- **Source selector** -- lists cameras enumerated by the backend, plus "none" and any `--video FILE` replay file. Selection persisted by the backend, applied immediately.
332	- **Recording controls** -- start / stop / save buffer (writes paired video + ADC log; see [Recording & paired CSV replay](#recording--paired-csv-replay)). Default off.
333	- **Pause / scrub** -- synchronized with the charts' pause; chart center time drives the displayed frame.
334	- **Overlays** -- always-on minimum (5 fret pressed-state indicators, strum state, scrub time) plus any layers the active detector registers via [Overlay extension](#overlay-extension).
335	
336	### Recording & paired CSV replay
337	
338	- A live session can be **recorded**: the backend drains the reference ring buffer to a video file alongside the ADC sample log (CSV), with a shared time anchor written into the recording so the two replay in sync.
339	- `python fret-tuner.py --csv FILE [--video FILE]` replays both. If `--video` is omitted, the video viewport shows "no recorded video for this CSV" and disables source selection for the duration of the replay.
340	- Recording is started/stopped explicitly from the sidebar; default off.
341	
342	### WebSocket Protocol
343	
344	Sample data, detector state, and overlay metadata flow over the WebSocket; raw video frames are delivered over a parallel HTTP video transport (implementation choice; the existing tool uses MJPEG). Both share the same sample-clock timestamps so chart and video scrubbing target the same *t*.
345	
346	#### Master clock: the displayed video frame
347	
348	The currently displayed video frame is the single source of truth for *now*. Each captured frame has a `seq` (monotonic id) and a `t` (sample-clock timestamp), and every UI element (chart cursor, viewport scroll, overlay text) aligns to the *currently displayed* frame's `t` -- not to the latest ADC sample, the wall clock, or the network arrival time.
349	
350	- **Live mode**: the server emits a `frame_tick` message on every buffer write (~30 Hz). The browser updates `currentFrame = {seq, t}` and re-clips the chart's leading edge to that `t`. ADC samples that arrived *after* the latest displayed frame are buffered but not yet visible; they are revealed on the next tick. Chart movement is therefore quantized at the camera frame rate, which is the trade-off we accept to keep video, charts, and overlays exactly aligned.
351	- **Pause / scrub**: `frame_tick` is ignored. The user moves `currentFrame` via the timeline, frame-step buttons, or slow-mo playback. Each scrub action returns from the server with a `{seq, t}` pair, which the browser writes back into `currentFrame`.
352	- **CSV / no-camera fallback**: when no camera is attached, no `frame_tick` is emitted. The browser falls back to the latest ingested ADC sample timestamp as `currentFrame.t`, with `seq=null`.
353	
354	Server → client:
355	
356	```json
357	{"type": "data", "samples": [...], "state": [...], "actuator_mask": 0}
358	{"type": "frame_tick", "seq": 1234, "t": 12.345}          // ~30 Hz, camera only
359	{"type": "detector", "name": "...", "params": {...}, "available": [...],
360	 "timing": {...}, "actuate_enabled": false}
361	{"type": "serial_status", "connected": true}              // data port
362	{"type": "actuator_status", "connected": true,
363	 "available": [...], "active": "/dev/cu.usbmodem21202"}   // actuator port
364	{"type": "video_meta", "t": 12.345, "layers": [...]}
365	{"type": "sources", "available": [...], "active": "..."}  // camera sources
366	{"type": "recording", "active": false, "path": null}
367	```
368	
369	Client → server:
370	
371	```json
372	{"type": "pause"}
373	{"type": "resume"}
374	{"type": "set_params", "params": {"KEY": value}}
375	{"type": "set_detector", "name": "detect_trough"}
376	{"type": "set_timing", "params": {"STRUM_DELAY_MS": 200}}
377	{"type": "set_actuate", "enabled": true}
378	{"type": "set_source", "name": "..."}            // camera source
379	{"type": "set_actuator_port", "name": "/dev/cu.usbmodem21202"}  // or "none"
380	{"type": "manual_output", "mask": 0}
381	{"type": "record_start"}
382	{"type": "record_stop"}
383	```
384	
385	The backend also exposes:
386	
387	- `GET /api/sources` -- camera sources (mirror of the WS `sources` message)
388	- `GET /api/serial-ports` -- enumerated serial ports for the actuator dropdown
389	- `GET /video` -- live MJPEG of the working-resolution buffer (server-rendered overlays applied)
390	- `GET /video/snap?t=<sec>` -- single JPEG of the buffered frame closest to *t*. Response carries `X-Frame-Seq` and `X-Frame-Time` headers (and a matching `Access-Control-Expose-Headers`) so the browser can sync `currentFrame` to the snapped frame even when the snapped *t* differs from the requested *t*.
391	- `GET /video/step?dir=next|prev&n=N&{seq=S | t=T}` -- walk the ring buffer to the n-th next/prev frame. Address by `seq` for exact stepping (preferred when the browser holds a known frame); fall back to `t` for the first scrub when seq is unknown. Returns `{"seq": int, "t": float, "buffered": int}`.
392	
393	## CLI Reference
394	
395	```
396	usage: fret-tuner.py [-h] (--port PORT | --csv FILE) [--video FILE]
397	                     [--actuator-port PORT] [--camera ID]
398	                     [--detector MODULE] [--param KEY=VALUE] [--fast]
399	                     [--host HOST] [--web-port PORT]
400	```
401	
402	`--port` selects the **data** serial port (ADC frame source). `--actuator-port` selects the **actuator** serial port; if omitted, the actuator starts idle and a port can be chosen at runtime from the sidebar dropdown. If `--actuator-port` names the same device as `--port`, the backend opens it once and shares the handle for read and write.
403	
404	### Examples
405	
406	```bash
407	# Single board: ADC stream + actuator on the same port (handle is shared)
408	python fret-tuner.py --port /dev/cu.usbmodem21202 \
409	    --actuator-port /dev/cu.usbmodem21202
410	
411	# Two boards: ADC stream on one device, actuator on another
412	python fret-tuner.py --port /dev/cu.usbmodem21202 \
413	    --actuator-port /dev/cu.usbmodem31301
414	
415	# CSV replay against a live actuator board
416	python fret-tuner.py --csv session.csv --actuator-port /dev/cu.usbmodem31301
417	
418	# CSV replay, no actuator (UI dropdown can attach one later)
419	python fret-tuner.py --csv ../../firmware/fretboard/fretboard-sample-raw.csv
420	
421	# Start with trough detector and custom parameters
422	python fret-tuner.py --port /dev/cu.usbmodem21202 --detector detect_trough \
423	    --param MIN_DROP=150 --param RISE_CONFIRM=30
424	
425	# Fast CSV replay (no real-time pacing)
426	python fret-tuner.py --csv capture.csv --fast
427	```
428	
429	## Dependencies
430	
431	Managed with `uv` (inline script metadata in `ds_monitor.py`; `pyproject.toml` for the main tool). Required packages:
432	
433	- `pyserial >= 3.5`
434	- `numpy >= 1.24`
435	- `fastapi >= 0.115`
436	- `uvicorn[standard] >= 0.30`
437	- `websockets >= 12.0`
438	- `opencv-python` (server-side video capture and `detect_video`)
439	
440	## Bundled Detector: detect_video
441	
442	Pixel-sampling detector that **consumes the shared reference video buffer**. It does not own a camera and does not serve its own video stream; sensor sample points and per-button signal levels are exposed as an [overlay layer](#overlay-extension) for the viewport.
443	
444	Two sensor points per button, both above the strike line:
445	
446	- **Sensor 1 (hold)** -- brightness detect (color OR white). Sets `pressed=True` whenever max channel brightness exceeds `THRESHOLD`.
447	- **Sensor 2 (edge)** -- color-filtered leading-edge detect. Increments `press_count` on each new note arrival for strum timing.
448	
449	Detection thresholds are applied directly to raw pixel values (dark background is implicit zero, no settle/calibration phase).
450	
451	### Observed Game Colors (camera-captured BGR)
452	
453	Colors are highly saturated with negligible off-channel values:
454	
455	| Color  | B    | G    | R    | Notes |
456	|--------|------|------|------|-------|
457	| Red    | <10  | <10  | >100 | Almost completely red |
458	| Green  | <10  | >100 | <10  | Completely green |
459	| Blue   | >100 | ~67  | <10  | B dominant, G about 2/3 of B, low R |
460	| Yellow | <10  | ~100 | ~100 | Even mix of G and R, very low B |
461	| Orange | <10  | ~50  | >100 | R dominant, G about half of R, low B |
462	| White (fret bar) | ~160 | ~160 | ~160 | Equal channels at brightest, sat near 0 |
463	
464	The edge detector uses a color filter with saturation scaling `(max-min)/max` to reject white/gray fret bars regardless of camera white balance.
465	
466	### Parameters
467	
468	| Parameter | Default | Description |
469	|-----------|---------|-------------|
470	| `THRESHOLD` | 50 | Detection threshold (brightness for hold, color signal for edge) |
471	| `RELEASE_FRAC` | 60 | Release threshold as % of press threshold (hysteresis) |
472	| `PATCH_RADIUS` | 2 | Pixel averaging radius around sample point |
473	| `{COLOR}_X/Y` | varies | Hold sensor pixel coordinates per button |
474	| `{COLOR}_EX/EY` | varies | Edge sensor pixel coordinates per button |
475	
476	Camera selection lives in the always-on video subsystem, not the detector; there is no `DEVICE_ID` parameter here. Sensor markers are drawn through the `overlays()` hook, replacing the previous `SHOW_PREVIEW`/`/video` path.
477	
478	### Calibration
479	
480	Use `video_calibrate.py` to interactively mark sensor positions:
481	
482	```bash
483	# Full calibration (10 points: 5 hold + 5 edge)
484	python video_calibrate.py --device 0
485	
486	# Color sampling mode (inspect BGR values without calibrating)
487	python video_calibrate.py --sample
488	```
489	
490	## Future Work
491	
492	- **Detector-owned data sources**: lift the ADC stream out of the top-level CLI into the detector itself, so each detector declares what inputs it needs (ADC serial / CSV / camera frames / nothing). The runtime UI would then expose a per-detector source picker. (Chart schemas already follow this model: each detector returns a `chart_schema()` and the browser rebuilds the 5 chart slots from it.) The current scope keeps `--port` / `--csv` as a top-level concern.
493	- Multi-detector overlay (compare two algorithms side-by-side on the same chart)
494	- Per-channel enable/disable toggles for actuation
495	- Latency measurement display (round-trip time from ADC sample to GPIO assertion)
496	- Multi-camera reference (more than one source recorded and replayable in sync)
497
```

static void process_frame(const detector_state_t *state)
{
    /* Detector frame timestamps drive the clock so this is replay-
     * deterministic. timestamp_us is monotonic per spec §4.2.3. */
    s_now_ms = (uint32_t)(state->timestamp_us / 1000ull);
    s_last_frame_us = state->timestamp_us;

    uint8_t presses, releases, pressed_mask;
    derive_edges(state, &presses, &releases, &pressed_mask);

    if (presses)
    {
        if (!s_chord_open)
        {
            s_chord_open     = true;
            s_chord_start_ms = s_now_ms;
            s_chord_mask     = 0u;
        }
        s_chord_mask |= presses;
    }

    for (uint8_t i = 0u; i < FRET_COUNT; i++)
    {
        if (releases & s_fret_bit[i])
        {
            s_release_at_ms[i]      = s_now_ms + TP_STRUM_DELAY_MS;
            s_release_pending_mask |= s_fret_bit[i];
        }
    }

    advance(pressed_mask);
```

18	 *
19	 * Every detector publishes detector_state_t records onto a single FreeRTOS
20	 * queue (the "detector-state bus"). The timing pipeline (§4.4) is the sole
21	 * consumer in steady state; until it lands a stub task drains the queue so
22	 * producers don't block. */
23	
24	typedef enum
25	{
26	    DETECTOR_CV_MARVIN_V1  = 0,
27	    DETECTOR_ADC_FRETBOARD = 1,
28	} detector_id_t;
29	
30	/* Canonical record. Layout is fixed-width / naturally aligned / little-endian
31	 * because this is also the on-disk format for state.bin (spec §4.6.5). Do not
32	 * reorder fields without bumping the recording schema version. */
33	typedef struct
34	{
35	    uint32_t frame_epoch;     /* master sync token, spec §4.6.4 */
36	    uint64_t timestamp_us;    /* monotonic, marvin-local */
37	    uint8_t  detector_id;     /* detector_id_t */
38	    uint8_t  reserved[3];
39	    struct
40	    {
41	        uint8_t  pressed;     /* 0/1 hard call */
42	        uint16_t confidence;  /* 0..65535, detector-defined */
43	        uint16_t raw_value;   /* detector-defined: ADC sample, pixel mean, etc. */
44	    } fret[FRET_COUNT];
45	} detector_state_t;
46	
47	/* Brings up the detector-state bus queue, the cv_marvin_v1 detector task,
48	 * and (for now) a stub consumer. All detectors start disabled; the app
49	 * must Detector_Enable() each one it wants publishing. Active selection
50	 * defaults to DETECTOR_CV_MARVIN_V1 for symmetry but is independent of
51	 * enabled-state. Call after Video_Initialize so the video frame queue
52	 * can be subscribed to from inside cv_marvin_v1. */
53	void Detector_Initialize(void);
54	
55	/* Producers post records here; consumers (timing pipeline, eventually) read
56	 * them. Returns NULL until Detector_Initialize has run. */
57	QueueHandle_t Detector_BusQueue(void);
58	
59	/* Per-detector enable: controls whether a detector publishes records onto
60	 * the bus. Multiple detectors may be enabled simultaneously — recording
61	 * (§4.6) snoops everything for side-by-side training data. Disabled
62	 * detectors still consume their input (frames, ADC samples) so input
63	 * queues don't back up; they just don't emit. Bit operations are atomic
64	 * on aligned 32-bit reads; writes use a critical section. */
65	void Detector_Enable(detector_id_t id);
66	void Detector_Disable(detector_id_t id);
67	bool Detector_IsEnabled(detector_id_t id);
68	
69	/* Active selector: which detector's records the timing pipeline (§4.4)
70	 * acts on. Only one active at a time, irrespective of how many are
71	 * enabled. The timing pipeline is responsible for filtering by
72	 * detector_id when it lands; for M1 this is a held setting only. */
73	void          Detector_SetActive(detector_id_t id);
74	detector_id_t Detector_GetActive(void);
75	
76	#endif
77

```text
1	# fretboard ↔ marvin link — 10BASE-T1S + PoDL
2	
3	Low-level design for moving the fretboard ↔ marvin link from a FLEXCOM2/SERCOM
4	UART pair to **10BASE-T1S single-pair Ethernet with "dumb" Power-over-Data-Lines
5	(PoDL)**. System-level summary and rationale live in [`../SPEC.md`](../SPEC.md)
6	§6; this document holds the engineering detail.
7	
8	Status: **scoped, not yet built — marvin-side coding held on two prerequisites.**
9	The link today is FLEXCOM1 UART (marvin) / SERCOM1 UART (fretboard). Nothing here
10	is flashed. As of 2026-06-16 the scope widened from a 2-node swap to a **multi-node
11	PLCA bus** (several guitars + phototransistor detector nodes on one pair) and the
12	key forks are settled — see §7.1 (addressing), §9 (decisions/open items) and the
13	marvin journal 2026-06-16 entry. Coding waits on: (1) a free FLEXCOM regenerated in
14	**SPI-master mode in MCC** (no SPI PLib exists yet — only USART/TWI), and (2)
15	`oa-tc6-lib` added on disk as a subproject.
16	
17	---
18	
19	## 1. Why T1S here
20	
21	- **PoDL** — one twisted pair carries both data *and* the fretboard's power, so
22	  the cable to the guitar is a single 2-wire link instead of a data pair plus a
23	  separate power feed. This is the primary motivation.
24	- **Robustness / reach** — differential single-pair Ethernet tolerates a long,
25	  electrically noisy run to a moving instrument better than a TTL UART pair.
26	- **Multidrop headroom** — 10BASE-T1S/PLCA puts up to 8 nodes on one pair, so a
27	  second sensor node or fretboard can share the same pair *and* the same power.
28	- **Demonstration** — showcasing 10BASE-T1S + PoDL doing real work inside a
29	  larger Microchip system (SAM9X7 + LAN8651 + PIC32CM) is an explicit goal, not
30	  just an incidental benefit. Bandwidth is *not* a motivation — the existing
31	  500 kbaud UART already carries the ~4 KB/s payload with ~12× headroom.
32	
33	## 2. The part: LAN8651B1
34	
35	A **MAC-PHY**: integrates the full IEEE 802.3 Clause 4 MAC *and* the 10BASE-T1S
36	PHY on one chip, and talks to the host MCU over **SPI** using the OPEN Alliance
37	TC6 ("10BASE-T1x MAC-PHY Serial Interface", v1.1) protocol. It exists precisely
38	to give a small MCU with no built-in Ethernet MAC a single-pair Ethernet link
39	over ~5 pins.
40	
41	Done in hardware by the LAN8651 (the MCU never touches these):
42	
43	- Line coding, PLCA / CSMA-CD media access, preamble/SFD.
44	- **FCS (CRC32) generation on TX and checking on RX.**
45	- On-wire framing and minimum-frame padding.
46	
47	SPI: LAN8651 is an SPI client, SCLK up to 25 MHz. Pins: `SDI`, `SDO`, `CS_N`,
48	`SCLK`, `IRQ_N` (active-low interrupt), plus a reset.
49	
50	**SPI mode — Mode 0 (CPOL = 0, CPHA = 0), MSB first.** Mandated by the OA TC6
51	v1.1 spec the part conforms to, and confirmed in the LAN8650/1 datasheet
52	(DS60001734 §5.1 *SPI Format*, §9 timing): "on the rising edge of SCLK the data
53	is captured, while on the falling edge … the data will change … always
54	transferred most significant bit/byte first," and the `tcss` ("CS_N low to SCLK
55	rising") timing means **SCLK idles low** → CPOL = 0, sample-on-leading-edge →
56	CPHA = 0. Host SPI-master config: 8-bit words, MSB first, CPOL = 0 / CPHA = 0
57	(Harmony: *Clock Polarity = Idle Low*, *Clock Phase = Valid Leading Edge*),
58	`CS_N` active-low idling high. The same mode applies to the fretboard SERCOM.
59	
60	Bring-up watch items: if the device-ID read returns `0x00`/`0xFF`, flip the
61	Harmony phase setting first (the dropdown wording varies) — the target is Mode 0.
62	And a TC6 chunk transaction (header + 64-byte data) needs `CS_N` held low for the
63	*whole* transfer; if the FLEXCOM SPI PLib toggles hardware CS per byte, drive
64	`CS_N` as a plain GPIO instead.
65	
66	## 3. What the host MCU must implement
67	
68	No TCP/IP, ARP, DHCP, or any IP stack. Three layers, none large:
69	
70	1. **SPI transport** — one SERCOM in SPI-master mode + GPIO for `CS_N`,
71	   `IRQ_N` (external interrupt), and reset.
72	2. **OA TC6 chunk protocol** — the only real "driver." Unlike a UART, the SPI
73	   link is *not* byte-transparent: it exchanges fixed-size **chunks** (default
74	   64-byte data payload + a 4-byte header on TX / 4-byte footer on RX), with
75	   credit-based flow control (TX credits and RX-chunks-available are reported in
76	   each footer), plus a separate control-transaction format for register
77	   read/writes during init. Microchip publishes an open-source reference driver
78	   ([`MicrochipTech/oa-tc6-lib`](https://github.com/MicrochipTech/oa-tc6-lib),
79	   §References) small enough to run on an Arduino — the candidate base for both
80	   ends here.
81	3. **Minimal L2 framing** — the MAC-PHY only transmits *valid Ethernet frames*,
82	   so the host prepends a fixed 14-byte Ethernet header (dest MAC, src MAC,
83	   ethertype) to the payload. For this link the MACs are hardcoded and a custom
84	   ethertype carries the existing frame formats verbatim:
85	   - fretboard → marvin: the 17-byte data-stream frame (see fretboard SPEC).
86	   - marvin → fretboard: the 1-byte button bitmask.
87	
88	   17 B + 14 B header = 31 B → a single chunk. The 1-byte command likewise. The
89	   existing UART framing (`0x03 … 0xFC`, `sample_seq`, etc.) can ride unchanged
90	   inside the Ethernet payload, so higher layers don't need to know the
91	   transport changed.
92	
93	## 4. Resource budget — fretboard (PIC32CM6408PL10048, 64 KB flash / 8 KB SRAM)
94	
95	Estimates; static allocation only (no malloc), per project rule.
96	
97	| Resource | Estimate | Notes |
98	|---|---|---|
99	| Flash | ~6–10 KB | OA TC6 lib (~4–8 KB) + SPI glue + L2 framing. Reclaim the UART data path if the UART link is fully retired. |
100	| SRAM | ~1–2 KB | A couple of chunk buffers + one TX/RX frame buffer. |
101	| SERCOM | 1 (SPI master) | A free SERCOM alongside SERCOM1 (still UART for now). |
102	| GPIO | 2–3 | `CS_N`, `IRQ_N` (ext-int), reset. |
103	| CPU | negligible | One chunk per 240 Hz tick, interrupt-driven off `IRQ_N`; the TC0 ISR stays lean. |
104	
105	SPI clock: SERCOM SPI master maxes at GCLK/2 ≈ **12 MHz** on the 24 MHz part
106	(not the chip's 25 MHz ceiling) — irrelevant for this data rate.
107	
108	Everything fits comfortably inside 64 KB / 8 KB.
109	
110	## 5. marvin side
111	
112	marvin runs **FreeRTOS + Harmony (no Linux)**, so it does *not* get a free
113	netdev — it needs its own TC6 driver. The TC6 service runs as a task woken by
114	the LAN8651 `IRQ_N` (a PIO external interrupt → `xSemaphoreGiveFromISR`, the
115	same pattern as `fretboard_link.c`'s RX path). The plan **adapts
116	[`MicrochipTech/oa-tc6-lib`](https://github.com/MicrochipTech/oa-tc6-lib)** (its
117	hardware-agnostic core + thin Harmony FLEXCOM-SPI glue), rather than writing a
118	TC6 from scratch — proven chunk/credit logic, and a **single portable `oa_tc6`
119	layer shared between marvin (Cortex-A5) and fretboard (Cortex-M0+)** is itself a
120	tidy demonstration that the OPEN Alliance SPI driver scales across the family.
121	marvin resources are not a concern. Hand-authored T1S code lives in
122	`firmware/marvin/default/src/net/t1s/`, kept out of the MCC-generated `config/`
123	tree and added via `user.cmake` (same discipline as `perf_log`/`console`).
124	
125	## 6. PoDL — "dumb" (no negotiation)
126	
127	PoDL is **not in the LAN8651** — the MAC-PHY only moves data. PoDL is external
128	coupling circuitry around the pair, and it is **transparent to both MCUs** (zero
129	firmware footprint, the §4 budget is unaffected):
130	
131	- **PSE side (marvin):** a fixed-voltage source + coupling inductors that inject
132	  DC onto the pair.
133	- **PD side (fretboard):** coupling inductors to extract DC + a regulator down to
134	  the PIC32CM rail.
135	- **Dumb / unmanaged:** no SCCP classification or negotiation handshake. Fixed
136	  supply voltage, fixed point-to-point pair, decided at design time. Simplest
137	  PoDL form; appropriate because the topology is fixed and both ends are ours.
138	
139	Microchip has PoDL reference designs that pair with the LAN865x EVBs, which also
140	helps the demonstration story.
141	
142	## 7. Topology — PLCA multidrop, marvin as coordinator
143	
144	**Decided (2026-06-16): PLCA from the start, multi-node.** The system is expected
145	to grow several nodes on one pair — multiple guitars and phototransistor
146	fretboard-detector nodes coexisting — so PLCA multidrop is a requirement, not just
147	headroom. marvin is the **PLCA coordinator (ID 0)**; every other node is a
148	follower. The single marvin↔fretboard link is brought up first, but the
149	addressing and demux are designed for N from the start so a new node joins with a
150	table entry, not a transport rewrite.
151	
152	### 7.1 Addressing (static — no discovery, keeps the M0+ node dumb)
153	
154	| Node | PLCA ID | MAC (locally administered) | Notes |
155	|---|---|---|---|
156	| marvin | 0 (coordinator) | `02:00:00:00:00:00` | beacons the PLCA cycle |
157	| node *k* | *k* | `02:00:00:00:00:0k` | e.g. fretboard = ID 1 |
158	
159	- One **custom ethertype** `0x88B5` (IEEE local/experimental range; no
160	  registration needed for a private bus) carries the existing payloads verbatim.
161	- A static **node table** on marvin maps `{PLCA ID, MAC, node_type}` → the bus
162	  `detector_id` (and the actuator target for TX). The single fretboard keeps
163	  `detector_id = 1`, matching today's `adc_fretboard` bus slot. No discovery /
164	  enumeration protocol — the table is compiled in.
165	- The 17-byte fretboard→marvin frame and the 1-byte marvin→fretboard bitmask ride
166	  inside the Ethernet payload unchanged; marvin demuxes incoming frames by src MAC
167	  and addresses outgoing ones to a specific node.
168	
169	## 8. Transport coexistence
170	
171	The marvin `FretboardLink_{Initialize,Send,IsConnected}` API is preserved (with
172	`Send` gaining a node target). UART and T1S transports live behind a
173	`MARVIN_FRETBOARD_TRANSPORT={UART,T1S}` **build flag**, default UART: the working
174	FLEXCOM1 UART link stays intact during T1S bring-up and is cut over (and its data
175	path reclaimed) only once T1S is proven.
176	
177	## 9. Decisions & open items
178	
179	Settled 2026-06-16 (see marvin journal): multi-node design-for-N / build-one-link;
180	PLCA coordinator on marvin (§7); adapt `oa-tc6-lib` (§5); UART kept in parallel
181	behind a build flag (§8); develop against a LAN8651 EVB/Click on the SAM9X75
182	Curiosity.
183	
184	Still open (non-blocking; settle during bring-up unless noted):
185	
186	- **Prereq (blocking):** a free FLEXCOM regenerated in SPI-master mode in MCC with
187	  the EVB pinout — no SPI PLib exists yet.
188	- **Prereq (blocking):** `oa-tc6-lib` added on disk as a subproject.
189	- PoDL supply voltage and the PD-side regulator topology (BOM, not firmware).
190	- Magnetics-free coupling component selection on the Sensor-LCD5 PCB.
191	
192	## References
193	
194	- **OA TC6 driver (candidate base, both ends):**
195	  [`MicrochipTech/oa-tc6-lib`](https://github.com/MicrochipTech/oa-tc6-lib) —
196	  Microchip's open-source OPEN Alliance TC6 (10BASE-T1x MAC-PHY Serial
197	  Interface) library: SPI chunk protocol + control transactions, used as the
198	  shared portable layer (§3, §5).
199	- LAN8650/1 (LAN8651B1) datasheet — 10BASE-T1S MAC-PHY Ethernet Controller with
200	  SPI, on [Microchip online docs](https://onlinedocs.microchip.com/) /
201	  the LAN8651 product page.
202	- OPEN Alliance *10BASE-T1x MAC-PHY Serial Interface* specification (TC6), v1.1.
203

52	/* Parse a validated 17-byte fretboard frame and emit a PERF_REC_FRETBOARD_RAW
53	 * record. Shared by both transports; the caller guarantees the frame markers.
54	 * Frame: [0x03, 5×ADC_u16 LE, seq_u32 LE, applied_mask_u8, 0xFC]. */
55	static void emit_fretboard_frame(const uint8_t *frame)
56	{

78	    {

124	        const pending_note_t *n = &s_note_q[idx];
125	        if ((n->fret_mask & bit) && (int32_t)(n->assert_at_ms - by_ms) <= 0)
126	        {
127	            return true;
128	        }
129	    }
130	    return false;
131	}
132	
133	static bool strum_q_needs_by(uint8_t bit, uint32_t by_ms)
134	{
135	    for (uint8_t i = 0u; i < s_strum_count; i++)
136	    {
137	        uint8_t idx = (uint8_t)((s_strum_head + i) % TP_FIFO_CAP);
138	        const pending_strum_t *s = &s_strum_q[idx];
139	        if ((s->fret_mask & bit) && (int32_t)(s->strum_at_ms - by_ms) <= 0)
140	        {
141	            return true;
142	        }
143	    }
144	    return false;
145	}
146	
147	static void publish_mask(uint8_t mask)
148	{
149	    s_output_mask = mask;
150	    if (s_pipeline_enabled)
151	    {
152	        FretboardLink_Send(mask, (uint8_t)PERF_ACTUATOR_PRODUCER_TIMING);
153	    }
154	}
155	
156	/* Edge derivation:
157	 *   - presses_mask: rising edge of pressed
158	 *   - releases_mask: falling edge of pressed */
159	static void derive_edges(const detector_state_t *state,
160	                         uint8_t *presses_mask, uint8_t *releases_mask,
161	                         uint8_t *pressed_mask)
162	{
163	    uint8_t pm = 0u;
164	    uint8_t rm = 0u;
165	    uint8_t cm = 0u;
166	
167	    for (uint8_t i = 0u; i < FRET_COUNT; i++)
168	    {
169	        bool pressed = state->fret[i].pressed != 0u;
170	        if (pressed) { cm |= s_fret_bit[i]; }
171	
172	        bool was_pressed = (s_prev_pressed_mask & s_fret_bit[i]) != 0u;
173	        if (pressed && !was_pressed) { pm |= s_fret_bit[i]; }
174	        if (!pressed && was_pressed) { rm |= s_fret_bit[i]; }
175	    }
176	
177	    s_prev_pressed_mask = cm;
178	    *presses_mask  = pm;
179	    *releases_mask = rm;
180	    *pressed_mask  = cm;
181	}
182	
183	static void chord_commit(void)
184	{
185	    if (note_q_full() || strum_q_full())
186	    {
187	        s_chord_open = false;
188	        s_chord_mask = 0u;
189	        return;
190	    }
191	
192	    uint32_t assert_at = s_now_ms + TP_STRUM_DELAY_MS - TP_FRET_EARLY_MS;
193	    uint32_t strum_at  = s_now_ms + TP_STRUM_DELAY_MS;
194	
195	    if (!strum_q_empty())
196	    {
197	        uint8_t  last_idx = (uint8_t)((s_strum_tail + TP_FIFO_CAP - 1u) % TP_FIFO_CAP);
198	        uint32_t earliest = s_strum_q[last_idx].strum_at_ms + TP_STRUM_PULSE_MS;
199	        if ((int32_t)(assert_at - earliest) < 0)
200	        {
201	            assert_at = earliest;
202	            strum_at  = assert_at + TP_FRET_EARLY_MS;
203	        }
204	    }
205	
206	    pending_note_t  n = { .assert_at_ms = assert_at, .fret_mask = s_chord_mask };
207	    pending_strum_t s = { .strum_at_ms  = strum_at,  .fret_mask = s_chord_mask };
208	    note_q_push(n);
209	    strum_q_push(s);
210	
211	    s_chord_open = false;
212	    s_chord_mask = 0u;
213	}
214	
215	static void process_notes(void)
216	{
217	    while (!note_q_empty())
218	    {
219	        const pending_note_t *n = &s_note_q[s_note_head];
220	        if ((int32_t)(s_now_ms - n->assert_at_ms) < 0) { break; }
221	
222	        for (uint8_t i = 0u; i < FRET_COUNT; i++)
223	        {
224	            uint8_t bit = s_fret_bit[i];
225	            bool need = (n->fret_mask & bit) != 0u;
226	            bool have = (s_frets_active & bit) != 0u;
227	            if (need && !have)      { s_frets_active |= bit; }
228	            else if (!need && have) { s_frets_active &= (uint8_t)~bit; }
229	        }
230	        note_q_pop();
231	    }
232	}
233	
234	static void process_strums(void)
235	{
236	    while (!strum_q_empty())
237	    {
238	        const pending_strum_t *s = &s_strum_q[s_strum_head];
239	        if ((int32_t)(s_now_ms - s->strum_at_ms) < 0) { break; }
240	
241	        s_strum_active        = true;
242	        s_strum_direction     = !s_strum_direction;
243	        s_strum_release_at_ms = s_now_ms + TP_STRUM_PULSE_MS;
244	
245	        strum_q_pop();
246	    }
247	}
248	
249	static void process_releases(uint8_t live_pressed_mask)
250	{
251	    for (uint8_t i = 0u; i < FRET_COUNT; i++)
252	    {
253	        uint8_t bit = s_fret_bit[i];
254	        if ((s_release_pending_mask & bit) == 0u) { continue; }
255	        if ((int32_t)(s_now_ms - s_release_at_ms[i]) < 0) { continue; }
256	        if (live_pressed_mask & bit) { continue; }
257	        /* Hold only if re-needed at/before this release (back-to-back); a need
258	         * further out releases now for a clean per-note command. */
259	        if (note_q_needs_by(bit, s_release_at_ms[i]) ||
260	            strum_q_needs_by(bit, s_release_at_ms[i])) { continue; }
261	
262	        s_frets_active        &= (uint8_t)~bit;
263	        s_release_pending_mask &= (uint8_t)~bit;
264	    }
265	}
266	
267	static void advance(uint8_t live_pressed_mask)
268	{
269	    if (s_chord_open && (int32_t)(s_now_ms - s_chord_start_ms) >= (int32_t)TP_CHORD_WINDOW_MS)
270	    {
271	        chord_commit();
272	    }
273	
274	    if (s_strum_active && (int32_t)(s_now_ms - s_strum_release_at_ms) >= 0)
275	    {
276	        s_strum_active = false;
277	    }
278	
279	    process_notes();
280	    process_strums();
281	    process_releases(live_pressed_mask);
282	
283	    uint8_t mask = s_frets_active;
284	    if (s_strum_active)
285	    {
286	        mask |= s_strum_direction ? TIMING_BIT_STRUM_UP : TIMING_BIT_STRUM_DOWN;
287	    }
288	    publish_mask(mask);
289	}
290	
291	/* Build the per-frame TIMING snapshot from current pipeline state. Called
292	 * once per process_frame after advance() has settled all queues and the
293	 * publish_mask. Deadlines for empty queues are zeroed; host inspects the
294	 * count fields before treating *_at_ms as meaningful. */
295	static void fill_timing_snapshot(perf_timing_snapshot_t *snap)
296	{
297	    memset(snap, 0, sizeof(*snap));
298	    snap->now_ms = s_now_ms;
299	
300	    snap->chord_open   = s_chord_open ? 1u : 0u;
301	    snap->chord_mask   = s_chord_open ? s_chord_mask : 0u;
302	    snap->chord_age_ms = s_chord_open
303	                       ? (uint16_t)(s_now_ms - s_chord_start_ms)
304	                       : 0u;
305	
306	    snap->note_q_count = s_note_count;
307	    if (s_note_count > 0u)
308	    {
309	        const pending_note_t *head = &s_note_q[s_note_head];
310	        snap->note_head_mask  = head->fret_mask;
311	        snap->note_head_at_ms = head->assert_at_ms;
312	        uint8_t tail_union = 0u;
313	        for (uint8_t i = 0u; i < s_note_count; i++)
314	        {
315	            uint8_t idx = (uint8_t)((s_note_head + i) % TP_FIFO_CAP);
316	            tail_union |= s_note_q[idx].fret_mask;
317	        }
318	        snap->note_tail_mask = tail_union;
319	    }
320	
321	    snap->strum_q_count = s_strum_count;
322	    if (s_strum_count > 0u)
323	    {
324	        const pending_strum_t *head = &s_strum_q[s_strum_head];
325	        snap->strum_head_mask  = head->fret_mask;
326	        snap->strum_head_at_ms = head->strum_at_ms;
327	    }
328	    /* strum_dir toggles each fired strum; report the *next* direction
329	     * (what would fire if the front of strum_q reaches its deadline now). */
330	    snap->strum_dir_next = s_strum_direction ? 2u /*up*/ : 1u /*down*/;
331	
332	    snap->frets_active         = s_frets_active;
333	    snap->strum_active         = s_strum_active ? 1u : 0u;
334	    snap->release_pending_mask = s_release_pending_mask;
335	    snap->publish_mask         = s_output_mask;
336	    snap->strum_release_at_ms  = s_strum_active ? s_strum_release_at_ms : 0u;
337	
338	    if (s_release_pending_mask != 0u)
339	    {
340	        uint32_t min_at = 0xFFFFFFFFu;
341	        for (uint8_t i = 0u; i < FRET_COUNT; i++)
342	        {
343	            if ((s_release_pending_mask & s_fret_bit[i]) == 0u) { continue; }
344	            if (s_release_at_ms[i] < min_at) { min_at = s_release_at_ms[i]; }
345	        }
346	        snap->release_min_at_ms = (min_at == 0xFFFFFFFFu) ? 0u : min_at;
347	    }
348	}
349	
350	static void process_frame(const detector_state_t *state)
351	{
352	    /* Detector frame timestamps drive the clock so this is replay-
353	     * deterministic. timestamp_us is monotonic per spec §4.2.3. */
354	    s_now_ms = (uint32_t)(state->timestamp_us / 1000ull);
355	    s_last_frame_us = state->timestamp_us;
356	
357	    uint8_t presses, releases, pressed_mask;
358	    derive_edges(state, &presses, &releases, &pressed_mask);
359	
360	    if (presses)
361	    {
362	        if (!s_chord_open)
363	        {
364	            s_chord_open     = true;
365	            s_chord_start_ms = s_now_ms;
366	            s_chord_mask     = 0u;
367	        }
368	        s_chord_mask |= presses;
369	    }
370	
371	    for (uint8_t i = 0u; i < FRET_COUNT; i++)
372	    {
373	        if (releases & s_fret_bit[i])
374	        {
375	            s_release_at_ms[i]      = s_now_ms + TP_STRUM_DELAY_MS;
376	            s_release_pending_mask |= s_fret_bit[i];
377	        }
378	    }
379	
380	    advance(pressed_mask);
381	
382	    PerfLog_EmitStamp(PERF_STAGE_TP_TICK, state->frame_epoch,
383	                      (uint32_t)s_output_mask);
384	
385	    perf_timing_snapshot_t snap;
386	    fill_timing_snapshot(&snap);
387	    PerfLog_EmitTiming(state->frame_epoch, &snap);
388	}
389	
390	static void timing_pipeline_task(void *param)
391	{
392	    (void)param;
393	
394	    QueueHandle_t bus = Detector_BusQueue();
395	    configASSERT(bus != NULL);
396	
397	    LOG_INFO("TIMING: pipeline started\r\n");
398	
399	    for (;;)
400	    {
401	        detector_state_t state;
402	        if (xQueueReceive(bus, &state, pdMS_TO_TICKS(TP_TICK_MS)) == pdTRUE)
403	        {
404	            if ((detector_id_t)state.detector_id != Detector_GetActive())
405	            {
406	                continue;
407	            }
408	            process_frame(&state);
409	        }
410	        else
411	        {
412	            /* No new frame; advance the clock so deadlines that fell
413	             * between frames (strum pulses, release timers) still fire. */
414	            s_now_ms += TP_TICK_MS;
415	            advance(s_prev_pressed_mask);
416	        }
417	    }
418	}
419	
420	void TimingPipeline_Initialize(void)
421	{
422	    TaskHandle_t h = xTaskCreateStatic(timing_pipeline_task,
423	                                       "Timing",
424	                                       TP_TASK_STACK_WORDS,
425	                                       NULL,
426	                                       TP_TASK_PRIORITY,
427	                                       s_task_stack,
428	                                       &s_task_tcb);
429	    PerfLog_RegisterTaskForHighwater(PERF_TASK_TIMING, h);
430	}
431	
432	void TimingPipeline_SetEnabled(bool enabled)
433	{
434	    s_pipeline_enabled = enabled;
435	}

6	/*
7	 * Remote-control command receiver.
8	 *
9	 * Reads single-byte bitmask commands from SERCOM1 UART RX.
10	 * Each bit directly controls one output:
11	 *
12	 *   Bit 0 = Green fret
13	 *   Bit 1 = Red fret
14	 *   Bit 2 = Yellow fret
15	 *   Bit 3 = Blue fret
16	 *   Bit 4 = Orange fret
17	 *   Bit 5 = Strum down
18	 *   Bit 6 = Strum up
19	 *
20	 * Bit = 1 → assert (drive low), Bit = 0 → release (tri-state).
21	 */
22	
23	#define CMD_BIT_GREEN       (1U << 0)
24	#define CMD_BIT_RED         (1U << 1)
25	#define CMD_BIT_YELLOW      (1U << 2)
26	#define CMD_BIT_BLUE        (1U << 3)
27	#define CMD_BIT_ORANGE      (1U << 4)
28	#define CMD_BIT_STRUM_DOWN  (1U << 5)
29	#define CMD_BIT_STRUM_UP    (1U << 6)
30	
31	void cmd_receive_init(void);
32	
33	/* Call each tick.  Drains RX buffer and applies the latest bitmask. */
34	void cmd_receive_update(void);
35	
36	/* Drive the outputs from an explicit bitmask (CMD_BIT_* layout). Lets the
37	 * standalone model path reuse the same GPIO assert/release logic. */
38	void cmd_receive_apply_mask(uint8_t mask);
39	
40	/* The bitmask currently driven on the outputs (most recent applied command).
41	 * Bit layout matches CMD_BIT_*. */
42	uint8_t cmd_receive_current_mask(void);
43	
44	#endif

38	{
39	    apply_output(mask, CMD_BIT_GREEN,      green_assert,      green_release);

41	    apply_output(mask, CMD_BIT_YELLOW,     yellow_assert,     yellow_release);
42	    apply_output(mask, CMD_BIT_BLUE,       blue_assert,       blue_release);
43	    apply_output(mask, CMD_BIT_ORANGE,     orange_assert,     orange_release);
44	    apply_output(mask, CMD_BIT_STRUM_DOWN, strum_down_assert, strum_down_release);
45	    apply_output(mask, CMD_BIT_STRUM_UP,   strum_up_assert,   strum_up_release);
46	    current_mask = mask;

54	void cmd_receive_update(void)
55	{
56	    size_t avail = SERCOM1_USART_ReadCountGet();
57	    if (avail == 0)
58	        return;
59	
60	    uint8_t buf[64];
61	    size_t n = (avail > sizeof(buf)) ? sizeof(buf) : avail;
62	    SERCOM1_USART_Read(buf, n);
63	
64	    cmd_receive_apply_mask(buf[n - 1]);
65	}

7	/*
8	 * Streaming variant of the on-device inference. Instead of recomputing the whole
9	 * receptive field every tick (model_infer.c), it caches each layer's output
10	 * column in a small ring and advances ONE new column per sample — ~1 conv column
11	 * per layer per tick (~4x fewer MACs), so inference clears 240 Hz.
12	 *
13	 * Stateful and per-sample: call model_infer_stream_step() exactly once per ADC
14	 * scan, in order. It computes a CONTINUOUS causal conv, which is bit-exact with a
15	 * model TRAINED AT window >= receptive field (85) — at a shorter window the
16	 * windowed model's moving zero-pad boundary would not match (see runtime.md /
17	 * edge-ai journal). Output is 0 until the receptive field has filled.
18	 *
19	 * Output bitmask matches CMD_BIT_* (bits 0..4 frets, bit 5 strum-down).
20	 */
21	
22	void model_infer_stream_init(void);
23	
24	/* Select the active model (per-difficulty swap); recomputes the receptive field. */
25	void model_infer_stream_set_model(const model_def_t *m);
26	
27	/* Process one 240 Hz scan and return the command bitmask. Advances the stream by
28	 * one sample (do not skip or repeat samples). */
29	uint8_t model_infer_stream_step(const uint16_t adc[5]);

_**Agent - sidechain (claude-haiku-4-5-20251001 2026-06-16 22:40:40Z)**_

<tool-use data-tool-type="read" data-tool-name="Read"><details>
<summary>Tool use: **Read**</summary>
 `./tools/marvin-perf/marvin_perf/exporters/sensiml_csv.py`

```text
1	"""Export a marvin-perf capture as a SensiML-compatible CSV for MPLAB ML.
2	
3	One row per PERF_REC_FRETBOARD_RAW (~240 Hz). Each row carries the five raw
4	ADC values plus a set of binary labels whose meaning depends on `labels`:
5	
6	- `labels="detector"` (default, back-compat): five per-fret labels drawn from
7	  the most-recent PERF_REC_DETECTOR.pressed_mask, broadcast forward by
8	  frame_epoch (~4 fretboard samples per cv frame). Columns:
9	      timestamp,ph_green,...,ph_orange,
10	      label_green,label_red,label_yellow,label_blue,label_orange
11	- `labels="actuator"` (edge-ai distillation target): six labels drawn from the
12	  most-recent PERF_REC_ACTUATOR.intended_mask — five frets verbatim plus one
13	  collapsed strum bit (logical OR of strum-down and strum-up, since alternating
14	  direction is a human ergonomic constraint the controller doesn't enforce).
15	  Columns:
16	      timestamp,ph_green,...,ph_orange,
17	      fret_green,fret_red,fret_yellow,fret_blue,fret_orange,strum
18	
19	- `labels="actuator-fb"` (preferred edge-ai target, schema v4+): same six
20	  labels, but sourced from the actuator bitmask the fretboard reports *inside*
21	  each FRETBOARD_RAW frame (`applied_mask`) — paired with the ADC atomically on
22	  the device, with no cross-stream forward-fill. Adds an `fb_seq` column (the
23	  fretboard's monotonic sample counter) so downstream can detect dropped frames.
24	  Columns:
25	      timestamp,fb_seq,ph_green,...,ph_orange,
26	      fret_green,fret_red,fret_yellow,fret_blue,fret_orange,strum

29	PERF_REC_ACTUATOR keeps both strum bits as marvin emitted them, so a future
30	direction-aware corpus can preserve them. See tools/edge-ai/docs/training.md §2.
31	
32	`timestamp` is decimal seconds since the first emitted row's ts_counter.

38	- Capture missing the SESSION record raises ExportError (no timer_freq_hz

124	def export_sensiml_csv(

134	    default, back-compat), "actuator" (5 frets + collapsed strum from
135	    Actuator.intended_mask, cross-stream), "actuator-fb" (same from the
136	    fretboard's in-frame applied_mask + fb_seq column), or "detector-fb" (a
137	    diagnostic probe: detector pressed_mask frets — clean per-note structure
138	    without the pipeline's legato hold — plus the in-frame applied strum and
139	    fb_seq). The fb modes clock off fb_seq and need no SESSION.
140	
141	    `strict=True` drops FretboardRaw rows that arrive before the first
142	    label-source record (so every emitted row has a real label). Default is
143	    to emit them with all labels = 0 — useful when the capture starts before
144	    the label source has produced its first record.
145	    """

149	        )
150	
151	    capture = open_capture(capture_path)
152	
153	    session: Session | None = None
154	    last_detector: Detector | None = None

156	    n_skipped_unlabeled = 0
157	    n_detector_records = 0
158	    n_actuator_records = 0
159	    n_fretboard_records = 0
160	    n_rows = 0
161	    n_strum_events = 0
162	    n_seq_gaps = 0
163	    prev_strum = 0
164	    prev_seq: int | None = None
165	    t_baseline: int | None = None  # ts_counter of the first emitted row
166	    t_end_s = 0.0
167	
168	    fb_clock = labels in _FB_CLOCK_MODES
169	    header = {
170	        "actuator": _HEADER_ACTUATOR,
171	        "actuator-fb": _HEADER_ACTUATOR_FB,
172	        "detector-fb": _HEADER_ACTUATOR_FB,  # same schema, detector-sourced frets
173	    }.get(labels, _HEADER_DETECTOR)
174	
175	    out_path = Path(out_path)
176	    with FileSource(capture.bin_path) as src, out_path.open("w", newline="") as fh:
177	        writer = csv.writer(fh)
178	        writer.writerow(header)
179	        stats = FrameStats()
180	
181	        for frame in iter_frames(src, stats):
182	            try:
183	                rec = decode_record(frame.payload)
184	            except Exception:
185	                continue
186	
187	            if isinstance(rec, Session) and session is None:
188	                session = rec
189	                continue
190	
191	            if isinstance(rec, Detector):
192	                last_detector = rec
193	                n_detector_records += 1
194	                continue
195	
196	            if isinstance(rec, Actuator):
197	                last_actuator = rec
198	                n_actuator_records += 1
199	                continue
200	
201	            if isinstance(rec, FretboardRaw):
202	                n_fretboard_records += 1
203	
204	                # Track dropped frames via the fretboard's own sample counter.
205	                if prev_seq is not None and rec.fb_sample_seq != (prev_seq + 1):
206	                    n_seq_gaps += 1
207	                prev_seq = rec.fb_sample_seq
208	
209	                # fb-clock modes derive the timestamp from fb_sample_seq (the
210	                # fretboard's own 240 Hz clock), so they need no SESSION; other
211	                # modes need timer_freq_hz from SESSION for the ts_counter clock.
212	                if session is None and not fb_clock:
213	                    # Defer rejection to after the loop so we still tally
214	                    # how many records were skipped for diagnostics.
215	                    n_skipped_unlabeled += 1
216	                    continue
217	
218	                # actuator-fb labels live inside the frame → always present;
219	                # other modes need their forward-filled source record.
220	                if labels == "actuator":
221	                    have_label = last_actuator is not None
222	                elif labels == "actuator-fb":
223	                    have_label = True
224	                else:  # detector, detector-fb
225	                    have_label = last_detector is not None
226	                if not have_label and strict:
227	                    n_skipped_unlabeled += 1

233	                    t_s = (rec.fb_sample_seq - t_baseline) / FRETBOARD_HZ
234	                else:
235	                    if t_baseline is None:
236	                        t_baseline = rec.hdr.ts_counter
237	                    t_s = (rec.hdr.ts_counter - t_baseline) / float(

> "**Planned: fretboard ↔ marvin link moves to 10BASE-T1S + dumb PoDL.** Replace the FLEXCOM2/SERCOM UART pair with single-pair Ethernet via a LAN8651B1 MAC-PHY on each end. Motivation, in order: PoDL carries power *and* data on one pair to the guitar; better noise/cable tolerance; PLCA multidrop headroom; and demonstrating 10BASE-T1S + PoDL inside a larger Microchip system (SAM9X7 + LAN8651 + PIC32CM). Bandwidth is not a driver — the existing UART has ~12× headroom. PoDL is **dumb** (fixed voltage, no SCCP negotiation) and transparent to both MCUs. No IP stack — the host implements only SPI + the OPEN Alliance TC6 chunk protocol + minimal L2 framing, with the existing frame formats riding unchanged inside the Ethernet payload. Fits comfortably on the PIC32CM (est. ~6–10 KB flash / ~1–2 KB SRAM); marvin is bare-metal so it gets a shared portable `oa_tc6` driver, not a free netdev. ### 6. TIMING PIPELINE ACTIVE DETECTOR FILTERING

**File:** `/Users/gregmrozek/Projects/microchip/guitar-pic/firmware/marvin/default/src/actuator/timing_pipeline.c`

The timing pipeline reads detector_state_t records from the detector-state bus queue and filters by active detector (line snippet from the task loop):

```c
for (;;)
{
    detector_state_t state;
    if (xQueueReceive(bus, &state, pdMS_TO_TICKS(TP_TICK_MS)) == pdTRUE)
    {
        if ((detector_id_t)state.detector_id != Detector_GetActive())
        {
            continue;  /* Skip records from inactive detectors */
        }
        process_frame(&state);
    }
    else
    {
        /* No new frame; advance the clock so deadlines that fell
         * between frames (strum pulses, release timers) still fire. */
        s_now_ms += TP_TICK_MS;
    }
}
```

2. **Detector ID is decoupled from node** — a node has a `type` (T1S_NODE_FRETBOARD, etc.) but feeds its data to a `detector_id` (e.g., DETECTOR_ADC_FRETBOARD). A new guitar node type gets a new detector ID slot and registers in the node table by node_id, MAC, and type.

3. **Timing pipeline filters by `Detector_GetActive()`** — independent of how many detectors/nodes are enabled, only one is active for the timing pipeline at a time (console command `active <cv|adc>` switches). Adding a third detector ID requires only a new enum value and console command enhancement.

4. **Frame format is transport-agnostic** — the 17-byte fretboard ADC stream rides inside the Ethernet payload unchanged (docs/t1s-podl-link.md §3). A new guitar node stream can follow the same pattern.

## Comprehensive Fretboard Firmware Exploration Report

I have thoroughly analyzed the fretboard firmware (`PIC32CM6408PL10048`) and can provide you with a complete picture for planning the detector/guitar split.

### Executive Summary

The firmware has **two build-time modes** controlled by `FRETBOARD_MODE` in `fretboard_config.h`:
1. **`MARVIN_DRIVEN` (I/O bridge mode)** — pure detector: scan ADCs, emit frames, apply remote commands
2. **`MODEL_DRIVEN` (current default)** — hybrid: detector + local inference (on-device ML model)

The code cleanly separates **detector** (sensor reading & UART output) from **actuator** (GPIO button control). Model inference is a **third, independent concern**.

### 1. HARDWARE CONFIGURATION

**Device:** PIC32CM6408PL10048 (ARM Cortex-M0+, 24 MHz, 8 KB SRAM, 64 KB Flash)

#### ADC Inputs (Phototransistor Detector — **STAY in fretboard**)
- **Green:** AIN28 (PA28)
- **Red:** AIN16 (PA16)  
- **Yellow:** AIN19 (PA19)
- **Blue:** AIN27 (PA27)
- **Orange:** AIN26 (PA26)

Read in `/firmware/fretboard/fret_scan.c:4-9` (channel mapping).

#### GPIO Outputs (Wii Guitar Button Actuator — **MOVE to new guitar project**)
Open-drain tri-state GPIOs (assert=drive low, release=input+pull-up):
- **PA06** (bit 0) — Green fret
- **PA05** (bit 1) — Red fret
- **PA07** (bit 2) — Yellow fret
- **PA04** (bit 3) — Blue fret
- **PA01** (bit 4) — Orange fret
- **PA03** (bit 5) — Strum down
- **PA00** (bit 6) — Strum up

All driven via `BUTTON_*` macros in MCC-generated `/firmware/fretboard/fretboard-mcc/src/config/default/peripheral/port/plib_port.h`.

#### UART (SERCOM1 — Transport layer)
- **TX (PB00)** — data stream out (17 or 21 bytes/frame @ 240 Hz)
- **RX (PB01)** — command in (1 byte/tick, bitmask)
- **Baud:** 500,000 (8N1)

#### Timer (TC0 — ISR Backbone)
240 Hz callback drives the sampling/apply/send loop.

### 4. BUILD-TIME MODES & CODE BRANCHING

#### Mode A: `MARVIN_DRIVEN` (Default fallback; I/O bridge)
- **Purpose:** Pure detector. No game logic, no inference. Sends raw ADCs; applies remote bitmask commands.
- **TC0 ISR:** `fret_scan_all()` → `data_stream_send()` → `cmd_receive_update()`
- **Main loop:** Empty while(true) loop
- **Orphaned files:** Still compiled (`fret_detect.c`, `fret_button.c` in fileset), but not called
- **Flash footprint:** ~8–10 KB (core + MCC)
- **SRAM:** ~1 KB

#### Mode B: `MODEL_DRIVEN` (Current default; standalone inference)
- **Purpose:** Detector + on-device ML inference. Marvin disconnected (except for initial commissioning/fallback).
- **TC0 ISR:** `fret_scan_all()` → push to model's ring/queue → apply `s_latest_cmd` → `data_stream_send_model()`
- **Main loop:** Drain sample queue/recompute inference, publish `s_latest_cmd`
- **SW0 (PB03, active-low momentary):** Toggles model on/off (debounced, ~50 ms window)
- **LED0 (PB02, active-low):** Lit when model enabled; off at boot
- **Model selection:** Runtime pointer swap via `model_infer_set_model()` (per-difficulty)
- **Flash footprint:** ~18–22 KB (core + MCC + model weights)
- **SRAM:** ~4–5 KB (input ring + layer activations + scratch)
- **Compilation guard:** Both `model_infer.c` and `model_infer_stream.c` included; `MODEL_INFER_STREAMING` selects which compiles its static buffers

### 5. WIRE PROTOCOL (SERCOM1, 500 kbaud)

#### MARVIN_DRIVEN data frame (17 bytes, sent every 4.17 ms @ 240 Hz):
```
Offset  Size  Field
0       1     start = 0x03
1–2     2×u16 green (LE)
3–4     2×u16 red (LE)
5–6     2×u16 yellow (LE)
7–8     2×u16 blue (LE)
9–10    2×u16 orange (LE)
11–14   1×u32 sample_seq (LE, monotonic; gaps = dropped frames)
15      1×u8  applied_mask (bitmask currently driving GPIO)
16      1     end = 0xFC
```

**Applied mask:** Bits [0–6] = frets [0–4], strum-down, strum-up. Snapshot at send time (from `cmd_receive_current_mask()`).

#### MODEL_DRIVEN data frame (21 bytes):
```
Offset  Size  Field
0–16    (as above)
17–20   1×u32 infer_count (total inferences run in main loop)
16      1     end = 0xFC (shifted to offset 20)
```

**Total bandwidth:** 17 B × 240 Hz = 4.08 KB/s (12× headroom at 500 kbaud).

#### RX command (single byte):
```
Bit  Function
0    Green fret
1    Red fret
2    Yellow fret
3    Blue fret
4    Orange fret
5    Strum down
6    Strum up
7    (unused)
```

**Coalescing:** Only the **last byte in the current tick** is applied (older bytes in the same tick are discarded).

### 11. T1S/ETHERCAT FUTURE (From journal §3, open questions)

**Direction (2026-06-09, not yet built):**
- Replace SERCOM1 UART (500 kbaud) with **10BASE-T1S Ethernet** (LAN8651B1 MAC-PHY + TC6 SPI driver).
- **Fretboard side:** OA TC6 SPI driver + L2 framing (~6–10 KB flash, ~1–2 KB SRAM). Reuse one free SERCOM in SPI mode + CS_N/IRQ_N/reset GPIO.
- **Frame formats unchanged:** 17-byte data + 1-byte command ride inside Ethernet payload; `data_stream.c` / `cmd_receive.c` logic unaffected.
- **PLCA multi-node bus:** Marvin = ID 0; fretboard = ID 1, MAC `02:00:00:00:00:01`.
- **Open items:** Ethertype (candidate `0x88B5`), MAC allocation, PoDL BOM, UART fallback flag.

**Implication for split:** When planning the guitar project, **do not assume UART**. Either build it to use whatever marvin-side link is finalized, or design the guitar → detector communication to ride the same link protocol (TBD).

**Current stated purpose (lines 3–10):**
> Firmware for PIC32CM6408PL10048 (Cortex-M0+, 24 MHz) that acts as an **I/O bridge** between a Guitar Hero controller and an off-board host. Five phototransistors above the TV strike line are sampled and streamed out continuously; the host runs detection / chord / strum logic and sends back a single-byte bitmask that drives the controller's button GPIOs directly.

**Two build-time modes (lines 12–20):**

> - `MODEL_DRIVEN` (current default): on-device int8 neural net maps ADC window to button bitmask, standalone (marvin disconnected).

You now have the complete anatomy of the fretboard firmware. The **detector → UART output** and **UART input → actuator GPIO** flows are cleanly isolated; model inference is orthogonal and currently runs standalone on the detector hardware. The next step would be to discuss whether the guitar project:

1. **Only receives commands** (model stays with detector) — simplest split

# New `guitar` subproject + T1S node-class taxonomy

## Context

The marvin↔node T1S link now works (Phases 1–4 committed on the `t1s` branch). The next
structural step is to formalize the **multi-node taxonomy** the bus was built for.

Today the `firmware/fretboard/` firmware fuses three roles on one PIC32CM PL10: the
phototransistor **detector** (ADC → stream), the Wii-guitar **actuator** (`cmd_receive.c` →
open-drain GPIO), and an edge-ai **on-device model** (MODEL_DRIVEN). The intended end state
is separate node *classes* on the one PLCA bus:

- **Detector nodes** — observe game state and stream it to marvin (`fretboard` keeps its name
  and becomes detector-only; future variants possible).
- **Guitar nodes** — receive marvin's command bitmask and actuate a Wii guitar (new `guitar`
  subproject; future variants possible).

marvin is the PLCA coordinator and **selects the active detector and the active guitar** among
whatever is on the bus (active-detector selection already exists via `Detector_SetActive`).

**This pass = skeleton + taxonomy + design only** — no firmware code. It stands up the new
subproject, records the taxonomy in the specs, and writes the guitar firmware design for a
follow-up. Decisions locked this session:

1	# Guitar Hero Bot — System Specification
2	
3	> Top-level overview. For implementation detail of any single subproject, follow the pointers in §3. Each subproject owns its own spec; this document does not duplicate them.
4	
5	---
6	
7	## 1. Mission
8	
9	Build an autonomous robot that plays Guitar Hero / Rock Band on a real Wii guitar controller by watching the game video, detecting notes in real time, and pressing physical buttons in sync with the music. The system must run end-to-end without a host PC in the runtime path, produce reference-quality detector output that lighter detectors can be trained against, and provide an on-device operator UI for calibration, mode control, and replay.
10	
11	## 2. Current architecture
12	
13	Three pieces, one runtime brain:
14	
15	```
16	Wii ──HDMI──► ElectronWarp ──HDMI──► TC358743 ──CSI-2──┐
17	                                                       ▼
18	   ┌──────────────────────  marvin (SAM9X75)  ────────────┐
19	   │  HDMI capture → CV detect → timing pipeline → cmds   │
20	   │           ↑              detector-state bus          │
21	   │           │                       ▲                  │
22	   │           │  10.1″ LVDS + maxtouch │                  │
23	   │           │       (operator UI)    │                  │
24	   │           └────────── SD card ─────┘  (recording)    │
25	   └────────┬──────────────────────────┬───────────────────┘
26	            │ FLEXCOM2 UART (cmds)     │ FLEXCOM2 UART (ADC)
27	            ▼                          │
28	   ┌──────────────────────────────────┐│
29	   │   fretboard (PIC32CM6408)        │┘
30	   │   ADC scan ↔ open-drain GPIO     │
31	   └────────┬─────────────────────────┘
32	            │ GPIO
33	            ▼
34	   Wii guitar controller ──► Wii (closes the loop)
35	
36	                ◇ off-band: dev PC running fret-tuner
37	                  (calibration / detector tuning / replay)
38	```
39	
40	**Per-tier role summary:**
41	
42	- **marvin** — SAM9X75 Curiosity host. Owns HDMI capture, the *reference* CV note detector, ingest of fretboard ADC samples, the chord/strum timing pipeline, command emission to fretboard, the on-device LVDS+touch operator UI, and reference-data recording to SD. The runtime brain.
43	- **fretboard** — PIC32CM6408PL10048 MCU on a sensor/actuator board. Streams 5-channel phototransistor ADC up to marvin and converts incoming bitmask commands into open-drain GPIO presses on a Wii guitar controller. Has a standalone fallback mode where it runs its own chord FIFO without marvin in the loop.
44	- **fret-tuner** — Off-band Python tool (FastAPI + browser UI, Linux/macOS PC). Used at the bench for sensor calibration, detector-algorithm tuning, and replay analysis of recordings produced by marvin. Not in the runtime path.

Offline development first; Phase 1 data pipeline in progress. | [`tools/edge-ai/docs/journal.md`](tools/edge-ai/docs/journal.md) |
55	| gameplay | marvin spec [§4.8](firmware/marvin/docs/spec.md) + [`firmware/marvin/docs/gh3_navigation.md`](firmware/marvin/docs/gh3_navigation.md) — GH3 game-state observer/controller offline prototype; algorithms proven against the screen corpus, then ported to the marvin firmware `gameplay_engine`. | [`tools/gameplay/docs/journal.md`](tools/gameplay/docs/journal.md) |

Not yet in the runtime path; fretboard stays authoritative. | [`firmware/fauxmote/docs/journal.md`](firmware/fauxmote/docs/journal.md) |
