86	## 5. Hardware platforms (high-level)
87	
88	| Component | Role | Where to look |
89	|---|---|---|
90	| SAM9X75 Curiosity | marvin host | [marvin spec §3](firmware/marvin/docs/spec.md) |
91	| Waveshare HDMI→CSI-2 adapter (TC358743) | HDMI bridge into marvin | [marvin spec §3](firmware/marvin/docs/spec.md), [capture pipeline](firmware/marvin/docs/capture_pipeline.md) |
92	| 10.1″ 1280×800 LVDS panel + maxtouch | marvin operator UI surface | [marvin display path](firmware/marvin/docs/display_path.md) |
93	| Sensor/actuator PCB (Sensor-LCD5) | fretboard board: 5 phototransistors + GPIO out | [`hardware/Sensor-LCD5/`](hardware/Sensor-LCD5/) |
94	| PIC32CM6408PL10048 | fretboard MCU | [fretboard spec](firmware/fretboard/SPEC.md) |
95	| LAN8651B1 (10BASE-T1S MAC-PHY) | *planned* fretboard ↔ marvin link over single-pair Ethernet + PoDL | [T1S/PoDL link](docs/t1s-podl-link.md) |
96	| Actuator mechanism (TBD: voice coil / electromagnet / DIY solenoid) | physical fret + strum drive | [`hardware/actuators/`](hardware/actuators/) and [`hardware/3d-models/`](hardware/3d-models/) |
97	| ElectronWarp | component → HDMI converter for Wii | external commercial part |
98	
99	The actuator choice is intentionally still open — `hardware/actuators/` contains design + test-protocol docs for three candidates.
100	
101	## 6. Cross-cutting decisions
102	
103	- **Architecture pivot.** The original PC-hosted / Elgato-USB-capture / PS2 / single-PIC-actuator design is retired. Source documents are preserved at [`docs/archive/`](docs/archive/) for design-rationale reference; they are *not* maintained.
104	- **`frame_epoch` is the master sync token.** A 32-bit counter incremented by marvin's video task on every captured ISC frame. Every detector-state record, emitted command, and recording artifact — including data from off-board observers — keys off this token so multi-source data can be aligned post-hoc. Detail in [marvin spec §4.6](firmware/marvin/docs/spec.md).
105	- **Reference data persists on marvin's SD card.** Detector-state + sparse raw BGR888 keyframes (default 1 keyframe/sec) + raw ADC stream + emitted commands. Off-board detectors record their own data keyed by `frame_epoch` and align offline.
106	- **Centralized timing on marvin, with a fretboard-takeover fallback.** marvin runs the chord-window FIFO and strum scheduler by default; an operator-mode toggle hands timing back to fretboard's standalone `fret_button.c` while marvin still records observations.
107	- **Operating modes are independent toggles**, not a global state machine: `detect_enable`, `marvin_timing_enable`, `actuate_enable`, `record_enable`. Named modes (idle / calibrate / dry-run / play / replay / record) are presets over them.
108	- **Planned: fretboard ↔ marvin link moves to 10BASE-T1S + dumb PoDL.** Replace the FLEXCOM2/SERCOM UART pair with single-pair Ethernet via a LAN8651B1 MAC-PHY on each end. Motivation, in order: PoDL carries power *and* data on one pair to the guitar; better noise/cable tolerance; PLCA multidrop headroom; and demonstrating 10BASE-T1S + PoDL inside a larger Microchip system (SAM9X7 + LAN8651 + PIC32CM). Bandwidth is not a driver — the existing UART has ~12× headroom. PoDL is **dumb** (fixed voltage, no SCCP negotiation) and transparent to both MCUs. No IP stack — the host implements only SPI + the OPEN Alliance TC6 chunk protocol + minimal L2 framing, with the existing frame formats riding unchanged inside the Ethernet payload. Fits comfortably on the PIC32CM (est. ~6–10 KB flash / ~1–2 KB SRAM); marvin is bare-metal so it gets a shared portable `oa_tc6` driver, not a free netdev. Detail in [`docs/t1s-podl-link.md`](docs/t1s-podl-link.md).
109	
110	## 7. Project-wide phasing
111	
112	| Status | Item |
113	|---|---|
114	| ✅ | marvin HDMI capture → DDR (BGR888 packed) at 480p60 and 720p60 |
115	| ✅ | marvin DDR → 10.1″ LVDS panel display (HEO, per-frame swap, pillarboxed/letterboxed) |
116	| ✅ | marvin FreeRTOS scheduler, video task, static task priorities, analytics |
117	| ✅ | fretboard standalone play (phototransistors + open-drain GPIO) |
118	| ✅ | fret-tuner used at the bench for detector tuning |
119	| ✅ | marvin perf-log USB CDC export — live RTOS analytics + pixel strip viewer (`tools/marvin-perf`) |
120	| ✅ | **M1** — marvin reference detector v0 (`cv_marvin_v1` running, `detector_state_t` bus active) |
121	| ✅ | **M2** — fretboard ↔ marvin link (commands flowing; link rewired USB CDC host → FLEXCOM2 UART for the Curiosity Hybrid board, pending on-hardware re-validation) |
122	| ✅ | **M3** — end-to-end play (timing pipeline + fretboard actuation; Expert and Easy tested) |
123	| 🚧 | **M4** — recording-to-SD (detector-state + keyframes + ADC + commands) |
124	| 🚧 | **M5** — operator UI v0; manual-control surface (8 buttons) done; full live-view + mode-toggle UI not started |
125	| 🚧 | **M6**+ — calibration UI, replay, fretboard-takeover validation |
126	| 🚧 | **M9** — game-state observer: Phases 1+2 (screen classifier + section-select/song readers) ported to firmware `gameplay_engine`, MPLAB build confirmed, pending hardware test; Phase 3 (number/score readers) not started |
127	| 🚧 | **M10** — game-state controller: navigator/closed-loop algorithm complete in `tools/gameplay` prototype; firmware port not started |
128	| 🔭 | **T1S link** — re-architect fretboard ↔ marvin onto 10BASE-T1S + dumb PoDL (LAN8651B1 each end). Direction only; not started. [Detail](docs/t1s-podl-link.md) |
129	
130	Detail (definitions of done, demos) in [marvin spec §8](firmware/marvin/docs/spec.md).
131	
132	## 8. What this is *not*
133	
134	To anchor against the original architecture (preserved in `docs/archive/`):
135	
136	- **Not PC-hosted.** marvin is the runtime brain; no host PC is required for play.
137	- **Not USB-capture / Elgato.** Video is captured directly off HDMI via a TC358743 → MIPI CSI-2 path into the SAM9X75's ISC.
138	- **Not PS2.** The supported console is the Nintendo Wii (with an ElectronWarp component → HDMI converter).
139	- **Not a single-MCU actuator.** Sensing and timing live on marvin; fretboard is a sensor/actuator MCU, not a solo controller (with the explicit exception of the standalone-fallback mode).
140	- **Not OpenCV / Python at runtime.** CV runs natively on the SAM9X75 (Cortex-A5). Python (`fret-tuner`) is a bench tool only.

1	# Fretboard Firmware Specification
2	
3	## Overview
4	
5	Firmware for PIC32CM6408PL10048 (Cortex-M0+, 24 MHz) that acts as an
6	**I/O bridge** between a Guitar Hero controller and an off-board host.
7	Five phototransistors above the TV strike line are sampled and streamed
8	out continuously; the host runs detection / chord / strum logic and
9	sends back a single-byte bitmask that drives the controller's button
10	GPIOs directly.
11	
12	In its `MARVIN_DRIVEN` mode the firmware contains **no game logic** — it only
13	scans ADCs, emits frames, and applies received bitmasks. A second build-time
14	mode, **`MODEL_DRIVEN`** (`FRETBOARD_MODE` in `main.c`, the current default),
15	makes the board standalone: an on-device int8 neural net (`model_infer.c`,
16	weights in the generated `model_weights.h`) maps the ADC window to the button
17	bitmask itself, no host required. SW0 toggles it; LED0 shows the state.
18	Inference runs in the main loop; the 240 Hz TC0 ISR only samples and applies.
19	See [`docs/journal.md`](docs/journal.md) and edge-ai
20	[`runtime.md`](../../tools/edge-ai/docs/runtime.md).
21	
22	## Hardware
23	
24	### Target
25	
26	| Spec | Value |
27	|------|-------|
28	| Device | PIC32CM6408PL10048 |
29	| Core | ARM Cortex-M0+ |
30	| Clock | 24 MHz |
31	| Toolchain | XC32 5.10 |
32	| Programmer | PKOB nano |
33	
34	### Pin Map
35	
36	#### Sensor Inputs (ADC)
37	
38	Five phototransistors positioned above the TV strike line. Each
39	produces an analog voltage that drops when a note passes the sensor.
40	ADC reads 12-bit unsigned (0–4095); lower values indicate note
41	presence.
42	
43	| Channel | ADC Input | Pin |
44	|---------|-----------|-----|
45	| Green | AIN28 | PA28 |
46	| Red | AIN16 | PA16 |
47	| Yellow | AIN19 | PA19 |
48	| Blue | AIN27 | PA27 |
49	| Orange | AIN26 | PA26 |
50	
51	#### Button Outputs (Open-Drain GPIO)
52	
53	Each button output is normally tri-stated (input mode). To "press" a
54	button the pin is driven low (clear + output-enable). To "release" it
55	the pin returns to input mode, which floats the line and lets the
56	guitar controller's own pull-up restore the idle state.
57	
58	| Function | Pin | Cmd bit |
59	|----------|-----|---------|
60	| Green fret | PA06 | 0 |
61	| Red fret | PA05 | 1 |
62	| Yellow fret | PA07 | 2 |
63	| Blue fret | PA04 | 3 |
64	| Orange fret | PA01 | 4 |
65	| Strum down | PA03 | 5 |
66	| Strum up | PA00 | 6 |
67	
68	#### UART (SERCOM1)
69	
70	| Function | Pin |
71	|----------|-----|
72	| TX (data stream out) | PB00 |
73	| RX (command in) | PB01 |
74	
75	Baud: **500 000**, 8N1.
76	
77	## Software Architecture
78	
79	### Processing Loop
80	
81	`TC0` is configured to fire a periodic callback at **240 Hz**
82	(≈4.17 ms period). Each tick runs three stages in sequence from the
83	timer ISR:
84	
85	```
86	TC0 callback (240 Hz)
87	    |
88	    v
89	fret_scan_all()          Blocking ADC read of all 5 channels
90	    |
91	    v
92	data_stream_send()       17-byte frame over SERCOM1 TX
93	    |
94	    v
95	cmd_receive_update()     Drains SERCOM1 RX, applies latest bitmask
96	```
97	
98	`main()` is just init + idle loop; all work happens in the TC0 ISR.
99	
100	### Module Descriptions
101	
102	#### fret_scan ([fret_scan.c](fret_scan.c) / [fret_scan.h](fret_scan.h))
103	
104	Reads all five ADC channels sequentially using blocking polling.
105	Results are stored in a static array and accessed via
106	`fret_scan_result(channel)`.
107	
108	The channel enum defines the canonical fret ordering used throughout
109	the firmware:
110	
111	```
112	FRET_GREEN = 0, FRET_RED = 1, FRET_YELLOW = 2, FRET_BLUE = 3, FRET_ORANGE = 4
113	```
114	
115	#### data_stream ([data_stream.c](data_stream.c) / [data_stream.h](data_stream.h))
116	
117	Emits one 17-byte little-endian frame per tick over SERCOM1 TX:
118	
119	| Offset | Size | Field |
120	|-------:|-----:|-------|
121	| 0 | 1 | start = `0x03` |
122	| 1 | 2 | green (uint16) |
123	| 3 | 2 | red |
124	| 5 | 2 | yellow |
125	| 7 | 2 | blue |
126	| 9 | 2 | orange |
127	| 11 | 4 | sample_seq (uint32) — monotonic, one per tick |
128	| 15 | 1 | applied_mask — actuator bitmask driven this scan |
129	| 16 | 1 | end = `0xFC` (`~start`) |
130	
131	`sample_seq` lets the host reconstruct true sample order and detect frames
132	dropped in transit (it advances per tick even when a send is skipped).
133	`applied_mask` is the bitmask `cmd_receive` currently drives, captured in the
134	same tick as the scan so sensor and actuator state are paired at the source
135	(used by edge-ai training-data export). The frame is dropped silently if the
136	TX free-buffer count is below the frame size. At 240 Hz this is 4 080 B/s —
137	well within the 50 000 B/s budget at 500 000 baud.
138	
139	#### cmd_receive ([cmd_receive.c](cmd_receive.c) / [cmd_receive.h](cmd_receive.h))
140	
141	Drains the SERCOM1 RX buffer each tick. The **last byte received** in
142	the tick is interpreted as a button bitmask and applied directly:
143	
144	| Bit | Output |
145	|----:|--------|
146	| 0 | Green fret |
147	| 1 | Red fret |
148	| 2 | Yellow fret |
149	| 3 | Blue fret |
150	| 4 | Orange fret |
151	| 5 | Strum down |
152	| 6 | Strum up |
153	
154	Bit set → drive low (assert). Bit clear → tri-state (release).
155	
156	Note: only the most recent byte each tick is honoured. The host is
157	expected to send commands at a rate ≤ the loop rate; older bytes in
158	the same tick are coalesced away.
159	
160	## Tools
161	
162	### Host-side data-stream monitor
163	
164	[`tools/ds_monitor.py`](tools/ds_monitor.py) opens the serial port,
165	resyncs on `0x03 … 0xFC` framing, and reports actual frame rate, byte
166	rate, framing-error count, and current ADC values once per second.
167	
168	The script declares its dependencies inline (PEP 723) and is run via
169	[`uv`](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) — no manual venv or `pip install`
170	needed:
171	
172	```
173	./tools/ds_monitor.py /dev/tty.usbmodem<...>
174	# or, equivalently:
175	uv run tools/ds_monitor.py /dev/tty.usbmodem<...>
176	```
177	
178	Defaults: `--baud 500000 --expect-hz 240`.
179	
180	## Build System
181	
182	MPLAB Extensions for VS Code. Project config is in
183	`.vscode/fretboard.mplab.json`. Source files are listed in the
184	`fileSets[0].files` array. MCC/Harmony-generated code lives under
185	`fretboard-mcc/` and should not be edited.
186	
187	## File Map
188	
189	| File | Purpose |
190	|------|---------|
191	| [main.c](main.c) | Init + TC0 callback wiring |
192	| [fret_scan.c](fret_scan.c) / [.h](fret_scan.h) | ADC channel scanning |
193	| [data_stream.c](data_stream.c) / [.h](data_stream.h) | UART output frame |
194	| [cmd_receive.c](cmd_receive.c) / [.h](cmd_receive.h) | UART input bitmask |
195	| [tools/ds_monitor.py](tools/ds_monitor.py) | Host-side frame-rate / content check |
196	| `fret_detect.c` / `.h` | **Orphaned** (see [docs/journal.md](docs/journal.md)) |
197	| `fret_button.c` / `.h` | **Orphaned** (see [docs/journal.md](docs/journal.md)) |
198	| `fretboard-mcc/` | MCC Harmony peripheral libraries (generated) |
199

# fauxmote — Specification

> What fauxmote *is* (purpose, hardware, interfaces, success criteria, milestones).
> The running diary of decisions and progress lives in [`docs/journal.md`](docs/journal.md) — read it alongside this on any non-trivial task.

## 1. Purpose

fauxmote is an **ESP32 firmware that emulates a Nintendo Wiimote with an attached
Guitar Hero guitar extension**, speaking Bluetooth straight to a real Wii console.
It is a **parallel proof-of-concept** alternative to the existing actuation path:
today the [fretboard](../fretboard/SPEC.md) MCU physically presses buttons on a
*real* Wii guitar controller via open-drain GPIO. fauxmote instead *becomes* the
controller — eventually driven by [marvin](../marvin/docs/spec.md)'s high-level
fret/strum commands, removing the physical actuator + real controller from the loop.

The fretboard GPIO-press path stays authoritative until fauxmote is proven; nothing
in marvin/fretboard/edge-ai changes as part of this subproject.

## 2. Hardware

| Component | Detail |
|---|---|
| Board | **Adafruit ESP32 Feather V2** (product 5400) — *original* dual-core ESP32 (Tensilica LX6), 8 MB flash, 2 MB PSRAM, USB-C. |
| Radio | ESP32 has a **Bluetooth Classic (BR/EDR)** radio — required, because the Wiimote link is Classic HID. (ESP32-S3/C3 are BLE-only and would *not* work.) |
| Wii console | Real retail Wii; pairing via the sync button or the controller's 1+2 button. |

## 3. The link fauxmote emulates (verified protocol facts)

- **Transport:** Bluetooth Classic **HID** over L2CAP — PSM `0x11` (control),
  PSM `0x13` (data). Input reports (device→host) prefixed `0xa1`; output reports
  (host→device) prefixed `0xa2`.
- **Identity the Wii expects (SDP):** device name `Nintendo RVL-CNT-01`,
  VID `0x057e`, PID `0x0306`, matching Class-of-Device, and the Wiimote HID report
  descriptor.
- **Pairing PIN (legacy):** the PIN is a BD_ADDR in **reverse byte order** (raw 6
  bytes). The 1+2 temporary-pair flow uses the *Wiimote's own* address — which
  fauxmote knows — so fauxmote can answer the GAP PIN request itself.
- **Guitar extension:** identity bytes `00 00 A4 20 01 03` at register offset `0xfa`
  of the `0xa4` extension space. The 6-byte report (frets G/R/Y/B/O, strum up/down,
  whammy in byte 3, touch bar, analog stick, +/− buttons; **byte 0/1 bits 7-6 = 1**

# fauxmote — Working Journal

Running log of planning, decisions, open questions, and work-in-progress for fauxmote. Newest entries at the top. For *what fauxmote is* (purpose, hardware, interfaces, milestones), read [`../SPEC.md`](../SPEC.md) — this journal does not duplicate it.

---

## Current focus

**Phase 1 DONE — the Wii pairs with fauxmote and opens both HID channels.** Custom
Wiimote SDP record (built via Bluedroid's internal `SDP_*` API in `wiimote_sdp.c`,
with SDP buffers raised to 512/1024) + raw `esp_bt_l2cap` servers on PSM 0x11/0x13.
On a red-SYNC press the Wii: accepts our SDP, completes legacy PIN pairing
(`auth OK`), and opens both HID L2CAP channels (control CID 0x40 / interrupt CID 0x41,
both `mtu 640`), then starts sending us data. Wii BD_ADDR `00:17:ab:07:2c:21`.

**Phase 2 DONE — the Wii fully initializes fauxmote as an assigned Wiimote.**
`wiimote.c` answers the Wii's output reports (`0x17` read→`0x21`, `0x15`→`0x20`
status, `0x16` write→`0x22` ack, `0x11` LEDs, `0x12` reporting mode, `0x13`/`0x1a`
IR-enable acks) and streams `0x30` core-button reports (~15 ms) for keep-alive.
On hardware: clean full handshake, the Wii assigns a player slot (`0x11`), and the
GPIO13 status LED (no real player LEDs on a Feather) goes **solid = assigned**
(heartbeat=waiting, fast-blink=connected). IR is acked but not implemented (only
needed for the pointer, not guitar gameplay).

**Core-Wiimote + test-CLI workstream (before guitar).**

- **Step A DONE — manual test CLI + connection management.** `esp_console` REPL
  (`console_cli.c`): `pair`/`stop`/`reconnect`/`unlink`/`status`/`btn`/`tap` — all
  thin pass-throughs over the module API (logic lives in `wiimote.c`/`bt_hid_device.c`,
  so Marvin can drive the same API later). Boots idle; `pair` arms the HID listeners
  for that sync window and `stop` tears them down; servers are **armed per pairing
  window**, not at boot or auto-re-armed (re-arming leaked L2CAP slots, since
  `reconnect` uses client connects). Honors the Wii's requested reporting mode
  (`0x12` → builds that report ID; buttons populated, accel/IR/ext zeroed). Disconnect
  fully resets state (`Wiimote_NotifyDisconnected`) and readers exit by L2CAP handle
  (robust to fd reuse). Bond persists in NVS (recalled at boot via
  `esp_bt_gap_get_bond_device_list`); `unlink` removes it. Status LED on GPIO13:
  blip/~3 s = idle, fast blink = pairing/connecting, N flashes = assigned player N.
- **Step B DONE — IR pointer.** Pointer `(x,y)` is a state variable in `wiimote.c`
  (`Wiimote_SetPointer`/`ClearPointer`), CLI `point x y` / `point off`. `build_ir_extended`

# fretboard — Working Journal

Running log of planning, decisions, open questions, and work-in-progress for the fretboard firmware. Newest entries at the top. For *what fretboard is* (purpose, hardware, modules, frame format), read [`../SPEC.md`](../SPEC.md) — this journal does not duplicate it.

---

## Current focus

**Two build-time modes (`FRETBOARD_MODE` in `main.c`):**

- **`MARVIN_DRIVEN`** (I/O bridge) — 240 Hz TC0 callback: scan five ADCs, emit a 17-byte frame on SERCOM1 TX, drain RX and apply the latest button bitmask. Frame carries `sample_seq` + the applied actuator bitmask (edge-ai training-data sync). Chord/strum logic off-board.
- **`MODEL_DRIVEN`** (new, current default — standalone edge-ai inference) — the on-device int8 model ([`model_infer.c`](../model_infer.c), weights in [`model_weights.h`](../model_weights.h)) reads the ADC window and drives the buttons itself; marvin disconnected. **SW0 (PB03)** toggles model control, **LED0 (PB02)** shows enabled (boots disabled). The 240 Hz TC0 ISR only samples + applies the latest command + streams; `model_infer_run()` runs in the **main loop** (it overruns the tick if put in the ISR — see decision log + edge-ai `runtime.md` §3). Build at `-O2`/`-O3`.

Baud is 500 000. Host checks: [`tools/ds_monitor.py`](../tools/ds_monitor.py) (framing) and [`../../../tools/marvin-perf/fretboard_rate.py`](../../../tools/marvin-perf/fretboard_rate.py) (true tick rate from `sample_seq` + strums/s).

# guitar — Specification

> What guitar *is* (purpose, hardware, interfaces, firmware design, milestones).
> The running diary of decisions and progress lives in [`docs/journal.md`](docs/journal.md) — read it alongside this on any non-trivial task.

> **Status: skeleton + design.** No firmware written yet. This document captures the
> intended design; the actuation/T1S code is the next step (see [`docs/journal.md`](docs/journal.md)).

## 1. Purpose

guitar is the **Wii-guitar actuator node** on the marvin T1S bus. It receives a 1-byte
button bitmask from [marvin](../marvin/docs/spec.md) over 10BASE-T1S and drives a real Wii
guitar controller's buttons via open-drain GPIO. It does **no sensing and no game logic** —
it is purely the actuation half of what today's [fretboard](../fretboard/SPEC.md) firmware
does, lifted onto its own node.

This split lets sensing (detector nodes) and actuation (guitar nodes) live on separate nodes
of one PLCA bus, with marvin selecting the active one of each class (see top-level
[`SPEC.md`](../../SPEC.md) §2 "Node classes"). Multiple guitar variants may coexist on the bus.

The actuation logic is a direct port of fretboard's [`cmd_receive.c`](../fretboard/cmd_receive.c)
(bitmask → open-drain assert / tri-state release) — it has no detector dependencies. fretboard
keeps actuating until this node is proven; marvin flips its command target then.

## 2. Hardware

| Spec | Value |
|------|-------|
| Device | PIC32CM PL10 (same family as fretboard; Cortex-M0+, 24 MHz) |
| Toolchain | XC32 |
| MAC-PHY | LAN8651 (10BASE-T1S), SPI Mode 0, ≤ ~12 MHz on the 24 MHz part |

**To be fixed when the guitar MCC project is generated** (Greg, in MPLAB — same shape as
marvin's FLEXCOM4 setup):

- One SERCOM in **SPI-master mode** (Mode 0: CPOL=0/CPHA=0, MSB first) for the LAN8651, plus
  GPIO for `CS_N` (hardware SS if held across a transaction, else bit-banged), `IRQ_N`
  (external-interrupt pin), and `RST`.
- Seven **open-drain** button-output GPIOs (assert = drive low, release = input/tri-state so the
  controller's pull-up restores idle), bit layout matching the wire command:

  | Bit | Output |
  |----:|--------|
  | 0 | Green fret |
  | 1 | Red fret |
  | 2 | Yellow fret |
  | 3 | Blue fret |
  | 4 | Orange fret |
  | 5 | Strum down |
  | 6 | Strum up |

- A periodic timer (TC) tick to service the bus / apply commands (no 240 Hz ADC scan — that's
  the detector's job).

PoDL on the pair powers the node (transparent to firmware; see [T1S/PoDL link](../../docs/t1s-podl-link.md) §6).

## 3. The T1S link

A **PLCA follower** — the mirror of marvin's coordinator glue, reusing the shared
[`third_party/oa-tc6-lib`](../../third_party/oa-tc6-lib) and the same L2 framing:

- **Node id 2**, MAC `02:00:00:00:00:02` (addressing scheme: [T1S/PoDL link](../../docs/t1s-podl-link.md) §7.1).
- `TC6_Init` + `TC6Regs_Init(enablePlca=true, nodeId=2, nodeCount=8, …)` — follower, **not**
  coordinator.
- Custom ethertype `0x88B5`; marvin's command rides as a 1-byte payload inside the 14-byte
  Ethernet header. The guitar accepts frames addressed to its MAC from the coordinator.
- **Bare-metal** (no FreeRTOS on PL10): the TC6 service loop runs from the main loop / timer
  tick, not a task; `IRQ_N` is wired to a SERCOM-EIC pin (not a PIO controller as on marvin).

The marvin-side reference for all of this is [`firmware/marvin/default/src/net/t1s/t1s_link.c`](../marvin/default/src/net/t1s/t1s_link.c)
(coordinator) — the follower inverts the roles: RX the command, no detector-stream TX.

## 4. Firmware design (to build)

1. **Bring-up:** reset the LAN8651 (`RST` pulse), configure SPI (Mode 0), `TC6_Init` +
   `TC6Regs_Init` as follower id 2. Gate: read chip revision + PLCA *follower* status.
2. **RX path:** TC6 delivers the marvin command frame → validate ethertype `0x88B5` → take the
   1-byte payload as the button bitmask → apply to the 7 GPIOs (port fretboard's
   `cmd_receive_apply_mask` logic).
3. **TX path:** none required initially. Optional `applied_mask` telemetry back to marvin (for
   edge-ai zero-skew labels) is **deferred** with the edge-ai re-homing effort.
4. **Service:** call `TC6_Service` from the main loop / tick, woken by `IRQ_N`.

## 5. What this is *not*

- **Not a sensor.** No phototransistors, no ADC — sensing is the detector node's job.
- **Not an on-device model.** The edge-ai MODEL_DRIVEN inference stays on fretboard for now;
  re-homing it (detector infers → T1S → guitar) is out of scope.
- **Not a game brain.** No chord/strum timing — marvin's timing pipeline owns that and sends
  the resulting bitmask.
- **Not the PLCA coordinator.** marvin (node 0) beacons the cycle; guitar is a follower.

## 6. Milestones

| Status | Item |
|---|---|
| 🔭 | **G0** — guitar MCC project (SPI + `IRQ_N`/`RST` + 7 button GPIOs) generated |
| 🔭 | **G1** — T1S follower bring-up: chipRev + PLCA follower status |
| 🔭 | **G2** — command RX → Wii GPIO actuation (single button on demand) |
| 🔭 | **G3** — end-to-end: marvin (`MARVIN_FRETBOARD_TRANSPORT=1`) drives the guitar node; play with fretboard (detector) + guitar (actuator) both on the bus |

# guitar — Working Journal

Running log of planning, decisions, open questions, and work-in-progress for the guitar (Wii-guitar actuator node) firmware. Newest entries at the top. For *what guitar is* (purpose, hardware, link, firmware design, milestones), read [`../SPEC.md`](../SPEC.md) — this journal does not duplicate it.

---

## Current focus

**Skeleton + design only — no firmware written yet.** guitar is a new subproject created when the
marvin↔node T1S link split sensing from actuation into separate node classes. It is the **Wii-guitar
actuator node**: a PIC32CM PL10 T1S PLCA *follower* (node id 2) that receives marvin's 1-byte button
bitmask and drives a Wii guitar controller via open-drain GPIO — the actuation half of today's
[fretboard](../../fretboard/SPEC.md) firmware, on its own node.

Next step (G0/G1): Greg generates the guitar MCC project (a SERCOM in SPI-master mode + `IRQ_N`/`RST`
GPIO for the LAN8651, and the 7 button GPIOs), then the T1S-follower glue lands — the mirror of marvin's
coordinator glue in [`firmware/marvin/default/src/net/t1s/t1s_link.c`](../../marvin/default/src/net/t1s/t1s_link.c),
reusing [`third_party/oa-tc6-lib`](../../../third_party/oa-tc6-lib) and the shared L2 framing.

---

## Decision log

| Date | Decision | Rationale |
|------|----------|-----------|
| 2026-06-16 | **Wii-guitar actuation becomes its own subproject (`guitar`), split out of fretboard.** PIC32CM PL10, T1S PLCA **follower** node id 2 (MAC `02:00:00:00:00:02`), receives a 1-byte bitmask over ethertype `0x88B5` and drives 7 open-drain Wii-guitar GPIOs. Sensing stays on `fretboard` (detector node). Actuation logic is a verbatim port of fretboard's `cmd_receive.c`. The link reuses `oa-tc6-lib` + the shared L2 framing as the mirror of marvin's coordinator glue. **Bare-metal** (no FreeRTOS on PL10): TC6 serviced from the main loop / tick; `IRQ_N` on a SERCOM-EIC pin. | The T1S bus was built for multiple node classes; separating detector from actuator lets multiple guitar/detector variants coexist on one PLCA pair with marvin selecting the active of each. Same MCU family as fretboard keeps the "OA SPI driver scales across the family" demo and minimizes bring-up. Greg spins up a *fresh* guitar MCC project (not a fork of fretboard). |
| 2026-06-16 | **Edge-ai / on-device model is out of scope; fretboard keeps actuating until guitar is proven.** This subproject covers only the marvin-driven actuation path. fretboard's MODEL_DRIVEN/standalone modes stay untouched; re-homing the model (detector infers → T1S → guitar) and the `applied_mask` training-label coupling are deferred. marvin flips its command target from the fretboard node to the guitar node only once G3 passes. | Contains the blast radius — the playing system stays up throughout, mirroring the UART/T1S parallel-coexistence approach. |

---

## Open questions

- **Guitar MCC pinout** — which SERCOM for the LAN8651 SPI, the `IRQ_N`/`RST` pins, and the 7 button GPIOs on the PL10 board. Settle when the MCC project is generated (G0).
- **CS handling** — whether the chosen SERCOM holds SS low across a full TC6 chunk (like marvin's FLEXCOM CSAAT) or `CS_N` must be bit-banged as GPIO. Confirm at G1 bring-up.
- **Active-guitar selection on marvin** — how marvin picks which guitar node is active (mirror of `Detector_SetActive`); designed on the marvin side, tracked there.

---

## Session log

### 2026-06-16 — Subproject created (skeleton + design)

- Created `firmware/guitar/` (SPEC.md, this journal, README) as part of the T1S node-class restructuring. Recorded the actuator-node design: PIC32CM PL10, PLCA follower id 2, command RX → Wii GPIO (port of fretboard `cmd_receive.c`), reusing `oa-tc6-lib` + the shared L2 framing.
- Registered in top-level [`SPEC.md`](../../SPEC.md) (§2 node classes, §3 registry, §4 map, §5 hardware) and [`CLAUDE.md`](../../CLAUDE.md); node id 2 / MAC `02:..:02` added to [`docs/t1s-podl-link.md`](../../docs/t1s-podl-link.md) §7.1.
- **No firmware code yet.** Next: G0 (MCC project) then G1 (follower bring-up).

# guitar

Wii-guitar **actuator node** for the Guitar Hero bot's T1S bus. A PIC32CM PL10
(10BASE-T1S PLCA follower) that receives a 1-byte button bitmask from
[marvin](../marvin/) and drives a real Wii guitar controller via open-drain GPIO.

It is the actuation half of the original [fretboard](../fretboard/) firmware, split
onto its own node so sensing (detector nodes) and actuation (guitar nodes) are
separate node classes on one PLCA bus.

- **What it is / firmware design:** [`SPEC.md`](SPEC.md)
- **Decisions + progress:** [`docs/journal.md`](docs/journal.md)
- **System context:** top-level [`SPEC.md`](../../SPEC.md), [`docs/t1s-podl-link.md`](../../docs/t1s-podl-link.md)

Status: skeleton + design — firmware not yet built.

Moving `model_infer_run()` to the main loop and having the ISR only sample + apply a `volatile uint8_t` latest-command restored clean 240/240 Hz. 23	| 2026-06-03 | Data-stream frame grows 12→17 bytes: `0x03 \| g r y b o (5×u16 LE) \| sample_seq (u32 LE) \| applied_mask (u8) \| 0xFC`. `sample_seq` is a monotonic counter incremented once per tick in `data_stream_send` (before the TX-buffer check, so a dropped send shows as a gap); `applied_mask` comes from a new `cmd_receive_current_mask()` getter. Resolves open-questions #3 and #4. | Closes the edge-ai data-sync hole (edge-ai journal 2026-06-03). The seq counter lets the host reconstruct true 240 Hz ordering and detect dropped frames. Callback order is scan→send→receive, so `current_mask` at send time is exactly the state driven *during* this scan. === SERCOM0 SPI Initialize (mode/CS/baud) ===
    void SERCOM0_SPI_Initialize(void);

  Summary:
    Initializes instance SERCOM0 of the SERCOM module operating in SPI mode.

  Description:
    This function initializes instance SERCOM0 of SERCOM module operating in SPI mode.
    This function should be called before any other library function. The SERCOM
    module will be configured as per the MHC settings.

  Remarks:
    Refer plib_sercom0_spi.h file for more information.
*/

void SERCOM0_SPI_Initialize(void)
{
    /* Instantiate the SERCOM0 SPI object */
    sercom0SPIObj.callback = NULL ;
    sercom0SPIObj.transferIsBusy = false ;
    sercom0SPIObj.txSize = 0U;
    sercom0SPIObj.rxSize = 0U;

    /* Selection of the Character Size and Receiver Enable */
    SERCOM0_REGS->SPI.SERCOM_CTRLB = SERCOM_SPI_CTRLB_CHSIZE_8_BIT | SERCOM_SPI_CTRLB_RXEN_Msk ;

    /* Wait for synchronization */
    while((SERCOM0_REGS->SPI.SERCOM_SYNCBUSY) != 0U)
    {
        /* Do nothing */
    }

    /* Selection of the Baud Value */
    SERCOM0_REGS->SPI.SERCOM_BAUD = (uint8_t)SERCOM_SPI_BAUD_BAUD(SERCOM0_SPIM_BAUD_VALUE);

    /* Configure Data Out Pin Out , Master Mode,
     * Data In and Pin Out,Data Order and Standby mode if configured
     * and Selection of the Clock Phase and Polarity and Enable the SPI Module
     */
    SERCOM0_REGS->SPI.SERCOM_CTRLA = SERCOM_SPI_CTRLA_MODE_SPI_MASTER | SERCOM_SPI_CTRLA_DOPO_MUX0 | SERCOM_SPI_CTRLA_DIPO_MUX3 | SERCOM_SPI_CTRLA_CPOL_IDLE_LOW | SERCOM_SPI_CTRLA_CPHA_LEADING_EDGE | SERCOM_SPI_CTRLA_DORD_MSB | SERCOM_SPI_CTRLA_ENABLE_Msk ;

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-16 23:44:51Z)**_

Reviewed. The SPI side is solid; two gaps to fix in MCC before the firmware can work, plus a couple of notes.

## ✅ Correct and ready

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| Device | PIC32CM6408PL10048 (same as fretboard) ✓ |
| **SERCOM0 SPI = Mode 0** | `plib_sercom0_spi_master.c`: `CPOL_IDLE_LOW \| CPHA_LEADING_EDGE \| DORD_MSB`, 8-bit, master — correct for the LAN8651 ✓ |
| SPI pins | MOSI=PA04 (PAD0), SCK=PA05 (PAD1), MISO=PA07 (PAD3); `DOPO_MUX0`/`DIPO_MUX3` match ✓ |
| SPI API | `WriteRead`/`Write`/`Read`, `TransferSetup`, `CallbackRegister`, `IsBusy` — interrupt-driven, same shape as marvin's ✓ |
| **CS = GPIO** | `T1S_CS` = PA13 (output, idle high), *not* hardware SS. This is the right choice — the glue drives CS low across the whole TC6 chunk, cleanly resolving the "CS held across a multi-byte transaction" concern ✓ |
| RST | `T1S_RST` = PA14 (output, idle high) ✓ |
| IRQ_N pin | `T1S_IRQ_N` = PA15 muxed to `EIC_EXTINT15`; `NVIC_EnableIRQ(EIC_IRQn)` present ✓ |

## ❌ Gap 1 — the EIC peripheral isn't actually configured

The pin is muxed to `EIC_EXTINT15` and NVIC enables `EIC_IRQn`, but **there is no EIC driver**: no `peripheral/eic/`, no `EIC_Initialize()` (init calls only PORT/CLOCK/SERCOM1/EVSYS/SERCOM0/NVIC), and `EIC_Handler` resolves to the weak dummy. So `IRQ_N` won't generate a usable interrupt — the EIC channel's sense (edge), enable, and callback are all missing. This is the exact analog of marvin's "PIO Interrupt = Disabled" first pass.

**Fix in MCC:** add the **EIC component**, configure **EXTINT15 = Falling Edge** (with the IRQ_N pull-up note below), enable its interrupt, and regenerate. That gives `EIC_Initialize`, a real `EIC_Handler`, and an `EIC_CallbackRegister` for the glue to hook `IRQ_N → service`.

## ❌ Gap 2 — the 7 Wii-guitar button output GPIOs are missing

`pin_configurations.csv` has the board-template **LED0–5 / SW1–3** but **none of the actuation outputs** (Green/Red/Yellow/Blue/Orange/Strum-down/Strum-up) — which are the entire point of this node. Note the old fretboard button pins (PA05/PA07/PA04) are now the SPI bus, so they need new homes. Plenty are free (PA06, PB04/05, PA10, PA16–20, PA23, PA24/25, PA27–31, PA00–03).

**Fix in MCC:** assign **7 GPIOs** named for the buttons. Like fretboard, they're *software* open-drain — the actuation logic drives low to assert and switches to input to release — so plain GPIO (the `cmd_receive` logic toggles direction via the `*_Set/Clear/OutputEnable/InputEnable` macros). Bit order must match the wire command: bit0 Green … bit4 Orange, bit5 strum-down, bit6 strum-up.

## Notes (no action required)

- **SERCOM1 USART** (`CDC_TX`=PB00 / `CDC_RX`=PB01) — I read this as a **debug/log console** (no UART link to marvin anymore; that's T1S). Good to have for bring-up. Confirm that's the intent.
- **IRQ_N pull-up**: PA15 has no pull configured. With falling-edge + the RCA backstop this is low-risk (same as marvin), but enabling the internal pull-up is cheap insurance against a float during reset — optional.
- **SPI clock**: I'll set/verify the target (~8–12 MHz, ≤ the part's GCLK/2) via `TransferSetup` in the glue; the MCC default baud doesn't matter.
- **LED0–5/SW1–3** are dev-board defaults — fine to leave; we could later use one LED as a link-status indicator.

## Bottom line

Add the **EIC (EXTINT15, falling edge)** and the **7 button GPIOs** in MCC and regenerate — then the hardware layer is complete and I can write the follower glue (mirror of marvin's `t1s_link.c` with `nodeId=2`, GPIO-CS driven around each transfer, `IRQ_N`→service via the EIC callback, RX command → `cmd_receive`-style GPIO). Want me to also note these two gaps in the guitar journal so they're tracked?

=== EIC_Initialize body ===
void EIC_Initialize (void)
{
    /* Reset all registers in the EIC module to their initial state and
       EIC will be disabled. */
    EIC_REGS->EIC_CTRLA |= EIC_CTRLA_SWRST_Msk;

    while((EIC_REGS->EIC_SYNCBUSY & EIC_SYNCBUSY_SWRST_Msk) == EIC_SYNCBUSY_SWRST_Msk)
    {
        /* Wait for sync */
    }

    /* EIC is by default clocked by GCLK */

    /* NMI Control register */

    /* Interrupt sense type and filter control for EXTINT channels 0 to 7*/
    EIC_REGS->EIC_CONFIG0 =  EIC_CONFIG0_SENSE0_NONE  |
                              EIC_CONFIG0_SENSE1_NONE  |
                              EIC_CONFIG0_SENSE2_NONE  |
                              EIC_CONFIG0_SENSE3_NONE  |
                              EIC_CONFIG0_SENSE4_NONE  |
                              EIC_CONFIG0_SENSE5_NONE  |
                              EIC_CONFIG0_SENSE6_NONE  |
                              EIC_CONFIG0_SENSE7_NONE ;

    /* Interrupt sense type and filter control for EXTINT channels 8 to 15 */
    EIC_REGS->EIC_CONFIG1 =  EIC_CONFIG1_SENSE8_NONE  |
                              EIC_CONFIG1_SENSE9_NONE  |
                              EIC_CONFIG1_SENSE10_NONE  |
                              EIC_CONFIG1_SENSE11_NONE  |
                              EIC_CONFIG1_SENSE12_NONE  |
                              EIC_CONFIG1_SENSE13_NONE  |
                              EIC_CONFIG1_SENSE14_NONE  |
                              EIC_CONFIG1_SENSE15_FALL ;





    /* External Interrupt enable*/
    EIC_REGS->EIC_INTENSET = 0x8000;

    /* Callbacks for enabled interrupts */
    eicCallbackObject[0].eicPinNo = EIC_PIN_MAX;
    eicCallbackObject[1].eicPinNo = EIC_PIN_MAX;
    eicCallbackObject[2].eicPinNo = EIC_PIN_MAX;
    eicCallbackObject[3].eicPinNo = EIC_PIN_MAX;
    eicCallbackObject[4].eicPinNo = EIC_PIN_MAX;
    eicCallbackObject[5].eicPinNo = EIC_PIN_MAX;
    eicCallbackObject[6].eicPinNo = EIC_PIN_MAX;
    eicCallbackObject[7].eicPinNo = EIC_PIN_MAX;
    eicCallbackObject[8].eicPinNo = EIC_PIN_MAX;
    eicCallbackObject[9].eicPinNo = EIC_PIN_MAX;
    eicCallbackObject[10].eicPinNo = EIC_PIN_MAX;
    eicCallbackObject[11].eicPinNo = EIC_PIN_MAX;
    eicCallbackObject[12].eicPinNo = EIC_PIN_MAX;
    eicCallbackObject[13].eicPinNo = EIC_PIN_MAX;
    eicCallbackObject[14].eicPinNo = EIC_PIN_MAX;
    eicCallbackObject[15].eicPinNo = EIC_PIN_15;
    /* Enable the EIC */
    EIC_REGS->EIC_CTRLA |= EIC_CTRLA_ENABLE_Msk;

    while((EIC_REGS->EIC_SYNCBUSY & EIC_SYNCBUSY_ENABLE_Msk) == EIC_SYNCBUSY_ENABLE_Msk)
    {
        /* Wait for sync */
    }
}

**EIC (IRQ_N) ✓**

- `EIC_INTENSET = 0x8000` — channel 15 enabled; `EIC_PIN_15` callback slot wired
- `EIC_Initialize()` called; `EIC_CallbackRegister(EIC_PIN_15, …)` + `EIC_InterruptEnable` API present. Glue hooks `IRQ_N → service` cleanly.

**7 Wii button GPIOs ✓** — all present with `Set/Clear/OutputEnable/InputEnable/Get`, which is exactly the software open-drain set (assert = `Clear`+`OutputEnable` → drive low; release = `InputEnable` → tri-state):

| Cmd bit | Name | Pin |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | FRET_GREEN | PA22 |
| 1 | FRET_RED | PA21 |
| 2 | FRET_YELLOW | PA08 |
| 3 | FRET_BLUE | PA09 |
| 4 | FRET_ORANGE | PB02 |
| 5 | STRUM_DOWN | PA18 |
| 6 | STRUM_UP | PB03 |

**Everything else still good** — SPI SERCOM0 Mode 0 (8-bit, MSB), `T1S_CS`/`T1S_RST` GPIO (idle high), `T1S_IRQ_N_Get()` available for level reads alongside the EIC interrupt.

## Two firmware-side notes (not MCC gaps — I'll handle them in the glue)

1. **Buttons boot asserted.** MCC sets the 7 button pins to `Direction=Out, Latch=Low`, so between `PORT_Initialize` and our actuator init they're *driving low = all buttons pressed*. The glue's first act must release all 7 (`*_InputEnable()`). (Keeping `OUT=Low` is actually correct for the open-drain scheme — we only ever drive low or tri-state, never high. If you'd rather they boot released at the hardware level, set their initial Direction to `In` in MCC, but it's not necessary — the firmware releases them immediately.)

2. **Millisecond tick.** `TC6Regs_CheckTimers`/`GetTicksMs` need a 1 ms time source, and there's no TC/SysTick in the init list. No MCC change needed — I'll configure the Cortex-M0+ **SysTick** directly in the firmware (1 ms) for the bare-metal service loop.

## Green light

The guitar MCC config has everything the follower firmware needs. I can now write the glue: a bare-metal mirror of marvin's `t1s_link.c` — reset pulse on `T1S_RST`, SERCOM0 SPI at ~8–12 MHz, `T1S_CS` driven low around each TC6 transfer, `IRQ_N`→service via the EIC callback, `TC6_Init` + `TC6Regs_Init(nodeId=2, follower)`, then RX command → release/assert the 7 button GPIOs (port of fretboard's `cmd_receive` mask logic), SysTick for timers, serviced from `main()`.

## Next session (G1/G2 — guitar firmware)

The hardware layer is ready; the remaining work is the bare-metal follower firmware — the mirror of marvin's `t1s_link.c`:
- reset pulse → SERCOM0 SPI → `TC6_Init` + `TC6Regs_Init(nodeId=2, follower)`, gate on chipRev + PLCA follower status
- `IRQ_N`→service via the EIC callback; **SysTick at 1 ms** for the TC6 timers; serviced from `main()`

    "main" function calls the "SYS_Initialize" function to initialize the state
    machines of all modules in the system
 *******************************************************************************/

// *****************************************************************************
// *****************************************************************************
// Section: Included Files
// *****************************************************************************
// *****************************************************************************

#include <stddef.h>                     // Defines NULL
#include <stdbool.h>                    // Defines true
#include <stdlib.h>                     // Defines EXIT_FAILURE
#include "definitions.h"                // SYS function prototypes


// *****************************************************************************
// *****************************************************************************
// Section: Main Entry Point
// *****************************************************************************
// *****************************************************************************

int main ( void )
{
    /* Initialize all modules */
    SYS_Initialize ( NULL );

    while ( true )
    {
        /* Maintain state machines of all polled MPLAB Harmony modules. */
        SYS_Tasks ( );
    }

    /* Execution should not come here during normal operation */

    return ( EXIT_FAILURE );
}

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-17 00:41:13Z)**_

Good question to settle before I write the firmware — it changes the scope. Short answer: **yes, with one easy tuning lever.** Let me give you the real numbers.

The PL10 budget is **64 KB flash / 8 KB SRAM**. The thing that dominates SRAM isn't the CLI — it's the TC6 chunk buffers, and they're oversized for this node by default:

- `TC6_CHUNKS_XACT = 31` × 68 B ≈ **2 KB per SPI buffer** (the marvin/default value, sized for bursty Ethernet). The guitar only ever moves a **single 15-byte command frame**, so dropping this to ~4 chunks reclaims most of that.
- My planned `s_rx_buf[1518]` copied marvin's MTU-sized buffer — the guitar needs maybe **64 B**. Another ~1.4 KB back.

With those two (which we'd want regardless), the picture is:

| | Flash | SRAM |
|---|---|---|
| TC6 lib + glue (tuned: CHUNKS_XACT≈4, rx_buf 64 B) | ~8–10 KB | ~1 KB |
| MCC peripheral libs + runtime | ~10–12 KB | ~1.5 KB (stack) |
| **embedded-cli (status + manual btn/tap)** | **~4 KB** | **~0.5–0.7 KB** |
| **Total** | **~24–28 KB / 64 KB** | **~3.5–4 KB / 8 KB** |

So a CLI fits comfortably — roughly half of each budget free.

**And it's genuinely worth having here**, specifically for bring-up: a `btn <mask>` / `tap` command lets you actuate the 7 Wii-guitar GPIOs **locally, before T1S works**, to verify the controller wiring (G2) independently of the link. Plus a `status` command (link up?, chipRev, PLCA follower status, last RX command, RX count) is the natural feedback channel now that the LEDs became buttons — it'd ride the SERCOM1 debug UART you already configured.

The `embedded-cli` is vendored in marvin (`firmware/marvin/default/src/third_party/embedded-cli/`, MIT, static-allocation mode); I'd reuse it the same way. Bare-metal integration is simpler than marvin's — just poll SERCOM1 RX in the main loop and feed the parser (no task).

My recommendation: **include a minimal CLI** (`status`, `btn`, `tap`) in the guitar firmware. Want me to fold it into this firmware drop, or build the bare T1S-follower first and add the CLI as a follow-up?

 * (third_party/oa-tc6-lib) on the guitar node. The library #includes
 * "tc6-conf.h" from the include path; this is the guitar's copy.
 *
 * Tuned smaller than the library defaults for the PIC32CM PL10 (8 KB SRAM):
 * this node only exchanges a single ~60-byte command frame, so the SPI burst

#ifdef __cplusplus

#define TC6_HEADER_SIZE         (4u)

#define TC6_CHUNK_BUF_SIZE      (TC6_CHUNK_SIZE + TC6_HEADER_SIZE)

#define REG_OP_ARRAY_SIZE       (4u)

#define TC6_CHUNKS_XACT         (4u)
#define TC6_CONCAT_THRESHOLD    (1024u)

#define TC6_MAX_CNTRL_VARS      (1u)

#ifdef __cplusplus
}

#endif /* TC6_CONFIG_H_ */

/* 10BASE-T1S follower for the guitar node (LAN8651 MAC-PHY on SERCOM0 SPI).
 *
 * marvin is the PLCA coordinator (node 0); this node is follower id 2. It
 * receives marvin's 1-byte button bitmask (ethertype 0x88B5) over T1S and
 * drives the 7 Wii-guitar GPIOs. Transport is the vendored OPEN Alliance TC6
 * driver (third_party/oa-tc6-lib) wrapped with the SERCOM0 SPI PLib, a
 * GPIO chip-select held across each transfer, the T1S_RST / T1S_IRQ_N pins
 * (EIC EXTINT15), and a SysTick-based millisecond clock. Bare-metal: the
 * protocol is serviced from the main loop, woken by IRQ_N. See
 * firmware/guitar/SPEC.md and docs/t1s-podl-link.md.
 *
 * Call T1SFollower_Initialize() once after SYS_Initialize (SERCOM0_SPI/EIC
 * brought up by MCC), then T1SFollower_Tasks() repeatedly from the main loop. */

void T1SFollower_Initialize(void);
void T1SFollower_Tasks(void);

/* True once the MAC-PHY is configured and the data path is enabled. */
bool T1SFollower_IsConnected(void);

#endif /* T1S_FOLLOWER_H */

#include "t1s_follower.h"

#include <stdint.h>
#include <stdbool.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <stdio.h>

#include "definitions.h"   /* SERCOM0_SPI_*, SERCOM1_USART_*, EIC_*, PORT macros, CMSIS */

#include "tc6.h"
#include "tc6-regs.h"

/* PLCA follower identity (docs/t1s-podl-link.md §7.1). */
#define T1S_NODE_ID         (2u)
#define T1S_NODE_COUNT      (8u)     /* PLCA cycle length (must match the coordinator) */
#define T1S_INSTANCE        (0u)

#define T1S_ETHERTYPE       (0x88B5u)
#define T1S_ETH_HDR_LEN     (14u)
#define T1S_CMD_BIT_MASK    (0x7Fu)  /* 5 frets + 2 strum */

/* Coordinator-assigned MAC for this node: 02:00:00:00:00:02. */
static uint8_t s_mac[6] = { 0x02u, 0x00u, 0x00u, 0x00u, 0x00u, (uint8_t)T1S_NODE_ID };

static TC6_t            *s_tc6;
static volatile bool     s_need_service;
static volatile bool     s_link_up;
static volatile bool     s_spi_busy;

/* Command frames are ~60 B after min-frame padding; this only needs the header
 * plus the first payload byte, but size for a padded frame. */
static uint8_t           s_rx_buf[64];

/* SysTick millisecond clock for the TC6 timers. */
static volatile uint32_t s_ms;

void SysTick_Handler(void)
{
    s_ms++;
}

static void delay_ms(uint32_t ms)
{
    uint32_t t0 = s_ms;
    while ((s_ms - t0) < ms) { /* wait */ }
}

static void log_str(const char *s)
{
    (void)SERCOM1_USART_Write((uint8_t *)s, strlen(s));
}

/*>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>  Wii-guitar actuation  >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>*/

/* Software open-drain: assert = drive low (Clear + OutputEnable), release =
 * tri-state (InputEnable, controller pull-up restores idle). */
#define BTN_APPLY(mask, bit, NAME)                          \
    do {                                                    \
        if ((mask) & (1u << (bit))) {                       \
            NAME##_Clear();                                 \
            NAME##_OutputEnable();                          \
        } else {                                            \
            NAME##_InputEnable();                           \
        }                                                   \
    } while (0)

static void buttons_release_all(void)
{
    FRET_GREEN_InputEnable();
    FRET_RED_InputEnable();
    FRET_YELLOW_InputEnable();
    FRET_BLUE_InputEnable();
    FRET_ORANGE_InputEnable();
    STRUM_DOWN_InputEnable();
    STRUM_UP_InputEnable();
}

static void buttons_apply_mask(uint8_t mask)
{
    BTN_APPLY(mask, 0u, FRET_GREEN);
    BTN_APPLY(mask, 1u, FRET_RED);
    BTN_APPLY(mask, 2u, FRET_YELLOW);
    BTN_APPLY(mask, 3u, FRET_BLUE);
    BTN_APPLY(mask, 4u, FRET_ORANGE);
    BTN_APPLY(mask, 5u, STRUM_DOWN);
    BTN_APPLY(mask, 6u, STRUM_UP);
}

/*>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>  SPI + IRQ  >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>*/

/* SERCOM0 SPI completion ISR: the chunk transfer is done — deassert the GPIO
 * chip-select, hand the buffer back to the driver, and flag for servicing. */
static void spi_done_cb(uintptr_t context)
{
    (void)context;
    T1S_CS_Set();            /* CS high — end of transaction */
    s_spi_busy = false;
    s_need_service = true;
    TC6_SpiBufferDone(T1S_INSTANCE, true);
}

/* T1S_IRQ_N falling-edge (EIC EXTINT15): the MAC-PHY needs servicing. */
static void irq_cb(uintptr_t context)
{
    (void)context;
    s_need_service = true;
}

/* Run the protocol stack until it has no immediately pending work. IRQ_N is
 * active-low; TC6_Service treats a false interruptLevel as "interrupt active". */
static void service_pump(void)
{
    do {
        s_need_service = false;
        bool no_int = (T1S_IRQ_N_Get() != 0u);
        (void)TC6_Service(s_tc6, no_int);
    } while (s_need_service);
    TC6Regs_CheckTimers();
}

/*>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>  Public API  >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>*/

void T1SFollower_Initialize(void)
{
    (void)SysTick_Config(CPU_CLOCK_FREQUENCY / 1000u);  /* 1 ms tick */

    buttons_release_all();   /* pins boot Out/Low (asserted) — release first */

    /* Hardware reset pulse (T1S_RST active-low, idle high). */
    T1S_CS_Set();
    T1S_RST_Clear();
    delay_ms(10u);
    T1S_RST_Set();
    delay_ms(10u);

    SERCOM0_SPI_CallbackRegister(spi_done_cb, 0u);  /* Mode 0 set by MCC init */

    s_tc6 = TC6_Init(NULL);
    if (s_tc6 == NULL) {
        log_str("guitar: TC6_Init failed\r\n");
        return;
    }

    EIC_CallbackRegister(EIC_PIN_15, irq_cb, 0u);   /* EXTINT15 enabled in EIC_Initialize */

    /* Configure the LAN8651 + PLCA as follower id 2. Not promiscuous — the
     * MAC-PHY filters to this node's MAC + broadcast. */
    while (!TC6Regs_Init(s_tc6, NULL, s_mac, true, T1S_NODE_ID, T1S_NODE_COUNT,
                         0u, 0u, false, false, false)) {
        log_str("guitar: TC6Regs_Init busy, retry\r\n");
        delay_ms(50u);
    }

    uint32_t deadline = s_ms + 3000u;
    while (!TC6Regs_GetInitDone(s_tc6) && ((int32_t)(deadline - s_ms) > 0)) {
        service_pump();
    }

    if (TC6Regs_GetInitDone(s_tc6)) {
        s_link_up = true;
        TC6_EnableData(s_tc6, true);
        char buf[80];
        (void)snprintf(buf, sizeof(buf),
                       "guitar: LAN8651 up - chipRev=%u, MAC=02:00:00:00:00:%02X, "
                       "PLCA follower id=%u/%u\r\n",
                       (unsigned)TC6Regs_GetChipRevision(s_tc6),
                       (unsigned)T1S_NODE_ID, (unsigned)T1S_NODE_ID,
                       (unsigned)T1S_NODE_COUNT);
        log_str(buf);
    } else {
        log_str("guitar: MAC-PHY not responding (check EVB/wiring); still servicing\r\n");
    }
}

void T1SFollower_Tasks(void)
{
    if (s_tc6 == NULL) {
        return;
    }
    service_pump();
    if (!s_link_up && TC6Regs_GetInitDone(s_tc6)) {
        s_link_up = true;
        TC6_EnableData(s_tc6, true);
        log_str("guitar: LAN8651 up (late)\r\n");
    }
}

bool T1SFollower_IsConnected(void)
{
    return s_link_up;
}

/*>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>  TC6 driver callbacks (integrator)  >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>*/

bool TC6_CB_OnSpiTransaction(uint8_t tc6instance, uint8_t *pTx, uint8_t *pRx,
                             uint16_t len, void *pGlobalTag)
{
    (void)tc6instance;
    (void)pGlobalTag;
    if (s_spi_busy) {
        return false;
    }
    s_spi_busy = true;
    T1S_CS_Clear();          /* CS low — start of transaction (held across the chunk) */
    if (!SERCOM0_SPI_WriteRead(pTx, len, pRx, len)) {
        T1S_CS_Set();
        s_spi_busy = false;
        return false;
    }
    return true;
}

void TC6_CB_OnNeedService(TC6_t *pInst, void *pGlobalTag)
{
    (void)pInst;
    (void)pGlobalTag;
    s_need_service = true;
}

void TC6_CB_OnRxEthernetSlice(TC6_t *pInst, const uint8_t *pRx, uint16_t offset,
                              uint16_t len, void *pGlobalTag)
{
    (void)pInst;
    (void)pGlobalTag;
    if (((uint32_t)offset + len) <= sizeof(s_rx_buf)) {
        memcpy(&s_rx_buf[offset], pRx, len);
    }
}

void TC6_CB_OnRxEthernetPacket(TC6_t *pInst, bool success, uint16_t len,
                               uint64_t *rxTimestamp, void *pGlobalTag)
{
    (void)pInst;
    (void)rxTimestamp;
    (void)pGlobalTag;

    if (!success || (len < (T1S_ETH_HDR_LEN + 1u))) {
        return;
    }
    uint16_t ethertype = (uint16_t)((s_rx_buf[12] << 8) | s_rx_buf[13]);
    if (ethertype != T1S_ETHERTYPE) {
        return;
    }
    /* Command byte is the first payload octet; trailing min-frame padding is
     * ignored. Apply directly (latest-wins). */
    buttons_apply_mask((uint8_t)(s_rx_buf[T1S_ETH_HDR_LEN] & T1S_CMD_BIT_MASK));
}

void TC6_CB_OnError(TC6_t *pInst, TC6_Error_t err, void *pGlobalTag)
{
    (void)pGlobalTag;
    log_str("guitar: t1s error: ");
    log_str(TC6_GetErrorStr(err));
    log_str("\r\n");
    switch (err) {
        case TC6Error_NoHardware:
        case TC6Error_BadChecksum:
        case TC6Error_UnexpectedCtrl:
        case TC6Error_BadTxData:
        case TC6Error_SyncLost:
        case TC6Error_SpiError:
            TC6Regs_Reinit(pInst);
            break;
        default:
            break;
    }
}

/*>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>  TC6Regs callbacks (integrator)  >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>*/

uint32_t TC6Regs_CB_GetTicksMs(void)
{
    return s_ms;
}

void TC6Regs_CB_OnEvent(TC6_t *pInst, TC6Regs_Event_t event, void *pTag)
{
    (void)pTag;
    log_str("guitar: t1s event: ");
    log_str(TC6Regs_GetEventStr(event));
    log_str("\r\n");
    switch (event) {
        case TC6Regs_Event_Loss_of_Framing_Error:
        case TC6Regs_Event_RX_Non_Recoverable_Error:
        case TC6Regs_Event_TX_Non_Recoverable_Error:
            TC6Regs_Reinit(pInst);
            break;
        default:
            break;
    }
}

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-17 01:08:11Z)**_

Yes — but by *our* firmware, not by MCC. MCC didn't configure SysTick (it's not in `SYS_Initialize` — there's no SYS_TIME component), so `t1s_follower.c` sets it up itself.

It's enabled on the **first line of `T1SFollower_Initialize()`**:

```c
(void)SysTick_Config(CPU_CLOCK_FREQUENCY / 1000u);  /* 1 ms tick */
```

`SysTick_Config` (CMSIS) loads the reload (24000000/1000 = 24000), clears the counter, sets the exception priority, and enables it with **`CLKSOURCE | TICKINT | ENABLE`** — i.e. processor-clock-sourced, interrupt on, running. Our strong `SysTick_Handler` increments `s_ms`, which feeds `delay_ms()` and `TC6Regs_CB_GetTicksMs()`.

Two things that make it actually tick, both satisfied:
- **Ordering** — `SysTick_Config` runs *before* the first `delay_ms()` (the `T1S_RST` reset pulse), so the reset delay is real.
- **Global interrupts** — enabled by default coming out of reset / `SYS_Initialize` on the Cortex-M0+ (nothing masks PRIMASK), and SysTick is a core exception (not gated by the NVIC), so the handler fires.

So nothing more is needed in MCC. If you'd *prefer* it MCC-managed instead, the alternative is adding a TC/SYS_TIME component and sourcing the ms tick from that — but the self-contained SysTick is simpler and keeps the time source inside the hand-written module. One caveat worth knowing: if a future change adds a Harmony component that also calls `SysTick_Config` (some `SYS_TIME` configs use SysTick), they'd collide — at that point we'd drop our `SysTick_Config`/`SysTick_Handler` and read the Harmony time source instead.

49	    (void)cli;
50	    /* TX ring drains at line rate regardless of any listener (the UART clocks
51	     * bytes onto the wire), so a bounded retry only ever waits for ring space,
52	     * never for a reader. Cap it so a pathological full-ring can't spin. */
53	    for (uint32_t tries = 0u; tries < 1000u; tries++)

246	            (void)xSemaphoreGiveFromISR(s_rx_notify, &hpw);

249	            (void)FLEXCOM2_USART_ErrorGet();
250	            (void)xSemaphoreGiveFromISR(s_rx_notify, &hpw);
251	            break;
252	        default:
253	            break;
254	    }
255	
256	    portYIELD_FROM_ISR(hpw);
257	}

8	 * marvin is the PLCA coordinator (node 0); this node is follower id 2. It

12	 * GPIO chip-select held across each transfer, the T1S_RST / T1S_IRQ_N pins

14	 * protocol is serviced from the main loop, woken by IRQ_N. See
15	 * firmware/guitar/SPEC.md and docs/t1s-podl-link.md.
16	 *
17	 * Call T1SFollower_Initialize() once after SYS_Initialize (SERCOM0_SPI/EIC

8	#include "definitions.h"   /* SERCOM0_SPI_*, SERCOM1_USART_*, EIC_*, PORT macros, CMSIS */
9	
10	#include "tc6.h"
11	#include "tc6-regs.h"
12	
13	/* PLCA follower identity (docs/t1s-podl-link.md §7.1). */
14	#define T1S_NODE_ID         (2u)
15	#define T1S_NODE_COUNT      (8u)     /* PLCA cycle length (must match the coordinator) */
16	#define T1S_INSTANCE        (0u)
17	
18	#define T1S_ETHERTYPE       (0x88B5u)
19	#define T1S_ETH_HDR_LEN     (14u)
20	#define T1S_CMD_BIT_MASK    (0x7Fu)  /* 5 frets + 2 strum */
21	
22	/* Coordinator-assigned MAC for this node: 02:00:00:00:00:02. */
23	static uint8_t s_mac[6] = { 0x02u, 0x00u, 0x00u, 0x00u, 0x00u, (uint8_t)T1S_NODE_ID };
24	
25	static TC6_t            *s_tc6;
26	static volatile bool     s_need_service;
27	static volatile bool     s_link_up;
28	static volatile bool     s_spi_busy;
29	
30	/* Command frames are ~60 B after min-frame padding; this only needs the header
31	 * plus the first payload byte, but size for a padded frame. */
32	static uint8_t           s_rx_buf[64];
33	
34	/* The 1 ms time base is the MCC SYSTICK plib: SYS_Initialize runs
35	 * SYSTICK_TimerInitialize; this module starts it and reads
36	 * SYSTICK_GetTickCounter() (milliseconds) / SYSTICK_DelayMs(). */
37	
38	static void log_str(const char *s)
39	{
40	    (void)SERCOM1_USART_Write((uint8_t *)s, strlen(s));
41	}
42	
43	/*>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>  Wii-guitar actuation  >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>*/
44	
45	/* Software open-drain: assert = drive low (Clear + OutputEnable), release =
46	 * tri-state (InputEnable, controller pull-up restores idle). */
47	#define BTN_APPLY(mask, bit, NAME)                          \
48	    do {                                                    \
49	        if ((mask) & (1u << (bit))) {                       \
50	            NAME##_Clear();                                 \
51	            NAME##_OutputEnable();                          \
52	        } else {                                            \
53	            NAME##_InputEnable();                           \
54	        }                                                   \
55	    } while (0)
56	
57	static void buttons_release_all(void)
58	{
59	    FRET_GREEN_InputEnable();
60	    FRET_RED_InputEnable();
61	    FRET_YELLOW_InputEnable();
62	    FRET_BLUE_InputEnable();
63	    FRET_ORANGE_InputEnable();
64	    STRUM_DOWN_InputEnable();
65	    STRUM_UP_InputEnable();
66	}
67	
68	static void buttons_apply_mask(uint8_t mask)
69	{
70	    BTN_APPLY(mask, 0u, FRET_GREEN);
71	    BTN_APPLY(mask, 1u, FRET_RED);
72	    BTN_APPLY(mask, 2u, FRET_YELLOW);
73	    BTN_APPLY(mask, 3u, FRET_BLUE);
74	    BTN_APPLY(mask, 4u, FRET_ORANGE);
75	    BTN_APPLY(mask, 5u, STRUM_DOWN);
76	    BTN_APPLY(mask, 6u, STRUM_UP);
77	}
78	
79	/*>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>  SPI + IRQ  >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>*/
80	
81	/* SERCOM0 SPI completion ISR: the chunk transfer is done — deassert the GPIO
82	 * chip-select, hand the buffer back to the driver, and flag for servicing. */
83	static void spi_done_cb(uintptr_t context)
84	{
85	    (void)context;
86	    T1S_CS_Set();            /* CS high — end of transaction */
87	    s_spi_busy = false;
88	    s_need_service = true;
89	    TC6_SpiBufferDone(T1S_INSTANCE, true);
90	}
91	
92	/* T1S_IRQ_N falling-edge (EIC EXTINT15): the MAC-PHY needs servicing. */
93	static void irq_cb(uintptr_t context)
94	{
95	    (void)context;
96	    s_need_service = true;
97	}
98	
99	/* Run the protocol stack until it has no immediately pending work. IRQ_N is
100	 * active-low; TC6_Service treats a false interruptLevel as "interrupt active". */
101	static void service_pump(void)
102	{
103	    do {
104	        s_need_service = false;
105	        bool no_int = (T1S_IRQ_N_Get() != 0u);
106	        (void)TC6_Service(s_tc6, no_int);
107	    } while (s_need_service);
108	    TC6Regs_CheckTimers();
109	}
110	
111	/*>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>  Public API  >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>*/
112	
113	void T1SFollower_Initialize(void)
114	{
115	    SYSTICK_TimerStart();    /* MCC inits the timer; the app enables it */
116	
117	    buttons_release_all();   /* pins boot Out/Low (asserted) — release first */
118	
119	    /* Hardware reset pulse (T1S_RST active-low, idle high). */
120	    T1S_CS_Set();
121	    T1S_RST_Clear();
122	    SYSTICK_DelayMs(10u);
123	    T1S_RST_Set();
124	    SYSTICK_DelayMs(10u);
125	
126	    SERCOM0_SPI_CallbackRegister(spi_done_cb, 0u);  /* Mode 0 set by MCC init */
127	
128	    s_tc6 = TC6_Init(NULL);
129	    if (s_tc6 == NULL) {
130	        log_str("guitar: TC6_Init failed\r\n");
131	        return;
132	    }
133	
134	    EIC_CallbackRegister(EIC_PIN_15, irq_cb, 0u);   /* EXTINT15 enabled in EIC_Initialize */
135	
136	    /* Configure the LAN8651 + PLCA as follower id 2. Not promiscuous — the
137	     * MAC-PHY filters to this node's MAC + broadcast. */
138	    while (!TC6Regs_Init(s_tc6, NULL, s_mac, true, T1S_NODE_ID, T1S_NODE_COUNT,
139	                         0u, 0u, false, false, false)) {
140	        log_str("guitar: TC6Regs_Init busy, retry\r\n");
141	        SYSTICK_DelayMs(50u);
142	    }
143	
144	    uint32_t deadline = SYSTICK_GetTickCounter() + 3000u;
145	    while (!TC6Regs_GetInitDone(s_tc6) &&
146	           ((int32_t)(deadline - SYSTICK_GetTickCounter()) > 0)) {
147	        service_pump();
148	    }
149	
150	    if (TC6Regs_GetInitDone(s_tc6)) {
151	        s_link_up = true;
152	        TC6_EnableData(s_tc6, true);
153	        char buf[80];
154	        (void)snprintf(buf, sizeof(buf),
155	                       "guitar: LAN8651 up - chipRev=%u, MAC=02:00:00:00:00:%02X, "
156	                       "PLCA follower id=%u/%u\r\n",
157	                       (unsigned)TC6Regs_GetChipRevision(s_tc6),
158	                       (unsigned)T1S_NODE_ID, (unsigned)T1S_NODE_ID,
159	                       (unsigned)T1S_NODE_COUNT);
160	        log_str(buf);
161	    } else {
162	        log_str("guitar: MAC-PHY not responding (check EVB/wiring); still servicing\r\n");
163	    }
164	}
165	
166	void T1SFollower_Tasks(void)
167	{
168	    if (s_tc6 == NULL) {
169	        return;
170	    }
171	    service_pump();
172	    if (!s_link_up && TC6Regs_GetInitDone(s_tc6)) {
173	        s_link_up = true;
174	        TC6_EnableData(s_tc6, true);
175	        log_str("guitar: LAN8651 up (late)\r\n");
176	    }
177	}
178	
179	bool T1SFollower_IsConnected(void)
180	{
181	    return s_link_up;
182	}
183	
184	/*>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>  TC6 driver callbacks (integrator)  >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>*/
185	
186	bool TC6_CB_OnSpiTransaction(uint8_t tc6instance, uint8_t *pTx, uint8_t *pRx,
187	                             uint16_t len, void *pGlobalTag)
188	{
189	    (void)tc6instance;
190	    (void)pGlobalTag;
191	    if (s_spi_busy) {
192	        return false;
193	    }
194	    s_spi_busy = true;
195	    T1S_CS_Clear();          /* CS low — start of transaction (held across the chunk) */
196	    if (!SERCOM0_SPI_WriteRead(pTx, len, pRx, len)) {
197	        T1S_CS_Set();
198	        s_spi_busy = false;
199	        return false;
200	    }
201	    return true;
202	}
203	
204	void TC6_CB_OnNeedService(TC6_t *pInst, void *pGlobalTag)
205	{
206	    (void)pInst;
207	    (void)pGlobalTag;
208	    s_need_service = true;
209	}
210	
211	void TC6_CB_OnRxEthernetSlice(TC6_t *pInst, const uint8_t *pRx, uint16_t offset,
212	                              uint16_t len, void *pGlobalTag)
213	{
214	    (void)pInst;
215	    (void)pGlobalTag;
216	    if (((uint32_t)offset + len) <= sizeof(s_rx_buf)) {
217	        memcpy(&s_rx_buf[offset], pRx, len);
218	    }
219	}
220	
221	void TC6_CB_OnRxEthernetPacket(TC6_t *pInst, bool success, uint16_t len,
222	                               uint64_t *rxTimestamp, void *pGlobalTag)
223	{
224	    (void)pInst;
225	    (void)rxTimestamp;
226	    (void)pGlobalTag;
227	
228	    if (!success || (len < (T1S_ETH_HDR_LEN + 1u))) {
229	        return;
230	    }
231	    uint16_t ethertype = (uint16_t)((s_rx_buf[12] << 8) | s_rx_buf[13]);
232	    if (ethertype != T1S_ETHERTYPE) {
233	        return;
234	    }
235	    /* Command byte is the first payload octet; trailing min-frame padding is
236	     * ignored. Apply directly (latest-wins). */
237	    buttons_apply_mask((uint8_t)(s_rx_buf[T1S_ETH_HDR_LEN] & T1S_CMD_BIT_MASK));
238	}
239	
240	void TC6_CB_OnError(TC6_t *pInst, TC6_Error_t err, void *pGlobalTag)
241	{
242	    (void)pGlobalTag;
243	    log_str("guitar: t1s error: ");
244	    log_str(TC6_GetErrorStr(err));
245	    log_str("\r\n");
246	    switch (err) {
247	        case TC6Error_NoHardware:
248	        case TC6Error_BadChecksum:
249	        case TC6Error_UnexpectedCtrl:
250	        case TC6Error_BadTxData:
251	        case TC6Error_SyncLost:
252	        case TC6Error_SpiError:
253	            TC6Regs_Reinit(pInst);
254	            break;
255	        default:
256	            break;
257	    }
258	}
259	
260	/*>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>  TC6Regs callbacks (integrator)  >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>*/
261	
262	uint32_t TC6Regs_CB_GetTicksMs(void)
263	{
264	    return SYSTICK_GetTickCounter();
265	}
266	
267	void TC6Regs_CB_OnEvent(TC6_t *pInst, TC6Regs_Event_t event, void *pTag)
268	{
269	    (void)pTag;
270	    log_str("guitar: t1s event: ");
271	    log_str(TC6Regs_GetEventStr(event));
272	    log_str("\r\n");
273	    switch (event) {
274	        case TC6Regs_Event_Loss_of_Framing_Error:
275	        case TC6Regs_Event_RX_Non_Recoverable_Error:
276	        case TC6Regs_Event_TX_Non_Recoverable_Error:
277	            TC6Regs_Reinit(pInst);
278	            break;
279	        default:
280	            break;
281	    }
282	}

#ifndef CLI_H
#define CLI_H

/* Operator CLI on the SERCOM1 debug UART (embedded-cli, static allocation).
 * Bare-metal: CLI_Tasks() polls the RX ring each main-loop pass — no task.
 * Commands: status, btn <mask>, tap <mask> [ms] (manual Wii-guitar actuation,
 * useful for verifying the controller wiring before the T1S link is up).
 *
 * Call CLI_Initialize() after SYS_Initialize (SERCOM1 brought up by MCC), then
 * CLI_Tasks() repeatedly from the main loop. */

void CLI_Initialize(void);
void CLI_Tasks(void);

#endif /* CLI_H */

```

#include "cli.h"

#include <stdint.h>
#include <stdbool.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <stdarg.h>

#include "definitions.h"   /* SERCOM1_USART_*, SYSTICK_* */
#include "embedded_cli.h"
#include "t1s_follower.h"

/* embedded-cli working buffer (static-allocation mode → no malloc). Sized for
 * the small config below; the requirement is checked at init. */
static CLI_UINT     s_cli_buf[BYTES_TO_CLI_UINTS(1024)];
static EmbeddedCli *s_cli;

static void uart_str(const char *s)
{
    (void)SERCOM1_USART_Write((uint8_t *)s, strlen(s));
}

/* Char sink for embedded-cli. The SERCOM1 TX ring drains at the wire rate via
 * its ISR regardless of any listener, so a bounded retry only ever waits for
 * ring space. */
static void cli_write_char(EmbeddedCli *cli, char c)
{
    (void)cli;
    for (uint32_t tries = 0u; tries < 1000u; tries++)
    {
        if (SERCOM1_USART_Write((uint8_t *)&c, 1u) == 1u) { return; }
        SYSTICK_DelayMs(1u);
    }
}

static void cli_printf(const char *fmt, ...)
{
    static char buf[128];
    va_list ap;
    va_start(ap, fmt);
    (void)vsnprintf(buf, sizeof(buf), fmt, ap);
    va_end(ap);
    embeddedCliPrint(s_cli, buf);   /* appends newline */
}

/* ---- commands ----------------------------------------------------------- */

static void cmd_status(EmbeddedCli *cli, char *args, void *ctx)
{
    (void)cli;
    (void)args;
    (void)ctx;
    cli_printf("link:    %s", T1SFollower_IsConnected() ? "up" : "down");
    cli_printf("chipRev: %u", (unsigned)T1SFollower_ChipRev());
    cli_printf("rx cmds: %lu", (unsigned long)T1SFollower_RxCount());
    cli_printf("last:    0x%02X", (unsigned)T1SFollower_LastCmd());
}

static void cmd_btn(EmbeddedCli *cli, char *args, void *ctx)
{
    (void)cli;
    (void)ctx;
    const char *a = embeddedCliGetToken(args, 1);
    if (a == NULL)
    {
        cli_printf("usage: btn <mask hex>  (bit0 G,1 R,2 Y,3 B,4 O,5 Sdn,6 Sup; 0=release)");
        return;
    }
    uint8_t m = (uint8_t)(strtoul(a, NULL, 16) & 0x7Fu);
    T1SFollower_ApplyButtons(m);
    cli_printf("buttons = 0x%02X", (unsigned)m);
}

static void cmd_tap(EmbeddedCli *cli, char *args, void *ctx)
{
    (void)cli;
    (void)ctx;
    const char *a = embeddedCliGetToken(args, 1);
    if (a == NULL)
    {
        cli_printf("usage: tap <mask hex> [ms]");
        return;
    }
    uint8_t  m  = (uint8_t)(strtoul(a, NULL, 16) & 0x7Fu);
    const char *b = embeddedCliGetToken(args, 2);
    uint32_t ms = (b != NULL) ? (uint32_t)strtoul(b, NULL, 10) : 60u;

    T1SFollower_ApplyButtons(m);
    SYSTICK_DelayMs(ms);
    T1SFollower_ReleaseButtons();
    cli_printf("tap 0x%02X %lums", (unsigned)m, (unsigned long)ms);
}

static void register_commands(void)
{
    static const CliCommandBinding bindings[] = {
        { "status", "Print link / chipRev / rx count / last command", false, NULL, cmd_status },
        { "btn",    "btn <mask hex>: drive the 7 button GPIOs (0 = release all)", true, NULL, cmd_btn },
        { "tap",    "tap <mask hex> [ms]: assert then release (default 60 ms)",   true, NULL, cmd_tap },
    };
    for (size_t i = 0u; i < (sizeof(bindings) / sizeof(bindings[0])); i++)
    {
        (void)embeddedCliAddBinding(s_cli, bindings[i]);
    }
}

void CLI_Initialize(void)
{
    EmbeddedCliConfig *cfg = embeddedCliDefaultConfig();
    cfg->invitation         = "guitar> ";
    cfg->rxBufferSize       = 32u;
    cfg->cmdBufferSize      = 32u;
    cfg->historyBufferSize  = 64u;
    cfg->maxBindingCount    = 8u;
    cfg->enableAutoComplete = true;
    cfg->cliBuffer          = s_cli_buf;
    cfg->cliBufferSize      = sizeof(s_cli_buf);

    if (embeddedCliRequiredSize(cfg) > sizeof(s_cli_buf))
    {
        uart_str("cli: buffer too small\r\n");
        return;
    }

    s_cli = embeddedCliNew(cfg);
    if (s_cli == NULL)
    {
        uart_str("cli: init failed\r\n");
        return;
    }
    s_cli->writeChar = cli_write_char;

    register_commands();
    embeddedCliProcess(s_cli);   /* emit the first prompt */
}

void CLI_Tasks(void)
{
    if (s_cli == NULL)
    {
        return;
    }
    uint8_t c;
    while (SERCOM1_USART_Read(&c, 1u) == 1u)
    {
        embeddedCliReceiveChar(s_cli, (char)c);
    }
    embeddedCliProcess(s_cli);
}

```

```text
71	(coordinator) — the follower inverts the roles: RX the command, no detector-stream TX.
72	
73	## 4. Firmware design (to build)
74	
75	1. **Bring-up:** reset the LAN8651 (`RST` pulse), configure SPI (Mode 0), `TC6_Init` +
76	   `TC6Regs_Init` as follower id 2. Gate: read chip revision + PLCA *follower* status.
77	2. **RX path:** TC6 delivers the marvin command frame → validate ethertype `0x88B5` → take the
78	   1-byte payload as the button bitmask → apply to the 7 GPIOs (port fretboard's
79	   `cmd_receive_apply_mask` logic).
80	3. **TX path:** none required initially. Optional `applied_mask` telemetry back to marvin (for
81	   edge-ai zero-skew labels) is **deferred** with the edge-ai re-homing effort.
82	4. **Service:** call `TC6_Service` from the main loop / tick, woken by `IRQ_N`.
83	
84	## 5. What this is *not*
85	
86	- **Not a sensor.** No phototransistors, no ADC — sensing is the detector node's job.
87	- **Not an on-device model.** The edge-ai MODEL_DRIVEN inference stays on fretboard for now;
88	  re-homing it (detector infers → T1S → guitar) is out of scope.
89	- **Not a game brain.** No chord/strum timing — marvin's timing pipeline owns that and sends
90	  the resulting bitmask.
91	- **Not the PLCA coordinator.** marvin (node 0) beacons the cycle; guitar is a follower.
92	
93	## 6. Milestones
94	
95	| Status | Item |
96	|---|---|
97	| ✅ | **G0** — guitar MCC project generated: SERCOM0 SPI (Mode 0), EIC EXTINT15 (falling) on `IRQ_N`, `CS`/`RST` GPIO, 7 button GPIOs, SERCOM1 debug UART |
98	| 🚧 | **G1** — T1S follower bring-up: chipRev + PLCA follower status (firmware written; pending build/hardware) |
99	| 🚧 | **G2** — command RX → Wii GPIO actuation (firmware written; pending build/hardware) |

int main ( void )
{
    /* Initialize all modules */
    SYS_Initialize ( NULL );

    T1SFollower_Initialize ( );
    CLI_Initialize ( );

    while ( true )
    {
        /* Maintain state machines of all polled MPLAB Harmony modules. */

         * the Wii-guitar GPIOs. */

=== SYSTICK_DelayMs + TimerStart bodies ===
void SYSTICK_TimerStart ( void )
{
    SysTick->VAL = 0U;
    SysTick->CTRL |= SysTick_CTRL_ENABLE_Msk;
}
void SYSTICK_DelayMs ( uint32_t delay_ms)
{
   uint32_t elapsedCount=0U, delayCount;
   uint32_t deltaCount, oldCount, newCount, period;

   period = SysTick->LOAD + 1U;

   /* Calculate the count for the given delay */
   delayCount=(SYSTICK_FREQ/1000U)*delay_ms;

   if((SysTick->CTRL & SysTick_CTRL_ENABLE_Msk) == SysTick_CTRL_ENABLE_Msk)
   {
       oldCount = SysTick->VAL;

       while (elapsedCount < delayCount)
       {
           newCount = SysTick->VAL;
           deltaCount = oldCount - newCount;

           if(newCount > oldCount)
           {
               deltaCount = period - newCount + oldCount;
           }

           oldCount = newCount;
           elapsedCount = elapsedCount + deltaCount;
       }
   }
}

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-17 14:03:32Z)**_

That output tells us a lot — the CLI **is** reachable, the problem is the opposite of what it looks like.

## Answer: the console is reached; it's being *drowned out*

`T1SFollower_Initialize()` doesn't hang on a failed link — the init-done wait is bounded to 3 s, after which it logs `MAC-PHY not responding` and **returns**, so `CLI_Initialize()` runs and the prompt is emitted. The CLI is up.

The problem is what happens *next*: the main loop calls `T1SFollower_Tasks()` → `service_pump()` → `TC6_Service()` **every iteration**, and with no MAC-PHY responding, each pass raises `TC6_CB_OnError` (and `TC6Regs_Reinit`), and my handler logs *every single one* via `log_str`. That's thousands of `guitar: t1s error: …` lines per second saturating the SERCOM1 TX ring — so the prompt and your keystrokes are buried under the flood. It looks like "no console," but really the console is unusable.

I dropped a safeguard the reference `tc6-noip.c` had here: its `OnError`/`OnEvent` use a **rate-limited print**. I used a plain `log_str`. That's the bug.

## Fix: rate-limit the T1S diagnostics (and count them for `status`)

Let me cap the error/event logging to ~1/sec and expose an error count so `status` still tells you the link is unhappy without flooding:

The fix is coherent and complete. To recap your question and what I changed:

## Why it looked like "no console"
The CLI **was** running — `T1SFollower_Initialize()` returns after a bounded 3 s timeout when the link doesn't come up, so `CLI_Initialize()` runs and the prompt is emitted. But with no LAN8651, `TC6_Service()` raises an error on **every** main-loop pass, and my handler logged each one unconditionally → thousands of `t1s error:` lines/sec saturating the TX ring and burying the prompt. So: console reached, just flooded.

## What I changed
- `OnError`/`OnEvent` now log through a **rate-limited `diag_log()` (≤ ~1/sec)** — restoring the `PrintRateLimited` behavior the reference `tc6-noip.c` has, which I'd dropped in the bare-metal port.
- Errors are **counted** (`T1SFollower_ErrCount()`) and surfaced in `status` (`errors: N`), so you still see the link is unhappy without the spam.

Now, with no board, you'll get roughly one `t1s error:` line per second and a usable `guitar>` prompt — `status`, `btn <mask>`, and `tap <mask> [ms]` should work, so you can exercise the Wii-guitar wiring while the link is down.

This is the same uncommitted CLI drop (now with the flood fix). Rebuild and confirm the prompt is usable; if good, say the word and I'll commit the CLI + fix together. 

One forward note: once the LAN8651 is actually connected and the link comes up, errors should stop entirely (the flood only happens with no MAC-PHY answering) — so this rate-limit is really about making the no-board/bring-up experience sane, not masking a steady-state problem.

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-17 14:34:16Z)**_

All coherent. Here's the situation and what I changed.

## Diagnosis
- **SysTick is correctly wired** (`interrupts.c` vector → `plib_systick` handler, `SYSTICK_FREQ=24 MHz`, LOAD=24000 → a true 1 ms tick). So `GetTickCounter()` *is* milliseconds, which means a binary flooding at 10 Hz **cannot contain the 1 s rate-limit** — you're running a pre-fix build. A clean rebuild + reflash is needed.
- **"No CLI activity" had a real cause:** `T1SFollower_Initialize()` blocked up to 3 s waiting for the link, and `CLI_Initialize()` only ran *after* it. The CLI was gated behind the T1S link — wrong.

## Two fixes
1. **Non-blocking init.** `T1SFollower_Initialize()` now kicks off `TC6Regs_Init` and returns immediately; `T1SFollower_Tasks()` finishes bring-up in the background and logs `LAN8651 up …` when the link comes up. So the CLI is responsive from boot, link or no link.
2. **Rate-limited diagnostics** (the earlier fix): `OnError`/`OnEvent` log through `diag_log` (≤1/sec); errors are counted and shown in `status`.
3. **Boot banner** — `guitar: boot - t1s follower + cli` prints once at startup, so you can confirm the new binary is actually running.

## What to expect after a clean rebuild + reflash
- `guitar: boot - t1s follower + cli` once,
- `guitar> ` prompt, **responsive immediately** (try `status`),
- with no board: ~1 `t1s error:` line/sec (not a flood),
- `status` shows `link: down`, `errors: N` climbing.

**If you still see 10 Hz after reflashing**, then the build isn't picking up `t1s_follower.c` — do a clean/rebuild (delete `_build/`), since that would mean the object wasn't recompiled. The banner is the tell: no banner = stale binary.

Still uncommitted (debugging). Once you confirm the prompt is usable, I'll commit the CLI + these fixes together. Want to rebuild and report what the banner/prompt do?
